title: SupportDesk User Manual
subtitle: Tickets, live chat, customers, knowledge, analytics, administration, the customer portal and the mobile app
audience: Everyone who uses SupportDesk: agents, supervisors, administrators, customers and platform operators. Each chapter says who it is for. You do not need any technical knowledge.
support: If you need help, contact your SupportDesk administrator. Say what you were trying to do and what you saw on the screen. Give the ticket number if there is one. Customers can contact the support team through the portal.

versionHistory.changes: First edition. Covers the agent desk, supervision, administration, the customer portal, the mobile app and the platform console.

chapters.title: Introduction
intro: This chapter is for everyone. It explains what SupportDesk does, which part of it you use, and the ideas you meet in every chapter.
Read it first. Then go to the chapters for your role.

sections.title: What SupportDesk does
intro: SupportDesk is a help desk. It collects customer questions from e-mail, the customer portal, live chat, messaging apps and phone calls in one place.
Each question becomes a ticket. Agents answer tickets, and timers show how much time is left to respond. Customers follow their tickets in the portal or the mobile app.

SupportDesk also keeps your customers, their products and their contracts. It has a knowledge base of help articles and reports on how the team performs. An AI assistant can summarise tickets and draft replies for you to check.

sections.title: Who uses which part
sections.intro: SupportDesk has several apps. You use only the ones your role needs.

rows: Answer tickets and chats, look up customers, use the knowledge base, see your work and the team's work.
Set up the workspace: users and roles, channels, SLA policies, automation, brands, security and billing.
Raise and follow tickets, read help articles, ask the community and chat with support.
Work on tickets or follow your own tickets from a phone, even with a weak connection.
Run the SupportDesk service: workspaces, plans, invoices and support access.

blocks.note: You see only the menus and buttons your role allows. If a task in this manual names a menu you cannot see, ask your administrator for access.

sections.title: The desk at a glance
sections.intro: The desk opens after you sign in. The same frame surrounds every page: the menu on the left and the top bar above the page.

blocks.caption: The desk with the **Command Center** page open.
blocks.alt: SupportDesk desk with the navigation menu, top bar and the Command Center page, with numbered highlights

callouts: The **navigation menu** opens each part of the desk. It is grouped into **Work**, **Customers**, **Operations** and **Settings**.
**Search** finds tickets and opens pages and commands. Press [[Ctrl+K]] to open it from anywhere.
**New ticket** creates a ticket for a customer.
The **notifications** bell shows how many notifications you have not read.
**Availability** tells your team whether you can take new work, for example **Online** or **Away**.
Your **account menu** holds your profile, your preferences and **Sign out**.
The **page header** shows the page title and its main buttons.

blocks.tip: Select **Collapse** at the bottom of the menu to show icons only. This gives the page more room.

sections.title: Key ideas
sections.intro: These words appear throughout the manual. The glossary at the end explains more of them.

rows: One customer question or problem, with every message, note and change about it. Each ticket has a number, such as **#1004**.
Where a ticket is in its life, such as **Open**, **In Progress** or **Resolved**. Chapter 5 lists every status.
How urgent a ticket is: **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Critical**.
The service level agreement. It sets how soon the team must respond to and resolve a ticket. Timers count down on each ticket.
The way a ticket arrives, such as e-mail, the portal, live chat, a messaging app or a phone call.
A saved list of tickets, such as **My open tickets** or **Unassigned**. Agents work from views.
Groups of agents. A ticket belongs to a department, and routing assigns it to a team or an agent.
Your organisation's own SupportDesk. You enter its short name when you sign in.
A company name, logo and portal that customers see. One workspace can serve several brands.
Help articles for agents and customers. Customers read published articles in the portal.

sections.title: How to use this manual
intro: Each chapter starts by saying who it is for. Tasks have numbered steps, and the result tells you what you see when you finish.
The screenshots come from a demonstration workspace. Your workspace has its own names, numbers and settings, so your screens look a little different.

list: New to the desk? Read chapters 2 to 6 first.
Supervisors: read chapters 12, 15 and 16 as well.
Administrators: start with chapter 17, then the chapters for each setting you manage.
Customers: go straight to chapter 29.
Platform operators: go straight to chapter 31.

chapters.title: Getting started
intro: This chapter is for everyone who uses the SupportDesk desk: agents, supervisors and administrators.
It shows how to join your team, sign in and find your way around. It also covers your profile, your password, two-step verification and signing out.

sections.title: What you need to sign in
intro: You sign in to the desk with three details. Your administrator gives them to you.
Customers do not use the desk. They use the customer portal, which has its own sign-in.

rows: Your company's SupportDesk name, for example `acme`. Every company has its own workspace.
The e-mail address your administrator used when they added you.
The password you chose when you accepted your invitation.

blocks.note: If you are new, you first get an invitation e-mail. Accept it to choose your password. See [Accept an invitation](#gs-accept-invitation).

sections.title: Accept an invitation
sections.intro: When an administrator adds you as an agent, SupportDesk sends you an invitation e-mail. Use it to choose your password.
prerequisites: You have the invitation e-mail. It contains a link and an invitation code.

steps.text: Open the link in the invitation e-mail.
steps.note: The **Join your team** page opens. **Workspace** and **Work e-mail** are often filled in for you.

steps: Check the **Workspace** and **Work e-mail** fields.
In **Invitation code**, enter the code from the e-mail. It looks like `K7QM-4ZP2`.
If your name is wrong, enter it in **Your name**. Leave it empty to keep the name your administrator entered.
In **New password**, enter a password. Use at least 10 characters with upper-case and lower-case letters and a digit.
In **Confirm password**, enter the same password again.

steps.text: Select **Set password**.
steps.caption: The **Join your team** page with the invitation code filled in.
steps.alt: Join your team form with workspace, work e-mail, invitation code, name and password fields

sections.result: The page says **You're all set**. Select **Go to sign in** to sign in for the first time.

blocks.note: Your organisation may ask for longer or stronger passwords. **Set password** stays unavailable until both password fields match.

sections.title: Sign in to the desk
sections.intro: Sign in at the start of each working day, or when your session has ended.
prerequisites: You know your workspace name, work e-mail and password.
steps: Open the desk address that your administrator gave you. The **Sign in to SupportDesk** page opens.
In **Workspace**, enter your workspace name.
In **Work e-mail**, enter your work e-mail address.
In **Password**, enter your password.

steps.text: To check what you typed, select the eye button at the end of the **Password** field.
steps.note: The button shows or hides your password. Hide it again if someone can see your screen.

steps: Select **Sign in**.
sections.result: The desk opens on the first module you can use, usually **Command Center**. If two-step verification is on, the **Two-step verification** page opens first.

blocks.caption: The sign-in page with the workspace and work e-mail filled in.
blocks.alt: Sign in to SupportDesk page with numbered highlights on the fields, the eye button, the Sign in button and the theme button

callouts: **Workspace**: your company's SupportDesk name.
**Work e-mail**: the address you were invited with.
**Password**: your desk password.
The eye button shows or hides the password.
**Sign in** checks your details and opens the desk.
The moon or sun button switches between light and dark theme.

blocks.note: The page remembers your workspace and e-mail on this device. It never stores your password.

blocks.tip: If you open a desk link while signed out, the desk takes you to that page after you sign in.

blocks.caption: If a field is empty or wrong, a message appears under it.
blocks.alt: Sign in form with the messages Enter your workspace name, Enter a valid e-mail address and Enter your password

sections.title: Enter a two-step verification code
sections.intro: Two-step verification adds a code to your password. You need it when you turned it on, or when your workspace requires it.
prerequisites: You entered your workspace, e-mail and password, and selected **Sign in**.
steps: Wait for the **Two-step verification** page to open.

steps.text: If you see two buttons, choose **E-mail code** or **Authenticator app**.
steps.note: **Authenticator app** is chosen for you when you have set one up.

steps: Find the 6-digit code in the e-mail from SupportDesk, or in your authenticator app.
In **Verification code**, enter the code.

steps.text: Select **Verify**.
steps.caption: The **Two-step verification** page for an e-mailed code.
steps.alt: Two-step verification page with the verification code field, the Verify button and the Use a different account button

sections.result: The desk opens.

callouts: **Verification code**: enter the code from the e-mail or the app.
**Verify** checks the code and opens the desk.
**Use a different account** takes you back to the sign-in page.

blocks.note: In a demo workspace, a box on this page shows the code for you. Real workspaces never show it.

blocks.tip: Codes expire after a short time. If a code fails, get a new one and try again.

sections.title: Forgotten passwords, expired passwords and ended sessions
intro: The desk has no self-service password reset. If you forget your password, ask your SupportDesk administrator to reset it.

Your workspace may make passwords expire. When yours has expired, the **Password expired** page opens after you sign in. Ask your administrator to reset your password. Then select **Back to sign in** and sign in again.

blocks.caption: The sign-in page after a session has ended.
blocks.alt: Sign in page with the message Your session ended. Please sign in again.

blocks: Sessions end after a time set by your administrator. They also end when an administrator signs you out. The sign-in page then shows **Your session ended.** and asks you to sign in again.
The desk sign-in page has no single sign-on button yet. Sign in with your workspace, e-mail and password.

blocks.heading: Other links on the sign-in page

list: **Start a free trial** creates a new workspace. See the chapter about subscription, billing and the free trial.
**Platform console** is for the people who run the SupportDesk service. See the chapter about the platform console.

sections.title: The desk screen
sections.intro: Every desk page has the same frame. The navigation rail is on the left. The top bar is above the page.

blocks.caption: The desk with the navigation rail and the top bar highlighted.
blocks.alt: Desk screen with numbered highlights on the navigation rail, Collapse, search box, New ticket, bell, availability, theme button and account menu

callouts: The navigation rail lists the modules you can open, grouped under **Work**, **Customers**, **Operations** and **Settings**.
**Collapse** shrinks the rail to icons only.
The search box opens the command palette.
**New ticket** creates a ticket. You see it only if your role lets you create tickets.
The bell shows your notifications and the number of unread ones.
Your availability, such as **Online**. Select it to change it.
The theme button switches between light and dark theme.
Your avatar opens the account menu.

blocks: You see only the modules your role allows. If a module is missing, ask your administrator for access.
When the connection drops, a bar says **Live updates paused — reconnecting…**. The desk keeps working. Lists catch up when the connection returns.

blocks.tip: On a phone, the rail is hidden. Select the menu button at the top left to open it.

sections.title: Modules in the navigation rail
sections.intro: This table lists every module. The keys are the shortcut that opens the module.

rows: Your live queue, SLA risk and team activity at a glance.
Saved views, the ticket list and the ticket workbench.
Live chat, social and messaging conversations.
Accounts, contacts, locations and their support history.
Products, modules, versions, installations, assets and contracts.
Departments, teams, skills, shifts and agent availability.
SLA policies, business hours, holidays and live breach risk.
Assignment rules, workflows, macros, escalations and schedules.
Articles, categories, review and portal publishing.
Dashboards, reports, scheduled exports and drill-downs.
Summaries, reply drafts, triage suggestions and approved AI actions.
The engineering board: escalated defects, fix versions and releases.
Users, roles, channels, ticket configuration, security and audit.

sections.title: Collapse or expand the navigation rail
sections.intro: Collapse the rail to give the page more room.
steps: At the bottom of the navigation rail, select **Collapse**.

steps.text: To see the name of a module, point to its icon.
steps.caption: The collapsed rail shows icons only.
steps.alt: Narrow navigation rail with module icons and an expand button at the bottom

steps: To show the labels again, select the expand button at the bottom of the rail.
sections.result: The rail shows icons only, or icons with labels. The desk remembers your choice on this device.

sections.title: Run a command from the command palette
sections.intro: The command palette lets you go anywhere and do common jobs without the mouse.

steps.text: Press [[Ctrl+K]], or [[⌘+K]] on a Mac. You can also press [[/]] or select the search box in the top bar.
steps.caption: The command palette before you type.
steps.alt: Command palette listing Navigation commands with their shortcut keys

steps: Type part of what you want, such as `analytics` or `password`.
Press [[↑]] or [[↓]] to choose a result.
Press [[Enter]] to run it, or select it with the mouse.
sections.result: The palette closes and runs the command. To close it without running anything, press [[Esc]].

blocks.heading: What you can do from the palette

list: Go to any module you can open.
Create a ticket with **New ticket**.
Open **My profile**, **Change password** or **Two-factor authentication**.
Set your availability, for example **Set availability: Away**.
Switch the theme with **Toggle light / dark theme**.
Show **Keyboard shortcuts** or **Sign out**.
Find a ticket. See [Find a ticket from the command palette](#gs-find-ticket).

blocks: On the **Tickets** screen, the palette also offers commands for the open ticket. The ticket chapters describe them.

blocks.note: When the search box is empty, a **Recent** group lists the last five commands you ran.

sections.title: Find a ticket from the command palette
sections.intro: Open a ticket by its number, or search tickets and customers by text.
prerequisites: You can view tickets.
steps: Press [[Ctrl+K]] to open the command palette.
Enter the ticket number, such as `#1042` or `1042`. Or enter at least two characters of text.

steps.text: Wait for the **Tickets** group to appear.
steps.caption: Search results for `report` in the command palette.
steps.alt: Command palette with a Tickets group listing six tickets and their statuses, and a Commands group below

steps: Select the ticket you want.
sections.result: The ticket opens.

blocks.note: Text search shows up to six tickets, newest activity first. A **Customers** group lists up to five customers whose name or code matches. Select one to open its Customer 360 page.

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts
sections.intro: Press [[?]] on any page to see the shortcuts that work there. You can also open the account menu and select **Keyboard shortcuts**.

blocks.caption: The **Keyboard shortcuts** dialog on the Command Center.
blocks.alt: Keyboard shortcuts dialog with General, Navigation and Actions groups

rows: Open or close the command palette.
Everywhere, even while you type in a field.
Open search, that is, the command palette.
Switch between light and dark theme.
Go to a module. See [Modules in the navigation rail](#gs-modules).
If you can open that module.

blocks: For two-key shortcuts, press the second key within about one second.
Single-key shortcuts do nothing while you type in a field. Press [[Esc]] or select an empty part of the page first.

blocks.note: The **Tickets** screen adds its own shortcuts, such as moving through the list and replying. The dialog lists them while you are on that screen.

sections.title: Set your availability
sections.intro: Your availability tells routing and your team whether you can take new work.
steps: In the top bar, select your availability, such as **Online**.

steps.text: Choose **Online**, **Away**, **Busy** or **Offline**.
steps.caption: The availability menu. A tick marks your current status.
steps.alt: Availability menu with Online, Away, Busy and Offline and a short hint under each

sections.result: The coloured dot and the label in the top bar change. Your avatar shows the same colour.

blocks.note: Your shifts and idle time do not change your availability. Set it yourself when you start, pause or stop work.

blocks.tip: You can also open the command palette and run **Set availability: Away**, or another status.

sections.title: Switch between light and dark theme
sections.intro: The desk follows your computer's light or dark setting at first. You can choose your own.
steps: In the top bar, select the moon button for dark theme, or the sun button for light theme.
To switch back, select the button again, or press [[Shift+T]].
sections.result: The desk changes theme at once. After you switch, it no longer follows your computer's setting.

blocks.tip: The sign-in page has the same button at the top right.

sections.title: The account menu
sections.intro: Select your avatar at the top right to open the account menu. It shows your name, e-mail and workspace.

blocks.caption: The account menu.
blocks.alt: Account menu with the user's name, e-mail and workspace, and the items My profile, Change password, Two-factor authentication, Keyboard shortcuts and Sign out

rows: Opens your profile. See [Update your profile](#gs-profile).
Opens the **Password** tab. See [Change your password](#gs-change-password).
Opens the **Two-factor** tab. The hint shows **On** or **Off**.

sections.title: Update your profile
sections.intro: Your profile holds your name, time zone, language and e-mail signature.
steps: Select your avatar, then select **My profile**. You can also press [[G]] then [[M]].
On the **Profile** tab, check or change **Display name**.
In **Time zone**, choose your time zone. Dates and SLA times use this zone.
In **Language & format**, choose how dates and numbers look.
In **E-mail signature**, write the text that ends your e-mail replies.
Select **Save profile**.
sections.result: A **Profile saved** message appears.

blocks.caption: The **Profile** tab of **My profile**.
blocks.alt: My profile page with numbered highlights on the tabs, identity card, display name, time zone, language, e-mail signature and Save profile

callouts: The tabs: **Profile**, **Password** and **Two-factor**.
Your name, e-mail and workspace, your roles and your departments. A **Light agent** badge shows if you are one.
**Display name**: the name colleagues and customers see.
**Time zone**: used for dates and SLA times.
**Language & format**: how dates and numbers look.
**E-mail signature**: added to your outgoing e-mail replies.
**Save profile** saves your changes.

blocks.note: SupportDesk adds the signature when it sends an e-mail reply. You do not see it in the reply editor.

sections.title: Change your password
sections.intro: Change your password at any time, for example if you think someone else knows it.
steps: Select your avatar, then select **Change password**. The **Password** tab opens.
In **Current password**, enter the password you use now.
In **New password**, enter a new password of at least 12 characters.
In **Confirm new password**, enter the new password again.

steps.text: Select **Change password**.
steps.caption: The **Change password** form.
steps.alt: Change password form with current, new and confirm password fields

sections.result: A **Password changed** message appears. Use the new password the next time you sign in.

blocks.tip: A passphrase of several words is easy to remember and hard to guess.

blocks.caption: The form shows a message under each field that needs a fix.
blocks.alt: Change password form with the messages Enter your current password, Use at least 12 characters and The passwords do not match

sections.title: Turn on two-factor authentication
sections.intro: Two-factor authentication protects your account with a code from an authenticator app. You need the app on your phone first.
prerequisites: An authenticator app on your phone, such as Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or 1Password.
steps: Select your avatar, then select **Two-factor authentication**.

steps.text: Select **Set up two-factor**.
steps.caption: The **Two-factor** tab while two-factor authentication is off.
steps.alt: Two-factor authentication card with status Off and the Set up two-factor button

steps: In your authenticator app, scan the QR code that appears.
If you cannot scan it, enter the key shown under **Can't scan? Enter this key manually** in the app instead.
In **Verification code**, enter the 6-digit code the app shows.
Select **Turn on**.
sections.result: A **Two-factor authentication is on** message appears. **Status** shows **On**. From now on, the sign-in asks for a code from the app.

blocks.note: Finish the setup within 15 minutes. After that, select **Set up two-factor** again to get a new QR code.

blocks.tip: To stop without turning it on, select **Cancel**.

sections.title: Turn off two-factor authentication
sections.intro: Turn it off only if you lose your phone or move to another app. You can set it up again at once.
prerequisites: Two-factor authentication is on for your account.

steps.text: Select your avatar, then select **Two-factor authentication**.
steps.caption: The **Two-factor** tab while two-factor authentication is on.
steps.alt: Two-factor authentication card with status On and the Turn off two-factor button

steps: Select **Turn off two-factor**. The **Turn off two-factor authentication?** dialog opens.
Select **Turn off**.
sections.result: A **Two-factor authentication is off** message appears. Your password alone now protects your account.

blocks.warning: Without two-factor authentication, anyone who learns your password can sign in as you.

blocks.note: If your workspace requires two-step verification, the sign-in still asks for a code. The code then comes by e-mail.

sections.title: Sign out
sections.intro: Sign out when you finish work, and always on a shared computer.
steps: Select your avatar at the top right.
Select **Sign out**.
sections.result: The sign-in page opens. Your session on this device has ended.

blocks.tip: You can also open the command palette and run **Sign out**.

sections.title: When a page is missing or closed to you
sections.intro: What you can see depends on your role. Your administrator sets it.

rows: **You don't have access to this area**
Your role lacks the permission for that page.
Select **Go to my workspace**. Ask an administrator if you need the page for your work.
The page does not exist or has moved.
Select **Go to my workspace**, or select **Search** to use the command palette.
**No modules are enabled for your role yet.**
Your role does not open any module.
Ask an administrator for access. You can still open your profile.

chapters.title: Command Center
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors. It explains the Command Center, your live overview of the desk.
It also covers the **Approvals** page, where supervisors approve or reject requests.

sections.title: What the Command Center shows
intro: The Command Center is usually the first page you see after you sign in. To open it from anywhere, select **Command Center** in the rail, or press [[G]] then [[C]].
Everything on the page is live. Numbers and lists update when tickets change, so you do not need to reload.

blocks.caption: The Command Center for an agent, from top to bottom.
blocks.alt: Command Center page with numbered highlights on the header buttons, the key number tiles and the six cards

callouts: **Enable desktop alerts** asks your browser to show SupportDesk alerts on your desktop. It disappears once you have answered.
**Open workspace** opens the **Tickets** module.
The key number tiles. Select a tile to open the matching ticket list.
**SLA risk board**: open tickets that are close to, or past, their SLA target.
**My open tickets by status**: a chart of your open tickets and the next ones due.
**My team**: open tickets against capacity for each colleague. Supervisors see **Team workload** here.
**Customer replies & mentions**: your latest customer replies and @mentions.
**Pending approvals**: requests that wait for a decision.
**Escalations**: open tickets that someone has escalated.

sections.title: Key number tiles
sections.intro: The tiles at the top count tickets you can see. Select a tile to open its list.

rows: Your open tickets whose due time has passed.
Your open tickets due between now and midnight.
Open tickets with no assignee. Supervisors see **Unassigned (my departments)**.
Open tickets close to an SLA target.
Every overdue ticket you can see, not only yours.
Open tickets that someone has escalated.
Requests that wait for a decision.

blocks.note: **My overdue** and **My due today** count only your open tickets that have a due time.

sections.title: Open a ticket list from a tile
sections.intro: Use a tile to jump straight to the tickets behind a number.
steps: Open the **Command Center**.
Select a tile, such as **SLA at risk**.
sections.result: The **Tickets** module opens with the matching queue selected. The ticket chapters explain how to work through the list.

blocks.tip: To open **Tickets** without choosing a queue, select **Open workspace** at the top right.

sections.title: The SLA risk board
sections.intro: The SLA risk board lists open tickets whose SLA is at risk or already breached. The ticket due soonest is at the top.

blocks.caption: The **SLA risk board** with breached tickets.
blocks.alt: SLA risk board with counts of breached and at-risk tickets, a refresh button and rows with countdowns, ticket numbers, subjects, priorities and assignees

list: The two counts at the top show how many tickets are **breached** and how many are **at risk**.
Each row shows the time left, or how long ago the target passed. It then shows the ticket number, subject and priority.
The last column shows the assignee's initials. A person icon with a minus sign means nobody is assigned.
Select a row to open the ticket.
Select the refresh button to reload the board at once.

blocks: The board updates as soon as an SLA alert arrives. A row with a new alert is highlighted for a few seconds. The board also re-sorts every minute.

blocks.note: When every open ticket is on track, the board says **No SLA risk right now**.

sections.title: My open tickets by status
sections.intro: This card shows your own open tickets as a ring chart, one colour for each status.

blocks.caption: The **My open tickets by status** card.
blocks.alt: Ring chart of open tickets by status with a legend and a list of the next tickets due

blocks: Point to a part of the ring to see the status and its count. Below the chart, the card lists up to five of your tickets that are due next. Select one to open it.

blocks.note: When nothing is assigned to you, the card says **Your queue is clear**.

sections.title: My team and Team workload
intro: This card compares each colleague's open tickets with their capacity. Capacity is the most tickets that person should hold at once.
Agents see **My team**, with the colleagues in their teams. Supervisors see **Team workload**, with everyone in their departments.

blocks.caption: The **Team workload** card for a supervisor.
blocks.alt: Team workload card with a bar chart of open tickets and capacity per agent and a table of agent, load and open over capacity

list: The line at the top says whose work you see and how many people are online.
The chart shows open tickets and capacity side by side for up to twelve people.
The table lists every person, the busiest first. The dot on each avatar shows their availability.
The **Load** bar changes colour when a person reaches 70% of capacity, and again at 90%.
**Open / capacity** shows the numbers. The ∞ sign means no capacity limit is set.
The word **light** marks a light agent.

blocks.caption: The **My team** card for an agent.
blocks.alt: My team card showing four colleagues of an agent's team with their load

sections.title: Customer replies and mentions
sections.intro: This card shows your latest twelve notifications about customer replies and @mentions. Unread ones are in bold.

list: Select an item to open its ticket. The item is then marked as read.
Select **All notifications** to open the **Notifications** page. See [The Notifications page](#nt-page).

blocks.note: New replies and mentions appear at the top as soon as they arrive.

sections.title: Pending approvals and escalations
sections.intro: The last two cards show work that needs a decision or extra attention.

rows: Up to four requests that wait for a decision. If you may decide them, **Approve** and **Reject** appear on each one. Select **View all** to open the **Approvals** page.
Up to ten open escalated tickets, with their status and assignee. Select a ticket to open it.

blocks.note: When there is nothing to show, the cards say **Nothing waiting for approval** and **No open escalations**.

sections.title: Agent view and supervisor view
sections.intro: Agents and supervisors see the same page. Supervisors see numbers for their whole departments.

blocks.caption: The top of the Command Center for a supervisor.
blocks.alt: Command Center for a supervisor with the header and the Unassigned (my departments) tile highlighted

callouts: The greeting says **Numbers cover your departments.**
The tile is called **Unassigned (my departments)**.

rows: **Your queue, SLA risk and team at a glance.**
Requests you raised, or that are addressed to you.
Requests you can approve or reject.

blocks.note: The tiles that start with **My** always count only your own tickets, for agents and supervisors alike.

sections.title: Turn on desktop alerts from the Command Center
sections.intro: Desktop alerts show urgent notifications even when the desk is in a background tab.
steps: Open the **Command Center**.
At the top right, select **Enable desktop alerts**.
When your browser asks, select **Allow**.
sections.result: The button disappears. Warnings and critical notifications now also appear as desktop alerts. See [Turn on desktop alerts](#nt-desktop-alerts).

sections.title: The Approvals page
intro: Some actions need a supervisor's approval first. Examples are moving a ticket to another department, some workflow steps and some AI actions.
The **Approvals** page lists these requests. Open it from the **Pending approvals** tile, or select **View all** on the **Pending approvals** card.

blocks.caption: The **Approvals** page with nothing waiting for a decision.
blocks.alt: Approvals page with numbered highlights on the Refresh button, the Pending, Decided and My requests tabs, and the list

callouts: **Refresh** reloads the lists.
**Pending**: requests that wait for a decision. The badge shows how many.
**Decided**: requests that were approved, rejected, cancelled or expired.
**My requests**: requests that you raised.
The list for the selected tab.

list: A label with the request type, such as **Department transfer**, **Workflow transition**, **AI action** or **Request**.
A link to the ticket, with its number and subject. Select it to open the ticket.
Who asked, when, and when the request expires.
What the request would do, such as **Transfer to Billing**, and the reason the requester gave.

blocks.caption: A decided request on the **Decided** tab, with its status at the right.
blocks.alt: Decided tab with one expired leave request showing the requester, the reason and the status Expired

blocks.note: Leave requests from agents also appear on this page.

sections.title: Approve or reject a request
sections.intro: Decide a request so that the work behind it can go ahead or stop.
prerequisites: Your role lets you decide approvals. Supervisors and administrators usually can.
You did not raise the request yourself. Nobody can decide their own request.
steps: Open the **Approvals** page from the **Pending approvals** tile.
On the **Pending** tab, find the request.
Read what the request would do and the reason. To see the ticket, select its number.
In **Note (optional)**, enter a short note for the requester, if you want to.
Select **Approve** or **Reject**.
sections.result: A **Request approved** or **Request rejected** message appears. The request moves to the **Decided** tab. The requester gets a notification.

blocks.tip: You can also approve or reject from the **Pending approvals** card on the Command Center.

blocks.note: If someone else decided the request first, a message says so and the list reloads.

sections.title: Check the requests you raised
sections.intro: See whether your own requests are still waiting or have been decided.
steps: Open the **Approvals** page.
Select the **My requests** tab.
Find your request in the list.
sections.result: A waiting request says **Waiting for a supervisor’s decision.** A decided request shows its status, who decided it, when, and any note.

rows: The request waits for a decision. It has no status label in the list.
A supervisor approved it. The action goes ahead.
A supervisor rejected it. The action does not happen.
The request no longer applies. For example, the agent cancelled the leave they asked for.
Nobody decided it before its expiry time.

chapters.title: Ticket views and the ticket list
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who work through tickets in the **Tickets** module.
It explains queues and saved views, the ticket list, and how to update many tickets at once. It also covers the recycle bin and the **New ticket** form.

sections.title: The ticket workspace
intro: Open **Tickets** in the navigation rail, or press [[G]] then [[T]]. The ticket workspace has three panes.
Queues and saved views are on the left. The ticket list is in the middle. When you open a ticket, the customer's details appear on the right.

blocks.caption: The ticket workspace with the **My open tickets** queue and two tickets open as tabs.
blocks.alt: Ticket workspace with numbered highlights on the queues, the New view button, the tab strip, the filter box, the refresh button, a sort button and the New ticket button

callouts: **Queues**: ready-made ticket lists with live counts. A red count warns you about overdue tickets.
**New view**: creates your own saved view. Your views appear under **Views**.
The tab strip. The first tab shows the list. Each ticket you open gets its own tab.
**Filter by #, subject, customer…**: narrows the list while you type.
**Refresh**: reloads the list and the queue counts.
Sort buttons in the column headers, such as **Priority**.
**New ticket**: logs a new ticket for a customer.

list: Up to 12 tickets stay open as tabs. Each tab keeps its place while you switch.
Select **×** on a tab to close it. Select the **×** at the right end of the strip to close all tabs.
Select the panel buttons at either end of the tab strip to hide or show the left and right panels.
Drag the border between two panes to make a pane wider or narrower.

blocks.tip: To switch lists from the keyboard, open the command palette and type `Switch view`. See [Run a command from the command palette](#gs-command-palette).

sections.title: Queues
intro: Queues are fixed lists that every agent has. The number next to each queue is the count of tickets in it.
You only see tickets inside your role's data scope. Two agents can see different counts for the same queue.

rows: Open tickets that nobody owns yet.
Every open ticket you are allowed to see.
Tickets past their due time. The count turns red when there are any.
Open tickets close to missing a service target. The count turns red when there are any.
Open tickets that someone escalated, or that the service clock escalated.
Tickets in a waiting status, such as **Waiting on Customer**.
The recycle bin. Only people who may delete tickets see it.

sections.title: Open a queue or a saved view
sections.intro: Choose which tickets the list shows.
steps: Open **Tickets** in the navigation rail.
In the left panel, select a queue under **Queues**.
To use a saved view instead, select it under **Views**.
sections.result: The list shows the tickets. The heading above the list shows the name and the number of tickets.

blocks.tip: The address of the page names the list. Bookmark it, or share it with a colleague, to open the same list later.

sections.title: How saved views work
intro: A saved view is a ticket list that you define with conditions. For example, all critical tickets assigned to you.
A view always shows every ticket that matches its conditions. It never shows tickets outside what you are allowed to see.

rows: Everyone in the help desk. Only supervisors and administrators can share a view.

list: Each view shows how many tickets match it.
A star next to a view means it opens by default.
A view can keep its own column layout and its own sort order.
The owner of a view, or a supervisor, can edit or delete it. Anyone can copy it.

sections.title: Create a saved view
sections.intro: Build a list you use often, so it is one selection away.
prerequisites: To create a **Shared** view, you need supervisor rights. Without them, the **Shared** option shows **Needs supervisor rights**.

steps.text: Under **Views**, select **New view** (the plus button).
steps.note: The **New view** dialog opens.

steps: In **Name**, enter a short name, such as `Critical tickets for me`.
Under **Who can use it**, choose **Personal** or **Shared**.

steps.text: Under **Conditions**, select **Condition**. Then choose a field, an operator and a value.
steps.caption: A personal view with two conditions: the priority is **Critical** and the assignee is whoever views the list.
steps.alt: New view dialog with a name, the Personal option and two conditions

steps: Repeat the previous step for each extra condition. Select the bin button to remove a condition.
Choose **All (AND)** if every condition must match. Choose **Any (OR)** if one match is enough.
In **Sort by**, choose the order of the list. In **Position**, enter a number to place the view in the panel.
Tick **Open this view by default** if this view should open when you go to **Tickets**.
Select **Create view**.
sections.result: The view appears under **Views** and opens at once. The message **View created** appears.

blocks.tip: In the **Assignee** field, choose the first option, your name followed by **(whoever views it)**. A shared view with this option shows every person their own tickets.

blocks.note: Select **Group** to add a group of conditions with its own **All (AND)** or **Any (OR)** choice. **Position** puts lower numbers higher in the panel.

list: Ticket: subject, priority, severity, status, status category, channel, language, sentiment, reopen count and satisfaction score.
Routing: department, team, assignee and brand.
Product: product, module and version.
Classification: category, subcategory, issue type and tags.
Service: SLA state, escalated or not, and entitlement.
Dates: created, due and last activity.

blocks.p: **Save the current column layout with this view** keeps the columns you chose for the list you were looking at. The view then opens with the same columns.

sections.title: Edit, copy or delete a saved view
sections.intro: Change a view's conditions, make a copy to start a similar view, or remove a view you no longer use.
prerequisites: To edit or delete a view, you must own it or have supervisor rights.
steps: Under **Views**, point to the view.
Select the **⋯** button that appears at the right of the view.

steps.text: Choose **Edit…**, **Duplicate…** or **Delete**.
substeps: **Edit…** opens the **Edit view** dialog. Change the fields, then select **Save view**.
**Duplicate…** opens a copy named after the view with **(copy)** at the end. Change it, then select **Create view**.
**Delete** asks you to confirm. Select **Delete view**.

sections.result: The panel shows the changed view, the copy, or no view.

blocks.warning: Deleting a shared view removes it for everyone. Deleting a view never deletes its tickets.

sections.title: Which list opens by default
intro: When you open **Tickets** without choosing a list, SupportDesk picks one. It uses the first rule that applies.
There is one personal default per person and one shared default for the whole workspace. Departments and teams cannot have their own default.

steps: If the page address names a list, that list opens. This happens when you open a bookmark or a shared link.
On your first visit in a browser tab, your personal default view opens. Without one, the shared default view opens.
Otherwise, the queue or view you used last in this browser opens.
If none of these apply, **My open tickets** opens.
Under **Views**, point to the view and select the **⋯** button.
Choose **Edit…**.
Tick **Open this view by default**.
Select **Save view**.

blocks.note: A new personal default replaces your previous one. A shared default applies to everyone without a personal default.

sections.title: The ticket list
intro: The list loads 50 tickets at a time. Scroll down, or select **Load more**, to see more.
When tickets change while you work, the list updates itself. If you have tickets selected, a **New activity** button appears instead. Select it to reload the list.

rows: The subject. This column is always shown.
The current status, in its colour.
A countdown to the resolution target, such as **Breached 14d ago**. Resolved tickets show **SLA met** when the target was met.
The agent who owns the ticket, or **Unassigned**.
The customer organisation, with the contact's name below it.
**Channel**, **Department**, **Team**, **Product**, **Category**, **Severity**, **Created**, **Tags** and **Replies**. **Replies** shows agent replies and customer replies, such as `3 / 2`.
Bold subject with a blue dot
The customer replied and nobody has read it yet.
Red bar at the left edge of the row
The ticket missed its service target.
Open the ticket in the current row.
Select or clear the current row.
Open the next or previous ticket in the list.

sections.title: Filter and sort the list
sections.intro: Find a ticket in a long list without building a view.
steps: Open the queue or view you want to search.

steps.text: In **Filter by #, subject, customer…**, enter part of a ticket number, subject, customer or contact name.
steps.caption: The **All open** queue filtered by the text `POS`.
steps.alt: Ticket list with POS in the filter box and five matching tickets

steps: To clear the filter, select **×** in the box or press [[Esc]].
To sort, select a column header with arrows, such as **#**, **Priority**, **Due**, **Updated** or **Created**.
Select the same header again to reverse the order.
sections.result: The list shows only matching tickets, in the order you chose. The count next to the heading shows how many match.

blocks.note: **Due** always sorts the soonest due first. **Priority** always sorts the highest priority first. A saved view opens with its own sort order.

sections.title: Choose the list columns
sections.intro: Show the columns you need and hide the rest.
steps: Scroll the list to the right end of the header row.

steps.text: Select **Choose columns** (the columns button in the last header cell).
steps.caption: The **Columns** list. Ticked columns are shown.
steps.alt: Columns popup with check boxes and up and down arrows for each column

steps: Tick a column to show it. Clear it to hide it.
Use the arrows, or drag a column by its handle, to change the order.
Press [[Esc]] to close the list.
sections.result: The list shows the columns in the order you chose.

blocks.note: SupportDesk remembers the columns for each queue and view in this browser. Select **Reset** to go back to the standard columns.

sections.title: Update many tickets at once
sections.intro: Assign, close or tag a group of tickets in one step, instead of opening each one.
prerequisites: You need the bulk update permission. Supervisors and administrators have it by default.
You can update up to 500 tickets at a time.

steps.text: Tick the check box at the start of each ticket row.
steps.caption: Three tickets selected. The bulk actions bar appears above the list.
steps.alt: Ticket list with three rows ticked and the bulk actions bar highlighted

steps: To select every loaded ticket, tick the check box in the header row.

steps.text: In the bulk actions bar, select **Assign**, **Status** or **Priority**. For other actions, open **More**.
steps.caption: The **More** menu of the bulk actions bar.
steps.alt: More menu with Change priority, Add tags, Remove tags, Transfer, Watch, Close, Mark as spam and Delete

steps.text: Fill in the dialog that opens.
steps.caption: The **Assign tickets** dialog for three tickets.
steps.alt: Assign tickets dialog with Team and Agent fields

steps: Select **Apply**, or the action's own button, such as **Close tickets**.
Read the result, such as **3 of 3 tickets updated**.
Select **Done**.
sections.result: The list reloads. Tickets that could not be updated stay selected. The result lists each of them with the reason.

blocks.tip: Select **Clear** in the bar to clear the selection.

blocks.note: Without the bulk update permission, the bar shows a message instead of the buttons.

sections.title: Bulk actions
sections.intro: These actions are in the bulk actions bar and its **More** menu.

rows: Leave **Agent** empty to unassign. The team stays.
Pick from tags that already exist.
Adds you as a watcher of every selected ticket.
Needs the resolve permission. Customers are not asked to confirm.
Needs the delete permission. The tickets leave every queue.
Type `DELETE` and the number of tickets, such as `DELETE 3`.
Needs the delete permission. The tickets move to the recycle bin.

blocks.caption: The **Delete tickets** dialog asks you to type **DELETE 3** before **Delete** works.
blocks.alt: Delete tickets dialog with a box to type the confirmation text

blocks.warning: Closing, marking as spam and deleting affect every selected ticket. Check the selection before you confirm.

sections.title: Restore a deleted ticket
sections.intro: Deleted tickets and spam tickets go to the recycle bin. Nothing is lost until someone restores them.
prerequisites: You need the delete permission. Supervisors and administrators have it by default.

steps.text: Under **Queues**, select **Deleted tickets**.
steps.caption: The **Deleted tickets** list. Here the recycle bin is empty.
steps.alt: Deleted tickets page with a filter box and the message The recycle bin is empty

steps: To find a ticket, enter its number or part of its subject in **Filter by # or subject…**.
Select **Restore** next to the ticket.
Select **Restore** in the confirmation dialog.
sections.result: The ticket returns to its queues with its conversation and history. A message offers **Open** to open it.

list: The list shows the newest deletions first, with who deleted each ticket and when.
A **Spam** badge marks tickets marked as spam. Restoring them also stops treating them as spam.
A **Legal hold** badge means a legal hold covers the ticket. SupportDesk keeps it for the hold.
The recycle bin is never emptied automatically.

sections.title: Log a new ticket
sections.intro: Log a ticket when a customer calls, walks in or writes to you outside SupportDesk.
prerequisites: You need the create tickets permission. Agents, supervisors and administrators have it by default.
steps: In the top bar, select **New ticket**, or press [[C]].
In **Customer**, enter part of the customer's name, code or e-mail address. Then choose the customer.

steps.text: In **Contact**, choose the person who asked for help.
steps.caption: The **Requester** section with a customer, a contact and the **Phone** channel.
steps.alt: Requester section with Customer, Contact, a new contact check box and channel buttons

steps: Under **Channel**, choose how the customer contacted you, such as **Phone** or **Walk-in**.

steps.text: Enter the **Subject** and the **Description**.
steps.caption: The **Request** section with a subject and a description.
steps.alt: Request section with Subject, Description, Attach files, Priority, Severity, Category, Subcategory, Issue type and Tags

steps: Choose the **Priority**. Add the classification fields and **Tags** if you know them.
Under **Product**, choose the product, module, version and installation if the request is about one.

steps.text: Under **Routing**, choose a department, team or assignee. Leave them empty to let routing rules decide.
steps.caption: The **Routing** section with an assignee chosen.
steps.alt: Routing section with Department, Team and Assignee, and the Keep my choice check box ticked

steps: Fill in any **Additional fields**, then select **Create ticket**.
sections.result: A card shows **#number created** with the customer's support eligibility. Select **Open ticket** to work on it, or **Create another**.

blocks.tip: If the requester is not in SupportDesk yet, tick **The requester is a new contact**. Then enter the **Full name** and an **E-mail** or **Phone**.

blocks.note: Select **Attach files** under the description to add files. **Create ticket** waits until every file has uploaded.

sections.title: New ticket fields and checks
sections.intro: Only **Subject** is always required. Your administrator can make some **Additional fields** required.

rows: The customer organisation. Choose it first to see its contacts and installations.
The person who asked. Choosing a contact also fills in the customer.
Tick it to add a person who is not in SupportDesk. An existing contact with the same e-mail address or phone number is reused.
A short summary of the request. Required.
What the customer needs: steps, error messages and impact.
How urgent the request is, and how serious its impact is.
Keywords. Type a tag and press [[Enter]].
What the request is about. **Installation** needs a customer first.
Where the ticket goes. Leave them empty to let routing rules decide.
Appears when you choose an assignee. Tick it so that rules do not reassign the ticket.
Fields your administrator added for the department.

blocks.heading: Checks before the ticket is created

blocks.caption: **Create ticket** without a subject. The **Subject** field shows **Enter a subject.**
blocks.alt: Request section with the Subject field outlined in red and the message Enter a subject

blocks.p: When a field fails a check, nothing is created. A message next to **Create ticket** asks you to fix the highlighted fields. Fix the fields shown in red, then try again.

rows: Whether the customer may get support for this request, such as **Entitled** or **Not entitled**.
The contract that covers the ticket, or **No covering contract**.
The department, team and agent that received the ticket.

blocks.note: If the customer is not entitled, a warning appears. A supervisor can override the entitlement from the ticket's **More actions** menu.

chapters.title: Working on a ticket
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who handle tickets day to day.

It explains the ticket screen, statuses and service targets. It shows how to assign, resolve, escalate, merge and link tickets. It also covers tasks, time, watchers, follow-ups and what automation does on your tickets.

sections.title: Open a ticket
sections.intro: Open a ticket from a list, or go straight to it by its number.
steps: In the ticket list, select the ticket's row.
To open a ticket by number, press [[Ctrl+K]] and enter the number, such as `1042`.
Select the ticket in the results.
sections.result: The ticket opens in its own tab in the ticket workspace.

blocks.note: If the ticket is deleted, merged or outside what you can see, **Ticket not found** appears. Select **Close tab** to close it. See also [Find a ticket from the command palette](#gs-find-ticket).

sections.title: The ticket screen
intro: The ticket screen has a header, the conversation and the composer. The customer's context pane is on the right.
On most laptop screens, the side tabs open in a **Ticket details** panel. On wide screens, they appear next to the conversation.

blocks.caption: Ticket #1002 with the header, the conversation, the composer bar and the context pane.
blocks.alt: Ticket screen with numbered highlights on the ticket number, facts, quick edit fields, Ticket details button, More actions button, conversation header, composer bar and the customer section

callouts: The ticket number. Select it to copy a link to the ticket. The subject and the **Edit subject** button are next to it.
Facts: channel, customer, contact, badges and the service target countdowns.
Quick edit fields: **Status**, **Priority**, **Assignee**, **Department** and **Team**.
**Ticket details**: opens the side tabs, such as **Details**, **Tasks**, **Time** and **People**.
**More actions**: assign, transfer, escalate, resolve, merge and the other ticket actions.
The conversation, with the **Activity** switch and the **Expand all** and **Collapse all** buttons.
The composer bar: **Reply**, **Internal note** and **Handover**.
The context pane, starting with the customer.

blocks.tip: To give the ticket more room, select the panel buttons at either end of the tab strip. They hide the queue panel and the context pane.

sections.title: Badges in the ticket header
sections.intro: Badges under the subject tell you about the ticket at a glance.

rows: The ticket is escalated. The number is the escalation level.
A contract covers the request. Point to the badge to see the contract.
No valid contract covers the request.
Someone allowed support although the customer is not entitled.
The ticket is resolved, and SupportDesk waits for the customer to confirm the fix.
Another person locked the ticket while they work on it.
This ticket was merged into another. Select the badge to open the other ticket.
Shown on resolved and closed tickets instead of countdowns.

sections.title: The conversation
intro: The conversation shows every message on the ticket, oldest first. The newest entry is at the bottom.
Customer messages and replies show the channel, such as **wrote via WhatsApp**. Internal notes and handover notes have an amber background. Customers never see them.

list: Turn on **Activity** to also see field changes, routing, SLA events and automation.
Select **Expand all** or **Collapse all** to open or fold every message. Long older messages start folded.
E-mail messages show **From**, **To** and **Cc** above the text.
Replies show a delivery status, such as **Delivered**.
Select an attachment to download it. **Scanning** means the malware scan is still running. **Blocked** means the file failed the scan.

blocks.note: If the description is not part of the conversation, it appears in a box above the conversation.

sections.title: The context pane
sections.intro: The context pane on the right shows what you need to know about the customer. Select a section heading to fold or unfold it.

rows: Name, tier, account manager, open tickets, tickets in 90 days, satisfaction score and breaches. **Open customer** opens the customer's page.
Job title, location, e-mail address, phone, language, preferred channel and open tickets.
Each service target with its status, due time and target. See [Service targets](#wt-sla).
The customer's contracts. **Covers** marks the one that covers this ticket. Prepaid contracts show the hours used.
The customer's installed products, with versions.
The customer's earlier tickets. Select one to open it.
Related documents in the ERP system, such as invoices.
Knowledge base articles that match the ticket, with a match score.
Suggestions from the AI assistant, with a confidence level.
Linked engineering work items and their state.

blocks.note: Sections without data are hidden.

sections.title: Change fields from the header
sections.intro: Use the quick edit fields to change the most common fields without opening a dialog.
prerequisites: The fields you may change depend on your permissions. Fields you cannot change are greyed out.
steps: To change the subject, select **Edit subject** (the pencil). Enter the new subject and select **Save**.
To change the status, choose a status in **Status**.
To change the priority, choose it in **Priority**.
To assign the ticket, choose an agent in **Assignee**. Select **Assign to me** next to it to take the ticket yourself.
To move the ticket, choose another **Department** or **Team**.
sections.result: Each change saves at once. A message confirms it, such as **Priority set to High**.

blocks.warning: Quick edit fields save as soon as you choose a value. There is no **Save** button.

blocks.note: Some departments need a supervisor's approval for transfers. Then the message **Approval requested** appears, and the ticket stays where it is until someone approves.

sections.title: Ticket statuses
intro: Every status belongs to one fixed category: Open, Assigned, In progress, Waiting, Resolved or Closed. New workspaces start with the statuses below.
Your administrator can add statuses and limit which status may follow which. The status list only offers the statuses allowed next.

rows: A new ticket. The customer portal shows **Received**.
Assign it, reply, or change the status.
Set automatically when an open ticket gets an assignee.
Reply. Your reply moves the ticket to **In Progress**.
Set automatically when an agent replies to an open or assigned ticket.
Keep working, wait for someone, or resolve.
You asked the customer for something. The service clock pauses. Sub-statuses: information requested, confirmation requested, scheduling.
Wait. A customer reply moves the ticket back to **In Progress**, or to **Open** when nobody owns it.
You wait for engineering, a vendor or a partner. The clock keeps running. Sub-statuses: engineering, vendor, partner.
Follow up with the third party. A customer reply moves the ticket back as above.
An example status in the demo workspace. The ticket waits for an engineering fix.
Follow the work item in the context pane.
The fix is delivered. The ticket closes itself after a set number of days. The standard is 7 days.
Close it, or reopen it. A customer reply reopens it.
Reopen it. A customer reply within the reopen window also reopens it.

blocks.note: Some fields can be required for a status. For example, a vendor reference while the ticket waits on a third party. Fill them in on the **Details** tab before you change the status.
Tickets that follow a blueprint cannot change status freely. Use the **Blueprint** tab instead. See [Follow a blueprint](#rn-blueprint).

sections.title: Change the status with a comment
sections.intro: Use the **Change status** dialog when you want to add a sub-status or a comment.
steps: Press [[S]], or open **More actions** and choose **Change status…**.

steps.text: In **Status**, choose the new status.
steps.caption: The **Change status** dialog with **Waiting on Customer** chosen. A **Sub-status** list appears.
steps.alt: Change status dialog with Status, Sub-status and Comment fields

steps: If **Sub-status** appears, choose one.
In **Comment**, enter a short note for the ticket history.
Select **Change status**.
sections.result: The status changes. The message **Status changed to** and the status name appears.

sections.title: Service targets
intro: A service level agreement (SLA) sets time targets for each ticket. The header shows a countdown for each target that is still running.
**First response** shows until someone replies. After that, **Next response** shows the time for the next reply. **Resolve** shows the time left to resolve the ticket.

rows: At risk. The ticket passed the warning point, normally 75% of the target.
The ticket is in a status that pauses the clock, such as **Waiting on Customer**.

blocks.caption: The SLA section of the context pane: the first response was met, the other two targets were breached.
blocks.alt: SLA section listing First response as Met, and Next response and Resolution as Breached, each with a due time and target

blocks.p: The SLA section of the context pane shows the true state of each target. It also shows the due time, the target in minutes and the escalation level.

blocks.note: The header countdowns use the ticket's overall SLA state. After one target is breached, every countdown in the header turns red. The first response clock never pauses.

sections.title: Assign a ticket
sections.intro: Give the ticket to an agent or a team. To take it yourself, press [[A]].
prerequisites: You need the assign permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Assign…**.

steps.text: In **Team**, choose a team, or leave it empty.
steps.caption: The **Assign ticket** dialog.
steps.alt: Assign ticket dialog with Team, Agent, an Assign to me link and Note

steps: In **Agent**, choose an agent of the ticket's department. Select **Assign to me** to choose yourself.
In **Note**, enter a note for the ticket history if you like.
Select **Assign**.
sections.result: The message **Assigned to** and the agent's name appears. An open ticket moves to **Assigned**.

blocks.note: Leave **Agent** empty to unassign the ticket. The agent list shows each agent's availability and open tickets.

sections.title: Transfer a ticket to another department
sections.intro: Move a ticket to another department's queue when another team must handle it.
prerequisites: You need the transfer permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Transfer…**.

steps.text: In **Department**, choose the new department.
steps.caption: The **Transfer ticket** dialog.
steps.alt: Transfer ticket dialog with Department, Team, Agent and Reason fields

steps: In **Team** and **Agent**, choose who should get it. Leave **Agent** empty to let routing pick an agent.
In **Reason**, say why you transfer the ticket.
Select **Transfer**.
sections.result: The message **Transferred to** and the department's name appears.

blocks.note: Some departments need a supervisor's approval first. Then **Approval requested** appears. The ticket moves when the request is approved on the **Approvals** page.

sections.title: Resolve a ticket
sections.intro: Resolve a ticket when you have delivered the fix or the answer.
prerequisites: You need the resolve permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Resolve…**.

steps.text: In **Resolution code**, choose how the problem was solved.
steps.caption: The **Resolve ticket** dialog.
steps.alt: Resolve ticket dialog with Resolution code, Root cause, Resolution notes and two check boxes

steps: In **Root cause**, choose or enter the cause.
In **Resolution notes**, describe the fix. The customer sees these notes when you notify them.
Keep **Notify the customer** ticked to send the resolution notice and the satisfaction survey.
Tick **Ask the customer to confirm the fix (keeps it open until they reply)** if the customer must confirm.
Select **Resolve**.
sections.result: The status changes to **Resolved**. With the confirmation option, the header shows **Awaiting customer confirmation**.

blocks.note: **Resolution code** is required when your workspace uses codes. The confirmation option needs a contact on the ticket. Your workspace may switch it on for every ticket.

blocks.p: Resolved tickets close themselves after the number of days your administrator sets. A customer reply before then reopens the ticket.

sections.title: Close or reopen a ticket
sections.intro: Close a ticket when the work is finished. Reopen it when the problem comes back.
prerequisites: Closing needs the resolve permission. Reopening needs the reopen permission.
steps: To close the ticket, open **More actions** and choose **Close**.
Select **Close ticket** to confirm.
To reopen a resolved or closed ticket, open **More actions** and choose **Reopen…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, say why you reopen it.
steps.caption: The **Reopen ticket** dialog on a closed ticket.
steps.alt: Reopen ticket dialog with a Reason box

steps: Select **Reopen**.
sections.result: A closed ticket shows **Closed**. A reopened ticket gets an open status, the service clocks restart, and the reopen count goes up.

blocks.note: A customer reply also reopens a closed ticket within the reopen window. The standard window is 30 days. After it, the reply becomes a new ticket. Merged tickets cannot be reopened.

sections.title: Escalate a ticket
sections.intro: Escalate a ticket when it needs more senior attention. Each escalation raises the escalation level by one.
prerequisites: You need the escalate permission.
steps: Press [[E]], or open **More actions** and choose **Escalate…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, say why the ticket needs escalating.
steps.caption: The **Escalate ticket** dialog with a reason.
steps.alt: Escalate ticket dialog with Reason, Escalate to and a Raise the priority one level check box

steps: In **Escalate to**, choose a person, or leave it empty for the department's escalation owner.
Keep **Raise the priority one level** ticked to raise the priority too.
Select **Escalate**.
sections.result: The header shows the **Escalated** badge with the new level. The escalation owner is notified.

blocks.note: On a ticket that is already escalated, the menu item reads **Escalate further…**. The person you choose in **Escalate to** also becomes a watcher.

sections.title: Merge duplicate tickets
sections.intro: When a customer reports the same problem twice, merge the duplicates into one ticket.
prerequisites: You need the merge permission.
Open the ticket you want to keep.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Merge tickets into this…**.
In **Find tickets**, enter a number, subject, customer or contact.

steps.text: Choose a duplicate in the results. Repeat for up to 10 tickets.
steps.caption: The **Merge tickets** dialog with ticket #1204 picked as a duplicate.
steps.alt: Merge tickets dialog with a search box, one picked ticket and a Note field

steps: In **Note**, say why you merge the tickets if you like.
Select **Merge** followed by the number of tickets.
sections.result: The conversation, attachments, time, watchers, tags and engineering links move to this ticket. The duplicates close with a link to this ticket.

blocks.warning: You cannot undo a merge. Merged tickets cannot be reopened.

blocks.tip: Select **×** next to a picked ticket to remove it from the merge.

sections.title: Split messages into a new ticket
sections.intro: When one ticket mixes two problems, move some messages to a new ticket for the same customer.
prerequisites: You need the split permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Split messages…**.
Check the **New subject**. Change it to describe the second problem.

steps.text: Under **Messages**, tick each message to move.
steps.caption: The **Split into a new ticket** dialog with the first customer message ticked.
steps.alt: Split dialog with a New subject field, a list of messages with check boxes and a child ticket option

steps: Keep **Link the new ticket as a child of this one** ticked to link the two tickets.
Select **Split**.
sections.result: The new ticket opens in a new tab. The message **Created** and the new number appears.

sections.title: Clone a ticket
sections.intro: Clone a ticket to start a similar one for the same customer.
prerequisites: You need the create tickets permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Clone**.

steps.text: Select **Clone** to confirm.
steps.caption: The confirmation before cloning ticket #1002.
steps.alt: Clone confirmation dialog with Cancel and Clone buttons

sections.result: The new ticket opens in a new tab. It has the same customer, fields, tags and description. It does not copy the conversation.

sections.title: Link related tickets
sections.intro: Link tickets that belong together, such as a ticket that blocks another.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Link to ticket…**.
In **Relationship**, choose **Related to**, **Duplicate of**, **Blocks** or **Caused by**.

steps.text: In **Ticket**, search for the other ticket and choose it.
steps.caption: The **Link ticket** dialog linking #1002 as a duplicate of #1204.
steps.alt: Link ticket dialog with a Relationship list and a Ticket search box

steps: Select **Link**.
sections.result: The message **Tickets linked** appears. The **Related** tab of both tickets shows the link.

blocks.caption: The **Related** tab of a ticket without related tickets.
blocks.alt: Related tab with Child tickets, Linked tickets with a Link button, and External references

blocks.p: The **Related** tab also lists the parent ticket, child tickets and external references, such as ERP documents. To remove a link, select **×** next to it.

sections.title: Edit tags, classification and custom fields
sections.intro: Keep the ticket's classification up to date. Reports, routing and service targets use it.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details** (the sliders button in the header).

steps.text: Select the **Details** tab.
steps.caption: The **Details** tab in the **Ticket details** panel.
steps.alt: Details tab with Tags, Category, Subcategory, Issue type, Severity, Product, Module, Version and Installation

steps: In **Tags**, type a tag and press [[Enter]]. Select **×** on a tag to remove it.
Change the classification and product fields you need.
Fill in the fields under **Additional fields**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The message **Ticket updated** appears. The bar at the bottom shows **All changes saved**.

blocks.note: Tags save at once. The other fields wait for **Save**. Select **Undo** to drop changes you have not saved.

blocks.p: **Installation** needs a customer on the ticket. **Subcategory** needs a category, and **Module** and **Version** need a product.
The **Facts** list shows the dates, the SLA policy and the contract. It also shows the time spent, the reopen count, the satisfaction score and the resolution.

sections.title: Add tasks and checklist items
sections.intro: Break the work into tasks, each with an owner and a due time.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets or the add notes permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Tasks** tab.

steps.text: In **New task or checklist item**, enter what needs doing.
steps.caption: The **Tasks** tab with a new task typed in.
steps.alt: Tasks tab with a task title, Assignee, a due date and time field and a Checklist item check box

steps: In **Assignee**, choose who does it. Enter a due date and time.
Tick **Checklist item** for a simple tick-off item.
Select **Add**.
sections.result: The task appears in the list. A progress bar shows how many tasks are done.

list: Tick a task to mark it done.
Select the pencil to edit a task.
Select the plus button on a task to add a subtask. Tasks have one level of subtasks.
Select the bin to delete a task. Deleting needs the edit tickets permission.

sections.title: Log time on a ticket
sections.intro: Log the time you spend, so contracts and costs stay accurate.
prerequisites: You need the log time permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Time** tab.

steps.text: Enter the **Hours** and **Minutes** you spent.
steps.caption: The **Time** tab with 30 minutes of billable remote work.
steps.alt: Time tab with totals, Hours, Minutes, Started, Activity, Notes, a Billable check box and Log time

steps: In **Started**, enter when the work started. Leave it empty for the current time.
In **Activity**, enter or choose the kind of work, such as `Remote session`.
In **Notes**, describe the work.
Keep **Billable** ticked if the customer pays for this time.
Select **Log time**.
sections.result: The entry appears under the form. The totals at the top, and the **Time** tab badge, go up.

blocks.note: Billable time uses up prepaid hours on the customer's contract. Only people allowed to see costs see **Cost** and **Billable value**. You can delete your own entries with the bin button.

sections.title: Add watchers, collaborators and specialists
sections.intro: Add people who should follow the ticket or help with it.
prerequisites: You can add or remove yourself. To add or remove others, you need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **People** tab.
In **Add a person**, choose an agent or a specialist.

steps.text: In **Role**, choose **Watcher**, **Collaborator** or **Temporary specialist**.
steps.caption: The **People** tab with **Temporary specialist** chosen. **Access until** is required.
steps.alt: People tab with Add a person, Role and Access until fields and an Add button

steps: For a temporary specialist, enter the date and time in **Access until**.
Select **Add**.
sections.result: The person appears in the list with their role. The **People** tab badge shows how many people follow the ticket.

rows: Gets a notification about every update.
Helps with the ticket. Mentioning someone in an internal note makes them a collaborator.
Gets access to the ticket until the end date, then loses it.

blocks.tip: To watch a ticket yourself, open **More actions** and choose **Watch**. Choose **Stop watching** to stop.

sections.title: Schedule a follow-up reminder
sections.intro: Get a reminder to check back on a ticket at a set time.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Follow-ups** tab.
In **Remind at**, enter the date and time.
In **Remind**, choose who to remind. Leave it empty to remind yourself.

steps.text: In **Note**, say what to check.
steps.caption: The **Follow-ups** tab with a note. **Schedule** works once **Remind at** has a value.
steps.alt: Follow-ups tab with Remind at, Remind and Note fields and a Schedule button

steps: Select **Schedule**.
sections.result: The reminder appears in the list as **Pending**. At the set time, a **Follow up on** notification arrives.

blocks.tip: Select **Cancel** next to a pending reminder to remove it.

sections.title: Lock a ticket while you work on it
sections.intro: Lock a ticket so that nobody changes it while you work on a fix.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Lock while I work on it**.
When you finish, open **More actions** and choose **Unlock**.
sections.result: The header shows **Locked by you**. Others see **Locked by** and your name.

list: A lock lasts 10 minutes. The message tells you when it ends.
While a ticket is locked, others cannot edit, assign, transfer, change the status or resolve it.
A lock does not block replies, notes, tags or links.
Supervisors can unlock a ticket that someone else locked. The menu item then shows the person's name.

sections.title: Mark a ticket as spam or delete it
sections.intro: Remove junk tickets from every queue. Both actions move the ticket to the recycle bin.
prerequisites: You need the delete permission. Supervisors and administrators have it by default.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Mark as spam…** or **Delete…**.
For **Delete…**, type the ticket number, such as `#1206`, to confirm.
Select **Mark as spam** or **Delete**.
sections.result: The ticket tab closes and the ticket leaves every queue.

blocks.note: After **Mark as spam**, future messages from the same sender are treated as spam. To bring a ticket back, see [Restore a deleted ticket](#tv-restore).

sections.title: The More actions menu
sections.intro: Open **More actions** (the **⋯** button in the header) for every ticket action. Greyed-out items need a permission you do not have.

blocks.caption: The **More actions** menu of an escalated, open ticket.
blocks.alt: More actions menu listing Assign, Transfer, Escalate further, Change status, Resolve, Close, Merge, Split, Clone, Link, Watch, Lock, Override entitlement, Mark as spam and Delete

rows: Assigns the ticket. See [Assign a ticket](#wt-assign).
Moves the ticket to another department. See [Transfer a ticket to another department](#wt-transfer).
Raises the escalation level. See [Escalate a ticket](#wt-escalate).
Changes the status with a comment. See [Change the status with a comment](#wt-change-status).
Resolves an open ticket, or reopens a resolved or closed one.
Closes the ticket after you confirm.
Merges duplicates into this ticket. See [Merge duplicate tickets](#wt-merge).
Moves messages to a new ticket. See [Split messages into a new ticket](#wt-split).
Creates a copy of the ticket without its conversation.
Links another ticket. See [Link related tickets](#wt-link).
Adds or removes you as a watcher at once.
**Lock while I work on it** or **Unlock**
Locks or unlocks the ticket at once. See [Lock a ticket while you work on it](#wt-lock).
Lets the team work the ticket although the customer is not entitled. It needs a reason, which is audited.
Remove the ticket from every queue. See [Mark a ticket as spam or delete it](#wt-spam-delete).

sections.title: When someone else changed the ticket
intro: Two people can change a ticket at the same time. If someone saved the ticket after you opened it, your change is not saved straight away.
Instead, the **Someone else changed this ticket** dialog opens. The ticket already shows the latest saved values.

rows: Each field you tried to change.
The value the other person saved.
The value you tried to save.

steps: Compare the two values for each field.
Select **Keep theirs** to keep the other person's values and drop your change.
Or select **Re-apply my change** to save your values over theirs.

sections.title: See who else is on the ticket
intro: Avatars at the right of the ticket header show who else has the ticket open. Point to an avatar to see the person's name and what they are doing.
A pulsing ring around an avatar means the person is typing. A banner then says, for example, **Priya Raman is writing a reply** or **is writing a note**.

blocks.tip: Before you reply, check the banner. If a colleague is already writing a reply, wait for it or add an internal note instead.

sections.title: What automation does on your tickets
intro: Your administrator sets up automation rules and blueprints. As an agent, you see what they do on your tickets.
Turn on **Activity** in the conversation to see these entries.
