blocks.caption: Activity entries on a ticket. A rule raised the priority to **Critical**, added a tag and notified two agents.
blocks.alt: Conversation with activity entries from an automation rule and an AI sentiment entry

list: Rule entries name the rule, such as **Rule** and the rule name with **applied** and what it did.
Rules can assign a ticket, change its priority, add tags, add notes or send replies.
The service clock adds entries when a target is at risk or breached. It can raise the escalation level, the priority or the assignee.
The AI assistant can flag the customer's mood, such as **AI flagged the customer as frustrated**.
Blueprints guide a ticket through set steps. You run the next step on the **Blueprint** tab. See [Follow a blueprint](#rn-blueprint).
When a step needs approval, the request appears on the **Approvals** page. See [The Approvals page](#cc-approvals-page).

blocks.note: SupportDesk has no agent macros. Reply templates insert text only. See [Use a reply template](#rn-templates).

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts on a ticket
sections.intro: These shortcuts work while a ticket is open, but not while you type in a field. See also [Keyboard shortcuts](#gs-shortcuts).

rows: Open the composer for an internal note.
Open the next or previous ticket in the list.

chapters.title: Replies, notes and templates
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who write to customers and colleagues from a ticket.

It explains the composer: replies, internal notes, handover notes, templates, attachments and drafts. It also covers the side tabs and composer buttons that other modules add, such as **Blueprint** and **Draft with AI**.

sections.title: The composer
intro: The composer sits at the bottom of every ticket. When it is closed, it shows three buttons: **Reply**, **Internal note** and **Handover**.
Select a button, or press [[R]] for a reply or [[N]] for a note. The composer opens with the editor ready for typing.

blocks.caption: The closed composer with its three buttons.
blocks.alt: Composer bar with Reply, Internal note and Handover buttons

blocks.caption: The open composer on an e-mail ticket, with a reply typed in.
blocks.alt: Open composer with numbered highlights on the message type, recipients, editor, attach button, Templates, Draft with AI and Send

callouts: The message type: **Reply**, **Internal note** or **Handover**. Below it are the draft status and the **Minimise** button.
Recipients. **To** holds the contact's e-mail address. The **Cc** and **Bcc** links add more rows.
The editor with its formatting toolbar.
**Attach files** (the paperclip).
**Templates**: inserts a reply template.
**Draft with AI**: writes a draft reply for you to check.
**Send**, and the arrow next to it for **Send and set status**.

blocks.note: Some roles may only view a ticket. For them, the bar shows **You can view this ticket but not reply to it.** Light agents can add internal notes but cannot reply to customers.

sections.title: Reply to a customer
sections.intro: Send an answer to the customer on the ticket's channel.
prerequisites: You need the reply permission.
steps: Select **Reply**, or press [[R]].
For an e-mail ticket, check the address in **To**. Select **Cc** or **Bcc** to add more people.
Write your reply in the editor. To start from a template, open **Templates** and choose one.
To add files, select **Attach files** and choose them.
Select **Send**, or press [[Ctrl+Enter]].
sections.result: The message **Reply sent** appears, and the reply appears at the end of the conversation. An open or assigned ticket moves to **In Progress**.

list: On e-mail tickets, **Send** works only when **To** has at least one address.
Type an address in **To**, **Cc** or **Bcc** and press [[Enter]]. Select **×** on an address to remove it.
**Bcc** recipients are hidden from the others. Saved drafts do not keep them.
On other channels, the composer shows **Sent to** with the contact's name and channel, such as WhatsApp. The reply goes out on that channel.

blocks.tip: Your e-mail signature from **My profile** is added to e-mail replies. It does not show in the composer.

sections.title: Send a reply and change the status
sections.intro: Send your reply and set the next status in one step. For example, send a question and set **Waiting on Customer**.
prerequisites: The reply has text and, on e-mail tickets, a recipient.
steps: Write your reply.

steps.text: Select the arrow next to **Send**.
steps.caption: The **Send and set status** menu.
steps.alt: Send and set status menu listing Open, In Progress, Waiting on Customer, Waiting on Third Party, Escalated to Engineering and Resolved

steps: Choose the status.
sections.result: The reply is sent, and the ticket gets the new status. The message **Reply sent and status updated** appears.

blocks.note: The menu only lists statuses allowed next. Closed statuses are never in the list.

sections.title: Add an internal note
sections.intro: Write a note that only agents see, such as what you tried or a question for a colleague.
prerequisites: You need the add notes permission.
steps: Select **Internal note**, or press [[N]].
Write the note.

steps.text: To bring in a colleague, type `@` and the first letters of their name. Choose the person in the list.
steps.caption: An internal note with the mention list open after typing `@Mee`.
steps.alt: Internal note composer with an amber background and a mention list showing Meera Iyer

steps: Select **Add note**.
sections.result: The message **Note added** appears. The note shows in the conversation with an amber background and an **Internal note** label.

blocks.note: Everyone you mention gets a notification. Mentioned colleagues also become collaborators on the ticket.

blocks.warning: Never paste information meant for the customer into a note. Customers do not see notes, so the customer never gets it.

sections.title: Write a handover note
sections.intro: Leave a note for the next agent, for example at the end of your shift.
prerequisites: You need the add notes permission.
steps: Select **Handover**.

steps.text: Answer the question in the editor: **What should the next agent know?**
steps.caption: A handover note before it is added.
steps.alt: Handover composer with a note for the next agent and an Add handover button

steps: Select **Add handover**.
sections.result: The message **Handover note added** appears. The note shows in the conversation with an amber background. Only agents see it.

blocks.note: Internal notes and handover notes share one draft. Text you type in one also shows in the other until you add it or discard it.

sections.title: Use a reply template
sections.intro: Templates give you ready-made answers to common questions. SupportDesk fills in names and numbers for you.
steps: Open the composer in **Reply** mode.
Place the cursor where the template text should go.

steps.text: Open **Templates** and choose a template.
steps.caption: The **Templates** menu, grouped by category.
steps.alt: Templates menu with an Engineering group containing Fix released and a Follow-up group containing Waiting on customer gentle reminder

steps: Read the inserted text and change it to fit the ticket.
Send the reply.
sections.result: The template text appears in the editor with the customer's and the ticket's details filled in.

rows: The contact's first name, or **there** when there is no contact.

list: **Templates** only appears in **Reply** mode.
A template can be personal, or shared with a team, a department or the whole workspace.
If no template is available to you, the menu shows **No templates available**.

blocks.note: You cannot create or change templates in the desk. Ask your administrator for new templates. Templates insert text only. They do not change the ticket.

sections.title: Attach files
sections.intro: Add screenshots, logs or documents to a reply or a note.
steps: In the open composer, select **Attach files** (the paperclip).
Choose one or more files, then confirm.
Wait until each file's progress bar disappears.
To remove a file, select **×** next to its name.
sections.result: The files are listed under the editor. They go out with the reply or note.

list: The size limit depends on your plan. The standard limit is 25 MB per file.
Programs and active content are blocked, such as `.exe`, `.js`, `.html`, `.svg` and `.docm` files.
Every file is scanned for malware. A file that fails shows **Blocked by the virus scanner**.
**Send** waits until every file has uploaded.

sections.title: Drafts
intro: The composer saves your text as a draft about a second after you stop typing. The draft status above the editor shows **Saving draft…**, then **Draft saved** and the time.
Drafts come back when you reopen the ticket, on any device. When the composer is closed, a **Draft saved** badge shows that a draft is waiting.

list: Select **Minimise** (the down arrow) to close the composer and keep the draft.
Select **Discard** to delete the draft and close the composer. You cannot undo this.
Replies and notes have separate drafts. Internal notes and handover notes share one draft.
Drafts keep **To** and **Cc**, but not **Bcc**.

blocks.note: If the status shows **Draft not saved**, keep the composer open and check your connection. Your text stays in the editor.

sections.title: When someone posts while you write
intro: A customer or a colleague may post on the ticket while you write your reply. Then SupportDesk does not send your reply straight away.
A yellow panel opens above the editor. It says how many entries were added while you were writing and shows each of them.

steps: Read the new entries in the panel.
To change your reply first, select **I've reviewed them — keep editing**.
To send your reply as it is, select **Send anyway**.

blocks.tip: Always read the new entries. The customer may have answered your question already.

sections.title: Draft a reply with AI
sections.intro: Let the AI assistant write a first draft from the ticket and your knowledge base. You check and send it.
prerequisites: You need the AI permission, and your plan must include AI.
steps: Open the composer in **Reply** mode.
Select **Draft with AI**.
Read the message under the editor. It says how many sources the draft used.
Check and edit the draft.
Select **Send**.
sections.result: The draft appears in the editor. If the editor already had text, the draft is added at the cursor.

blocks.warning: If no matching article or resolved ticket was found, the message says so. Check such a draft with extra care before you send it.

sections.title: Share a ticket to Teams or Slack
sections.intro: Post a ticket to a Microsoft Teams or Slack channel to ask colleagues for help.
prerequisites: You need the add notes permission.
An administrator has added the channel under **Administration** > **Teams & Slack**.
steps: Select **Internal note**.
Type a comment in the editor if you like. SupportDesk adds it to the post.

steps.text: Select **Share to Teams/Slack**.
steps.caption: The **Share to Teams / Slack** dialog in a workspace without channels.
steps.alt: Share to Teams or Slack dialog showing No channels and a hint for administrators

steps: In **Channel**, choose the channel.
In **Message**, enter a short text for the top of the post.
Select **Share**.
sections.result: The message **Shared to** and the channel name appears under the editor. The post links back to the ticket.

sections.title: Side tabs from other modules
sections.intro: Other modules add tabs to the **Ticket details** panel. You only see a tab when you have its permission and your plan includes it.

rows: Shows the guided process the ticket follows and the next steps you may run. See [Follow a blueprint](#rn-blueprint).
You may use AI, and your plan includes it.

Summary, sentiment, expected resolution and classification. It also offers a suggested reply with **Insert into composer**, similar and duplicate tickets, the likely root cause, **Draft article** and **Run agents**.
You may link or view engineering work items.
Lists linked engineering work items with their state, fix version and release. **Escalate to engineering** creates a work item. **Link existing** links one that already exists.

blocks.p: The composer also gets extra buttons from other modules. **Draft with AI** appears in **Reply** mode. **Share to Teams/Slack** appears in **Internal note** mode.

sections.title: Follow a blueprint
sections.intro: A blueprint guides a ticket through set steps, such as investigation, review and release. You move the ticket to its next step on the **Blueprint** tab.
prerequisites: The ticket follows a blueprint. Otherwise the tab says **This ticket doesn't follow a blueprint**.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Blueprint** tab.
Check the steps of the process and the **Current state**.

steps.text: Select the transition you want to run, such as **Confirm defect**.
steps.caption: The **Blueprint** tab with the **Confirm defect** transition open. It needs approval and two fields.
steps.alt: Blueprint tab with the process states, the current state Investigation, and an open transition form with Severity, Version and Comment

steps: Fill in the required fields that appear.
Enter a **Comment**. The step may make it mandatory.
Select **Move to** and the state name, or **Request approval** when the step needs approval.
sections.result: The ticket moves to the next state, and its status changes with it. For an approval step, the tab shows that the step is waiting for approval.

list: An **approval** badge means a supervisor must approve the step. The request appears on the **Approvals** page.
A badge such as **2 fields** shows how many required fields are still empty.
Some steps are greyed out, with the reason below them.
If no step is open to you, the tab says **No transitions are available to you from this state.**

blocks.note: People who manage automation also see **Remove ticket from blueprint**. Removing it lets the ticket change status freely again.

sections.title: Composer buttons
sections.intro: Every button and field you can find in the open composer.

rows: Switch the message type. Notes and handovers have an amber background.
Closes the composer and keeps the draft.
E-mail recipients. Only shown on e-mail tickets.
Bold, italic, underline, strike-through, lists, quotes, links and code. Press [[Ctrl+K]] in the editor to add a link.
Inserts a reply template. **Reply** mode only.
Writes a draft reply. **Reply** mode only, when AI is available.
Posts the ticket to a Teams or Slack channel. **Internal note** mode only.
Deletes the draft and closes the composer.
Sends the reply or adds the note. [[Ctrl+Enter]] does the same.

chapters.title: Inbox and live chat
intro: This chapter is for agents who answer customers on live chat, WhatsApp, SMS, Messenger, Instagram, e-mail and phone.
The **Inbox** shows every conversation from every channel in one list. The **Live chat** console is where you take and answer website chats in real time.

sections.title: The Inbox at a glance
intro: Open the Inbox from **Inbox** in the menu on the left. You can also press [[G]] and then [[I]].
The Inbox has three panels. The list of conversations is on the left. The selected conversation is in the middle. Facts about the customer and the ticket are on the right.

blocks.caption: The **Inbox** with a WhatsApp conversation open.
blocks.alt: Inbox with the conversation list, an open WhatsApp conversation and the context panel, each part numbered

callouts: The **Inbox** title and the **Live chat** button, which opens the chat console. Administrators also see a settings button for the channels.
Search and filters. Search by name, subject or address. Filter by channel, status and assignee.
The conversation list. Each row shows the customer, the subject, the last message, the status and the ticket number.
The conversation header. It shows the channel, the channel account, when the conversation started and its status. **Ticket #** opens the linked ticket.
A banner about the channel. For WhatsApp it shows the 24-hour service window. For a chat it shows whether the visitor is verified.
The messages, oldest at the top. Your replies are on the right.
The context panel. It shows the contact, the linked ticket and facts about the conversation.

blocks.note: The list updates by itself when a new message arrives. It shows 40 conversations at a time. Select **Load more** at the end of the list to see more.

sections.title: Find a conversation
sections.intro: Use the filters to find a customer's conversation or to see only the ones that need you.
steps: In the menu on the left, select **Inbox**.
To search, enter part of a name, subject or address in **Search name, subject, address…**.
To see one channel, choose it in the **All channels** list.
To change the status, choose it in the status list. The default is **Active**.
To see one person's conversations, choose **Me**, **Unassigned** or an agent in the **Anyone** list.

steps.text: Select a conversation in the list.
steps.note: If chats are waiting, a pill shows how many, for example **2 waiting for an agent**. Select it to see only those chats.

sections.result: The conversation opens in the middle panel. The Inbox remembers your filters the next time you open it.

sections.title: Inbox filters
sections.intro: The three lists under the search box narrow the conversation list.

rows: Shows only conversations from that channel.
**Active** hides closed conversations. The other options show one status, or all of them.
Shows conversations handled by that person, or by nobody yet.

sections.title: Conversation statuses
sections.intro: Each conversation has a status. It shows as a coloured badge in the list and in the header.

rows: The chat bot is talking to a website visitor. No agent has joined yet.
The visitor asked for a person. The chat waits in the **Waiting** list of the Live chat console.
An agent accepted the chat and is talking to the visitor.
An e-mail, messaging or call conversation that is still in progress.
The conversation has ended. For a chat, the transcript is on the ticket.

sections.title: How conversations become tickets
intro: SupportDesk creates tickets from conversations by itself. You cannot turn a conversation into a ticket by hand, or link it to another ticket.
Only live chats have a reply box in the Inbox. For every other channel, you reply on the ticket. The reply goes back on the channel the customer used.

list: A WhatsApp, SMS, Messenger or Instagram message joins the customer's open ticket. If there is no open ticket, SupportDesk creates one.
A missed call or a voicemail creates a ticket.
A live chat becomes a ticket when it is handed to a person.
An e-mail joins the ticket whose number is in the subject. Otherwise it creates a new ticket.

sections.title: Reply to a message from another channel
sections.intro: Answer an e-mail, WhatsApp, SMS, Messenger or Instagram message from its ticket.
steps: In the **Inbox**, select the conversation.
Read the banner under the header, if there is one.

steps.text: At the bottom of the conversation, select **Reply on ticket #** followed by the number.
steps.note: You can also select **Ticket #** in the header.

steps: Write and send your reply on the ticket. Chapter 6 explains the reply box.
sections.result: The customer gets your reply on the channel they wrote from. The reply also appears in the conversation.

blocks.note: WhatsApp allows free replies for 24 hours after the customer's last message. The banner shows when this service window ends. When it is closed, SupportDesk sends your reply as a pre-approved template. You can also wait for the customer to write again.

sections.title: Read e-mail, messaging and call conversations
sections.intro: Each channel looks a little different in the middle panel.

blocks.caption: An e-mail conversation. The customer's reply has an attachment and quoted history.
blocks.alt: E-mail message card with sender, To and Subject lines, the message, a Quoted history link, an attachment and the Original download button

list: Each e-mail shows the sender, the date, **To** and **Subject**.
Badges mark automatic messages: **Auto-reply**, **Acknowledgement** and **CSAT survey**.
Select **Quoted history** to see the earlier mail that the customer quoted.
Select an attachment to open or download it.
Select **Original (.eml)** to download the e-mail exactly as it arrived.
Messages from WhatsApp, SMS, Messenger and Instagram look like chat bubbles.
A **Template** badge marks a message sent as a pre-approved WhatsApp template.
Under your messages, a tick and a word show the delivery status.

blocks.caption: A phone conversation with a voicemail and a link to play the recording.
blocks.alt: Phone conversation showing a voicemail card with the caller's number, the time and a Play recording link

list: Each call shows its type: **Missed call**, **Voicemail**, an inbound or outbound call, **Call in progress** or **Call failed**.
The card shows the numbers, the time, the duration and the result of the call.
Select **Play recording** to listen to a recording or a voicemail.
Select **Ticket** to open the ticket made from the call.

blocks.tip: Select the refresh button in the header to reload a conversation.

sections.title: The context panel
sections.intro: The right-hand panel tells you who you are talking to and which ticket the conversation belongs to.

blocks.caption: The context panel of a WhatsApp conversation.
blocks.alt: Context panel with the contact card, the linked ticket and a list of conversation facts

rows: The contact's name. A chat from an unknown person shows **Website visitor**. It also shows the e-mail address or number the message came from.
The linked ticket and its status. A new chat shows that a ticket is created when an agent takes over.
The status, channel, channel account, assigned agent, start time and last activity. WhatsApp shows the **24h window**. A chat shows the page the visitor is on and their language.

sections.title: Check whether a message was delivered
sections.intro: Use this when a customer says they did not get your reply.
steps: In the **Inbox**, open the conversation.
Find your message in the conversation.

steps.text: Select the delivery status under the message. For an e-mail, select **Delivery details**.
steps.caption: The delivery details of an e-mail. It was queued and then sent.
steps.alt: E-mail card with the delivery details open, showing the recipient, one attempt and the status history

steps: Read the recipient, the number of attempts and the status history.
Select the status again to hide the details.
sections.result: You see when the message was queued, sent, delivered or read. If it failed, the reason appears in red.

rows: SupportDesk is still trying to send the message.
The customer's mail system or phone received it.
The customer opened the message. Only some channels report this.
The message did not arrive. Check the address or number, then reply again.

sections.title: The Live chat console
intro: The Live chat console is where you take website chats. Open it from **Inbox** > **Live chat**.
New chats play a sound and raise a desktop alert, so you can work on tickets while you wait.

blocks.caption: The **Live chat** console with no chats waiting.
blocks.alt: Live chat console with the back button, sound and alert buttons, the chat counter and the Waiting, My chats and With the bot lists

callouts: Back to the **Inbox**.
The sound button. It turns the sound for new chats on or off.
The desktop alert button. It appears until you allow or block alerts in your browser.
Your chat counter. It shows how many chats you have now and how many you may take, for example **1/3**.
**Waiting**: chats waiting for an agent, oldest first. Each one has an **Accept** button.
**My chats**: the chats you are handling now.
**With the bot**: chats the chat bot is still handling.
The selected chat. The visitor's details are in the panel on the right.

blocks.note: The console checks for new chats every 30 seconds, even if the live connection drops.

sections.title: Turn chat alerts on or off
sections.intro: Choose how SupportDesk tells you that a new chat is waiting.
steps: In the **Inbox**, select **Live chat**.
To mute the chime, select the sound button. Select it again to turn the sound back on.
To get desktop alerts, select the bell button.
When your browser asks, allow notifications.
sections.result: A new waiting chat now plays a chime and shows a desktop alert. A pop-up message also says that the visitor is waiting. Select the desktop alert to open that chat.

sections.title: Accept a chat
sections.intro: Take the next waiting chat. Take the oldest chat first, so that no visitor waits too long.
prerequisites: You can reply to tickets.
Your chat limit is above 0, and you have a free chat slot.
steps: In the **Inbox**, select **Live chat**.
In the **Waiting** list, find the chat at the top.

steps.text: Select **Accept** next to it.
steps.tip: You can also select the chat first and then select **Accept chat** in the header.

sections.result: The chat moves to **My chats** and opens in the middle panel. The visitor sees that you joined the chat. A ticket is created for the chat, if it has none.

blocks.note: If another agent was faster, you see the message **Another agent already accepted this chat.** Choose another chat.

sections.title: Chat capacity
intro: Each agent has a chat limit: the most chats they may handle at once. The default is 3. A manager sets it in the agent's routing profile.
The counter next to **Waiting** shows your load, for example **2/3**. It turns red when you are full.

list: When you are full, the **Accept** buttons are greyed out.
A banner says: **You're at your chat limit (3). End or transfer a chat to accept another.**
End or transfer one of your chats to free a slot.
A limit of 0 means you take no chats. Ask your manager if you should take chats.

sections.title: Chat with a visitor
sections.intro: Answer a chat you accepted.
prerequisites: You accepted the chat. It shows in **My chats**.
steps: In **My chats**, select the chat.
Read the banner above the messages. It shows whether the visitor proved who they are.
Type your message in the box at the bottom.

steps.text: Press [[Enter]] to send it.
steps.tip: Press [[Shift+Enter]] to start a new line without sending.

steps: Wait for the visitor's answer. A line shows **is typing…** after their name while they type.
sections.result: Your message appears on the right. The visitor sees it at once. The visitor also sees when you are typing.

sections.title: Insert a reply template in a chat
sections.intro: Reply templates save typing for common answers. In a chat, the template comes in as plain text.
prerequisites: The chat has a ticket. The menu stays greyed out until it has one.
steps: Open the chat.
Below the message box, select **Templates**.
Choose a template. The menu groups templates by category.
Change the text in the message box if you need to.
Press [[Enter]] to send it.
sections.result: The template text is added to your message. SupportDesk fills in details such as the customer's name from the ticket.

sections.title: Visitor identity
intro: Anyone can start a chat on your website. The banner above the messages tells you how sure you can be about who they are.
Agents cannot verify a visitor. Be careful with account details until the visitor is verified.

rows: The visitor proved their e-mail address with a code sent by SupportDesk.
The visitor did not prove who they are. If they typed an e-mail address, the banner shows it after **claims**.

blocks.p: The banner also shows the page the visitor is on. The context panel shows the same facts, plus the chat rating when the visitor gives one.

sections.title: Transfer a chat
sections.intro: Hand a chat to a colleague who knows the topic better, or to another department.
prerequisites: You are handling the chat, or it is still waiting. Supervisors can transfer any chat.
To send a chat to another department, you need permission to transfer tickets.
steps: Open the chat.
In the header, select **Transfer**. The **Transfer chat** dialog opens.
Under **Transfer to**, choose **Another agent** or **Another department**.

steps.text: For an agent, choose the agent in the **Agent** list.
steps.note: The list shows agents of the ticket's department who can take chats, with their availability.

steps.text: For a department, choose the **Department**. Then choose an **Agent**, or leave it empty.
steps.note: With no agent, the chat waits in that department's queue.

steps: Optionally, enter a **Note for the next agent**.
Select **Transfer**.
sections.result: A message says **Chat transferred**. The visitor sees who the chat went to. The new agent gets a notification, and the ticket moves with the chat.

blocks.note: Some departments need approval for transfers. Then you see **Transfer sent for approval**, and the chat stays with you until someone approves it.

sections.title: End a chat
sections.intro: End the chat when the visitor has what they need.
steps: Open the chat.
In the header, select **End chat**.
sections.result: The chat status changes to **Closed**. The visitor sees **This chat has ended. Thank you for contacting us!** A **Chat transcript** entry is added to the ticket.

blocks.note: After a chat ends, you cannot send more chat messages. Reply on the ticket instead. The customer gets that reply by e-mail.

chapters.title: Customers
intro: This chapter is for agents and account managers who look up customers or keep customer records up to date.

A customer is an organisation you support. A contact is a person who works there. The Customer 360 page shows everything about one customer: tickets, contacts, sites, products, contracts, visits and records from Wings ERP.

sections.title: The Customers module
intro: Open it from **Customers** in the menu on the left. You can also press [[G]] and then [[U]].
The module has five tabs: **Customers**, **Contacts**, **Duplicates**, **Service activities** and **Groups**.

blocks.caption: The **Customers** list with its search and filters.
blocks.alt: Customers page with the New customer button, the module tabs, the search and filter bar and the customer table, each numbered

callouts: **New customer** adds an organisation. You see it only if you can manage customers.
The module tabs.
Search and filters. The **Views** menu saves and opens sets of filters.
The customer list. Select a row to open the customer's Customer 360 page.

blocks.note: You need permission to view customers to open this module. You need permission to manage customers to add or change them. Some roles see only the customers they manage as account manager.

sections.title: Find a customer
sections.intro: Search and filter the list to find an organisation quickly.
steps: In the menu on the left, select **Customers**.
In the search box, enter part of the name, code, e-mail domain, e-mail address or phone number.
To narrow the list, choose values in **Status**, **Tier**, **Region**, **Industry**, **Group** or **Account manager**.

steps.text: Turn on a switch if you need it: **My accounts**, **Open tickets** or **Top level**.
steps.note: **My accounts** shows customers you manage. **Open tickets** shows customers with open tickets. **Top level** hides subsidiaries.

steps: Select the customer in the list.
sections.result: The customer's Customer 360 page opens.

blocks.tip: Select **Clear** to remove all filters. To show more columns, select **Choose columns** at the right of the table header. Extra columns include **Group**, **Subsidiaries** and **ERP code**.

sections.title: Save a customer view
sections.intro: A view saves your search and filters so you can open the same list again later.
steps: In the **Customers** list, set the search and filters you want.
Select **Views**.
Select **Save current filters as view…**. The **Save view** dialog opens.
Enter a **View name**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says **View saved**. The view appears under **Saved views** in the **Views** menu. It is a personal view.

list: To open a view, select **Views** and then the view's name. The list shows **View:** and its name above the table.
Views shared by others show a people icon and the word **shared**.
To delete your own view, open it, select **Views**, and then select **Delete** with the view's name.

sections.title: Add a customer
sections.intro: Add an organisation that you support.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: In the **Customers** list, select **New customer**. The **New customer** form opens.

steps.text: Enter the **Name**.
steps.caption: The **New customer** form.
steps.alt: New customer form with name, code, tier, status, group, industry, parent organisation, account manager and contact fields

steps: Choose the **Tier** and the **Status**.
Fill in the other fields you know. The table below explains them.
Select **Create customer**.
sections.result: A message says **Customer created**. The customer appears in the list.

sections.title: Customer fields
sections.intro: The same form opens when you add or edit a customer.

rows: A unique code, for example the customer code in Wings ERP.
**Platinum**, **Gold**, **Silver**, **Bronze** or **Standard**. The tier decides which SLA policy applies to the customer's tickets.
The customer group, such as **Key Accounts**. A customer belongs to one group at most.
Used to filter lists and reports.
The head company, if this customer is a subsidiary. Leave it empty for a top-level customer.
The person in your team who looks after this customer. They get contract renewal reminders.
Domains such as `abcretail.demo`. New contacts with an address on these domains are linked to this customer by themselves.
Used for messages to the customer and for dates.
Switches for **E-mail**, **Phone**, **SMS** and **WhatsApp**, and a **Preferred channel**.
Extra fields that your administrator added, if any.
Anything else your team should know.

sections.title: The Customer 360 page
sections.intro: Select a customer in the list to open its Customer 360 page. The **Overview** tab shows the customer's health at a glance.

blocks.caption: The top of the Customer 360 page for a Platinum customer.
blocks.alt: Customer 360 page with the header and buttons, the badges, the tabs and the key figures, each numbered

callouts: The customer's name, code, industry and region. The buttons are **Edit**, **Subsidiary**, **Merge…** and a delete button.
Badges for the tier, the status, the group and the Wings ERP code. The account manager's name follows them.
The tabs. A number shows how many items each tab has.
Key figures for the last 90 days, such as open tickets, SLA breaches and satisfaction.

list: Three charts: **Satisfaction trend**, **Ticket volume** and **Open tickets by priority**.
**Outstanding complaints & escalations**: tickets that are escalated, past their SLA, critical or rated badly by the customer.
**Recent conversations**: the latest messages with the customer on any channel. Select a ticket number to open it.
**Profile**: the customer's details from the customer form.
**Hierarchy**: the parent company and the subsidiaries, with totals that include the subsidiaries.
**Upcoming activities**: the next planned visits and calls.

blocks.caption: The **Profile** card of a customer.
blocks.alt: Profile card showing the account manager, industry, region, contact details, website, e-mail domains, preferences, language and last sync with Wings ERP

blocks.note: If other customers were merged into this one, a line says **Merged from** and the number of customers. Select it to see which ones.

sections.title: Customer 360 figures and tabs
sections.intro: These tables explain the key figures and the tabs of the Customer 360 page.

rows: Tickets that are not resolved or closed. The line below shows how many are overdue.
Tickets that missed a target in the last 90 days. The line below counts open tickets.
The average satisfaction score out of 5, and the number of answers.
The average time to resolve a ticket, in hours.
Tickets created in the last 90 days, with a small trend line.
Contracts in force now. The line below shows how many end within 60 days.
Sites where the customer runs your products. The line below counts contacts.
Key figures, charts, complaints, recent conversations, profile, hierarchy and upcoming activities.
The customer's tickets. Choose **Open**, **Resolved & closed** or **All**, filter by priority, or search by subject.
The customer's people and any possible duplicates.
Installations, licences and assets. You need permission to view products.
The support eligibility check, contracts and entitlements. You need permission to view contracts. Chapter 9 explains them.
A calendar of service visits and calls for this customer.
Invoices, orders, receipts, AMC contracts and installations from Wings ERP. You can only read them.

sections.title: Edit a customer
sections.intro: Change a customer's details, tier, group or account manager.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: Open the customer's Customer 360 page.
Select **Edit**. The form opens with the current values.
Change the fields you need.
Select **Save changes**.
sections.result: A message says **Customer updated**. The Customer 360 page shows the new values.

sections.title: Add a subsidiary
sections.intro: A subsidiary is a customer that belongs to a parent customer, such as a branch company or a franchise.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: Open the parent customer's Customer 360 page.
Select **Subsidiary**. The **New customer** form opens with the parent already filled in.
Enter the **Name** and the other details.
Select **Create customer**.
sections.result: A message says **Subsidiary created**. The new customer appears in the parent's **Hierarchy** card.

sections.title: Delete a customer
sections.intro: Delete a customer that you added by mistake or no longer support.
prerequisites: You have permission to delete customers. Otherwise the delete button does not appear.
steps: Open the customer's Customer 360 page.
Select the delete button at the right of the header.
Read the message, then select **Delete customer**.
sections.result: A message says **Customer deleted**. The customer is hidden from lists. Its tickets, contacts and history are kept.

blocks.note: There is no restore button in the desk. Ask your administrator if you deleted a customer by mistake.

sections.title: Merge two customer organisations
sections.intro: Use this when the same organisation exists twice, for example under two spellings.
prerequisites: You have permission to merge customer organisations.
steps: Go to the Customer 360 page of one of the two customers.
Select **Merge…**. The **Merge customer organisations** dialog opens.
In **Find the duplicate organisation**, enter part of the other customer's name, code, ERP code or domain.
Select the other customer in the results, then select **Next**.

steps.text: Choose which customer to keep, for example **Keep ABC Retail Pvt Ltd**.
steps.caption: Step 2 compares the two customers. Rows that differ are shaded.
steps.alt: Merge customer organisations dialog at step 2 with the Keep choice and a table comparing fields of the two customers

steps: Tick **Use merged value** for any value you want from the other customer.
Select **Review**.

steps.text: Read the summary of what moves.
steps.caption: Step 3 shows the final values before you merge.
steps.alt: Merge customer organisations dialog at step 3 with the field table and the Merge customers button

steps.text: Select **Merge customers**.
steps.warning: You cannot undo a merge. The merged customer cannot be edited or restored afterwards.

sections.result: The dialog says **Customers merged** and lists how many records moved. Select **Done**.

blocks.p: Everything of the merged customer moves to the kept one. That includes contacts, tickets, locations, departments, contracts, installations, licences, assets, service activities, subsidiaries and Wings ERP links. The merge is recorded in the audit log.
If someone opens the merged customer later, the page says **This customer was merged**. A button opens the customer that was kept.

sections.title: Contacts of a customer
sections.intro: The **Contacts** tab of the Customer 360 page lists the customer's people.

blocks.caption: The **Contacts** tab with one possible duplicate.
blocks.alt: Contacts tab with four contacts, their e-mail, phone, location, portal access and open tickets, and a possible duplicate below

list: Each row shows the e-mail, phone, location, portal access and open tickets. Badges mark the **Primary** contact and **VIP** contacts.
Select a name to open the contact's page.
Select **Add contact** to add a person to this customer.
**Possible duplicates** lists pairs of contacts that may be the same person. Select **Review & merge** to compare them.

sections.title: Manage locations and departments
sections.intro: Locations are the customer's sites, such as a head office and branches. Departments group the customer's contacts, such as Finance or IT.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.

steps.text: On the Customer 360 page, select the **Locations** tab.
steps.caption: The **Locations** tab with two sites and three departments.
steps.alt: Locations tab with a table of two locations and a row of customer departments with edit and delete buttons

steps: To add a site, select **Add location**. The **New location** form opens.
Enter the **Name** and, if you like, the code, address, phone, service region and time zone.
Tick **Head office** for the main site. Clear **Active** for a site that is no longer used.
Select **Save**.
To add a department, select **Add department**, enter the **Department name**, and select **Save**.
sections.result: The location or department appears on the tab. Use the pencil button to edit one and the bin button to delete one.

blocks.note: If contacts, installations or tickets use a location, deleting it makes it inactive instead. Deleting a department keeps its contacts with the customer.

sections.title: View Wings ERP records
sections.intro: See the customer's invoices, orders, receipts and AMC contracts from Wings ERP without leaving SupportDesk.
prerequisites: An administrator has connected Wings ERP.

steps.text: On the Customer 360 page, select the **ERP records** tab.
steps.caption: The **ERP records** tab with the AMC contracts list open.
steps.alt: ERP records tab with four key figures, the ERP customer card with tax numbers and credit limit, and a list of AMC contracts

steps: Read the key figures: **Outstanding**, **Invoices (latest)**, **Open orders** and **AMC contracts**.
Choose a list: **Invoices**, **Orders & deliveries**, **Receipts**, **AMC contracts** or **Installations**.

steps.text: Select an invoice, order or receipt to see its details.
steps.caption: The details of an invoice from Wings ERP.
steps.alt: Side panel with an invoice's type, date, status, place of supply, item lines, tax and total

steps: Select the close button to close the panel.
sections.result: The panel shows the document's lines, GST, total and balance due. **Tickets about this record** lists tickets raised about it.

sections.title: Find a contact
sections.intro: The **Contacts** tab lists the people at all your customers.
steps: In **Customers**, select the **Contacts** tab.
In the search box, enter part of a name, e-mail address, phone number or job title.
To change which contacts show, choose **Active**, **Inactive**, **Merged** or **All**.
To filter by portal access, choose a value in **Any portal access**.
To see only important people, turn on **VIP only**.
Select the contact in the list.
sections.result: The contact's page opens.

sections.title: Add a contact
sections.intro: Add a person who contacts your support team.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: In **Customers** > **Contacts**, select **New contact**. You can also select **Add contact** on a Customer 360 page.

steps.text: Enter the name, e-mail address and phone numbers.
steps.caption: The **New contact** form.
steps.alt: New contact form with name, e-mail, job title, phone, mobile, WhatsApp, customer, location, department, preferred channel, language, portal access, VIP and primary contact fields

steps.text: Choose the **Customer**.
steps.note: If you leave it empty, SupportDesk matches the customer by the e-mail domain.

steps: Choose the **Location** and **Department**, if you know them.
Choose the **Portal access**.
Tick **VIP** or **Primary contact** if they apply.
Select **Create contact**.
sections.result: A message says **Contact created**.

blocks.note: **Display name** fills itself from the first and last name. **Location** and **Department** stay greyed out until you choose a customer.

sections.title: The contact page
sections.intro: A contact's page shows who they are, how they reach you, what they agreed to receive and their portal access.

blocks.caption: The page of a VIP contact who is the customer's primary contact.
blocks.alt: Contact page with the header, the profile card, channel identities, consent grid, customer portal card, possible duplicates and tickets, each numbered

callouts: The contact's name and job title, with **Edit** and the delete button.
The profile: status, badges, customer, contact details, location, department, preferences and ticket totals.
**Channel identities**: the addresses and numbers that link incoming messages to this contact.
**Consent**: what the contact agreed to receive, per channel and purpose.
**Customer portal**: the contact's portal access, password status and last sign-in.
**Possible duplicates**: other contacts that may be the same person.
The contact's tickets. The **Merge history** shows below them if any contact was merged.

sections.title: Edit or delete a contact
sections.intro: Keep a contact's details up to date, or remove a contact.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: Open the contact's page.
Select **Edit**.

steps.text: Change the fields you need, then select **Save changes**.
steps.note: Tick **Inactive** for a person who has left the company.

steps: To delete the contact, select the delete button in the header instead.
Read the message, then select **Delete contact**.
sections.result: A message says **Contact updated** or **Contact deleted**. A deleted contact is hidden, and its identities become free for other contacts. Its tickets keep their history.

sections.title: Add a channel identity
sections.intro: Channel identities let SupportDesk recognise the contact when they write or call from another address or number.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: Open the contact's page.
In **Channel identities**, choose the channel in the list.
Enter the address, number or id in **Address, number or id**.
Select **Add**.
sections.result: The identity appears in the list. Messages from it now link to this contact. To remove an identity, select the cross next to it.

blocks.note: The channels are **Email**, **Phone**, **WhatsApp**, **Sms**, **Facebook**, **Instagram** and **Chat**. A **Verified** badge shows that the contact proved the address.

sections.title: Record a contact's consent
sections.intro: Record what each contact agreed to receive. An opt-out stops outbound messages on that channel for that purpose.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: Open the contact's page.
In the **Consent** card, find the row for the channel: **Email**, **SMS**, **WhatsApp** or **Phone**.
In the column for the purpose, choose **Opted in**, **Opted out** or **Unknown**.
sections.result: SupportDesk saves the change at once. The date appears under the choice. Point at the date to see where the consent came from.

rows: Messages about the contact's own tickets, such as replies and updates.
Satisfaction surveys after a ticket is resolved.

sections.title: Give a contact portal access
sections.intro: Let a contact sign in to the customer portal to raise and follow tickets.
prerequisites: You can manage portal access.
The contact is active and has an e-mail address.
steps: Open the contact's page.
In the **Customer portal** card, choose the level in the **Access** list.
Select **Send invitation**.
sections.result: A message says **Invitation sent**. The card shows the address and how long the code is valid. The invitation code is valid for 72 hours.

rows: Nothing. The contact cannot sign in to the portal.
The tickets of everyone at their location.

blocks.p: If the contact forgets their password, select **Send password reset**. The reset code is valid for 30 minutes. The card also shows whether a password is set, whether the account is **Locked**, and the last sign-in.

sections.title: How duplicate contacts are found
intro: The same person sometimes ends up as two contacts, for example after writing from a personal e-mail address. SupportDesk looks for such pairs.

It compares e-mail addresses, phone numbers, how similar the names are and the customer. The **Why** column lists the reasons. The **Match** column shows a score and a confidence of **High**, **Medium** or **Low**.

blocks.caption: The **Duplicate contacts** tab with one likely pair.
blocks.alt: Duplicate contacts page with the Minimum match list, the Rescan button and one pair of contacts with a 91 percent match

list: The same e-mail address or phone number counts anywhere in the workspace.
Near-identical names count only within the same customer.
Choose a **Minimum match** of 40% (all candidates), 60% (medium and high) or 85% (high only).

sections.title: Merge duplicate contacts
sections.intro: Combine two contacts that are the same person into one.
prerequisites: You have permission to merge contacts.
steps: In **Customers**, select the **Duplicates** tab.
Choose a **Minimum match**, then select **Rescan**.
Select **Review & merge** next to a pair. The **Merge duplicate contacts** dialog opens.

steps.text: Choose which contact to keep, then select **Next**.
steps.note: SupportDesk suggests the contact with more tickets. The kept contact fills its empty fields from the other one.

steps.text: Tick **Use merged value** for any value you want from the other contact.
steps.caption: Step 2 of the contact merge. Shaded rows have different values.
steps.alt: Merge duplicate contacts dialog at step 2 with a field comparison table and Use merged value check boxes

steps.text: Select **Merge contacts**.
steps.warning: There is no unmerge. The other contact becomes **Merged** and cannot be edited.

steps: Read the summary, then select **Done**.
sections.result: The dialog says **Contacts merged**. The kept contact now has the tickets, conversations, identities, consents and survey answers of both.

blocks.tip: You can also start a merge from a contact's page. Select **Merge…** next to a possible duplicate.

blocks.note: A merged contact's page says **This contact was merged.** Select **Open the surviving contact** to go to the kept one.

sections.title: Service activities
intro: Service activities are planned visits and calls, such as on-site visits, training or maintenance. Use them to plan work and to keep a history of what happened.
The **Service activities** tab shows all customers. The **Activities** tab on a Customer 360 page shows one customer.

blocks.caption: The **Service activities** calendar and agenda.
blocks.alt: Service activities page with a colour legend, the Schedule activity button, the calendar bar, a month calendar and the agenda list, each numbered

callouts: The colour of each activity type.
**Schedule activity** adds a new activity.
**Today**, the arrows and **Month** or **Week** move around the calendar.
The calendar. Select an activity to open it. Select an empty day to schedule an activity on that day.
The **Agenda** lists every activity in the period shown.

sections.title: Schedule a service activity
sections.intro: Plan a visit, a remote session, a training or another activity for a customer.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: In **Customers** > **Service activities**, select **Schedule activity**.

steps.text: Choose the **Customer**.
steps.caption: The **Schedule activity** form.
steps.alt: Schedule activity form with customer, type, status, title, start and end, assigned agent, location, installation, description and outcome fields

steps: Choose the **Type** and enter a **Title**.
Set **Starts** and **Ends**.
In **Assigned to**, choose the agent. Add the **Location** and **Installation** if they apply.
Enter a **Description** of the work.
Tick **Visible to the customer in the portal** if the customer should see it.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The activity appears in the calendar and the agenda.

sections.title: Record the outcome of an activity
sections.intro: After a visit or call, record what happened.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.
steps: In the calendar or the agenda, select the activity. The **Service activity** form opens.
Change the **Status**, for example to **Completed**.
Enter the **Outcome**. It appears in the customer's history.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The activity shows its new status. To remove an activity, open it and select **Delete**.

blocks.note: If you cannot manage customers, the form opens read-only with a **Close** button.

sections.title: Customer groups
sections.intro: Groups bundle customers, for example key accounts or customers of one partner. Use them to filter lists and saved views. Knowledge base access rules can use them too.
prerequisites: You can manage customers.

steps.text: In **Customers**, select the **Groups** tab.
steps.caption: The **Customer groups** tab with one group.
steps.alt: Customer groups page with the New group button and a table with the Key Accounts group

steps: Select **New group**. The **New customer group** dialog opens.
Enter the **Group name** and a **Description**.
Select **Create group**.
To put customers in the group, edit each customer and choose the group in **Group**.
sections.result: A message says **Group created**. The table shows how many customers belong to each group.

blocks.note: A customer belongs to one group at most. Deleting a group keeps its customers, but they no longer belong to a group. SLA and routing conditions cannot use groups yet.

chapters.title: Products, assets and contracts
intro: This chapter is for agents, account managers and supervisors. It shows what a customer runs and what support they paid for. Administrators who keep the product catalog use it too.
**Products & Assets** holds your product catalog, the customer installations and assets, and the support contracts. Contracts decide whether a ticket is covered.

sections.title: Products & Assets at a glance
intro: Open it from **Products & Assets** in the menu on the left. You can also press [[G]] and then [[P]].
The **Catalog** tab opens first. It lists your products by family, with their modules, versions and releases.

blocks.caption: The **Catalog** tab with the Wings ERP product selected.
blocks.alt: Products and Assets catalog with the New product button, the tabs, the product list, the product card, the modules and the versions table, each numbered

callouts: **New product** adds a product. Only people who can manage products see it.
The tabs of the module.
The products, grouped by family. Each shows its code and how many installations and customers it has.
The selected product: code, family, routing and install base. **Edit** and the delete button are at the top right.
**Modules**: the parts of the product, such as Finance or Payroll.
**Versions & releases**: each version with its status, dates and releases.

sections.title: Products & Assets tabs
sections.intro: You see only the tabs your role allows.

rows: Customer sites that run a product, with version, environment and deployment.
Licence keys (masked), edition, seats and expiry.
Hardware and other items with serial numbers and warranties.
How many installations run each version.
Contracts that end soon or ended recently.
The connection to Wings ERP. Chapter 25 explains it.

blocks.note: By default, only administrators can change the catalog, installations, licences and assets. Supervisors and administrators can manage contracts.

sections.title: Add a product
sections.intro: Add a product that you support, so agents can choose it on tickets.
prerequisites: You can manage products.
steps: In **Products & Assets** > **Catalog**, select **New product**.

steps.text: Enter the **Name** and a short unique **Code**, such as `WERP`.
steps.caption: The **New product** form.
steps.alt: New product form with name, code, family, default department, default team, description and an Active check box

steps: Choose the **Family**, if the product belongs to one.

steps.text: Choose the **Default department** and **Default team**.
steps.note: New tickets for this product go to them.

steps: Enter a **Description**.
Keep **Active (selectable on tickets)** ticked.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says **Product saved**. The product appears in the list on the left.

sections.title: Edit, retire or delete a product
sections.intro: Change a product's details, or remove a product you no longer support.
prerequisites: You can manage products.
steps: In the **Catalog**, select the product in the list.
To change it, select **Edit**, change the fields, and select **Save**.
To remove it, select the delete button next to **Edit**.
Type the product's code to confirm.
Select **Delete product**, or **Retire product** if the product is in use.
sections.result: An unused product is deleted. A product with installations, tickets or contracts is retired instead. It stays on old records but agents can no longer choose it.

blocks.tip: To retire a product without the delete button, edit it and clear **Active (selectable on tickets)**.

sections.title: Add or remove a module
sections.intro: Modules are the parts of a product, such as Finance, Inventory or Payroll. Agents choose a module on a ticket to say which part has the problem.
prerequisites: You can manage products.
steps: In the **Catalog**, select the product.
Under **Modules**, select **Add module**.
Enter the **Module name**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The module appears as a chip under **Modules**.

blocks.note: To remove a module, select the cross on its chip, then select **Remove**. A module that tickets use is made inactive instead of removed.

sections.title: Add a version
sections.intro: Record each version you ship, and when its support ends. Installations and tickets refer to versions.
prerequisites: You can manage products.
steps: In the **Catalog**, select the product.
Under **Versions & releases**, select **Add version**. The **New version** form opens.

steps.text: Enter the **Version**, for example `8.1`.
steps.caption: The **New version** form.
steps.alt: New version form with version, status, release date, end of support and notes fields

steps: Choose the **Status**.
Enter the **Release date** and the **End of support** date, if you know them.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The version appears in the **Versions & releases** table.

list: Use the pencil button on a version's row to edit it.
Use the bin button to delete it. If installations run the version, it is marked **End of life** instead.
A **Past end of support** badge appears when the end-of-support date has passed.

sections.title: Add a release to a version
sections.intro: A release is a build of a version, such as a patch or a hotfix.
prerequisites: You can manage products.
steps: In the **Catalog**, select the product.
On the version's row, select the plus button. The **New release** form opens.

steps.text: Enter the **Release** name, for example `8.0.2`, and the **Build** number.
steps.caption: The **New release** form.
steps.alt: New release form with release, build, type, release date, engineering release and release notes fields

steps: Choose the **Type** and enter the **Release date**.
In **Engineering release**, enter the matching release or tag of your engineering team, if any.
Enter the **Release notes**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The release appears in the **Releases** column of the version. Select its name to edit it.

blocks.note: You cannot delete a release that installations run. Its bin button is greyed out.

sections.title: Version statuses and release types
sections.intro: These values appear in the **Versions & releases** table.

rows: The current version that customers can install.
An older version that you still support.
No longer supported. Install base reports count installations on it.

blocks.p: Release types are **Major**, **Minor**, **Patch** and **Hotfix**.

sections.title: Manage product families
sections.intro: Families group related products, for example by product line. They are used in reports, routing and the portal.
prerequisites: You can manage products.
steps: In **Products & Assets**, select the **Families** tab.
Select **New family**. The **New product family** dialog opens.
Enter the **Family name** and a **Description**.
Select **Create family**.
To put a product in the family, edit the product and choose the family.
sections.result: A message says **Family created**. The table lists each family with its products.

blocks.note: You can delete a family only when it has no products. Move its products to another family first.

sections.title: Installations
intro: An installation is one place where a customer runs one of your products. For example, a customer can have a production system and a test system.
Tickets can name the installation. That tells agents the exact version, environment and setup.

blocks.caption: The **Installations** tab.
blocks.alt: Installations page with the New installation button, the search and filter bar and the installations table, each numbered

callouts: **New installation** adds an installation. Only people who can manage products see it.
Search and filters: product, version, environment, deployment and **End of support only**.
The installations. An **EOS** badge marks a version past its end of support. Select a row to see the details.

blocks.tip: Select **Choose columns** at the right of the table header to show **Go-live** and **Location**.

sections.title: View an installation
sections.intro: See everything about one installation in a side panel.
steps: In **Products & Assets**, select the **Installations** tab.
Search or filter the list.

steps.text: Select the installation.
steps.caption: The details of a production installation.
steps.alt: Side panel with the installation's badges, customer, product, code, operating system, database, server, users, dates, tickets, modules, integrations and licences

steps: Read the details. Select **Customer 360** to open the customer.
Select the close button to close the panel.
sections.result: The panel shows the customer, the product and release, the technical setup, users, dates and tickets. It also lists the enabled modules, integrations, licences and assets.

sections.title: Add an installation
sections.intro: Record a new customer site, for example after a go-live.
prerequisites: You can manage products.
steps: In the **Installations** tab, select **New installation**.

steps.text: Choose the **Customer**.
steps.caption: The **New installation** form.
steps.alt: New installation form with customer, name, code, product, version, release, environment, deployment, status, location, users, go-live, operating system, database, server configuration and modules fields

steps: Enter the **Name**, for example `ABC ERP – Production`.
Choose the **Product**, **Version** and **Release**.
Choose the **Environment**, **Deployment** and **Status**.
Fill in the site details you know, such as **Users**, **Go-live** and **Operating system**.
Choose the **Enabled modules**.
Under **Integrations**, select **Add integration** for each system it connects to.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says **Installation saved**.

blocks.note: To change an installation, open it and select **Edit**. To remove it, select **Delete**. If tickets or contracts refer to it, SupportDesk marks it **Decommissioned** instead.

sections.title: Installation fields
sections.intro: The fields of the installation form.

rows: Required. The customer, a name for the site and the product it runs.
Your own code for the site, such as `INS-1001-01`.
The version and build the site runs.
The customer's site where it runs.
The number of users and the go-live date.
The technical setup, for agents who troubleshoot.
The product modules the customer uses.
Other systems it connects to, each with a **Direction**: **Inbound**, **Outbound** or **Two-way**.

sections.title: Manage licences
sections.intro: Record the licence keys of each installation, with seats and expiry.
prerequisites: You can manage products.

steps.text: In **Products & Assets**, select the **Licences** tab.
steps.caption: The **Licences** tab. Keys are always shown masked.
steps.alt: Licences page with status and expiry filters and a table of masked licence keys with customer, installation, edition, seats, expiry and status

steps: To find licences that end soon, choose a value in **Any expiry**, such as **Expiring within 90 days**.
To add a licence, select **New licence**.
Choose the **Customer** and the **Installation**.

steps.text: Paste the **Licence key**.
steps.note: SupportDesk masks the key before it saves it.

steps: Enter the **Edition**, **Seats**, **Issued on** and **Expires on** values, and choose the **Status**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says **Licence saved**. An active licence that ends within 90 days shows the number of days left.

blocks.p: Licence statuses are **Active**, **Expired**, **Suspended** and **Revoked**. Use the pencil and bin buttons on a row to edit or delete a licence.

sections.title: Manage assets
sections.intro: Assets are hardware and other items with a serial number at a customer site, such as POS terminals and printers.
prerequisites: You can manage products.

steps.text: In **Products & Assets**, select the **Assets** tab.
steps.caption: The **Assets** tab with warranty badges.
steps.alt: Assets page with a search box, a warranty filter and a table of assets with serial numbers, customers, installations, purchase dates, warranty end dates and status

steps: To find an asset, enter its name, serial number or tag in the search box.
To check warranties, choose **Under warranty** or **Warranty expired**.
To add an asset, select **New asset**.
Choose the **Customer** and enter the **Name**.
Enter the **Serial number**, **Asset tag**, **Product** and **Installation**.
Enter the **Purchased** and **Warranty ends** dates, and choose the **Status**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says **Asset saved**. A green badge shows a warranty that is still valid. A red badge shows the date it ended.

blocks.note: Asset statuses are **In service**, **In repair** and **Retired**. Deleting an asset that tickets or entitlements use retires it instead.

sections.title: Install base
sections.intro: The **Install base** tab shows which versions your customers run. Use it to plan upgrade campaigns and to spot versions with many tickets.

blocks.caption: The **Install base** of Wings ERP by version.
blocks.alt: Install base page with four key figures, a product list, a bar chart of installations per version with open tickets and a version table

list: The key figures count installations, installations on end-of-support versions, products and customers.
Choose a **Product** to see its versions.
The chart shows production and other installations per version. The line shows open tickets.
The table adds users, open tickets and tickets per installation in the last 90 days.
Select a bar or a table row to open the installations that run that version.

sections.title: Contracts and entitlements
intro: A contract is what a customer bought: a warranty, an AMC or another kind of support. It has a period, a value and the channels it covers.

A contract can choose the SLA policy and the support hours for the customer's tickets. Entitlements limit the cover to a product, installation or asset. They can also allow a set number of incidents or hours.

rows: Free cover for hardware or software for a fixed time after purchase.
A yearly support subscription, often with an incident allowance.
A block of hours that the customer bought in advance.
Work that is charged by the hour.
Support included in a software subscription.

blocks.p: Contract statuses are **Draft**, **Active**, **Expired**, **Suspended** and **Cancelled**. Entitlement types are **Support**, **Warranty**, **Hours**, **Incidents** and **Onsite**.

blocks.note: A contract with no entitlements covers the customer for every product. This is called customer-wide cover.

sections.title: Find a contract
sections.intro: Look up a customer's contracts, or list contracts by type, status or end date.
prerequisites: You can view contracts.

steps.text: In **Products & Assets**, select the **Contracts** tab.
steps.caption: The **Contracts** list.
steps.alt: Contracts page with the New contract button, the search and filter bar, and the contracts table, each numbered

steps: In the search box, enter a contract number, name, customer or ERP reference.
To narrow the list, choose a **Type**, a **Status** or an expiry, such as **Expiring in 30 days**.
Select the contract to open it.
sections.result: The contract page opens.

callouts: **New contract** adds a contract. Only people who can manage contracts see it.
Search and filters.
The contracts. A badge after the end date shows the days left when 60 or fewer remain.

sections.title: Add a contract
sections.intro: Record a contract the customer signed. SupportDesk then checks the customer's open tickets against it again.
prerequisites: You can manage contracts.

steps.text: In the **Contracts** tab, select **New contract**.
steps.caption: The **New contract** form.
steps.alt: New contract form with customer, name, number, type, status, SLA policy, dates, support hours, value, currency, prepaid hours, hourly rate, renewal date, ERP reference, check boxes, covered channels and covered products

steps: Choose the **Customer** and enter the **Name**.
Leave **Number** empty to get one by itself, such as `AMC-2026-0007`.
Choose the **Type** and **Status**, and set the **Start date** and **End date**.
Choose an **SLA policy** and **Support hours**, if the contract sets them.
Enter the money and hours fields that apply. The table below explains them.
Tick **Billable**, **Auto-renew** or **On-site visits covered** if they apply.
Choose the **Covered channels** and **Covered products**.
Select **Create contract**.
sections.result: A message says **Contract created**. The customer's open tickets are checked again.

blocks.tip: You can also add a contract from the **Contracts** tab of a Customer 360 page. The customer is then filled in for you.

sections.title: Contract fields
sections.intro: The fields of the contract form that need some explanation.

rows: The SLA policy for the customer's covered tickets. **Default selection** uses the normal rules.
The working-hours calendar for SLA timers. **Policy / department hours** uses the normal hours.
The hours the customer bought. Time that agents log on covered tickets uses them up.
When the contract is due for renewal.
The order or contract number in Wings ERP.
Shows that the contract renews by itself.
Shows that visits to the customer's site are included.
Creates a support entitlement for each product. Empty means customer-wide cover.

sections.title: The contract page
sections.intro: Select a contract to see its terms, how much of it the customer has used and its entitlements.

blocks.caption: The page of an AMC contract that came from Wings ERP.
blocks.alt: Contract page with the header, badges, four key figures, the terms card, the consumption chart, and the entitlements table, each numbered

callouts: The contract number, name and customer, with **Edit** and the remove button.
Badges for the status, type, days left, **Auto-renews**, **Billable** and **From ERP**.
Key figures: contract value, hours consumed, billable hours and tickets covered.
**Terms**: period, renewal, SLA policy, support hours, hourly rate, coverage, ERP reference and account manager.
**Consumption by month**: hours logged on covered tickets, billable and not billable.
**Entitlements** with the **Add entitlement** button.
Each entitlement with what it covers, its dates and how much is used.

blocks.p: Lower on the page, **Time by agent** and **Time entries** list the time logged against the contract. The billable amount shows only to people who can see costs.

sections.title: Edit or remove a contract
sections.intro: Change a contract's terms, or remove a contract that was added by mistake.
prerequisites: You can manage contracts.
steps: Open the contract.
To change it, select **Edit**, change the fields, and select **Save changes**.
To remove it, select the remove button next to **Edit**.
Read the message, then select **Remove**.
sections.result: After an edit, a message says **Contract saved**, and the customer's open tickets are checked again. After a removal, a message says **Contract removed**.

blocks.note: A contract that tickets or time entries refer to is cancelled, not deleted, so its history stays.

sections.title: Add an entitlement
sections.intro: Limit a contract to a product, installation or asset, or give it an allowance of incidents or hours.
prerequisites: You can manage contracts.
steps: Open the contract.
Under **Entitlements**, select **Add entitlement**.

steps.text: Enter the **Name** and choose the **Type**.
steps.caption: The **New entitlement** form for an AMC contract.
steps.alt: New entitlement form with name, type, product, installation, asset, incidents allowed, hours allowed, from and until dates and an Active check box

steps: Choose the **Product**, **Installation** or **Asset** it covers. Leave them on **Any** to cover everything.

steps.text: Enter **Incidents allowed** or **Hours allowed**.
steps.note: Leave them empty for unlimited support. For the **Incidents** or **Hours** type, the matching field is required.

steps: Set **From** and **Until**, if they differ from the contract's dates.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The entitlement appears in the table. A bar shows how much of the allowance is used. It turns red when the allowance runs out.

blocks.note: To remove an entitlement, select its bin button and then **Remove**. An entitlement that tickets have used is made inactive instead.

sections.title: Renewals
intro: The **Renewals** tab lists contracts that end soon or ended in the last 60 days. Account managers use it to plan renewals.
Each customer's account manager gets a reminder 30 days and 7 days before a contract ends.

blocks.caption: The **Renewals** tab with a 12-month horizon.
blocks.alt: Renewals page with a horizon list, four key figures and a table of contracts with urgency, customer, type, end date, value, account manager and open tickets

rows: Ends later, within the horizon you chose.

list: Choose the **Horizon**: **30 days**, **90 days**, **6 months** or **12 months**.
**Value up for renewal** adds up the value of the listed contracts.
An **Auto-renew** badge marks contracts that renew by themselves.
The **Open tickets** column helps you see unhappy customers before you talk about renewal.

blocks.note: SupportDesk has no renew button. To record the new term, add a new contract for the next period.

sections.title: Support eligibility
intro: SupportDesk checks every ticket against the customer's active contracts. It checks when a ticket is created. It checks again when the ticket's customer, product, installation or asset changes.

The result shows as a badge in the ticket header, in the ticket's details and in the side panel. The check never blocks work. The covering contract's SLA policy and support hours do apply to the ticket.

rows: An active contract covers the ticket. The note names the contract and what is left of the allowance.
No contract covers the ticket, or the allowance is used up.
The customer has only contracts that have ended.
Someone overrode the result with a reason.

sections.title: Check support eligibility before you create a ticket
sections.intro: Find out what support a customer would get, for example while they are on the phone.
prerequisites: You can view contracts.
steps: Open the customer's Customer 360 page.
Select the **Contracts** tab.
In **Check support eligibility**, choose the installation, or **No specific product (ticket without product)**.

steps.text: Select **Check**.
steps.caption: The eligibility check for a customer whose AMC has expired.
steps.alt: Contracts tab of a customer with the eligibility check showing Expired, two expired AMC contracts and their entitlements

sections.result: A badge shows the result, such as **Entitled** or **Expired**, with a note. It also shows the SLA policy that would apply and a **Billable** badge if time is charged.

sections.title: Override support eligibility
sections.intro: Let your team work on a ticket that no contract covers. For example, do this while a renewal is in progress.
prerequisites: You have permission to override eligibility. Agents who can edit tickets can also override while the workspace allows it. It allows it by default.
steps: Open the ticket.
In the ticket header, select **More actions**.
Select **Override entitlement…**. The **Override entitlement** dialog opens.
In **Bill against contract**, choose a contract if the work should count against one.

steps.text: Enter the **Reason**.
steps.caption: The **Override entitlement** dialog with a reason filled in.
steps.alt: Override entitlement dialog with a Bill against contract list, a Reason box and the Override button

steps: Select **Override**.
sections.result: A message says **Entitlement overridden**. The ticket's badge changes to **Overridden**. The override and its reason go into the audit log.

blocks.note: The reason is required. An override stays in place even if the ticket's customer or product changes later.

chapters.title: Knowledge base
intro: This chapter is for agents who use articles, for authors who write them, and for reviewers who approve them. It is also for community moderators.
It covers articles, review and publishing, versions and translations. It also covers reader feedback, the community, troubleshooting flows and analytics.

sections.title: How the knowledge base is organised
sections.intro: Select **Knowledge Base** in the main menu. The page has six tabs. You see only the tabs your role allows.

rows: Find, write, review and publish help articles.
Arrange articles in a tree of topics for the help center.
Read what readers say about articles.
Answer and moderate the customer forums.
Build guided question-and-answer flows for customers.
See how articles, searches and flows perform.
Read articles that are for agents only.
Write drafts, submit them for review, import articles and build flows.
Approve or reject articles in review.
Publish and archive articles and flows, and manage categories.

blocks.note: By default, administrators, supervisors and knowledge managers can review and publish. Agents can write drafts.

sections.title: The article list at a glance
sections.intro: The **Articles** tab lists every article you may see. The newest changes come first.

blocks.caption: The Articles tab with its tabs, actions, filters and list.
