blocks.alt: Knowledge Base Articles tab with numbered highlights on the section tabs, Import / export, New article, the filters and the article list

callouts: The knowledge base tabs.
**Import / export** brings in articles or saves a copy of them.
**New article** opens an empty article.
The filters: **Search**, **Status**, **Visibility**, **Category**, **Sort by** and **More filters**.
The article list. Select a title to open the article. Tick rows to export only those.

rows: Readers can see a published version of the article.
Someone edited a live article. The changes are not published yet.
The main language. A plus number shows how many translations exist.
The share of readers who found the article helpful.
The date to check the article again. A red date is overdue.

sections.title: Find an article
sections.intro: Use search and filters to find the article you need.
prerequisites: You can read articles. Internal articles need the **Read internal knowledge articles** permission.
steps: Select **Knowledge Base**. The **Articles** tab opens.
In **Search**, enter words from the title, content or keywords.
Optionally, choose a **Status**, **Visibility** or **Category**.
For more filters, select **More filters**. Choose a **Locale**, **Owner**, **Article type**, **Product** or **Tag**.
To see only articles due for review, turn on **Review due**. To see only published articles, turn on **Live only**.
In **Sort by**, choose **Recently updated**, **Title (A–Z)**, **Most viewed**, **Most helpful** or **Review due soonest**.
Select the article's title to open it.
sections.result: The article opens in the article editor. If you cannot change it, a note says that you can only read it.

blocks.tip: Select **Clear all** to remove every filter. Use **Previous** and **Next** below the list to change pages.

sections.title: Write a new article
sections.intro: Write an article as a draft. Nobody outside your team sees it until it is published.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: On the **Articles** tab, select **New article**.
In **Title**, enter a clear title, such as `How to reset your password`.
Optionally, in **Summary**, enter one or two sentences. They appear in search results.
In **Body**, write the article. Use the toolbar for headings, lists, links, code, images, videos and tables.
In **Search keywords**, enter words readers might search for. Separate them with commas.
In the panel on the right, choose the category, article type, visibility and owner. See [Article properties](#kb-article-properties).
Select **Create draft**, or press [[Ctrl+S]].
sections.result: The message **Draft created** appears. The article shows the status **Draft** and its first version.

blocks.caption: A new article with its title, body and properties.
blocks.alt: New article editor with numbered highlights on Title, Body, the properties panel and Create draft

callouts: **Title**. It is required.
**Body**. Paste or drop images into it to upload them.
The properties panel: status, classification, audience, ownership and lifecycle.
**Create draft** saves the article. On a saved article, the button is **Save**.

blocks.tip: Each save creates a version. Enter a **Change note** to say what changed and why.

blocks.note: If you leave with unsaved changes, the app asks you to confirm. Select **Discard changes** only if you do not need them.

sections.title: Article properties
sections.intro: These fields are in the panel to the right of the article.

rows: Where the article appears in the help center.
Keywords for grouping. Press [[Enter]] or a comma after each tag.
The product the article is about.
Other articles to show next to this one.
Who can read it. See the table below.
The brand portals that show it. Leave it empty for every brand portal.
The language the article is written in.
The person responsible for keeping it accurate.
When the owner should check it again. The owner gets a reminder.
After this date, the article is unpublished automatically. It must be after the review date.
The last part of the article's web address. Leave it empty to make it from the title.
Anyone can read it on the help center.
Customers who have signed in to the portal.
Agents only. It never appears in the portal.
Only customers who match an access rule. See [Limit an article to some customers](#kb-restricted-article).

sections.title: Limit an article to some customers
sections.intro: Use **Restricted** visibility for content that only some customers may read, such as a premium guide.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: Open the article.
In **Visibility**, choose **Restricted**. The **Access rules** section appears.
Select **Add rule**.
Choose one or more conditions: **Customer**, **Customer group**, **Tier** and **Product**.
To allow another group of customers, select **Add rule** again.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A customer can read the article when they match any rule. Within a rule, every chosen condition must match.

blocks.note: Empty rules are ignored. A **Restricted** article needs at least one rule with a condition. Without a rule, no customer can read it.

sections.title: Attach files to an article
sections.intro: Add downloads such as PDFs or spreadsheets that readers may need.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
The article is saved. You cannot attach files to a new article before you select **Create draft**.
steps: Open the article.
Under **Attachments**, select **Attach files**.
Choose one or more files on your computer.
sections.result: The files appear under **Attachments**. Select a file name to download it.

blocks.tip: To remove a file, select its bin button and confirm with **Delete**. Readers can no longer download it.

sections.title: How review and publishing work
sections.intro: An article moves through these statuses. The buttons at the top of the article change with the status.

list: If you can both review and publish, **Publish** also appears on drafts and articles in review.
When you edit a published article, your saves create a new version. The published version stays live until you publish again. The article shows **Unpublished changes**.
An article expires on its **Expires** date. It is then removed from the help center.
Owners get a reminder when the **Review due** date arrives.
You cannot schedule publishing for a later date.

blocks.note: If a reviewer rejects an article, the **Reviewer note** box shows their note at the top of the article.

sections.title: Submit an article for review
sections.intro: Send a finished draft to a reviewer.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: Open the draft.
Save any changes.
Select **Submit for review**.
sections.result: The article shows the status **In review**. Reviewers can now approve or reject it.

sections.title: Approve or reject an article
sections.intro: Check an article in review and decide whether it is ready.
prerequisites: You have the **Review and approve articles** permission.
steps: On the **Articles** tab, in **Status**, choose **In review**.
Open the article and read it.

steps.text: If it is ready, select **Approve**.
steps.caption: The actions of an article in review: Approve, Reject and Publish.
steps.alt: Article header with Save, Approve, Reject, Publish and the more actions menu highlighted

steps: If it needs changes, select **Reject**.

steps.text: In **What needs to change?**, enter your note for the author. Then select **Reject**.
steps.caption: The Reject this article? dialog with a note for the author.
steps.alt: Reject this article dialog with the What needs to change field, Cancel and Reject

sections.result: An approved article shows **Approved**. A rejected article goes back to the author as a **Draft** with your note.

sections.title: Publish an article
sections.intro: Make an article visible to its readers.
prerequisites: You have the **Publish, archive and expire articles** permission.
steps: Open the approved article.
Select **Publish**.
sections.result: The article shows **Published** and **Live**. Readers can now find it in the help center and in agent suggestions.

sections.title: Archive an article
sections.intro: Archive an article that is out of date but may be useful later.
prerequisites: You have the **Publish, archive and expire articles** permission.
steps: Open the published article.
Select the **...** button at the top right.
Select **Archive**.
Select **Archive** again to confirm.
sections.result: The article is removed from the help center and from agent suggestions. Its status is **Archived**.

sections.title: Reopen an archived or expired article
sections.intro: Bring an old article back so you can update and publish it again.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: On the **Articles** tab, in **Status**, choose **Archived** or **Expired**.
Open the article.
Select **Reopen as draft**.
sections.result: The article becomes a **Draft**. Update it, then send it for review again.

sections.title: Delete an article
sections.intro: Delete an article only when you are sure nobody needs it.
prerequisites: Your role allows deleting articles.
steps: Open the article.
Select the **...** button at the top right.
Select **Delete article...**.
Select **Delete article** to confirm.
sections.result: The message **Article deleted** appears, and the list opens.

blocks.warning: Deleting removes the article, its versions, translations, attachments and feedback for good. Archive it instead if you may need it later.

sections.title: Compare and restore article versions
sections.intro: Each save creates a version. Compare versions to see what changed, or restore an older one.
prerequisites: To restore a version, you need the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: Open the article.

steps.text: Select the **Versions** tab.
steps.caption: The Versions tab with the version list and Compare selected.
steps.alt: Versions tab with Compare selected and the version table with its status, author, save date and change note

steps: To read an old version, select **View**.
To compare a version with the current one, select **Diff**.
To compare any two versions, tick both, then select **Compare selected**.
To go back to a version, select **Restore**. Optionally enter a **Change note**, then select **Restore**.
sections.result: A comparison shows the changes. Added text and removed text are marked. A restore saves the old content as a new working version.

sections.title: Translate an article
sections.intro: Add a version of the article in another language. Readers of that language see it instead of the original.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission. To publish a translation, you need the **Publish, archive and expire articles** permission.
steps: Open the article and select the **Translations** tab.
In **Add a translation**, choose a language. Select **Add**.
Enter the translated **Title**, **Summary** and **Body**. The tab shows the original text for reference.
If a translation tool wrote the text, tick **Machine translated (flag for human review)**.
Select **Save translation**.
When you finish the translation, select **Submit for review** on it.

steps.text: After the review, select **Publish** on the translation.
steps.caption: The Translations tab with a published Hindi translation.
steps.alt: Translations tab with Add a translation, a Hindi translation marked Published, and Edit, Reopen and delete buttons

sections.result: The translation shows **Published**. Readers who choose that language see it.

rows: The original article was published again after this translation.

blocks.note: SupportDesk does not translate text for you. Select **Edit** to change a translation. Select its bin button to delete it.

sections.title: Import and export articles
sections.intro: Export articles to keep a copy or move them. Import articles written elsewhere as drafts.
prerequisites: To import, you need the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: On the **Articles** tab, tick the articles to export. To export all of them, tick none.
Select **Import / export**.

steps.text: Choose one of the two export options. The file downloads.
steps.note: The ZIP file holds each article as Markdown and HTML.

steps: To import, select **Import / export**, then **Import articles...**.
Choose the file to import. The menu lists the file types it accepts.
In the **Import finished** dialog, check the counts and any **Issues**.
Select **Open first draft** to review the first new draft, or select **Done**.
sections.result: Imported articles appear as drafts. The dialog shows **Drafts created**, **Skipped** and **Categories created**.

sections.title: Review reader feedback
sections.intro: Portal readers rate articles as helpful or not, give one to five stars and may add a comment. Read the comments and fix articles that confuse readers.
prerequisites: You can write, review or publish articles.
steps: On the **Knowledge Base** page, select the **Feedback** tab.
In **Review state**, choose **Needs review**, **Reviewed** or **All**.
In **Verdict**, choose **Helpful**, **Not helpful**, or both.
To hide ratings without text, turn on **With comments only**.
Select the article title on a comment to open the article.
When you have dealt with a comment, select **Mark reviewed** on it.
sections.result: The comment shows **Reviewed** and leaves the **Needs review** list.

blocks.caption: The Feedback tab with comments that need review.
blocks.alt: Feedback tab with numbered highlights on the filters, the selection bar, a feedback item and its Mark reviewed button

callouts: The filters: **Review state**, **Verdict** and **With comments only**.
Tick **Select all on page**, then select **Mark reviewed** to mark many at once.
One reader's verdict, stars, article, comment, name and date. **New** means not reviewed yet.
**Mark reviewed** for this comment.

blocks.tip: An article's own **Feedback** tab shows its views, helpful rate, rating and comments. Turn on **Unreviewed only** there to see new comments.

sections.title: Organise articles into categories
sections.intro: Categories form a tree of topics in the help center, such as Billing > Invoices.
prerequisites: You have the **Publish, archive and expire articles** or **Manage knowledge base settings and portals** permission.
steps: On the **Knowledge Base** page, select the **Categories** tab.
Select **New category**. To add a sub-category, select the plus button on the parent row instead.

steps.text: Enter the **Name**. The app fills in the **Slug** for you.
steps.caption: The New category dialog with a name entered.
steps.alt: New category dialog with Name, Slug, Parent category, Description, Visibility, Icon, Brands and Sort order

steps: Optionally, choose a **Parent category** and enter a **Description**.
Choose the **Visibility** and, if needed, the **Brands**.
In **Sort order**, enter a number. Lower numbers come first.
Select **Create category**.
sections.result: The message **Category created** appears, and the category appears in the tree.

blocks.tip: Select the pencil button on a row to edit a category. Select the number in **Articles** to see its articles.

blocks.note: You can delete only an empty category. Move its articles and sub-categories first.

sections.title: The community forums
sections.intro: Customers ask questions and share tips in the portal's community. Moderators answer, accept answers and keep the forums tidy on the **Community** tab.

blocks.caption: A community question with its moderation buttons, replies and the agent reply box.
blocks.alt: Community topic with numbered highlights on the topic actions, the original post, a reply's actions and Reply as an agent

callouts: Topic actions: **Edit**, **Pin**, **Close**, **Hide** and **Convert to ticket**.
The customer's original post with its tags.
Reply actions: **Accept answer**, **Edit** and **Hide**.
**Reply as an agent**. Agent replies show an **Agent** badge.

rows: A reply was accepted as the answer.
Nobody can reply until it is reopened.

blocks.note: In the topic list, use **Search**, **Status** and **Sort by** to find topics. Select a tag to show only topics with that tag.

sections.title: Answer a community question
sections.intro: Reply to a customer's question in the community, and mark the best reply as the answer.
prerequisites: You have the **Moderate community forums** permission.
steps: On the **Knowledge Base** page, select the **Community** tab.
In **Status**, choose **Unanswered**.
Select a topic title to open it.
Under **Reply as an agent**, write your answer.
Select **Post reply**, or press [[Ctrl+Enter]].
If a reply solves the question, select **Accept answer** on that reply.
sections.result: Your reply appears with an **Agent** badge. An accepted reply moves to the top with the **Accepted answer** badge.

sections.title: Moderate a topic or reply
sections.intro: Keep the community useful and safe. Pin important topics, close finished ones and hide unsuitable posts.
prerequisites: You have the **Moderate community forums** permission.
steps: Open the topic on the **Community** tab.
To keep it at the top of the list, select **Pin**. Select **Unpin** to undo it.
To stop new replies, select **Close**. Enter a **Reason**, then select **Close topic**.
To hide the topic from customers, select **Hide**. Enter a **Reason**, then select **Hide topic**.
To correct the text or tags, select **Edit**. Make the changes, then select **Save changes**.
To hide one reply, select **Hide** on it. Enter a **Reason**, then select **Hide reply**.
sections.result: The topic or reply shows its new state. The reasons are kept in the moderation log.

blocks.tip: Select **Reopen** to allow replies again. Select **Unhide** to show a hidden topic or reply again.

sections.title: Convert a community topic to a ticket
sections.intro: When a question needs private follow-up, turn it into a ticket for its author.
prerequisites: You have the **Moderate community forums** permission.
You have the **Create and clone tickets** permission.
steps: Open the topic on the **Community** tab.
Select **Convert to ticket**.
Select **Create ticket** to confirm.
sections.result: The message shows the new ticket number. The topic gets an agent reply that a ticket was opened. A **Ticket** button on the topic opens the ticket.

blocks.note: The ticket gets the topic's title, text and tags. The community replies are not copied into it.

sections.title: Troubleshooting flows
sections.intro: A troubleshooting flow is a short decision tree. It asks the customer questions and leads them to a fix, an article or an agent. Customers run flows in the portal. Agents cannot run them from a ticket.

blocks.caption: The flow designer with the flow details, the problem check, the diagram and the step editor.
blocks.alt: Flow designer with numbered highlights on Design and Preview, the flow details, the problems bar, the diagram and the step editor

callouts: **Design** and **Preview** switch between building and testing the flow.
The flow details and its usage: **Started**, **Resolved** and **Escalated**.
The problem check. Fix every problem before you publish.
The diagram. Select a step to edit it. Use the minus and plus buttons to zoom.
The step editor for the selected step.

rows: Asks the customer to pick an answer. Each answer leads to another step.
Shows the fix and ends the flow. The customer is asked if it solved the problem.
Points to a published knowledge base article.
Hands over to an agent. The customer can open a ticket with their answers attached.

sections.title: Build a troubleshooting flow
sections.intro: Create a flow for a common problem, such as a printer that will not print.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: On the **Knowledge Base** page, select the **Troubleshooting** tab.
Select **New flow**.
Enter the **Name**. Choose the **Visibility** and, optionally, a **Product** and **Category**.
In **Description**, enter what the flow helps with. Customers see it before they start.
Select the first step in the diagram. Enter its **Question** and its answers.
To add a step after an answer, select **Add answer with new step** and choose the step type.
Select each new step and fill in its text, article or message.
Check the problem bar. Select a problem to go to the step that has it.
Select **Create flow**, or press [[Ctrl+S]].
sections.result: The message **Flow created** appears. The flow is saved but not yet published.

blocks.tip: Use **Go to step** below the diagram to jump to any step. Select **Set as start** to make the selected step the first one.

blocks.note: An **Article** step can link only to a published article. A flow can have up to 200 steps.

sections.title: Test and publish a flow
sections.intro: Walk through the flow as a customer would. Then publish it.
prerequisites: To publish, you need the **Publish, archive and expire articles** permission.
steps: Open the flow on the **Troubleshooting** tab.

steps.text: Select **Preview**.
steps.caption: The flow preview at its first question.
steps.alt: Flow preview showing step 1 with Yes and No answers, Back and Restart

steps: Select answers to go through the flow. Use **Back** and **Restart** to try other paths.
Select **Design** to fix anything that is wrong. Then select **Save**.
When the problem bar says **No problems found**, select **Publish**.
sections.result: The message **Flow published** appears. Customers can start the flow in the portal.

blocks.note: The preview records nothing. Select **Unpublish** to take a flow out of the portal. In the **...** menu, **Archive** stops customers from starting it.

blocks.warning: **Delete flow...** in the **...** menu deletes the flow and its usage numbers for good.

sections.title: Flow problems and how to fix them
sections.intro: The problem bar lists what stops a flow from working. Each problem names the step.

rows: Add a step to the diagram.
Select a step and select **Set as start**.
A question needs at least one answer.
An escalation step cannot have answers.
Remove the answers, or change the step type.
An article step must link an existing article, or links an article that is not published.
An answer points to a missing step, or back to the same step.
Choose another next step for the answer.
A step cannot be reached from the first step.
Link an answer to it, or delete the step.

sections.title: Knowledge base analytics
sections.intro: The **Analytics** tab shows how customers and agents use the knowledge base. It also shows where content is missing. Choose **7 days**, **30 days** or **90 days** at the top right.

blocks.caption: Knowledge base analytics with the period buttons and the counters.
blocks.alt: Knowledge base Analytics tab with 7, 30 and 90 days buttons and counters for articles, live, drafts, in review, review overdue, expiring soon, views, helpful, average rating, feedback to review, searches and searches without results

rows: Articles, live articles, drafts, articles in review, overdue reviews, articles expiring soon, views, helpful rate, average rating, feedback to review, searches and searches without results.
A daily chart. Select **Show the numbers** for a table.
The most read articles with their helpful rate and rating.
What readers search for most, with the average number of results.
Searches that found nothing, with **Create article**.
Starts, resolutions and escalations for each flow.

sections.title: Write an article for a search with no results
sections.intro: Close a content gap. Write an article for something readers search for but cannot find.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
steps: On the **Knowledge Base** page, select the **Analytics** tab.

steps.text: Under **Searches with no results**, find the search.
steps.caption: Top searches and searches with no results, each with Create article.
steps.alt: Top searches table next to the Searches with no results table with a Create article button on each row

steps: Select **Create article** on that row.
Write the article as in [Write a new article](#write-article). The app uses the search words as the title.
sections.result: A new article draft opens with the search words as its title.

sections.title: Use the knowledge base on a ticket
sections.intro: Articles help you answer tickets faster. You also turn solved tickets into new articles.

list: The context pane of a ticket lists **Suggested articles**. Each shows its visibility and a match score. Select a title to open the article.
**Draft with AI** in the reply editor and **Draft reply** on the **AI** tab write replies from published articles. The draft lists the articles it used. See [Draft a reply with AI](#draft-reply-ai).
**Draft article** on the **AI** tab turns a resolved ticket into a new article draft. See [Draft an article from a ticket](#kb-draft-from-ticket).

sections.title: Draft an article from a ticket
sections.intro: When you solve a problem that others may have, turn the ticket into an article.
prerequisites: You have the **Write and edit article drafts** permission.
You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the resolved ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Knowledge article**, select **Draft article**.
Select **Open draft** and the title to open the new article.
Check the text. Remove customer names and other private details.
Save the article and select **Submit for review**.
sections.result: The draft goes to reviewers. The article's **...** menu has **Open source ticket** to go back to the ticket.

blocks.note: If the draft cannot be saved, the AI tab shows the text instead. Select **Copy HTML** and paste it into a new article.

chapters.title: AI Assistant
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who use AI help in their daily work.
It covers the **AI Assistant** page and the **AI** tab on a ticket. It also covers AI reply drafts and AI proposals.

sections.title: What the AI can do for you
sections.intro: The AI reads your tickets and knowledge base. It suggests summaries, replies, classifications and next steps. A person stays in charge: you review every suggestion before it reaches a customer.

list: The **AI Assistant** page answers questions about your data, searches by meaning, lists AI proposals and shows unusual ticket volume.
The **AI** tab on a ticket summarises it and drafts replies, classifications and articles.
**Draft with AI** in the reply editor writes a first reply for you.

rows: Use the **AI** tab, **Draft with AI**, **Semantic search** and, with analytics access, **Ask analytics**.
**Supervisor monitoring (live queues, agent status)**, team analytics or AI settings

blocks.warning: AI text can be wrong. Always read a draft and check its sources before you send it.

blocks.note: The demo uses a built-in offline AI. Your administrator may connect another AI service and set a monthly budget.

sections.title: The AI Assistant page
sections.intro: Select **AI Assistant** in the main menu. The page opens on the first tab you may use.

rows: Answers a question about your tickets with a chart and a table.
Finds tickets and articles that mean the same as your words, even with different wording.
Lists actions that AI agents suggest. You approve, reject or revert them.
Shows days with unusually many tickets for a product, version, customer or category.

blocks.note: Administrators also see **AI settings** at the top right. It opens the AI configuration pages.

sections.title: Ask a question about your ticket data
sections.intro: Ask in plain words, such as “Open tickets per agent”. The AI turns your question into a report.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** and **View personal dashboards and reports** permissions.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Ask analytics**.
Enter your question in the question box.
Select **Ask**. You can also select one of the example questions below the box.
Check the line under the answer title. It shows how the question was understood.
Read the chart and the **Results** table.
sections.result: The answer shows the metric, the breakdown and the period. If nothing matches, **No matching tickets** appears.

blocks.caption: Ask analytics with an example question and its answer.
blocks.alt: Ask analytics tab with numbered highlights on the tabs, the question box, the example questions, the understood question and the results

callouts: The tabs of the AI Assistant page.
The question box and the **Ask** button.
Example questions. Select one to ask it at once.
How the question was understood: **Metric**, **Breakdown**, **Period**, **Order** and **Parsed by**.
The chart and the **Results** table.

blocks.tip: Select a bar or a row to open the matching tickets in the ticket list.
Select **Show structured intent** to see exactly what the question was turned into.

sections.title: What you can ask
sections.intro: Questions work best when they name one measure, one breakdown and a period.

rows: Tickets created, open or resolved, SLA violations, resolution time, first-response time, CSAT, and reopened, escalated or frustrated tickets.
Customer, product, category, priority, channel, department, agent, team, status, or over time.
Words such as this month, this quarter, or the last 30 or 90 days.

blocks.note: The answers cover only the tickets you may see. The AI never changes any data.

sections.title: Search tickets and articles by meaning
sections.intro: Describe a problem in your own words. The search finds similar tickets and articles, even when they use other words.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Semantic search**.
Describe the problem in the search box. Use at least two characters.
Choose where to search: **Everything**, **Tickets** or **Knowledge articles**.
Select **Search**.
Select a title to open the ticket or article.
sections.result: The results are listed with the best match first. Each result shows its type, status, a short extract and a relevance bar.

blocks.caption: Semantic search results for a description of an export problem.
blocks.alt: Semantic search tab with numbered highlights on the search box, the scope options and the first result

callouts: The search box and the **Search** button.
Where to search.
A result with its type, title, status, extract and relevance.

blocks.tip: Under a ticket result, select **AI insights for this ticket** to open the full-page AI assistant for it.

sections.title: How AI proposals work
sections.intro: AI agents watch new tickets. They suggest actions such as a category, a priority, tags, a note or a reply. Each suggestion is a proposal. Most proposals wait for a person to approve them.

list: Each proposal has a risk level: **Low risk**, **Medium risk** or **High risk**.
Each proposal shows a confidence bar, the AI agent's name and the reason for the suggestion.
Your administrator may let some low-risk actions apply automatically. Such cards say **applied automatically**.
A proposal expires after 14 days if nobody decides.

rows: Waiting for review. The **Waiting for review** filter shows these.
The change was made on the ticket.
A person undid an applied change.
The change could not be made. The card shows why.

columns: What happens when you approve it
rows: The ticket fields change. You can revert these later.
The message is sent to the customer under your name. You cannot undo it.
A note is added to the ticket.
Records that you approved handling the request. The AI never takes a financial, account or contract action.

sections.title: Review an AI proposal
sections.intro: Check what the AI suggests, then approve or reject it.
prerequisites: You have the **Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions** permission.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Proposals**. The list shows proposals waiting for review.
To narrow the list, choose a **Status**, **Risk** or **Action**, or enter text in **Search**.
Read the proposed change and the reason under it.
To see the ticket, select the ticket number on the card.
Select **Approve & apply**, or select **Reject**.
If a confirmation appears, read it and select **Approve & apply** again.
sections.result: The card shows the new status and who decided. A message confirms the action.

blocks.caption: The Proposals tab with all statuses shown.
blocks.alt: Proposals tab with numbered highlights on the counters, the filters, a card's risk and status badges and its confidence bar

callouts: Counters for proposals waiting, high-risk proposals waiting and applied proposals.
The filters and **Refresh**.
The risk and status of a proposal.
The AI's confidence in the proposal.

blocks.warning: An approved reply is sent to the customer under your name at once. Read it carefully first.

sections.title: Undo an applied AI action
sections.intro: Undo a category, priority or tag change that the AI made.
prerequisites: You have the **Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions** permission.
The proposal is **Applied** and can be reverted. Sent messages cannot be reverted.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Proposals**.
In **Status**, choose **Applied**.
On the card, select **Revert**.
Select **Revert** again to confirm.
sections.result: The fields the AI changed go back to their earlier values. Changes that people made since then are kept. The card shows **Reverted**.

sections.title: Watch for unusual ticket volume
sections.intro: The **Anomalies** tab flags days with far more tickets than usual. Each hour, the app compares each day with the previous 28 days. It checks every product, version, customer and category.
prerequisites: You have supervisor monitoring, team analytics or AI settings permission.
steps: Select **AI Assistant**, then **Anomalies**.
In **Period**, choose **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days** or **Last 90 days**.
In **Status**, choose **Open**, **Acknowledged** or **Dismissed**, or leave it empty for all.
Compare the bars in **Volume vs. typical day**. Select a bar to see the tickets of that day.
In the **Anomaly alerts** table, select **Acknowledge** when you are handling a spike. Select **Dismiss** when it needs no action.
sections.result: The alert shows its new status. If no spike was found, **No unusual volume** appears.

rows: The product, version, customer or category that had the spike.
The number of tickets on that day.
The average for a day over the previous 28 days.

sections.title: The AI tab on a ticket
sections.intro: Open a ticket and select the **AI** tab. On a narrow screen, select **Ticket details** (the sliders button) first. The tab loads the sentiment and the expected resolution time at once. The other parts run when you select their button.

blocks.caption: The AI tab of a ticket with sentiment and expected resolution.
blocks.alt: AI tab with Summary, Sentiment, Expected resolution, Classification, Suggested reply, Similar and duplicates, Likely root cause and Knowledge article

rows: A short summary, the current status and pending actions. The summary is saved on the ticket.
The customer's mood: **Positive**, **Neutral**, **Negative** or **Frustrated**. A dot shows each customer message.
The typical time to resolve similar tickets, with a range and an expected date.
Suggested category, product, priority and department. See [Apply AI classification suggestions](#apply-ai-classification).
A reply based on articles and resolved tickets. See [Draft a reply with AI](#draft-reply-ai).
Possible duplicates and similar resolved tickets.
Likely causes, based on similar resolved tickets.
A draft article from this ticket. See [Draft an article from a ticket](#kb-draft-from-ticket).
The proposals for this ticket. **Run agents** asks the AI agents to check it again.

blocks.note: When a customer is **Frustrated**, the tab says: acknowledge the impact and give a concrete next step.

sections.title: Summarise a ticket
sections.intro: Get a short summary of a long conversation before you take over a ticket.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Summary**, select **Summarize**. If a summary exists, the button says **Refresh**.
sections.result: The summary appears with the current status and any pending actions. The last line shows when it was made.

sections.title: Apply AI classification suggestions
sections.intro: Let the AI suggest the category, product, priority and department. Apply only the values you agree with.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
To apply values, you also need the **Edit ticket fields** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Classification**, select **Suggest**.

steps.text: Check each suggestion. A crossed-out value shows the current value, and the arrow shows the suggested one.
steps.caption: Classification suggestions. Ticked values are applied; values with a check mark already match.
steps.alt: Classification section with category and department suggestions, confidence bars and Apply selected

steps: Tick the suggestions you want to apply. Clear the others.
Select **Apply selected**.
sections.result: The message **Classification applied** appears, and the ticket fields change.

blocks.tip: The bar next to each value shows the AI's confidence. Be careful with short or red bars.

sections.title: Draft a reply with AI
sections.intro: The AI writes a reply from your knowledge base and similar resolved tickets. You review it, then send it from the reply editor.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Optionally, under **Suggested reply**, enter instructions, such as `mention the 8.0.1 upgrade`.
Select **Draft reply**.

steps.text: Check the badge. **Grounded in knowledge** means the draft uses your articles or resolved tickets.
steps.caption: A drafted reply with its badge, confidence and numbered sources.
steps.alt: Suggested reply with Grounded in knowledge badge, draft text, sources and Insert into composer, Copy, Helpful and Not helpful

steps: Read the draft and the sources listed under it.
Select **Insert into composer**. Or select **Copy** to copy the text.
In the reply editor, remove the [1], [2] source markers and edit the text.
Send the reply as usual.
sections.result: The reply reaches the customer under your name.

blocks.warning: **Not grounded — review carefully** means no matching article or resolved ticket was found. Check every fact before you send it.

blocks.tip: Select **Redraft** for a new version. Select the thumbs-up or thumbs-down button to tell the AI whether the draft helped.

sections.title: Draft a reply from the reply editor
sections.intro: You can also start an AI draft without opening the AI tab.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket.
Select **Reply** to open the reply editor.
In the editor toolbar, select **Draft with AI**.
Read the message that appears. It says how many sources the draft used.
Edit the draft and remove the source markers.
Send the reply as usual.
sections.result: The draft is inserted into the reply editor. If the editor was empty, the draft fills it.

sections.title: Find similar and duplicate tickets
sections.intro: Check whether the customer already reported the same problem. See how similar problems were solved.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Similar & duplicates**, select **Find**.
Under **Possible duplicates**, check the open tickets from the same contact or customer.
Under **Similar resolved tickets**, read how each one was resolved and its root cause.
To merge a duplicate, select **Merge this ticket into** and the ticket number. Confirm with **Merge**.
sections.result: The lists show matches with a similarity bar. After a merge, this ticket is closed as a duplicate.

blocks.warning: A merge moves the conversation, attachments and watchers to the other ticket. You need the **Merge tickets** permission.

sections.title: Find the likely root cause
sections.intro: See what usually caused this kind of problem before.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **Likely root cause**, select **Analyse**.
Read the causes. Each has a likelihood bar and an explanation.
Under **Evidence**, select a ticket number to open a similar ticket.
sections.result: The causes are listed with the most likely first. The last line shows how many tickets were considered.

sections.title: Ask the AI agents to check a ticket again
sections.intro: AI agents usually run when a ticket arrives. Run them again after the ticket changes.
prerequisites: You have the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** and **Edit ticket fields** permissions.
steps: Open the ticket and its **AI** tab.
Under **AI proposals**, select **Run agents**.
Read the new proposals. Approve or reject them as in [Review an AI proposal](#review-ai-proposal).
sections.result: The message **AI agents finished** says how many agents ran and how many proposals they made.

sections.title: The full-page AI assistant for one ticket
sections.intro: Links on the **Proposals**, **Semantic search** and **Anomalies** tabs open a full page for one ticket. It shows the ticket facts, a reply box and the same AI parts as the **AI** tab.

blocks.caption: The full-page AI assistant with the ticket facts, the reply box and the AI parts.
blocks.alt: AI assistant page for a ticket with ticket facts, Reply with AI draft and Send reply, and AI sections on the right

list: To open another ticket, enter its number in **Ticket #** at the top right and select **Open**.
Select **Ticket** at the top right to open the ticket itself.
In **Reply**, select **AI draft** to fill the reply box with a draft.
Remove the [n] source markers. Then select **Send reply**, or press [[Ctrl+Enter]].

sections.title: AI badges and scores
sections.intro: These badges and bars appear on AI results.

rows: The draft is based on your articles or resolved tickets.
No source was found. The text may contain guesses.
How sure the AI is. Green is high, amber is medium and red is low.
The expected resolution time is based on few similar tickets.
How close a ticket or article is to this one.
The customer seems upset. Respond with care.
The sentiment has not been worked out yet.

chapters.title: Analytics
intro: This chapter is for supervisors and managers who track support performance. Agents can also use it to see their own numbers.
It covers dashboards, standard reports, drilling down to tickets, exporting and scheduled e-mail reports.

sections.title: What you see in Analytics
sections.intro: Select **Analytics** in the main menu. The numbers cover only the tickets you may see. The line under the title says which tickets are counted and which time zone is used.

rows: See your own tickets only. The page says **Personal analytics**.
See every ticket in your data scope, and share dashboards.
Export reports and use the **Exports** tab.
Schedule e-mailed reports and use the **Scheduled** tab.
Pages of charts and figures. Four come ready-made, and you can build your own.
Ten standard reports with figures, charts and tables.
Reports that are e-mailed on a schedule.
Files you exported, ready to download.

blocks.note: Times are business hours where a figure says (bh). Spam, merged and deleted tickets are never counted.

sections.title: Dashboards at a glance
sections.intro: The **Dashboards** tab opens the dashboard you used last.

blocks.caption: The Service performance dashboard for the last 30 days.
blocks.alt: Analytics dashboards tab with numbered highlights on the tabs, the dashboard list, the period and filter bar, Edit layout, the dashboard menu and a widget

callouts: The **Analytics** tabs.
The dashboard list. It groups dashboards under **Role defaults**, **Shared** and **Personal**.
The period, **Compare** and **Filters**. They apply to every widget on the page.
**Edit layout** lets you add, move and resize widgets.
The dashboard menu: **New dashboard**, **Duplicate as personal**, **Settings** and **Delete dashboard**.
A widget. Select its number to see the tickets behind it.

rows: Your open and resolved tickets, first response and CSAT.
Backlog, SLA compliance, agent scorecard and channels.
Resolution time, departments, escalations and backlog.
Demand, CSAT, products, top customers and tiers.

sections.title: Choose the period and filters
sections.intro: Change what the dashboard or report counts.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: In the period list, choose a period, such as **Last 30 days**. Choose **Custom range** to enter your own dates.
To compare with an earlier period, turn on **Compare**. Then choose **Previous period** or **Same period last year**.

steps.text: Select **Filters**. The **Filters** panel opens.
steps.caption: The Filters panel with the fields you can filter by.
steps.alt: Filters panel with Department, Team, Agent, Channel, Priority, Customer, Product and Tier, and Reset and Apply filters

steps: Choose one or more values in the fields you need, such as **Department** or **Priority**.
Select **Apply filters**.
sections.result: Every widget or report figure updates. Each active filter appears as a chip next to **Filters**.

blocks.tip: Select the cross on a chip to remove one filter. Select **Clear filters** to remove them all. **Reset** in the panel clears your choices before you apply them.

sections.title: See the tickets behind a number
sections.intro: Find out which tickets make up a figure, a bar or a row.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: Open a dashboard or a report.
Select a figure, a bar, a point on a line or a table row.

steps.text: Read the list of tickets in the panel that opens.
steps.caption: The tickets behind the Tickets created figure.
steps.alt: Drill-down panel titled Tickets created with the period, ticket count and a list of tickets with status, assignee, customer, date, priority and SLA breached

steps: To see more, select **Load more** at the bottom.
Select a ticket to open it.
sections.result: The ticket opens. The panel shows the period and the number of tickets at the top.

blocks.note: **SLA breached** in red means the ticket missed an SLA target.

sections.title: Create your own dashboard
sections.intro: Build a dashboard with only the figures you need.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: On the **Dashboards** tab, select the dashboard menu (**...**).
Select **New dashboard**.

steps.text: Enter a **Name** and, optionally, a **Description**.
steps.caption: The New dashboard dialog.
steps.alt: New dashboard dialog with Name, Description, Default period, the share switch, Cancel and Create dashboard

steps: Choose the **Default period**.
To let others see it, turn on **Share with everyone who has analytics access**.
Select **Create dashboard**.
Add widgets as described in [Add a widget to a dashboard](#analytics-add-widget).
sections.result: The new dashboard opens in edit mode. It appears under **Personal**, or under **Shared** when shared.

blocks.note: Only people with the **View team, department and organisation analytics** permission can share a dashboard.

blocks.tip: To start from a built-in dashboard, open it and select **Duplicate as personal** in the menu.

sections.title: Add a widget to a dashboard
sections.intro: A widget shows one measure as a figure, a chart or a table.
prerequisites: You can edit the dashboard. You can always edit your own personal dashboards.
steps: Open the dashboard and select **Edit layout**.
Select **Add widget**.

steps.text: Under **Visualisation**, choose **KPI**, **Line**, **Bar**, **Pie** or **Table**.
steps.caption: The Add widget dialog with a KPI widget and its preview.
steps.alt: Add widget dialog with Visualisation choices, Metric, Title, Period, the compare switch, widget filters, a preview, Cancel and Add widget

steps: In **Metric**, choose what to measure. Change the **Title** if you want.
For a chart or table, choose **Break down by** and **Show top**. For a table, add **More columns** if needed.
Leave **Period** on **Dashboard period**, or choose a fixed period.
Optionally, choose **Widget filters**. The app adds them to the page filters.
Check the preview, then select **Add widget**.
Select **Save layout**.
sections.result: The message **Dashboard saved** appears. The widget shows on the dashboard.

blocks.tip: In edit mode, each widget has arrow buttons to move it. **W−** and **W+** change its width. **H−** and **H+** change its height. The pencil edits it and the bin removes it.

blocks.note: Select **Cancel** in the toolbar to leave edit mode without saving your changes.

sections.title: Rename, share or delete a dashboard
sections.intro: Change a dashboard's details, or remove it when nobody needs it.
prerequisites: You can edit the dashboard. Role default dashboards cannot be deleted.
steps: Open the dashboard.
Select the dashboard menu (**...**), then **Settings**.
Change the **Name**, **Description**, **Default period** or sharing. Select **Save**.
To delete it, select **Delete dashboard** in the menu instead. Confirm with **Delete**.
sections.result: The dashboard shows its new details, or it disappears from the list.

blocks.warning: Deleting a shared dashboard removes it for everyone who can see it.

sections.title: Standard reports
sections.intro: Select the **Reports** tab. Select a report card to open it. There is no free-form report builder.

blocks.caption: The report library, grouped by topic.
blocks.alt: Reports tab with report cards grouped under Operations, Quality, People, Product and Customers

rows: Created against resolved, the backlog trend and how long open tickets have waited.
Median and 90th percentile first response and resolution times in business hours.
Compliance by milestone, breaches by priority and department, and the breach list.
First contact resolution, reopen and escalation rates by agent and category.
Volume, speed, first contact resolution, SLA and CSAT by channel.
CSAT trend, rating spread, CSAT by agent and the lowest-rated tickets.
Resolved tickets, replies, handle time, use of time and current workload per agent.
The categories and root causes behind most tickets, and repeated issues.
Tickets, breaches and reopens per product, module and version.
Tickets, open backlog, breaches, reopens and CSAT per customer, with a health score.

sections.title: Run a report
sections.intro: Open a standard report and set the period and filters you need.
prerequisites: You have the **View personal dashboards and reports** permission.
steps: Select **Analytics**, then the **Reports** tab.
Select a report, such as **SLA compliance**.
Choose the period, **Compare** and **Filters** as in [Choose the period and filters](#analytics-period-filters).
Read the line under the filter bar. It shows the dates, the comparison, the filters and the time zone.
Read the key figures, charts and tables.
sections.result: The report shows figures for the chosen period and filters.

blocks.caption: The SLA compliance report with its key figures and charts.
blocks.alt: SLA compliance report with numbered highlights on All reports, the filter bar, Schedule, Export and the key figures

callouts: **All reports** returns to the report library.
The period, **Compare** and **Filters**.
**Schedule** e-mails this report regularly.
**Export** saves the report as a file.
The key figures. With **Compare** on, each shows the change against the comparison period.

sections.title: Export a report
sections.intro: Save a report as a file to share it or work on it in a spreadsheet.
prerequisites: You have the **Export reports (CSV/Excel/PDF)** permission.
steps: Open the report and set the period and filters.
Select **Export**.

steps.text: Choose **Excel workbook (.xlsx)**, **CSV (.csv)** or **PDF document (.pdf)**.
steps.caption: The Export menu with the three file formats.
steps.alt: Export menu with Excel workbook, CSV and PDF document

steps: Wait for the message **Export ready**. The file downloads.
sections.result: The file is saved on your computer. It also appears on the **Exports** tab.

blocks.note: Large exports run in the background. The message **Export still running** appears. Download the file later from the **Exports** tab.

sections.title: Download an earlier export
sections.intro: Get a file that you exported before.
prerequisites: You have the **Export reports (CSV/Excel/PDF)** permission.
steps: Select **Analytics**, then the **Exports** tab.
Find the export. The list shows the **Report**, **Format**, **Status**, **Requested** time, **Rows** and **Size**.
When the status shows **Succeeded**, select **Download**.
When the status shows **Queued** or **Running**, wait. Then select **Refresh**.
sections.result: The file downloads to your computer.

sections.title: Schedule a report
sections.intro: Have a report e-mailed as an attachment every day, week or month.
prerequisites: You have the **Schedule report delivery** permission.
steps: Open the report and select **Schedule**. Or select **New schedule** on the **Scheduled** tab.

steps.text: Check the **Name** and the **Report**.
steps.caption: The Schedule a report dialog for the SLA compliance report.
steps.alt: Schedule a report dialog with Name, Report, Period covered, Compare with, Format, Department, Priority, Channel, Frequency, Day, Time, Time zone, Recipients, Active, Cancel and Create schedule

steps: Choose the **Period covered**, **Compare with** and **Format**.
Optionally, choose a **Department**, **Priority** or **Channel**.
Choose the **Frequency**: **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly**. Then choose the **Day** or **Day of month**, and the **Time**.
Check the **Time zone**, such as `Asia/Kolkata`.
In **Recipients**, enter an e-mail address and press [[Enter]]. Repeat for up to 20 people.
Leave **Active** on, and select **Create schedule**.
sections.result: The message **Report scheduled** shows the next run. The schedule appears on the **Scheduled** tab.

blocks.note: The period is rolling. For example, **Last 7 days** always means the seven days before each run. The report uses your data scope.
**Day of month** can be 1 to 28, so the report runs in every month.

sections.title: Manage scheduled reports
sections.intro: Test, change, pause or delete a scheduled report, and see past deliveries.
prerequisites: You have the **Schedule report delivery** permission.
steps: Select **Analytics**, then the **Scheduled** tab.
To see past deliveries, select **History** on the schedule.
Select the schedule's menu (**...**).
Select **Run now** to send the report at once. Use it to test a new schedule.
Select **Edit** to change the schedule. Select **Save** in the dialog.
Select **Pause** to stop deliveries for a while. Select **Resume** to start them again.
sections.result: The schedule shows **Active** or **Paused**, its next run and its last run.

blocks.caption: The Scheduled tab with two scheduled reports.
blocks.alt: Scheduled tab with numbered highlights on New schedule, a schedule, History and the schedule menu

callouts: **New schedule** creates another schedule.
A schedule with its status, format, report, frequency, period, recipients, owner and next run.
**History** shows past deliveries.
The schedule menu: **Run now**, **Edit**, **Pause** or **Resume**, and **Delete**.

blocks.caption: The delivery history of a schedule.
blocks.alt: Delivery history panel with a succeeded delivery, its time, recipients and file

blocks.warning: **Delete** stops the deliveries and removes the delivery history.

sections.title: Rebuild the figures
sections.intro: If figures look out of date, ask the app to rebuild them from the tickets.
prerequisites: You have the **View team, department and organisation analytics** permission.
steps: On any **Analytics** tab, select the **...** button at the top right.
Select **Rebuild metrics from tickets**.
sections.result: A message says **Rebuild queued** or **Metrics are current**. It shows how many tickets have figures and how many are missing or out of date.

chapters.title: Engineering board
intro: This chapter is for agents who send product defects to engineering, and for engineers who fix them.
It explains the engineering board, escalating a ticket, linking tickets to work items, and releasing fixes.

sections.title: How engineering work connects to tickets
sections.intro: Some problems are product defects that only engineers can fix. You escalate such a ticket to engineering. SupportDesk then creates a work item and links it to the ticket.

list: A **work item** is a bug, feature or task for engineers. Each one has a key, such as `ENG-12`.
One work item can cover many tickets. All linked tickets follow the same fix.
A **release** is a product version, such as 8.1. You plan work items for a release.
When a release is published, linked tickets get an internal note, and their assignees are notified.

blocks: The **Engineering** board shows work items of the built-in tracker. Your administrator can also connect Azure DevOps or GitHub. Items from those trackers appear on the ticket, not on the board. Jira is not supported.

rows: **View the engineering board, work items and releases**
Open the **Engineering** board and the ticket's **Engineering** tab.
Escalate a ticket and link a ticket to an existing work item.
**Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases**
Create, edit and move work items. Add, publish and delete releases.

blocks.note: The board needs the built-in tracker. An administrator turns it on under **Administration** > **Engineering**.

sections.title: The engineering board at a glance
sections.intro: Select **Engineering** in the main menu. The board shows one column for each work item state.

blocks.caption: The engineering board with its filters, state columns and work item cards.
blocks.alt: Engineering board with numbered highlights on the filters, the New column, a card, the card menu, Releases and New work item

callouts: The filters: search, engineer, release and **Show closed**. The item count and the reload button are on the right.
A state column with its name, the number of cards and a short hint.
A work item card. It shows the key, title, priority, severity, fix version, linked tickets and assignee.
The card menu. Use it to move the card or open its details.
**Releases** opens the list of product versions.
**New work item** creates a work item without a ticket.

rows: Released or done. This column appears only when **Show closed** is on.

blocks.tip: The ticket badge on a card shows how many tickets are linked to it. A green fix version with a rocket means the version is released.

sections.title: Find work items on the board
sections.intro: Narrow the board to the items you care about.
prerequisites: You have the **View the engineering board, work items and releases** permission.
steps: Select **Engineering** in the main menu.
In the search box, enter part of a title, a key such as `ENG-12`, or a version. Press [[Enter]].
In the engineer list, choose an engineer, or choose **All engineers**.
In the release list, choose a release, or choose **All releases**.
To include finished items, turn on **Show closed**.
If **Load more** appears below the board, select it to see more cards.
sections.result: The board shows only the matching work items. The count next to the reload button shows how many there are.

sections.title: Move a work item to another state
sections.intro: Move a card when work starts, when the fix is ready, or when the item is done.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: Open the **Engineering** board.
Drag the card to the new column.

steps.text: Or select the card menu (**...**), then choose the new state under **Move to**.
steps.caption: The card menu with the states you can move the card to.
steps.alt: Card menu with Move to New, Resolved, Closed and Open details

sections.result: The card moves to the new column. A message shows how many linked tickets were updated.

blocks.note: When a work item becomes **Resolved**, its linked tickets get an internal note, and their assignees are notified.

sections.title: Open and edit a work item
sections.intro: Change a work item's details, plan it for a release, or see its linked tickets.
prerequisites: To change a work item, you need the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: Open the **Engineering** board.

steps.text: Select the title of a card. The work item panel opens.
steps.caption: The work item panel with its fields, repro steps and linked tickets.
steps.alt: Work item panel for ENG-2 with title, type, state, priority, severity, assignee, release, product, tags, description and linked tickets

steps: Change the fields you need. [Work item fields](#work-item-fields) lists them all.
To plan the fix, choose a version in **Release (fix version)**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The message **Work item saved** appears, and the card shows the new details.

blocks.tip: Under **Linked tickets**, select a ticket number to open that ticket.

blocks.warning: **Delete** removes the work item for good. Select it only for items created by mistake.

sections.title: Create a work item without a ticket
sections.intro: Use this for engineering work that no customer has reported yet. To start from a ticket, [escalate the ticket](#escalate-ticket) instead.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: Open the **Engineering** board.
Select **New work item**. An empty work item panel opens.
Enter the **Title**.
Choose the **Type**, **Priority** and, if needed, the **Severity**.
Fill in the other fields you need, such as **Assignee** and **Description / repro steps**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The message **Work item created** appears. The new card appears in the **New** column.

sections.title: Work item fields
sections.intro: These fields appear in the work item panel. Fields marked optional on the screen can stay empty.

rows: A short description of the problem. Required.
How badly customers are affected: **Cosmetic**, **Minor**, **Major** or **Critical**.
The engineer who works on the item, or **Unassigned**.
The release that will ship the fix, or **Not planned**.
The product the item belongs to.
Optional planning labels that your engineering team uses.
How to reproduce the problem. An escalation fills this from the ticket.
The tickets that follow this work item. You cannot edit this list here.

sections.title: Escalate a ticket to engineering
sections.intro: Escalate a ticket when the customer's problem is a product defect. SupportDesk creates a work item and fills the repro steps from the ticket.
prerequisites: You have the **Create and link engineering work items** permission.
Your administrator has set up at least one engineering tracker.
steps: Open the ticket.

steps.text: Open the **Engineering** tab.
steps.note: On a narrow screen, the tabs are in a side panel. Select **Ticket details** (the sliders button) to open it.
steps.caption: The ticket's Engineering tab with one linked work item.
steps.alt: Ticket details panel on the Engineering tab with Escalate, Link existing and the linked work item ENG-2

steps: Select **Escalate**. The **Escalate to engineering** form opens.

steps.text: Check the **Tracker**, **Type**, **Priority**, **Title** and **Severity**.
steps.caption: The Escalate to engineering form. The repro steps are filled from the ticket.
steps.alt: Escalate to engineering form with type, priority, title, severity, repro steps, engineer, tags, the substatus check box, Cancel and Create work item

steps.text: Read the **Repro steps** and add anything the engineers need.
steps.note: Some trackers also ask for an **Area path** and an **Iteration path**.

steps: If you know who should fix it, choose the engineer in **Assign to engineer**.
To show the ticket as waiting for engineering, tick **Set the ticket substatus “Engineering”**.
Select **Create work item**.
sections.result: The work item appears on the ticket's **Engineering** tab and in the **New** column of the board.

blocks.note: The repro steps include the description, the customer's messages, analysis notes, product details and impact. Remove anything private before you create the item.
If the message **Ticket status unchanged** appears, the work item was created, but the ticket status could not change. Change the status yourself if needed.

sections.title: Link a ticket to an existing work item
sections.intro: If engineering already tracks the problem, link the ticket to that work item. Do not create a second item.
prerequisites: You have the **Create and link engineering work items** permission.
steps: Open the ticket and its **Engineering** tab.
Select **Link existing**.
In **Tracker**, choose the tracker that holds the work item.

steps.text: In **Work item id or URL**, enter the key or number, such as `ENG-12` or `1234`. You can also paste the item's web address.
steps.caption: The Link existing work item form with a work item key entered.
steps.alt: Link existing work item form with Tracker, Work item id or URL, the substatus check box, Cancel and Link

steps: Tick or clear **Set the ticket substatus “Engineering”**.
Select **Link**.
sections.result: The work item appears on the ticket's **Engineering** tab.

sections.title: Follow engineering work from a ticket
sections.intro: The ticket's **Engineering** tab lists every linked work item. Each entry shows the item's state and fix version.

rows: The item's state in the tracker, such as **Active** or **Resolved**.
The item is planned for that release.
The fix has shipped in that release.
The customer was told that the fix is released.
The item left the tracker. SupportDesk keeps the last known details.
SupportDesk could not get the latest state from the tracker.
Select it to see the other tickets that follow the same item.

blocks.heading: Actions on a linked work item

list: Select the key, such as **ENG-2**, to open the item on the board or in the external tracker.
Select the refresh button on the item to get its latest state. The refresh button at the top refreshes all items.
Select the external link button to open the item in Azure DevOps or GitHub.
Select the cross button to unlink the item. Confirm with **Unlink**. The timeline keeps a record of the link.

blocks.note: When a linked work item is resolved or released, the ticket gets an internal note, and its assignee is notified. If your administrator turned it on, the customer also gets a reply that the fix is released.

sections.title: Releases and fix versions
sections.intro: A release groups the work items that ship together. Select **Releases** on the board to see them.

blocks.caption: The Releases panel with the form for a new release and the list of releases.
blocks.alt: Releases panel with Version, Planned date, Product, Release notes, Add release, and releases 8.1 Planned and 8.0.1 Deployed

rows: The version is not out yet. The line shows how many items are still open.
The version is published. Its items carry the fix version.
The version is installed. The deployment date is recorded.

sections.title: Add a release
sections.intro: Add the next version before you plan work items for it.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: On the **Engineering** board, select **Releases**.
In **Version**, enter the version name, such as `8.1.0`.
Optionally, choose a **Planned date** and a **Product**.
Optionally, enter **Release notes**.
Select **Add release**.
sections.result: The message **Release added** appears. The release appears in the list with the status **Planned**.

blocks.tip: To change a planned release, select its pencil button, change the fields and select **Save release**. Select **Cancel edit** to stop without saving.

blocks.note: You can delete a release only when no work items are planned for it. Otherwise its bin button is unavailable.

sections.title: Publish a release
sections.intro: Publish a release when the version ships to customers.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
steps: On the **Engineering** board, select **Releases**.
Find the release with the status **Planned**.
Select **Publish**. A message explains what happens next.
Select **Publish** again to confirm.
sections.result: The message **Release published** appears. The fix version is stamped on the release's work items, and resolved items are closed. Linked tickets get an internal note, and their assignees are notified.

blocks.warning: If your administrator turned on automatic customer notices, customers get a “fix released” reply at once. Check the release before you publish it.

sections.title: Mark a release as deployed
sections.intro: Record the date when a released version was installed.
prerequisites: You have the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.
The release is published.
steps: On the **Engineering** board, select **Releases**.
Find the released version.
Select **Mark deployed**.
Select **Mark deployed** again to confirm.
sections.result: The message **Deployment recorded** appears. The release shows the status **Deployed**.

chapters.title: Notifications
intro: This chapter is for everyone who uses the desk. It explains how SupportDesk tells you about new work and urgent events.
It covers the bell, the **Notifications** page, acknowledging critical alerts and desktop alerts.

sections.title: How notifications reach you
sections.intro: SupportDesk notifies you when something needs you. Examples are a new assignment, a customer reply or an SLA breach.

blocks.caption: The bell in the top bar with the number of unread notifications.
blocks.alt: Top bar with the bell highlighted and a red badge showing 99+

rows: A red badge with the number of unread notifications, or 99+ when there are more. The bell shows a ringing icon when an item needs acknowledgement.
Warnings and critical items also appear briefly on the screen.
After you allow them, warnings and critical items also appear on your computer's desktop.
The **Customer replies & mentions** card shows your latest replies and @mentions.
Your administrator decides which events also arrive this way.

blocks.note: New notifications arrive live. You do not need to reload the page.

sections.title: Check your notifications from the bell
sections.intro: The bell panel shows your latest notifications without leaving the page you are on.
steps: In the top bar, select the bell.

steps.text: Read the list. The newest notification is at the top.
steps.caption: The bell panel with critical items that need acknowledgement and unread warnings.
steps.alt: Notifications panel with Mark all read, a desktop alerts prompt and a list of notifications with Acknowledge buttons and unread dots

steps: To open the ticket or page behind a notification, select the notification.
To close the panel without opening anything, press [[Esc]] or select outside the panel.
sections.result: The notification you selected is marked as read, and its page opens. Links to other websites open in a new browser tab.

list: The icon colour shows how urgent the item is. See [Notification colours](#nt-colours).
A blue dot at the right marks an unread item.
**Acknowledge** appears on critical items that need it.
When the list is empty, the panel says **You're all caught up.**

sections.title: Mark notifications as read
sections.intro: Mark items as read when you have seen them, so that new ones stand out.
steps: Select the bell.
To mark one item, select the blue dot at its right.
To mark every item, select **Mark all read** at the top of the panel.
sections.result: The items lose their unread mark. The number on the bell goes down.

blocks.note: **Mark all read** skips items that need acknowledgement. They stay unread until you acknowledge them.

blocks.tip: On the **Notifications** page, each unread item has a **Mark read** button.

sections.title: Acknowledge a critical notification
sections.intro: Some critical notifications, such as SLA breaches, need you to confirm that you have seen them. While one waits, the bell shows a ringing icon.
steps: Select the bell, or open the **Notifications** page.
Find the item with the **Acknowledge** button.
Read the item. To see the ticket, select the item.
Select **Acknowledge**.
sections.result: The button disappears. On the **Notifications** page, an **Acknowledged** badge takes its place. The item is also marked as read.

blocks.note: Acknowledging also stops any copies of the alert that are still waiting to go out, such as e-mail or push.

blocks.tip: To see only the items you still need to acknowledge, use the **Needs acknowledgement** filter on the **Notifications** page.

sections.title: The Notifications page
sections.intro: The **Notifications** page shows your latest 200 notifications. To open it, select **View all notifications** at the bottom of the bell panel. You can also run **Go to Notifications** from the command palette.

blocks.caption: The **Notifications** page.
blocks.alt: Notifications page with numbered highlights on Enable desktop alerts, Mark all read, the filter buttons, the type list, a notification and its Acknowledge button

callouts: **Enable desktop alerts**. After you answer, this place shows whether desktop alerts are on or blocked.
**Mark all read** marks every unread item as read, except items that need acknowledgement.
The filters: **All**, **Unread** and **Needs acknowledgement**. Each shows how many items it has.
The type list. Choose a type, such as **SLA breaches**, to show only that type.
A notification: title, details, type, time and an **unread** mark. Select it to open its page.
The actions: **Acknowledge** for critical items, or **Mark read** for unread items.

blocks.note: When nothing matches your filter, the page says **No notifications here**.

sections.title: Filter the notifications list
sections.intro: Filter the list to find what needs your attention first.
steps: Open the **Notifications** page.
Select **All**, **Unread** or **Needs acknowledgement**.

steps.text: To show one kind of notification, choose it in the **All types** list.
steps.caption: The list filtered to items that need acknowledgement.
steps.alt: Notifications page with the Needs acknowledgement filter selected and a list of SLA breach items with Acknowledge buttons

steps: To show every type again, choose **All types**.
sections.result: The list shows only the matching notifications. Your filter stays while you are on the page.

sections.title: Notification types
sections.intro: The type list on the **Notifications** page offers only the types you have received.

rows: A ticket is assigned to you.
A customer replies on your ticket.
An SLA target is at risk.
An SLA target is missed. These often need acknowledgement.
A request waits for your decision.
Someone approved or rejected your request.
A follow-up reminder you set is due.
The AI Assistant suggests an action that needs a decision.
SupportDesk finds an unusual spike, such as many tickets about one issue.
A live chat is waiting for an agent.
A chat is transferred to you.
Something in the workspace needs attention, for example a connection to another system was turned off.

sections.title: Notification colours
sections.intro: The icon colour shows how urgent a notification is.

rows: Critical or error, such as an SLA breach.
Warning, such as an SLA at risk or an escalation.
Good news, such as a success.

sections.title: Turn on desktop alerts
sections.intro: Desktop alerts show warnings and critical items even when the desk is in a background tab. Your browser asks for your permission once.
steps: Select the bell.
In the box that says **Get desktop alerts for urgent notifications.**, select **Enable**.
When your browser asks, select **Allow**.
sections.result: The box disappears. The **Notifications** page now says **Desktop alerts on for warnings and critical items**.
blocks: You can also select **Enable desktop alerts** on the **Notifications** page or the Command Center.
Select a desktop alert to bring the desk to the front and open the item.

blocks.note: If you select **Block**, the page says **Desktop alerts are blocked in this browser.** To change your answer, open your browser's site settings for SupportDesk.

sections.title: Notification preferences
intro: You cannot change your own notification preferences in the desk yet.
Your administrator sets the defaults for everyone. For each event, they choose in-app, e-mail, push or a digest. They also set quiet hours, when e-mail and push wait until later.

blocks.note: Critical alerts ignore quiet hours. The chapter about notification settings explains the defaults.

chapters.title: Teams, agents and routing
intro: This chapter is for supervisors and administrators. It covers the **Teams & Agents** module.
You use it to watch live workload, organise departments and teams, and decide who gets new tickets. You also manage agents, skills, shifts, leave and out-of-office delegates.

sections.title: The Teams & Agents module
intro: Open **Teams & Agents** in the left rail. Tabs across the top take you to each part of the module.

You see the module when your role includes `agents.manage` or `supervisor.monitor`. What you can change depends on your other permissions. The [permission reference](#permission-reference) lists every permission.

rows: Departments, their e-mail alias, routing team, business hours and SLA default.
Teams, their members, and how new tickets are routed to them.
Every agent with roles, departments, availability, load and last sign-in.
Invite and edit: `admin.users`. Routing profile: also `agents.manage`.
The skills catalogue used by skill-based routing.
Shift patterns, shift assignments, leave requests and the team calendar.
Shifts: `agents.manage` or `admin.organisation`. Anyone can request leave.
Anyone for themselves. `agents.manage` or `admin.users` for others.
The live monitor of agents, queues, SLA risk and waiting chats.

blocks.tip: Supervisors who cannot manage the organisation land on **Monitor** when they open the module. Everyone else lands on **Departments**.

sections.title: The live monitor
intro: The live monitor shows the current state of your departments on one screen. It refreshes by itself when tickets, chats or availability change. It also refreshes every minute.
You need `supervisor.monitor`. Supervisors see their own departments. Administrators see all departments.

blocks.caption: The live monitor filtered to the Customer Success department.
blocks.alt: Live monitor with numbered areas: live indicator, tabs, department filter, KPI tiles, agents table, queues, SLA risk list and chats waiting
