callouts: **Live** shows that updates arrive as they happen. The refresh button reloads the view at once.
The module tabs.
The department filter. Choose **All my departments** or one department.
Tiles for agents online, open tickets, unassigned, SLA at risk, SLA breached and chats waiting.
**Agents**: availability, load against capacity, tickets in progress, overdue tickets, chats and idle time.
**Queues**: open, unassigned, at-risk and breached tickets for each team, with the oldest waiting ticket.
**SLA risk**: the riskiest open tickets, breached first, then by due time. Up to 50 are shown.
**Chats waiting**: visitors who wait for an agent, with the time they have waited.

list: **On leave** means the agent has approved leave now. **Off shift** means the agent is outside their shift. **Delegated** means a delegate covers the agent.
The load bar turns amber at 75% of capacity and red at 100%.
A waiting chat turns red after five minutes.

sections.title: Change an agent's availability from the monitor
sections.intro: Set an agent to **Online**, **Away**, **Busy** or **Offline** when they forgot to do it themselves.
prerequisites: Your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.users`. Otherwise the availability shows as a badge only.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Monitor**.
In the **Agents** table, find the agent.
In the **Availability** list of that row, choose the new value.
sections.result: A message confirms the change, for example "Priya Raman is now Away". Routing uses the new availability at once.

sections.title: Reassign an at-risk ticket
sections.intro: Move a ticket that is about to breach, or has breached, to an agent with more room.
prerequisites: Your role includes `tickets.assign`. Otherwise the **Reassign** button is hidden.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Monitor**.
In **SLA risk**, find the ticket.

steps.text: Select **Reassign** under the ticket.
steps.caption: The **Reassign** dialog for ticket #1010.
steps.alt: Reassign dialog with New owner and Note fields

steps: In **New owner**, choose an agent. The list shows the least loaded agents first.
Optionally, enter a **Note** for the new owner.
Select **Reassign**.
sections.result: A message confirms that the ticket is reassigned. The monitor refreshes.

blocks.note: The list offers agents of the ticket's department only. Agents on leave and the current owner are left out.

sections.title: Departments
intro: Every ticket belongs to exactly one department. The department's routing team, business calendar and SLA apply to its tickets.
Open **Teams & Agents** > **Departments** to see one card for each department.

blocks.caption: The **Departments** tab with one card for each department.
blocks.alt: Departments tab with numbered New department button, Show archived box, badges, details, edit and archive buttons and counts

callouts: **New department** creates a department.
**Show archived** adds archived departments to the list.
Badges show the department code, **In portal** and **Transfers need approval**.
The e-mail alias, routing team, business hours, default SLA and department head.
The edit button opens the department.
The archive button archives the department.
Links to the department's teams and agents, and its open tickets.

rows: 2–12 letters or digits. Left empty, the app makes one from the name.
A short explanation shown on the card.
Mail to this address lands in the department.
An agent shown as the head of the department.
The team that receives the department's new tickets. A new department gets a default team automatically.
The working hours for SLA clocks. **24x7** means no calendar.
Shown on the card. **Policy rules decide** leaves the choice to the SLA policies.
Customers can choose the department on portal forms.
Moving a ticket to another department creates an approval request first.
A number from 0 to 1000 that orders the departments in lists.

blocks.note: In this release, the department's **Default SLA policy** does not change which policy a ticket gets. Use SLA policy conditions instead. See [How a policy is chosen](#how-sla-policy-is-chosen).

sections.title: Create or edit a department
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.organisation`.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Departments**.
Select **New department**, or select the edit button on a department card.

steps.text: Enter the **Name** and, if you want, a **Code** and **Description**.
steps.caption: The department dialog for Technical Support.
steps.alt: Edit department dialog with name, code, description, e-mail alias, head, routing team, calendar, SLA policy and options

steps: Enter the **E-mail alias** and choose the **Department head**.
Choose the **Routing team**, **Business calendar** and **Default SLA policy**.
Turn on **Visible in the customer portal** or **Transfers out need supervisor approval** if you need them.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Department created" or "Department updated". The card shows the new details.

blocks.note: You can choose the **Routing team** only when you edit an existing department. A new department gets its routing team automatically.

sections.title: Archive or restore a department
sections.intro: Archive a department you no longer use. Archived departments receive no new tickets and disappear from the portal.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.organisation`.
At least one other active department exists.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Departments**.

steps.text: Select the archive button on the department card.
steps.caption: The archive dialog asks where to move open tickets.
steps.alt: Archive Technical Support dialog with the Move open tickets to list

steps: If the department has open tickets, choose a department in **Move open tickets to**.
Select **Archive**.
sections.result: A message says "Department archived". Open tickets move to the department you chose.

blocks.p: Moved tickets keep their owner when the owner belongs to the new department. Other tickets are routed again.

steps: Turn on **Show archived**.
Select **Restore** on the archived department's card.

blocks.note: You cannot archive a department that a brand uses as its default. Change the brand first.

sections.title: Teams and routing
intro: A team is a group of agents inside one department. Each department has one routing team that receives its new tickets.
Each team has routing settings. They decide which member gets a new ticket.

blocks.caption: The **Teams** tab filtered to the Technical Support department.
blocks.alt: Teams tab with numbered department filter, Test routing, New team, routing badges, routing, edit and delete buttons, and member list

callouts: The department filter.
**Test routing** opens a preview of who would get a sample ticket.
**New team** creates a team.
Badges show the assignment mode and routing options, such as **Shift-aware** and **Max 20 per agent**.
The routing button opens the team's routing settings.
The edit button opens the team.
The delete button. The department's routing team has no delete button.
Members with their availability and load. **Lead** marks the team lead.

rows: Nobody. Tickets wait in the team queue until someone picks or assigns them.
Eligible members take turns in a fixed rotation.
The eligible member with the lowest share of open tickets against capacity. This is the default.
The best match on product, category, territory, tier, language and skill levels, then load.
Members whose territory matches the customer's service region first, then load.

list: A customer's dedicated agent always gets the ticket first.
Routing skips inactive agents, light agents and agents who are not team members.
Routing skips agents on approved leave and agents with an active delegate.
Routing skips agents who are not online, when **Only agents who are Online** is on.
Routing skips agents who are off shift, when **Skip agents who are off shift** is on.
Routing skips agents who reached their own capacity or the team cap.

blocks.p: When nobody qualifies, the ticket goes to the **Fallback queue**. Without a fallback, it waits in the team queue.

blocks.note: **Skill based** routing uses each agent's average skill level. It does not yet match the skills a ticket needs.

sections.title: Create or edit a team
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.organisation` or `agents.manage`.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Teams**.
Select **New team**, or select the edit button on a team card.

steps.text: For a new team, choose the **Department** and enter a **Name**.
steps.caption: The team dialog with its members and team lead.
steps.alt: Edit team dialog with department, name, description, members, team lead and Active option

steps: In **Members**, add the agents of the department.
Choose the **Team lead**.
Leave **Active (receives routed tickets)** on, unless the team should stop receiving tickets.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Team created" or "Team updated".

blocks.note: You cannot move an existing team to another department. Light agents may be members, but they never own tickets.

sections.title: Set how a team routes tickets
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.organisation` or `agents.manage`.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Teams**.

steps.text: Select the routing button on the team card.
steps.caption: The routing dialog with the five assignment modes.
steps.alt: Routing dialog with assignment modes, online and shift options, team cap and fallback queue

steps: Under **Assignment mode**, choose a mode.
Turn on **Only agents who are Online** or **Skip agents who are off shift** if you need them.
In **Max open tickets per agent**, enter a team cap, or leave it empty.
In **Fallback queue**, choose the team that takes tickets when nobody here is eligible.
Select **Save routing**.
sections.result: A message says "Routing updated". New tickets for the team follow the new settings.

blocks.note: Routing settings apply to new tickets only. Manual assignment is never blocked.

sections.title: Delete a team
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.organisation` or `agents.manage`.
No open tickets wait in the team's queue.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Teams**.
Select the delete button on the team card.
In the confirmation, select **Delete**.
sections.result: A message says "Team removed".

blocks.note: A team with ticket history is deactivated instead of deleted. A department's routing team cannot be deleted. Choose another routing team first.

sections.title: Test routing for a sample ticket
sections.intro: See who would get a ticket right now, and why. Nothing is created or assigned.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Teams**.
Select **Test routing**.
Choose the **Department**, and a **Team** if you want a team other than the routing team.
Optionally, choose a **Customer**, **Product**, **Priority** and **Language**.
Select **Preview**.
sections.result: The panel shows the agent who would get the ticket, or **Stays in queue**. A table lists every candidate with the reason for the result.

blocks.caption: **Test routing** shows Meera Iyer as the best match, with all candidates below.
blocks.alt: Test routing panel with the chosen agent and a table of candidates with availability, load, shift, result and score

blocks.p: **Fallback used** means nobody in the team qualified and the fallback team took the ticket. Select **Test routing** again to close the panel.

sections.title: The agents list
sections.intro: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Agents** to see every agent of your organisation.

blocks.caption: The **Agents** tab with plan seats, filters and the agents table.
blocks.alt: Agents tab with numbered Invite agent button, seats panel, search box, status, department and agent type filters, and table header

callouts: **Invite agent** sends an invitation. You need `admin.users`.
Seats used against your plan for agents and light agents, and pending invitations.
Search by name or e-mail.
Filter by status: **Active**, **Invited** or **Deactivated**.
Filter by department.
Filter by agent type: **Full agents** or **Light agents**.
Each row shows status, roles, departments, availability, load and last sign-in. Select a row to open the agent.

blocks.note: Full agents, administrators and pending invitations count against the agent seats. Light agents count against a separate limit.

sections.title: Invite an agent
sections.intro: Add a new person to your desk. They receive an e-mail with a code to choose their password.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.users`.
Your plan has a free seat.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Agents**.

steps.text: Select **Invite agent**.
steps.caption: The **Invite an agent** dialog with sample details.
steps.alt: Invite an agent dialog with work e-mail, full name, title, time zone, light agent option, roles, departments, supervises and teams

steps: Enter the **Work e-mail** and **Full name**. Optionally, enter a **Title** and choose a **Time zone**.
Turn on **Light agent** if the person only views tickets and adds internal notes.
In **Roles**, choose one or more roles. Leave it empty to give the Agent role.
In **Departments**, choose at least one department.
Optionally, choose **Supervises** and **Teams**.
Select **Send invitation**.
sections.result: The **Invitation sent** dialog opens. It shows when the code expires and an accept link you can copy. Select **Done**.

blocks.note: The invitation code is valid for 72 hours. In demo mode, the dialog also shows the code itself.

sections.title: The agent page
sections.intro: Select an agent in the list to open their page. It shows who they are, what they can access and how routing treats them.

blocks.caption: The agent page for Priya Raman.
blocks.alt: Agent page with numbered Deactivate button, photo, status, availability, and Profile, Access, Routing profile, Shifts and Account-managed customers cards

callouts: Actions for the agent: **Deactivate**, **Reactivate**, **Resend invitation** or **Revoke**, depending on the status.
The photo. **Add photo**, **Change photo** and **Remove** appear for administrators and for the agents themselves.
Badges for status, **Light agent**, **MFA** and a pending or expired invitation.
**Availability**, with the time it last changed.
**Profile**: e-mail, phone, time zone, locale, last sign-in and e-mail signature.
**Access**: roles, departments (with supervisor marks), teams and the person the agent reports to.
**Routing profile**: capacity, languages, skills and routing attributes.
**Shifts**: the agent's shift assignments. **Manage shifts & leave** opens the **Shifts & leave** tab.
**Account-managed customers**: customers this agent manages. You set account managers on the customer record.

sections.title: Edit an agent's profile
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.users`.
steps: Open the agent page.

steps.text: In the **Profile** card, select **Edit**.
steps.caption: The profile dialog with name, title, phone, time zone, locale and signature.
steps.alt: Profile dialog for Priya Raman

steps: Change the **Display name**, **First name**, **Last name**, **Title** or **Phone**.
Choose the **Time zone** and enter the **Locale**, such as `en` or `en-IN`.
Edit the **E-mail signature**. You can use basic formatting.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Profile saved".

sections.title: Change an agent's roles and departments
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.users`.
You hold every permission of the roles you give or take away. See [The escalation guard](#escalation-guard).
steps: Open the agent page.

steps.text: In the **Access** card, select **Edit**.
steps.caption: The access dialog with roles, departments, supervised departments, teams and manager.
steps.alt: Access dialog for Priya Raman

steps: In **Roles**, add or remove roles. Keep at least one role.
In **Departments**, add or remove departments. Keep at least one department.
Optionally, change **Supervises**, **Teams** and **Reports to**.
Turn **Light agent** on or off.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Access saved". The change applies to the agent's open sessions at once.

blocks.note: **Reports to** receives the agent's leave requests.
You cannot remove a department while the agent still owns open tickets in it. Reassign those tickets first.

sections.title: Edit an agent's routing profile
sections.intro: The routing profile tells routing how much work the agent can take and what they are good at.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.users` or `agents.manage`.
steps: Open the agent page.

steps.text: In the **Routing profile** card, select **Edit**.
steps.caption: The routing profile with capacity, languages, skills and a territory attribute.
steps.alt: Routing profile dialog for Priya Raman

steps: Enter **Max open tickets** and **Max concurrent chats**.
In **Languages**, add language codes such as `en`, `hi` or `ta`.
Under **Skills**, select **Add skill**, choose a skill and its level from 1 (basic) to 5 (expert).
Under **Routing attributes**, select **Add attribute**, choose the kind and enter or choose the value.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Routing profile saved". The card shows the new capacity, skills and attributes.

rows: 1–1000. Default 25. Routing stops at this number.
0–50. Default 3. Live chats the agent can hold at once.
Skills from the catalogue, each with a level from 1 to 5.
**Territory**, **Product**, **Customer**, **Language**, **Category** or **CustomerTier**. Territory and skill-based routing use them.

sections.title: Set an agent's availability
prerequisites: You are the agent, or your role includes `admin.users` or `agents.manage`.
The agent is not deactivated.
steps: Open the agent page.
In **Availability**, choose **Online**, **Away**, **Busy** or **Offline**.
sections.result: A message says "Availability set to" and the new value.

sections.title: Change or remove an agent's photo
prerequisites: You are the agent, or your role includes `admin.users`.
steps: Open the agent page.
Select **Add photo** or **Change photo**.
Choose a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of up to 2 MB.
sections.result: A message says "Photo updated". To take the photo away, select **Remove** under it.

sections.title: Resend or revoke an invitation
sections.intro: Use these actions while an agent has the status **Invited**.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.users`.
steps: Open the agent page.
Select **Resend invitation** to send a new code. The **Invitation sent** dialog opens.
Or select **Revoke**, then **Revoke** again in the confirmation.
sections.result: A resent invitation has a new 72-hour code. A revoked invitation frees the seat, and the person cannot join.

sections.title: Deactivate an agent
sections.intro: Deactivate an agent who leaves. They are signed out everywhere, cannot sign in, and their seat is freed.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.users`.
You are not deactivating yourself.
The agent is not the last active administrator.
steps: Open the agent page.

steps.text: Select **Deactivate**.
steps.caption: The deactivate dialog asks what happens to the agent's open tickets.
steps.alt: Deactivate Priya Raman dialog with Route again, Give to an agent and Return to the team queue options

steps: Under **Their open tickets**, choose **Route again**, **Give to an agent** or **Return to the team queue**.
If you chose **Give to an agent**, choose the **New owner**.
Optionally, enter a **Reason**.
Select **Deactivate**.
sections.result: A message confirms the deactivation and how many open tickets are being reassigned. The status changes to **Deactivated**.

blocks.warning: The agent loses access at once. Check the open tickets choice before you select **Deactivate**.

blocks.p: **Give to an agent** moves only the tickets of departments that the new owner belongs to. Other tickets go back to the queue.

sections.title: Reactivate an agent
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.users`.
Your plan has a free seat.
steps: In the agents list, choose **Deactivated** in the status filter.
Open the agent.
Select **Reactivate**.
sections.result: A message says the agent is reactivated. They can sign in again.

sections.title: Manage the skills catalogue
sections.intro: Skills are things such as products, modules or languages. You give agents a level for each skill in their routing profile.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.organisation` or `agents.manage`.

steps.text: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Skills**.
steps.caption: The **Skills** tab with the skills catalogue.
steps.alt: Skills tab with numbered New skill button, filter box, table and edit and delete buttons

steps.text: Select **New skill**, or the edit button on a skill row.
steps.caption: The **New skill** dialog with a name and category.
steps.alt: New skill dialog with Name, Category and Description

steps: Enter the **Name**, and optionally a **Category** and **Description**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Skill added" or "Skill updated". The **Agents** column shows how many agents have the skill.

blocks.p: To delete a skill, select its delete button and confirm. Agents who have the skill lose it.

blocks.tip: Type in **Filter skills** to find a skill in a long list.

sections.title: Shifts
intro: A shift is a weekly working pattern in a time zone. You assign agents to a shift from a start date.
Shifts matter only for teams with **Skip agents who are off shift** turned on. Agents without a shift count as always on shift.

blocks.caption: The **Shifts & leave** tab with three shift patterns.
blocks.alt: Shifts and leave tab with numbered Request leave and New shift buttons, inner tabs and a shift card

callouts: **Request leave** and **New shift**.
Inner tabs: **Shifts**, **Assignments**, **Leave** and **Calendar**. **Leave** shows how many requests wait.
A shift card: colour, weekly hours, time zone, hours per week and agents on it today.
The edit and delete buttons.

sections.title: Create or edit a shift
prerequisites: Your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.organisation`.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Shifts & leave**.

steps.text: Select **New shift**, or the edit button on a shift card.
steps.caption: The shift dialog with weekly hours from Monday to Friday.
steps.alt: Edit India day shift dialog with name, time zone, colour, description, weekly hours and Active

steps: Enter the **Name**, choose the **Time zone** and pick a **Colour**.
Under **Weekly hours**, select a preset, such as **Mon–Fri 09–18**.
Adjust each day. Tick a day to make it a working day, and enter the start and end times.
To add a break, select **Split** and enter a second interval. A day can have up to four intervals.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Shift created" or "Shift updated".

blocks.tip: **Copy Monday to weekdays** copies Monday's hours to Tuesday to Friday. The end time can be `24:00`.

blocks.p: To delete a shift, select its delete button and confirm. Its assignments are removed too.

sections.title: Assign agents to a shift
prerequisites: Your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.organisation`.
At least one shift exists.

steps.text: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Shifts & leave**, then the **Assignments** tab.
steps.caption: The **Assignments** tab lists each agent's shift and whether they are on shift now.
steps.alt: Assignments tab with the Assign shift button and a table of agents, shifts, dates and status

steps.text: Select **Assign shift**.
steps.caption: The **Assign shift** dialog.
steps.alt: Assign shift dialog with Shift, Agents, From and To

steps: Choose the **Shift** and one or more **Agents**.
Enter the **From** date. Optionally, enter a **To** date.
Select **Assign**.
sections.result: A message says "Shift assigned" with the number of agents.

blocks.p: An empty **To** date means open-ended. A new assignment closes any older assignment that overlaps it.
To remove an assignment, select the remove button on its row and confirm.

sections.title: Leave
intro: Agents request leave on the **Leave** tab. Approved leave takes the agent out of routing for the period. Their existing tickets stay with them.
A request goes to the person the agent reports to. If nobody is set, it goes to a supervisor of one of the agent's departments. If there is none, anyone with `approvals.decide` can decide it.

blocks.caption: The **Leave** tab with one request waiting for approval.
blocks.alt: Leave tab with numbered status filter, Request leave button and Approve and Reject buttons

callouts: The status filter: **All**, **Awaiting approval**, **Approved**, **Rejected** or **Cancelled**.
**Request leave**.
**Approve** and **Reject** appear when you may decide. **Cancel** appears on leave you may cancel.

rows: The agent is skipped by routing during the period.
Declined. The reason shows in the **Reason** column.
Withdrawn before or during the period.

blocks.p: Leave types are **Leave**, **Sick**, **Training**, **Public holiday** and **Other**.

sections.title: Request leave
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Shifts & leave**.

steps.text: Select **Request leave**.
steps.caption: The **Leave** dialog with a reason filled in.
steps.alt: Leave dialog with Agent, Starts, Ends, Type and Reason

steps: Enter when the leave **Starts** and **Ends**.
Choose the **Type**.
Optionally, enter a **Reason**.
Select **Request leave**.
sections.result: A message says "Leave requested" and "Sent for approval". The request appears on the **Leave** tab as **Requested**.

blocks.note: A request cannot overlap another leave request of the same agent.

sections.title: Record leave for an agent
sections.intro: Managers can enter leave for someone else, for example a sick day reported by phone.
prerequisites: Your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.organisation`.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Shifts & leave**.
Select **Request leave**.
In **Agent**, choose the agent.
Enter the dates, the **Type** and a **Reason**.
Select **Record leave**.
sections.result: A message says "Leave recorded". Leave you record for someone else is approved at once.

sections.title: Approve or reject leave
prerequisites: The request waits for you. Or your role includes `approvals.decide` and also `agents.manage` or `admin.users`.
The leave is not your own.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Shifts & leave**, then the **Leave** tab.
Choose **Awaiting approval** in the status filter.

steps.text: Select **Approve** or **Reject** on the request.
steps.caption: The approval dialog with an optional note.
steps.alt: Approve leave dialog for Arjun Nair with a Note field

steps: Optionally, enter a **Note**. The agent sees it.
Select **Approve** or **Reject**.
sections.result: A message says "Leave approved" or "Leave rejected". The calendar updates.

sections.title: Cancel leave
prerequisites: The leave is your own, or your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.users`.
The leave is requested or approved, and has not ended yet.
steps: Open the **Leave** tab.
Select **Cancel** on the leave row.
In the confirmation, select **Cancel leave**.
sections.result: The status changes to **Cancelled**, and routing includes the agent again.

sections.title: The team calendar
sections.intro: The **Calendar** tab shows leave, leave requests, delegations and the holidays of the default business calendar. Use it to spot gaps before you approve leave.

blocks.caption: The **Calendar** tab for November 2026 with a holiday.
blocks.alt: Month calendar with a legend for leave, requested leave, delegations and holidays

blocks.p: Select **Month** or **Week** to change the view. Use the arrows to move between periods, and **Today** to come back.

sections.title: Set up a delegation
sections.intro: A delegation names someone to cover for an agent who is away. While it is active, routing skips the away agent. Their new assignments and approval requests go to the delegate.
prerequisites: To set up a delegation for someone else, your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.users`.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Delegations**.

steps.text: Select **New delegation**.
steps.caption: The **New delegation** dialog with a delegate and reason.
steps.alt: New delegation dialog with Away, Delegate, From, To, Reason and two options

steps: In **Away**, keep **Me** or choose the agent who will be away.
In **Delegate**, choose the agent who covers.
Enter the **From** and **To** dates and times, and a **Reason**.
Leave **Route approval requests to the delegate** on, unless approvals should wait.
Turn on **Also move open tickets when the window starts** to hand over open tickets too.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Delegation created". The delegation shows as **Scheduled**, then **Active** when the period starts.

blocks.note: Delegations of one agent cannot overlap. The delegate cannot be away during the same period.

sections.title: Edit or end a delegation
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Delegations**.
To change dates or options, select the edit button on the row, change the values, then select **Save**.
To stop a delegation early, select **End now**, then **End now** again in the confirmation.
sections.result: An ended delegation shows the state **Ended**. Turn on **Show ended** to see past delegations.

chapters.title: SLA policies and business hours
intro: This chapter is for supervisors and administrators. It explains how SupportDesk measures service commitments, and how you set them up.
Supervisors use the **SLA** module to watch tickets at risk. Administrators also create policies, business calendars and holidays.

sections.title: What an SLA measures
intro: An SLA policy sets time targets for each ticket priority. The clock for each target is called a milestone.
Open **SLA** in the left rail. Its tabs are **Policies**, **Calendars & holidays** and **Live breaches**.

rows: Time until an agent first replies to the customer. This clock never pauses.
Time until an agent answers the customer's latest message.
Time until the ticket is resolved.

list: **At risk**: the milestone passed its warning point, for example 75% of the target.
**Breached**: the target time has passed.
**Paused**: the ticket is in a status that pauses SLA clocks, such as **Waiting on Customer**.

blocks.p: SupportDesk checks every running milestone every 30 seconds. Warnings and escalations fire from that check.

rows: Open the SLA module and read policies and calendars
Create, change, reorder or delete policies
Create or change business calendars and holidays

blocks.note: Without the right permission, the forms show the settings but you cannot change them.

sections.title: How a policy is chosen
sections.intro: Each ticket gets exactly one SLA policy. SupportDesk picks it in this order:

list: First: the policy of the ticket's active contract.
Next: the first active policy, in evaluation order, whose conditions match the ticket.
Last: the default policy.

blocks.p: The business calendar comes from the contract's support hours first. Next come the policy's calendar and the department's calendar. With none of these, the clock runs 24x7.
When you change a policy or the evaluation order, open tickets are checked again. Time already elapsed is kept.

blocks.note: The department's **Default SLA policy** field does not take part in this choice in this release.

sections.title: The Policies tab
sections.intro: Open **SLA** > **Policies** to see every policy in evaluation order.

blocks.caption: The **Policies** tab with a Platinum policy and the default Standard SLA.
blocks.alt: Policies tab with numbered tabs, New policy button, explanation, table header and order buttons

callouts: The SLA tabs.
**New policy** opens an empty policy.
A reminder of how a policy is chosen.
Columns: order number, policy name and version, calendar, conditions, targets, escalations, running milestones and last update.
The arrows move a policy up or down the evaluation order.

blocks.p: **Default** marks the fallback policy. It always comes last and shows **Fallback** in the **Conditions** column. **Inactive** marks a policy that is switched off.

sections.title: Change the evaluation order
sections.intro: Put specific policies above general ones. The first matching policy wins.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.sla`.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Policies**.
Select the up or down arrow on a policy row. Repeat until the order is right.
Select **Save order**. To undo your moves, select **Discard**.
sections.result: A message says "Evaluation order saved". Open tickets are checked again.

sections.title: The policy editor
sections.intro: Select a policy to open it. The editor has five cards from top to bottom.

blocks.caption: The policy editor for the Platinum 24x7 policy.
blocks.alt: Policy editor with numbered Delete and Save policy buttons, and Policy, Applies to, Targets per priority, Escalation levels and Simulate cards

callouts: **Delete** and **Save policy**. The header also shows the version and how many tickets run on the policy.
**Policy**: name, status, business calendar and pause statuses.
**Applies to**: the conditions a ticket must meet. The default policy has no conditions.
**Targets per priority**: the time targets and the warning point.
**Escalation levels**: what happens before or after a breach.
**Simulate against a ticket**: test the form on a real ticket before you save.

sections.title: Create an SLA policy
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.sla`.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Policies** and select **New policy**.

steps.text: In the **Policy** card, enter the **Name** and a **Description**.
steps.caption: The **Policy** card of the Platinum 24x7 policy.
steps.alt: Policy card with name, description, Active, Default policy, business calendar, pause statuses and contract hours option

steps: Choose the **Business calendar** and any extra **Pause statuses**.
If contracts set their own support hours, tick the contract option at the bottom of the card.

steps.text: In **Applies to**, select **Condition** and build the rule, such as **Customer tier** is `Platinum`.
steps.caption: The **Applies to** card with one condition on the customer tier.
steps.alt: Applies to card with All (AND) and Any (OR), a customer tier condition, and Condition and Group buttons

steps: Set the targets. See [Set targets per priority](#sla-targets).
Add escalation levels if you need them. See [Add escalation levels](#sla-escalations).
Select **Save policy**.
sections.result: A message says "SLA policy saved". The policy joins the list as version 1.

blocks.p: The contract option reads **Use the contract's support hours when the ticket is covered by a contract**.
Choose **All (AND)** when every condition must match, or **Any (OR)** when one is enough. **Group** adds a nested group. Groups can go three levels deep.
Conditions can use the ticket, customer, contact and contract. Examples are tier, contract, priority, department, product, category and channel.

blocks.tip: A policy without conditions matches every ticket. Put it near the bottom of the evaluation order.

sections.title: Set targets per priority
steps: In the policy editor, go to **Targets per priority**.
Tick each priority that the policy covers: **Critical**, **High**, **Medium** or **Low**.
For each priority, enter the **First response**, **Next response** and **Resolution** times.
Choose the unit for each time: **min**, **h** or **d**.
Tick **Business** to count only the calendar's working time.
In **Warn at**, enter the warning point as a percentage of the target.
Select **Save policy**.
sections.result: The policy uses the new targets. Saving creates a new version and recalculates open tickets.

blocks.caption: Targets for four priorities with 24x7 counting.
blocks.alt: Targets per priority table with first response, next response and resolution times, business hours boxes and warning percentages

blocks.note: Targets can range from 1 minute to 365 days. **Warn at** takes 1–99%. The default is 75%.

sections.title: Add escalation levels
sections.intro: An escalation level acts when a milestone gets close to a breach, or after it. A policy can have up to 10 levels.
steps: In the policy editor, go to **Escalation levels** and select **Add level**.
Choose the **Milestone** and enter the **Level** number.
In **When**, choose **At % of target** or **Minutes from breach**.
Enter the **Percent** or the **Minutes**.
Choose the **Action**.
For a reassign action, choose **Reassign to agent** or **…or to team**.
For a notify action, tick **Notify assignee** and **Notify supervisors**, and add people under **Also notify**.
Select **Save policy**.
sections.result: The level fires when the milestone reaches the point you set.

blocks.caption: Three escalation levels: a breach notice, a warning an hour before, and a reassignment.
blocks.alt: Escalation levels card with milestone, level, when, minutes, action, reassign and notify fields for three levels

rows: Fires at a share of the target. `80` fires before the breach. `150` fires after it.
Fires a number of minutes around the breach. A negative number fires before it.
Moves the ticket to the agent or team you choose.
Sends a notification and moves the ticket.

blocks.p: To delete a level, select **Remove** on it. Without levels, breaches show on the risk boards only.

sections.title: Simulate a policy against a ticket
sections.intro: Check which policy a ticket would get, and its due times, before you save. The simulation uses the unsaved form.
steps: Open the policy and make your changes.
In **Simulate against a ticket**, enter a **Ticket number**.
Select **Simulate**.
sections.result: The card shows the selected policy and the reason. It lists every policy as **Selected**, **Matches** or **Skipped**, and the new due times.

blocks.caption: The simulation for ticket #1010 selects Platinum 24x7.
blocks.alt: Simulate card with ticket 1010, the selected policy, the evaluated policies and a table of milestones with targets and due times

blocks.p: **Differs from the current SLA** means saving would change the ticket's policy. The **Current** column shows the due time the ticket has now.

sections.title: Deactivate or delete a policy
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.sla`.
steps: Open the policy.
To switch it off, clear **Active**, then select **Save policy**.
To remove it, select **Delete**, then **Delete** in the confirmation.
sections.result: An inactive policy stays in the list but no longer matches tickets. A deleted policy disappears.

blocks.note: You cannot delete the default policy. You cannot delete a policy that tickets have used, or that a contract names. Deactivate those instead.

sections.title: Business calendars
intro: A business calendar sets the working hours and holidays in a time zone. SLA clocks with **Business** ticked count only this time.
Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays**. Departments, policies and contracts can each use a calendar.

blocks.caption: The **Calendars & holidays** tab with the default business hours calendar open.
blocks.alt: Calendars tab with numbered New calendar button, calendar list, edit form, weekly hours, Save calendar, holidays and business time preview

callouts: **New calendar**.
The calendars, with hours per week, time zone and holidays. **Default** and **Used** badges show how each is used.
The name, time zone, description, **Open 24x7** and **Default calendar** settings.
The weekly hours, with presets such as **Mon–Fri 09–18**.
**Save calendar**. Below it, **Used by** lists what uses the calendar.
**Holidays** for this calendar.
**Business time preview**.

sections.title: Create or edit a business calendar
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.sla` or `admin.organisation`.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays**.
Select **New calendar**, or select a calendar in the list.
Enter the **Name** and choose the **Time zone**.
Turn on **Open 24x7 (no business hours)**, or set the weekly hours.
For weekly hours, select a preset, then adjust each day. Select **Split** to add a break.
Turn on **Default calendar** if this calendar should be the default.
Select **Save calendar**.
sections.result: A message says "Calendar saved". The list shows the new hours per week.

blocks.p: To delete a calendar, select it and select **Delete**. You cannot delete the default calendar, or a calendar that departments, policies or contracts use.

sections.title: Add a holiday
sections.intro: Holidays are whole local days that SLA business time skips.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.sla` or `admin.organisation`.
The calendar is saved.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays** and select the calendar.
In **Holidays**, enter the **Date** and the **Name**.
Tick **Every year** for a holiday on the same date each year.
Select **Add**.
sections.result: The holiday appears in the table. **Repeats** shows **Every year** or **Once**.

blocks.caption: The **Holidays** card with five holidays.
blocks.alt: Holidays card with Import CSV, the add form and a table of dates, names and repeats

blocks.p: To remove a holiday, select the remove button on its row.

sections.title: Import holidays from a CSV file
sections.intro: Load a year of holidays at once from a spreadsheet.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.sla` or `admin.organisation`.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays** and select the calendar.

steps.text: In **Holidays**, select **Import CSV**.
steps.caption: The **Import holidays** dialog with three sample lines.
steps.alt: Import holidays dialog with a CSV text box, Choose File button and Replace all existing holidays option

steps: Paste the lines into **CSV**. Or use the file button below the box to load a CSV file.
Turn on **Replace all existing holidays** only if the file is the full new list.
Select **Import**.
Read the result, then select **Done**.
sections.result: A message says how many holidays were added, updated and skipped. Up to 50 line errors are listed.

blocks.warning: **Replace all existing holidays** deletes the current holidays, even if every imported line fails.

rows: Blank lines, lines starting with `#`, and a first line starting with `date`.

sections.title: Check business time with the preview
sections.intro: See how much business time lies between two moments, and when a target would fall due. Nothing is saved.
steps: Open **SLA** > **Calendars & holidays** and select the calendar.
In **Business time preview**, enter **From** and **To**.
Optionally, enter **Add business minutes**, such as the target of a milestone.
Select **Calculate**.
sections.result: The card shows the business time against the total time, the holidays in range, and each working interval. With minutes added, it shows when the target falls due.

blocks.caption: The preview counts 20 hours of business time across four working days.
blocks.alt: Business time preview with from and to dates, 120 business minutes and the result with working intervals

sections.title: Live breaches
intro: Open **SLA** > **Live breaches** to see every running milestone that is at risk or breached. The soonest due come first.
Each ticket can appear more than once, once for each milestone.

blocks.caption: The **Live breaches** tab with 23 open breaches.
blocks.alt: Live breaches tab with numbered Refresh button, KPI tiles, state, milestone and department filters, and table header

callouts: **Refresh** reloads the list.
Tiles for **At risk**, **Breached (open)**, **Breached today**, **Due in the next hour** and **Paused**. Select **At risk** or **Breached (open)** to filter the list.
The state filter: **At risk and breached**, **At risk** or **Breached**.
The milestone filter.
The department filter.
Columns: ticket, milestone with priority and escalation level, due time, elapsed time against the target, owner, department and policy.

blocks.p: **L1** and **L2** show the escalation level a milestone reached. The **Elapsed** bar turns amber at 75% and red at 100% of the target.

blocks.tip: Select a ticket number to open the ticket. Select **Load more** at the bottom for older items.

chapters.title: Administration, roles and permissions
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It starts with the **Administration** home, where every setting area begins.
It then explains roles. You learn what each built-in role may do and which records it sees. You also learn how to make your own roles safely.

sections.title: The Administration home
intro: Open **Administration** in the left rail. The page shows one card for each area you can manage, in seven groups.
A card appears when your role holds any of its permissions. Settings you change apply to the next request. Open desks refresh by themselves.

blocks.caption: The **Administration** home with the Organisation and Ticketing groups.
blocks.alt: Administration home with numbered search box, group heading and the Roles and permissions card

callouts: **Find a setting** filters the cards as you type. Press [[Enter]] to open the first match.
A group heading, such as **Organisation**.
A card. Select it to open the area.

sections.title: Administration cards
sections.intro: Some cards open screens outside **Administration**, because supervisors use the same screens. Reading is often allowed more widely than changing.

blocks.note: Hiding a card never replaces a permission check. Each screen checks the permission again when it opens.

sections.title: Built-in roles
sections.intro: Every new workspace gets six system roles. They are read-only. You can clone them to make your own versions.

rows: Agent work plus transfer, bulk changes, delete, approvals, monitoring, costs, team analytics, knowledge review and AI approvals.
Day-to-day ticket work, customers, knowledge drafts, AI help and engineering links.
View tickets and add internal notes.
Knowledge base writing, review, publishing and settings.

blocks.p: The [permission reference](#permission-reference) shows exactly which permissions each role holds.

sections.title: The Roles & permissions list
sections.intro: Open **Administration** > **Roles & permissions**. You need `admin.roles`.

blocks.caption: The **Roles & permissions** list with six system roles and two custom roles.
blocks.alt: Roles list with numbered New role button, filter box, role name and badges, scope and counts, and actions menu

callouts: **New role** creates a custom role.
**Filter roles** finds a role by name or description.
The role name with badges: **System** or **Custom**, **Administrator** for roles that can manage roles, and **Light agent**.
The ticket scope, the number of permissions and the number of members.
The actions menu: **View** or **Edit**, **Clone** and, for custom roles, **Delete**.

blocks.caption: The actions menu of the custom Account Manager role.
blocks.alt: Roles list with the actions menu open showing Edit, Clone and Delete

blocks.note: Custom roles need a plan that includes them, such as Trial, Professional or Enterprise. On other plans, **New role** and **Clone** are turned off.

sections.title: Data scope
intro: Each role has a ticket scope and a customer scope. They decide which records the role's members can see at all.
A user with several roles gets the broadest scope of them. Records outside the scope are invisible. They behave as if they did not exist.

rows: **Own tickets — assigned to or raised by the agent**
Only customers they manage as account manager.

blocks.caption: The **Data scope** card of the Account Manager role.
blocks.alt: Data scope card with ticket and customer scope options and the Light agent role switch

blocks.note: You cannot give a role a broader scope than your own. Those options are turned off.

sections.title: Open a system role
sections.intro: Select a system role to see its settings. Everything is read-only.

blocks.caption: The Administrator system role, which is read-only.
blocks.alt: Administrator role page with numbered Clone to customise button, read-only notice and General card

callouts: **Clone to customise** makes an editable copy.
The notice **System role — read-only.**
The **General** card with the name and description.

sections.title: Clone a role
sections.intro: Cloning is the quickest way to make a role that is close to an existing one.
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.roles`.
Your plan includes custom roles.
steps: Open **Administration** > **Roles & permissions**.
Open the actions menu of the role and select **Clone**. On a system role page, you can also select **Clone to customise**.

steps.text: In **Name of the new role**, enter a unique name.
steps.caption: The clone panel suggests a name ending in (copy).
steps.alt: Clone Account Manager panel with the Name of the new role field and Clone role button

steps: Select **Clone role**.
sections.result: A message says "Role cloned". The new role opens with the same permissions, data scope and light-agent setting.

sections.title: Create a custom role
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.roles`.
Your plan includes custom roles.
steps: Open **Administration** > **Roles & permissions** and select **New role**.

steps.text: In **General**, enter a **Name** and a **Description**.
steps.caption: The **General** card of a new role.
steps.alt: General card with the name Billing desk and a description

steps: In **Data scope**, choose the **Tickets** and **Customers** scopes.
Turn on **Light agent role** only for collaborators who must never reply or own tickets.

steps.text: Under **Permissions**, tick the permissions the role needs.
steps.caption: The permission matrix filtered by the word merge.
steps.alt: Permissions card with numbered filter box, group check box, permission code and Sensitive badge

steps.text: Select **Create role**.
steps.caption: The save bar shows **Unsaved changes** until you save.
steps.alt: Save bar with Unsaved changes, Discard and Create role

sections.result: A message says "Role created". The **Members** card appears, so you can add people to the role.

blocks.p: The name must be unique and 2–100 characters long. **Discard** throws away your changes.
In the matrix, each permission shows a description and its code. A group check box ticks or clears a whole group. **Sensitive** marks high-impact permissions.

blocks.tip: Type in **Filter permissions** to find a permission by its description or code.

blocks.note: A lock next to a permission means you do not hold it, so you cannot grant it.

sections.title: Add or remove role members
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.roles`.
The role is a custom role.
steps: Open the role.

steps.text: In **Members**, choose a user in **Add a user to this role…**.
steps.caption: The **Members** card with one member.
steps.alt: Members card with numbered user picker and Remove button

steps: Select **Add**.
To take someone out, select **Remove** on their row.
sections.result: A message says "Member added" or "Member removed". The change applies to the member's open sessions at once.

blocks.p: Each member row lists the other roles the person holds. You can also change roles from the agent page. See [Change an agent's roles and departments](#edit-agent-access).

sections.title: Light agents
sections.intro: A light agent is a collaborator who helps on tickets without talking to customers. Engineers and managers are typical light agents.

list: A user is a light agent when their agent record says so. Any light-agent role also makes them one.
Light agents can never reply to customers, own tickets, transfer, bulk-edit or delete. This holds whatever their permissions say.
Light agents count against a separate plan limit. By default it equals the plan's agent limit.
The limit is checked when you invite or reactivate a light agent.

sections.title: The escalation guard
sections.intro: You can never give away more than you have. SupportDesk blocks a change when:

list: you create, change or delete a role with a permission you do not hold;
you create, change or delete a role whose data scope is broader than yours;
you add a user to such a role, or remove a user from it;
you choose such a role as the single sign-on default role;
you create a key or client app for an integration with rights you do not have.

blocks.p: The message names the permissions you lack. Ask an administrator with those permissions to make the change.

blocks.note: This applies to a role's current contents too. You cannot edit a role that already holds permissions you lack.

sections.title: The last-administrator rule
sections.intro: The workspace must always keep at least one administrator. That is an active user with a role that holds `admin.roles`.

blocks.p: SupportDesk refuses any change that would remove the last one:

list: removing `admin.roles` from a role;
deleting an administrative role;
changing a user's roles;
deactivating or deleting the user.

blocks.tip: Make someone else an administrator first. Then make the change.

sections.title: Delete a custom role
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.roles`.
The role is a custom role.
The role is not the single sign-on default role.
steps: Open **Administration** > **Roles & permissions**.
Open the actions menu of the role and select **Delete**.

steps.text: If people hold the role, choose a role in **Move members to**.
steps.caption: The delete panel asks where the role's members move.
steps.alt: Delete Account Manager panel with the Move members to list and Delete role button

steps: Select **Delete role**. If nobody holds the role, select **Delete** in the confirmation.
sections.result: A message says "Role deleted". Its members now hold the role you chose.

blocks.warning: You cannot undo a delete. Clone the role first if you might need it again.

blocks.note: System roles cannot be deleted or changed.

sections.title: Permission reference
intro: This table lists every permission, grouped as in the permission matrix. A tick means the built-in role holds it.
**Sensitive** marks high-impact permissions. Light agents lose reply, assign, transfer, delete and bulk rights whatever their roles say.

rows: View tickets within the role's data scope
See support costs and billable amounts. **Sensitive**
Create and edit customers, contacts and locations
Manage products, versions, installations and assets
Manage agent availability, shifts, leave and delegation
Create and link engineering work items
View the engineering board, work items and releases
Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases
View team, department and organisation analytics
Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions. **Sensitive**
Manage departments, teams, brands and calendars
Manage ticket fields, statuses, categories and layouts
Manage email accounts and messaging channels. **Sensitive**
Manage knowledge base settings and portals
Manage AI models, prompts, budgets and agents. **Sensitive**
Manage integrations, API keys, OAuth clients and webhooks. **Sensitive**
Manage password, session, MFA and SSO policies. **Sensitive**
View audit logs and verify integrity
Retention, legal holds, data export and erasure. **Sensitive**
Export, import, publish and roll back configuration. **Sensitive**

blocks.p: There are 58 permissions in all. Column headings: Light means Light Agent, and Knowledge means Knowledge Manager.

chapters.title: Ticket configuration
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It explains how to shape the tickets everyone works with.
You set the statuses and their transitions, the categories and issue types, and the extra fields. You also design ticket forms and set numbering and lifecycle rules.

sections.title: Ticket configuration at a glance
intro: Open **Administration** > **Ticket configuration**. You need `admin.ticket_config`.
Changes apply to the next request. Open desks refresh by themselves.

rows: The statuses agents move tickets through, and which moves are allowed.
Two levels of categories, and the nature of each request.
Extra fields for tickets, contacts and customers.
How fields are arranged on the agent and portal ticket forms.
The ticket number prefix, reopen and auto-close rules, merge and split, surveys, and priority labels.

blocks.tip: The **Fields & form layouts** card on the **Administration** home opens **Custom fields** directly.

sections.title: Statuses
intro: Every status belongs to one fixed category: **Open**, **Assigned**, **In progress**, **Waiting**, **Resolved** or **Closed**. Reports, SLAs and the portal rely on the categories.
Built-in statuses have a lock badge. You can rename them, but you cannot delete them.

blocks.caption: The **Statuses** section with eight statuses in display order.
blocks.alt: Statuses list with numbered section tabs, New status button, drag handle, status badges, ticket count, order arrows and Edit button

callouts: The ticket configuration sections.
**New status**.
The drag handle. Drag a row to change the display order.
The status name with badges for category, **Default**, **Pauses SLA**, **Inactive** and **Built-in**. The line below shows the allowed next statuses, the customer label and substatuses.
How many tickets have the status now.
The arrows also move the status up or down.
**Edit** opens the status.

blocks.note: A new order is saved as soon as you drag a row or select an arrow.

sections.title: Create or edit a status
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Statuses**.

steps.text: Select **New status**, or **Edit** on a status.
steps.caption: The **Edit status** panel for Waiting on Customer.
steps.alt: Edit status panel with name, category, colour, customer label, switches, allowed next statuses and substatuses

steps: Enter the **Name**, and choose the **Category** and **Colour**.
Enter a **Label shown to customers** to keep the internal name private in the portal.
Turn on **Default status of its category** or **Pause SLA resolution clocks while in this status** if needed.
Under **Allowed next statuses**, leave **Any status (no restriction)** on, or turn it off and tick the allowed statuses.
In **Substatuses**, type a finer reason and press [[Enter]]. Repeat for each one.
Select **Create status** or **Save status**.
sections.result: A message says "Status created" or "Status saved". The list shows the new settings.

rows: Fixed for built-in statuses and for statuses in use.
A colour code such as `#d97706`, or pick one.
**Pause SLA resolution clocks while in this status**
Stops the next response and resolution clocks.
With restrictions on, tick at least one status.
Built-in statuses cannot be turned off.

blocks.note: Every category must keep at least one active status. Tickets that follow a blueprint ignore the allowed next statuses. The blueprint decides.

sections.title: Delete a status
prerequisites: The status is not built-in.
No tickets have the status.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Statuses** and select **Edit** on the status.
Select **Delete**.
In the confirmation, select **Delete**.
sections.result: A message says "Status deleted". Transitions that pointed to it are removed too.

blocks.tip: If tickets still use the status, turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Categories and issue types
intro: Categories classify what a ticket is about. They have two levels: a category and its subcategories. A category can be limited to one department.
Issue types describe the nature of the request, such as a question, an incident or a change request.

blocks.caption: The **Categories & issue types** section.
blocks.alt: Categories and issue types with numbered Category button, a category row, Sub button, a subcategory, Issue type button and issue type list

callouts: **Category** adds a top-level category.
A category with its department badge and ticket count.
**Sub** adds a subcategory to that category.
A subcategory. **Agents only** marks items hidden from the portal.
**Issue type** adds an issue type.
The issue types with their ticket counts.

blocks.p: Use the arrows on a row to change the order. The new order is saved at once.
Priorities and severities have fixed values. You can change only their labels and colours. See [Change numbering and lifecycle settings](#ticket-settings-task).

sections.title: Add or edit a category
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Categories & issue types**.

steps.text: Select **Category**, or **Sub** on a category. To edit, select the category's name.
steps.caption: The **New category** panel.
steps.alt: New category panel with name, parent category, department and two switches

steps: Enter the **Name**.
Choose a **Parent category**, or keep **None — top-level category**.
Choose a **Department**, or keep **All departments**.
Turn **Customers can choose it in the portal** on or off.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Category saved".

blocks.note: To delete a category, open it and select **Delete**. Delete or move its subcategories first. A category that tickets use cannot be deleted. Turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Add or edit an issue type
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Categories & issue types**.
Select **Issue type**, or select the name of an issue type.
Enter the **Name** and a **Description**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: A message says "Issue type saved".

blocks.note: An issue type that tickets use cannot be deleted. Turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Custom fields
sections.intro: Custom fields capture information your process needs, such as an ERP module or a vendor reference. They exist for tickets, contacts and customers.

blocks.caption: The **Custom fields** section with six ticket fields.
blocks.alt: Custom fields list with numbered record type tabs, New field button, field name and badges, order arrows and Edit button

callouts: Tabs for **Ticket fields**, **Contact fields** and **Customer fields**.
**New field**.
The field label, key and type, with badges such as **Required** and **Portal: editable**.
The arrows change the order of the fields.
**Edit** opens the field.

blocks.p: The line under each field shows its departments, the layouts that use it and its help text.

sections.title: Create a custom field
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Custom fields**.

steps.text: Select **New field**.
steps.caption: A new picklist field with two options.
steps.alt: New field panel with record type, type, label, key, options, default value, help text, visibility and required settings

steps: Choose the **Record type** and the **Type**.
Enter the **Label**. The **Key** fills in by itself, and you can change it before you save.
For a picklist, add the **Options**. For a record lookup, choose what it **Looks up**.
Optionally, enter a **Default value**, **Help text** and validation limits.
Under **Visibility** and **Required**, turn on the settings you need.
For a ticket field, optionally choose **Departments**.
Select **Create field**.
sections.result: A message says "Field created". Agents see the field on the matching records.

blocks.warning: You cannot change the **Key** or the **Type** after you create the field.

rows: 2–63 lower-case letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter. Unique for the record type.
1–500 options, each with a value and a label.
For text fields only. The length can be 1–10000.
Shows the field in the customer portal.
**Customers can fill it in when raising a ticket**
Needs the field to be visible in the portal.
**Always required when the record is created or edited**
Agents must fill it in every time.
Ticket fields only. The field must be filled in before a ticket may enter those statuses.
Ticket fields only. Leave empty to use the field everywhere.

blocks.note: Agents always see every active field.

rows: A longer text over several lines.
One value from a list of options.
Several values from a list of options.
A link to a web page.
A link to a product, customer, contact, user or installation.

sections.title: Delete a custom field
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Custom fields** and select **Edit** on the field.
Select **Delete**.
In the confirmation, type the field's key.
Select **Delete field**.
sections.result: A message says "Field deleted". The field disappears from every form layout.

blocks.note: Values already stored on records are kept, but they are no longer shown. To hide a field for now, turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Form layouts
intro: A form layout arranges ticket fields in sections and columns. It is either an **Agent ticket form** or a **Portal (customer) form**.
Without a layout, forms show every field that applies, in the default order.

blocks.caption: The **Form layouts** section before any layout exists.
blocks.alt: Form layouts section with an explanation, the New layout button and an empty state with Design a form

list: The most specific active layout wins. A layout for the ticket's department, and its brand or channel, comes first.
Otherwise, the default layout of the form applies.
Only one active layout can cover the same form, department, brand and channel.

blocks.p: Portal forms take only fields customers may fill in. These are department, priority, category, product, installation and custom fields set as editable in the portal. Layouts are for tickets only.

sections.title: Design a form layout
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Form layouts** and select **New layout**.
Enter a **Name** and choose the **Form**.
Choose a **Department**, and a **Brand** for portal forms or a **Channel** for agent forms.
Turn on **Default agent form** or **Default portal form** if this is the default.
Select **Add section**. Give it a title and choose 1, 2 or 3 columns.
Drag fields from **Available fields** into a section, or select the plus button on a field.
Tick **Required** on fields that agents or customers must fill in.
Select **Preview** to check the form, then **Design** to go back.
Select **Create layout**.
sections.result: A message says "Layout created". The layout appears under **Agent forms** or **Portal forms**.

blocks.caption: The layout builder for a new agent form.
blocks.alt: Layout builder with numbered settings card, Design and Preview tabs, Available fields, a section header, a Required box, Add section and the save bar

callouts: The layout settings: name, form, department, channel or brand, **Default** and **Active**.
**Design** and **Preview**.
**Available fields**. **custom** marks custom fields. **Filter fields** finds one.
A section: title, number of columns, order arrows and the delete button.
**Required**. **Subject** and **Department** are always required.
**Add section**. A layout can have up to 20 sections.
The save bar with **Discard** and **Create layout** or **Save layout**.

blocks.caption: The **Preview** of the new agent form. Controls are inactive.
blocks.alt: Form preview with the Request and Classification sections

sections.title: Edit or delete a form layout
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Form layouts**.
To change a layout, select **Edit** on it, make your changes, then select **Save layout**.
To remove a layout, select its delete button, then **Delete** in the confirmation.
sections.result: A saved layout applies to the next form that opens. After a delete, forms fall back to the next matching layout.

sections.title: Numbering and lifecycle
sections.intro: The **Numbering & lifecycle** section holds workspace-wide ticket rules on one page.

blocks.caption: The **Numbering & lifecycle** section.
blocks.alt: Numbering and lifecycle page with numbered cards for numbering, lifecycle, merge and split, surveys, priorities and severities, and the save bar

callouts: **Ticket numbering**: the prefix and a sample of the next number.
**Lifecycle**: reopening, automatic closure and resolution rules.
**Merge & split**: limits for merging duplicates and splitting messages.
**Satisfaction surveys**: the survey sent when a ticket is resolved.
**Priorities & severities**: labels and colours of the fixed values.
The save bar with **Discard** and **Save settings**.

rows: Shown before every ticket number, such as `#`, `SD-` or `WS/`.
Numbers have no gaps within your workspace.
A customer reply inside the window reopens the ticket. A later reply creates a follow-up ticket.
Resolved tickets close by themselves after this time. 0 means never.
How long an agent's edit lock lasts without activity.
**Customers may reopen resolved tickets (within the window)**
Lets customers reopen from the portal.
Agents must use the confirm option when they resolve.
Agents must pick a resolution code.
**Acknowledge new e-mail tickets automatically (where the mailbox allows it)**
Sends an automatic reply to new e-mail tickets.
The most tickets one merge can combine.
**Allow splitting messages into a new ticket**
Agents can move a message into a new ticket.
**Send a survey when a ticket is resolved**
How long the survey link works.

blocks.note: Resolution codes, root causes and close reasons have no screen yet. To change them, import them with **Configuration transfer**.

sections.title: Change numbering and lifecycle settings
prerequisites: Your role includes `admin.ticket_config`.
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Numbering & lifecycle**.
Change the **Prefix**, the day and minute limits, and the switches you need.
Under **Priorities & severities**, change a label or pick a new colour. The pill beside it shows the result.
Select **Save settings**.
sections.result: A message says "Ticket settings saved". The save bar shows the new version number.

blocks.warning: A new prefix changes how every ticket number is shown, including old tickets. Tell your team before you change it.

chapters.title: Channels
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It explains how to connect the ways customers reach you: mailboxes, WhatsApp, SMS, live chat, phone lines and social pages.
It also covers the chat widget for your website. Last, it shows the channel simulator, which tests a channel without real customers.

sections.title: How channels work
intro: A channel is one address where customers contact you. Examples are a support mailbox, a WhatsApp number or the chat widget on your website.
Each channel belongs to a brand. It sends its new tickets to a department, where routing picks a team and an agent.
Your plan sets how many channels you can have. To manage channels, you need the **Manage email accounts and messaging channels** permission.
blocks: To open the list, select **Administration** in the rail, then select **Channels**. Channels are grouped by type.

blocks.caption: The **Channels** page with the e-mail channels at the top.
blocks.alt: Channels page with numbered highlights on the Simulator and New channel buttons, the E-mail group, a status badge and the card buttons

callouts: **Simulator** opens the channel simulator for testing.
**New channel** adds a mailbox, number, widget or phone line.
Each group shows one channel type and how many channels it has.
The status of the channel, such as **Connected** or **Error**.
The card buttons. **Configure** opens the channel, **Test** checks the connection and **Poll** fetches new mail now. **Simulate** opens the simulator for this channel.

rows: The last test or check worked. Messages flow normally.
The last check failed. The card shows the error message in red.
The channel is switched off. It does not receive or send messages.
The channel is set up but has not been checked yet. Run a test.

blocks.note: Cards of inactive channels look faded. A channel with message history is never deleted, so you can always see its old conversations.

sections.title: Channel types and providers
intro: When you add a channel, you choose its type and its provider. The provider is the service that carries the messages.
You cannot change the type or the provider later. To switch providers, add a new channel and deactivate the old one.

rows: The incoming and outgoing mail server details, and a password or access token.
The outgoing mail server details. Use it for a mailbox that only sends.
Your Microsoft Entra ID tenant, an application (client) id and its client secret.
A Google client id, the client secret and a refresh token.
Nothing. It is for demos and testing only.
Meta sends each message to SupportDesk
The WhatsApp Business account details from Meta, an access token and the app secret.
Meta sends each message to SupportDesk
The page or Instagram account id, a page access token and the app secret.
Twilio sends each message to SupportDesk
The Twilio account SID and auth token.
Your SMS gateway sends each message to SupportDesk
The gateway's send address, its message format, a key and a shared secret.
Your phone system sends each call event to SupportDesk
A shared secret. Voice channels receive calls only.
Visitors chat in the widget on your website
Nothing. You paste a short code into your website.

blocks.tip: To try SupportDesk before you connect real accounts, add a **Simulator (demo/testing)** channel. It needs no credentials.

sections.title: Add a channel
sections.intro: Add a channel to receive tickets from a new mailbox, number, website or phone line.
prerequisites: You have the **Manage email accounts and messaging channels** permission.
You have the account details from the provider, such as the mail server names and the password.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Channels**.
Select **New channel**.

steps.text: In the **Channel** card, choose the **Type** and the **Provider**.
steps.note: The hint under **Provider** describes the provider you chose.

steps: Enter a **Name**, such as `Sales mailbox`. Only your team sees this name.

steps.text: Enter the address, such as the **Mailbox address** or the **WhatsApp number**.
steps.note: For a **Live chat** channel, leave **Widget key** empty. SupportDesk creates a key for you.

steps: Choose the **Brand** and the **Department** that receives the new tickets.

steps.text: Fill in the **Connection settings** and the **Credentials** cards for your provider.
steps.caption: A new mailbox with the **IMAP** provider. The connection settings and credentials follow the **Channel** card.
steps.alt: New channel form with connection settings, credentials, mailbox signature and the Create channel button

steps: For a mailbox, add a **Mailbox signature** if you want one.
Select **Create channel**.
sections.result: The app shows **Channel created** and opens the new channel. Select **Test connection** to check it. See [Test a channel and fetch mail now](#ch-test-and-poll).

sections.title: Channel fields
sections.intro: These fields are on the **Channel** card of every channel. The label of the address field changes with the type.

rows: **E-mail**, **WhatsApp**, **SMS**, **Live chat**, **Voice**, **Messenger** or **Instagram**. You cannot change it later.
The service that carries the messages. You cannot change it later.
A name your team recognises, such as `Billing mailbox`. Required.
E-mail only. The address customers write to, such as `support@example.com`.
The number in international format, starting with + and the country code.
Live chat only. Leave it empty to create a new key.
Messenger and Instagram only. The id of your Facebook page or Instagram professional account.
The sender name customers see. If you leave it empty, the brand name is used.
The brand the channel belongs to. **Default brand** uses your main brand.
Where new tickets from this channel go. **Brand default** uses the brand's setting.
Turn it off to stop the channel without deleting it.
E-mail only. Sends a confirmation e-mail when a new ticket arrives.
All types except live chat. Turn it off to accept messages only from known contacts.
E-mail only. Added below the agent's own signature on every reply from this mailbox.

sections.title: Mailbox connection settings
intro: An **IMAP** mailbox needs the details of your incoming and outgoing mail servers. Your e-mail provider or IT team can give you these values.
The **Microsoft 365** and **Gmail** providers need fewer fields. They ask for the ids your Microsoft or Google administrator created.

rows: The incoming mail server, such as `imap.example.com`, and its port. The usual port is `993`.
The outgoing mail server, such as `smtp.example.com`, and its port. The usual port is `587`.
The mailbox user name. If you leave it empty, the mailbox address is used.
**Password**, or **OAuth 2.0 (XOAUTH2 access token)** if your provider uses sign-in tokens.
The folder to read. The default is `INBOX`.
Turn it on to mark each e-mail as read after SupportDesk takes it.
How often SupportDesk checks for new mail, from 0 to 3600 seconds. The default is 30.
Used for replies on tickets that did not arrive by e-mail, such as portal tickets. Turn it on for one mailbox only.
Microsoft 365 only. Your Microsoft administrator gives you these values.
Gmail only. Leave **Gmail user id** as `me` unless told otherwise.

blocks: The **Credentials** card holds passwords, tokens and secrets. SupportDesk stores them encrypted and never shows them again.

list: A saved value shows as dots with the word **(saved)**.
To replace a value, type the new one.
To delete a value, select **Remove** next to it. To undo that before you save, select **Keep**.

blocks.warning: If your SupportDesk server administrator changes the server's encryption key, saved credentials stop working. Enter them again on each channel.

sections.title: WhatsApp, SMS, social and voice settings
sections.intro: These providers send messages to SupportDesk as they happen. Their settings link SupportDesk to your account at the provider.

rows: **Phone number id** and **WhatsApp Business account id** from WhatsApp Manager. A **Webhook verify token**, which is any secret phrase you also enter at Meta. A **Template outside the 24-hour window** and its **Template language**.
**Page / Instagram account id** and a **Webhook verify token**.
**Account SID**. Optionally a **Messaging service SID**, and a **Public webhook URL** if a proxy changes the address.

The gateway's **Send URL**, the sending method and the **Body format**. A **Body template** with placeholders such as `{{to}}` and `{{text}}`. The **Auth header name**, **Auth header value** and **Message id path in the response**.
**Create tickets for answered calls**. Missed calls and voicemails always create tickets.

blocks.note: WhatsApp lets you reply freely only within 24 hours of the customer's last message. After that, SupportDesk sends the approved template that you name here.

sections.title: Change a channel
sections.intro: Open a channel to change its settings, check its status or replace its credentials.
prerequisites: You have the **Manage email accounts and messaging channels** permission.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Channels**.
On the channel's card, select **Configure**. You can also select the channel's name.

steps.text: Change the fields you need.
steps.note: You cannot change the **Type** and **Provider** of a saved channel.

steps: Select **Save changes**.
sections.result: The app shows **Channel saved**. To leave without saving, select **Cancel**.

blocks.caption: A saved mailbox. The settings are on the left and the status panel is on the right.
blocks.alt: Channel page for the Support mailbox with numbered highlights on the Channel, Connection settings and Mailbox signature cards, the Save changes bar, the Status card and the Danger zone card

callouts: The **Channel** card: name, address, brand, department and the switches.
