blocks.caption: The **Single sign-on** tab before any provider is connected. The badge shows **SSO off**.
blocks.alt: Single sign-on tab with sign-in addresses, provider fields, Test connection and claims and provisioning settings

callouts: The **Redirect (callback) URI** and the **Sign-in start URL**. The copy buttons copy them.
The provider details: **Authority (issuer)**, **Client id**, **Client secret** and **Scopes**.
**Test connection** checks that SupportDesk can reach your identity provider.
**Claims & provisioning** matches people by e-mail and switches single sign-on on.
The save bar, with **Discard** and **Save SSO settings**.

blocks.warning: In this release, the desk sign-in page has no single sign-on button yet. Do not turn on **Require SSO** until your SupportDesk provider confirms that single sign-on works end to end.

sections.title: Register SupportDesk with your identity provider
sections.intro: Before you connect single sign-on, register SupportDesk as a web application in your identity provider.
prerequisites: You can add applications in your identity provider, or someone in your IT team can.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Security & sign-in** > **Single sign-on**.
Select the copy button next to **Redirect (callback) URI**.
In your identity provider, register SupportDesk as a web application.
Paste the copied address as the application's redirect address.
Note the issuer address, the client id and the client secret that the provider shows.
sections.result: You have the three details you need to connect single sign-on.

sections.title: Connect and switch on single sign-on
sections.intro: Enter your identity provider's details, test them, and then switch single sign-on on.
prerequisites: Your plan includes **Single sign-on**.
You have the issuer address, client id and client secret from [Register SupportDesk with your identity provider](#sec-sso-register).
steps: On the **Single sign-on** tab, enter the **Authority (issuer)**. It starts with `https://`.

steps.text: Enter the **Client id** and the **Client secret**.
steps.note: The secret is never shown again. Later, leave it empty to keep it, or select **Remove** to delete it at the next save.

steps: Check **Scopes**. The default is `openid profile email`, and it must include `openid`.
Select **Test connection**. Wait for the **Reachable** badge.
Under **Claims & provisioning**, check **E-mail claim** and **Display-name claim**.
To create agents at their first sign-in, turn on **Create agents automatically at their first SSO sign-in**. Then choose the **Role for new agents**.
Turn on **Single sign-on is on**.
Select **Save SSO settings**.
sections.result: The app shows **SSO settings saved**. The badge next to **Identity provider** shows **SSO on**.

sections.title: Single sign-on fields
sections.intro: This table explains each field on the **Single sign-on** tab.

rows: Your provider's sign-in address, such as `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0`. Required to switch single sign-on on.
The id your provider gave SupportDesk. Required to switch single sign-on on.
The secret your provider gave SupportDesk. The app stores it encrypted and never shows it again.
What SupportDesk asks the provider for. The default is `openid profile email`.
The provider field that holds the person's e-mail. The default is `email`. The app matches agents by e-mail address.
The provider field that holds the person's name. The default is `name`.
**Create agents automatically at their first SSO sign-in**
Creates an agent the first time an unknown person signs in through your provider.
The role that new agents get. You cannot choose a role with more rights than your own.
Lets agents sign in through your provider.
Agents can no longer sign in with a password. Administrators still can, as a fallback.

blocks.p: After a successful test, a panel appears under **Test connection**. It shows the provider's issuer, its sign-in addresses and its number of signing keys.

sections.title: Active sessions
intro: A session is one signed-in browser or phone. The **Active sessions** tab lists every agent session in your workspace, newest first.
Use it to check unusual sign-ins, or to sign someone out after a lost laptop or phone.

blocks.caption: The **Active sessions** tab for all users. Each row is one signed-in browser.
blocks.alt: Active sessions list with the user filter, the Refresh button and a Revoke button on each row

callouts: The user filter. **All users** shows everyone.
**Refresh** loads the list again.
The person, with badges. **This session** marks your own. **MFA** or **Password** shows how they signed in. The last badge shows web or mobile.
**Revoke** ends that one session.

blocks.p: Under each name, the row shows the network address and the browser. It also shows when the person signed in, when they were last active and when the session expires. Select **Load more** at the bottom to see older sessions.

sections.title: End one session
sections.intro: End a session when you do not recognise it, or when a device is lost.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Security & sign-in** > **Active sessions**.
Find the session. To narrow the list, choose the person in the user filter.
On the session's row, select **Revoke**.

steps.text: In the dialog, select **Revoke**.
steps.caption: The dialog asks you to confirm before it ends the session.
steps.alt: Revoke session confirmation dialog with Cancel and Revoke buttons
steps.note: If you revoke the row marked **This session**, the dialog says **Sign yourself out?** You are signed out at once.

sections.result: The app shows **Session revoked**. The person is signed out on that device at their next action.

sections.title: Sign a user out everywhere
sections.intro: End all of one person's sessions at once, for example when they leave the company or lose a device.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Security & sign-in** > **Active sessions**.
In the user filter, choose the person.

steps.text: Select **Sign this user out everywhere**.
steps.caption: The button appears after you choose one person in the filter.
steps.alt: Session toolbar with Priya Raman chosen and the Sign this user out everywhere button

steps: In the dialog, select **Sign out everywhere**.
sections.result: The app shows **Signed out everywhere** with the number of sessions it ended.

blocks.tip: To stop the person signing in again, also deactivate them on the **Agents** page.

sections.title: Keys and OAuth clients for other systems
intro: Other systems, such as Wings ERP or a company script, need their own sign-in to work with SupportDesk. You give them a key or an OAuth client.
A key is one secret that a script sends with every request. An OAuth client has an id and a secret. The other system swaps them for a pass that lasts one hour.

blocks.caption: The keys and OAuth clients page in the demo workspace, which has no keys yet.
blocks.alt: API keys and OAuth clients page with the two tabs and the New API key button

callouts: The two tabs, one for keys and one for OAuth clients. The number on a tab counts active credentials.
The button that creates a key. On the **OAuth clients** tab, it creates an OAuth client instead.

list: Each credential works only within the scopes you tick. A scope is one area, such as reading tickets.
Each row shows the name, the start of the key or the client id, the status and the scopes.
It also shows who created it, when it was last used and when it expires.
Each credential has its own limit of requests per minute.

blocks.note: To issue credentials, you need the **Manage integrations, API keys, OAuth clients and webhooks** permission. Your role must also see the whole organisation's data.

sections.title: Create a key
sections.intro: Create a key for a script or a simple integration.
prerequisites: You know which areas the integration needs, such as reading and creating tickets.
steps: Select **Administration** > **API keys & OAuth clients**.
On the **API keys** tab, select **New API key**.
Enter a **Name** that says where you use the key, such as `Wings ERP sync`.

steps.text: Under **Scopes**, tick only what the integration needs.
steps.caption: A new key for the ERP that can read and create tickets.
steps.alt: New API key panel with a name, two ticked ticket scopes, Act as user and Expires on
steps.note: A lock icon marks scopes you cannot grant, because they give rights you do not have.

steps: Optional: in **Act as user**, choose a person. The key then never does more than that person can.
In **Expires on**, choose a date up to three years ahead.

steps.text: Select **Create key**.
steps.warning: The app shows the key only once. Copy it before you leave the page.

steps: In the yellow box, select the copy button next to the key. Store the key somewhere safe.
Select the close button on the yellow box.
sections.result: The key appears in the list with the status **Active**.

sections.title: Create an OAuth client
sections.intro: Create an OAuth client for a system-to-system integration, such as your ERP or CRM.
steps: Select **Administration** > **API keys & OAuth clients**.
Select the **OAuth clients** tab, and then **New OAuth client**.
Enter a **Name**, and tick the **Scopes** the integration needs.
In **Expires on**, choose a date up to three years ahead.

steps.text: Select **Create client**.
steps.warning: The app shows the client secret only once. Copy it before you leave the page.

steps: In the yellow box, copy the **Client id**, the **Client secret** and the **Token endpoint**.
Give the three values to the team that sets up the other system.
sections.result: The client appears on the **OAuth clients** tab with the status **Active**.

sections.title: Replace an OAuth client secret
sections.intro: Replace a client secret when it may have leaked, or as part of regular security checks.
steps: Select **Administration** > **API keys & OAuth clients** > **OAuth clients**.
On the client's row, select **Rotate secret**.

steps.text: In the dialog, select **Rotate secret**.
steps.warning: The old secret stops working at once. The integration fails until it uses the new one.

steps: Copy the new **Client secret** from the yellow box.
Update the other system with the new secret.
sections.result: The yellow box shows **New secret for** and the client name. The client stays **Active**.

sections.title: Revoke a key or an OAuth client
sections.intro: Revoke a credential that is no longer used or that may have leaked.
steps: Select **Administration** > **API keys & OAuth clients**.
Find the key or client on its tab.
On its row, select **Revoke**.
In the dialog, select **Revoke key** or **Revoke client**.
sections.result: The status changes to **Revoked**. Integrations that use it stop working at once.

blocks.tip: You cannot replace a key's secret. To change a key, create a new one, update the integration, and then revoke the old key.

sections.title: Scopes and credential statuses
sections.intro: This table lists the scopes you can tick for a key or an OAuth client.

rows: Create and change tickets. Wings ERP needs it to create tickets from its screens.
Create and change customers and contacts.
Read the audit log. Settings have no read-only scope.
Everything, including rights added in later releases.
The **Expires on** date has passed. Create a new credential.
An administrator revoked it. It can never work again.

chapters.title: Integrations
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It explains how to connect SupportDesk to Wings ERP and Wings Books. It also covers engineering trackers, Microsoft Teams and Slack.
For each connection, it says what the connection does and how to set it up. It also shows how to check that it works, and what to do when it fails.

sections.title: Integrations at a glance
intro: You find the integrations in the **Integrations** group on the **Administration** page. You need the **Manage integrations, API keys, OAuth clients and webhooks** permission.
Passwords, tokens and webhook addresses you enter are stored encrypted. The app never shows them again. Leave such a field empty to keep the stored value.

rows: Brings customer masters and branches, installations, licences and AMC contracts from Wings ERP or Wings Books. ERP screens can also create tickets.
Sends escalated tickets to Azure DevOps, GitHub or the built-in engineering board. It brings fixes and releases back to the tickets.
Posts urgent tickets, SLA breaches, escalations, mentions and engineering news to team channels.

blocks.note: Outgoing webhooks and keys for other systems have their own pages. See the chapter on webhooks and [Keys and OAuth clients for other systems](#sec-api-about).

sections.title: The ERP integration page
intro: Open it with **Administration** > **Wings ERP & Books**. It is also the **ERP integration** tab under **Products & Assets**.
SupportDesk reads the ERP through the ERP's own service. It never reads the ERP's tables directly. Wings ERP and Wings Books each have their own settings.

blocks.caption: The **Wings ERP** tab of the demo workspace, which uses the simulator.
blocks.alt: ERP integration page with the system tabs, status bar, Connection and Synchronisation cards and the integration log

callouts: Choose **Wings ERP** or **Wings Books**.
The status and the last sync, with **Test connection** and **Sync now**.
The **Connection** card: name, mode and the **Integration enabled** switch.
The **Synchronisation** card: how often to sync and what to bring in.
**Save settings** saves both cards. Before the first connection, the button says **Connect** and the system name.
The **Integration log** and its filter.

sections.title: Connect Wings ERP or Wings Books
sections.intro: Connect the live ERP so that customers, installations and contracts stay up to date in SupportDesk.
prerequisites: You have the ERP service address and its sign-in details. Your Wings ERP administrator can give them to you.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Wings ERP & Books**.
Select the **Wings ERP** or the **Wings Books** tab.

steps.text: In **Mode**, choose **Wings API (HTTP)**.
steps.caption: The **Connection** card after you choose the live mode, with OAuth 2.0 sign-in.
steps.alt: Connection card with API base URL, Authentication, Timeout, Token URL, Client id, Client secret and Scope
steps.note: **Simulator (development / demo)** makes demo data from your own customers. Use it only for training and demos.

steps: Enter the **API base URL**, such as `https://erp.example.com`.
In **Authentication**, choose how SupportDesk signs in to the ERP. Then fill in the fields that appear.
Turn on **Integration enabled**.
In the **Synchronisation** card, choose what to bring in. See [Choose what to sync from the ERP](#int-erp-sync).
Select **Save settings**. On a first connection, the button says **Connect** and the system name.
sections.result: The app shows **ERP settings saved**. Next, [check the connection and sync now](#int-erp-test).

sections.title: ERP connection fields
sections.intro: This table explains each field in the **Connection** card.

rows: A name for this connection, such as `Wings ERP`.
**Simulator (development / demo)** for demo data, or **Wings API (HTTP)** for the live ERP.
Turns the connection and the automatic sync on or off.
The address of the ERP service. Required in the live mode.
How long to wait for the ERP to answer, from 5 to 300 seconds.
Optional. The default is the service address followed by `/oauth/token`.
The OAuth 2.0 secret. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
Optional. The rights to ask the ERP for, such as `erp.read erp.write`.
The key for key sign-in. Stored encrypted and never shown again.

sections.title: Choose what to sync from the ERP
sections.intro: Choose which records SupportDesk brings in from the ERP, and how often.
steps: In the **Synchronisation** card, enter **Sync every (minutes)**. You can enter 5 to 10080 minutes.
Turn on the records to bring in: **Customer masters & branches**, **Installations**, **Licences** and **AMC contracts**.
To add customers that exist only in the ERP, turn on **Create customers that exist only in the ERP**.
Select **Save settings**.
sections.result: The app shows **ERP settings saved**. The next sync uses your choices.

blocks.note: **Installations** and **Licences** appear only on the **Wings ERP** tab.

blocks.p: The ERP's record numbers match records in both systems. Fields your team owns in SupportDesk are never overwritten. These are the tier, the account manager, the SLA and the coverage.

sections.title: Check the ERP connection and sync now
sections.intro: Test the connection after you set it up, and whenever the status shows **Error**.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Wings ERP & Books**, and then the system's tab.
Select **Test connection**. A message shows whether the ERP answered, and how long it took.
Select **Sync now** to bring in changes at once.
Read the **Sync completed** card. For each kind of record, it shows how many were received, created, updated, unchanged and skipped.
sections.result: The status shows **Connected** and the time of the last sync.

blocks.note: **Sync now** works only while **Integration enabled** is on. If a sync fails, the card says **Sync failed** and shows the error.

sections.title: The integration log
sections.intro: The **Integration log** at the bottom of the page lists everything the connection did. Use it to find out why something failed.

list: The filter shows **All entries**, **Sync runs**, **Tickets from ERP** or **Record updates**.
Each row shows **When**, **Operation**, **Direction**, **Result**, **Duration** and **Details**.
**Result** shows **OK** or **Failed**, often with a status code.
Select a row to see the ERP's full answer. Select it again to close it.

blocks.tip: For ERP screens to create tickets, the ERP needs its own key or OAuth client with the `tickets:write` scope. See [Create a key](#sec-new-key).

sections.title: ERP connection statuses
sections.intro: The badge at the top of the ERP page shows the state of the connection.

rows: No settings are saved for this system yet.
Connect it. See [Connect Wings ERP or Wings Books](#int-erp-connect).
Turn on **Integration enabled**, and select **Save settings**.
The last test or sync worked.
The last test or sync failed. The error appears next to the badge.
Read the error, select **Test connection**, and check the address and sign-in details. Then check the integration log.

sections.title: The Engineering page
intro: Open it with **Administration** > **Engineering**. Here you connect the trackers where engineers fix bugs. Agents escalate tickets to them, and fixes flow back to the tickets.
Azure DevOps and GitHub need the **Engineering integration** plan feature. The built-in engineering board works on every plan.

blocks.caption: The **Engineering** page with the built-in board and the sync-back rules.
blocks.alt: Engineering administration page with the Add tracker menu, a tracker row and the sync-back rules

callouts: **Add tracker** connects Azure DevOps, GitHub or the built-in board.
A tracker, with its type, its status and the number of linked items.
**Edit** and the more menu. Azure DevOps and GitHub trackers also have **Test** and **Sync now**.
The sync-back rules decide what linked tickets get when engineering work changes.
The reply template, the escalation status and the default tracker.
**Save rules** saves the rules.

blocks.note: Agents can open the **Engineering** board in the left rail only after you enable the built-in board.

sections.title: Enable the built-in engineering board
sections.intro: Use the built-in board when your engineers do not use Azure DevOps or GitHub. Work items and releases then stay inside SupportDesk.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.
Select **Add tracker** > **Built-in engineering board**. On an empty page, select **Enable the built-in board**.
Enter a **Name** that agents see when they escalate.
Make sure **Active** is on.
Select **Create tracker**.
sections.result: The app shows **Tracker saved**. The board appears in the list as **Built-in board**.

blocks.note: A workspace has one built-in board. When it exists, the menu item is greyed out.

sections.title: Connect Azure DevOps
sections.intro: Connect Azure DevOps Services, or Azure DevOps Server (TFS) in your own network.
prerequisites: A personal access token with **Work Items (Read & write)** and **Project and Team (Read)**.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.

steps.text: Select **Add tracker** > **Azure DevOps Services / Server (TFS)**.
steps.caption: The **Add tracker** menu. The built-in board is greyed out because it already exists.
steps.alt: Add tracker menu with Azure DevOps, GitHub and Built-in engineering board

steps: Enter a **Name** that agents see when they escalate.
Enter the **Organization / collection URL** and the **Project**.
In **Authentication**, choose **Personal access token** or **OAuth access token**. Paste the token.

steps.text: Check the type, field and state mappings.
steps.caption: The **Connect Azure DevOps** panel with the default mappings.
steps.alt: Connect Azure DevOps panel with connection, type mapping, field mapping, state mapping and polling fields
steps.note: The defaults suit a standard Azure DevOps project. See [Tracker fields](#int-eng-fields).

steps: Set **Poll every (minutes)**.
Select **Create tracker**.
Copy the webhook secret from the yellow box. The app shows it only once.
sections.result: The tracker appears in the list with its **Webhook URL**. Next, [set up the tracker webhook](#int-eng-webhook).

sections.title: Connect GitHub
sections.intro: Connect a GitHub repository, on GitHub.com or on GitHub Enterprise Server.
prerequisites: A fine-grained token with **Issues** (read and write) and **Metadata** and **Contents** (read). A GitHub App installation also works.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.
Select **Add tracker** > **GitHub**.
Enter a **Name** that agents see when they escalate.
In **API URL**, keep `https://api.github.com`. For your own GitHub Enterprise, enter its address.
Enter the **Owner** and the **Repository**.
In **Authentication**, choose **Personal / fine-grained token** and paste the **Token**. For an app, choose **GitHub App installation** and fill in its fields.
Check the type, label and state mappings, and set **Poll every (minutes)**.
Select **Create tracker**.
Copy the webhook secret from the yellow box. The app shows it only once.
sections.result: The tracker appears in the list with its **Webhook URL**. Next, [set up the tracker webhook](#int-eng-webhook).

blocks.tip: When you edit a saved tracker, **Load repositories** or **Load projects** lists what the token can see. Pick one in the field above the button.

sections.title: Tracker fields
sections.intro: This table explains the fields in the tracker panel. Azure DevOps and GitHub show slightly different fields.

rows: The name agents see when they escalate a ticket.
Azure DevOps only. Where new work items go.
GitHub only. Where new issues go.
GitHub App sign-in only. The key is stored encrypted.
The work item type (Azure DevOps) or label (GitHub) for each kind of escalation.
**Repro steps field** and the other field boxes
Azure DevOps only. Which tracker fields receive the steps, severity, priority, fix version and customer impact.
GitHub only. Labels such as `severity:high` carry the severity and priority.
Tags or labels added to every new item.
Tracker states that mean fixed. You can also enter `label:x` or `tag:x`.
States that mean the fix is released. A reported release of the fix version also counts.
How often SupportDesk asks the tracker for changes, from 5 to 1440. It is a fallback when webhooks are not set up.
Turns the tracker on or off.

blocks.p: On GitHub, the issue milestone is the fix version. A published release whose tag or name matches it marks the fix as released.

sections.title: Set up the tracker webhook
sections.intro: A webhook lets the tracker tell SupportDesk about changes at once. Without it, SupportDesk checks for changes on the poll schedule.
prerequisites: The webhook secret you copied when you created the tracker. If you lost it, see [Replace a webhook secret](#int-eng-rotate).
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.
On the tracker's row, select the copy button next to **Webhook URL**.
In GitHub, add a webhook to the repository with that address. Paste the secret as the webhook secret.
In Azure DevOps, add a service hook with that address. Send the secret as the password of the hook.
Back in SupportDesk, open the tracker's more menu and select **Deliveries & call log**.
On the **Webhook deliveries** tab, check that new deliveries show **Processed**.
sections.result: Changes in the tracker reach the linked tickets within moments.

blocks.note: A **No secret** badge next to the webhook address means the tracker has no secret yet. Replace the secret to create one.

sections.title: Test a tracker and sync now
sections.intro: Check an Azure DevOps or GitHub tracker after you set it up, or when it shows an error.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.
On the tracker's row, select **Test**. The app shows **Connection OK** or **Connection problem**.
Select **Sync now**. The app shows how many linked items it checked and updated.
To see details, open the more menu and select **Deliveries & call log**.
On the **API calls** tab, read the result of each call to the tracker.
sections.result: The status badge shows **Connected**, and the row shows when the tracker last synced.

blocks.note: **Sync now** works only while the tracker is **Active**.

sections.title: Replace a webhook secret
sections.intro: Replace the secret if it leaked, or if you lost it before you set up the webhook.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.
Open the tracker's more menu, and select **Rotate webhook secret**.

steps.text: In the dialog, select **Rotate**.
steps.warning: Deliveries signed with the old secret are refused until you update the tracker.

steps: Copy the new secret from the yellow box.
Update the webhook in GitHub or Azure DevOps with the new secret.
sections.result: New deliveries show **Processed** again.

sections.title: Delete a tracker
sections.intro: Delete a tracker that you no longer use.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.
Open the tracker's more menu, and select **Delete**.
In the dialog, select **Delete**.
sections.result: The app shows **Tracker deleted**. Its sync and delivery logs are removed too.

blocks.note: You cannot delete a tracker that still has linked items. **Delete** is greyed out for it. Turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Set the sync-back rules
sections.intro: Sync-back rules decide what happens to linked tickets when engineering work changes. They apply to every tracker.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Engineering**.
Under **Sync-back rules**, turn each rule on or off.
If customers hear about releases, choose a **Customer reply template**. **Built-in message** uses the standard text.
If the substatus rule is on, choose an **Escalation status**. SupportDesk uses it when a ticket's status has no **Engineering** substatus.
In **Default tracker**, choose the tracker that agents get first.
Select **Save rules**.
sections.result: The app shows **Sync-back rules saved**.

rows: **Add an internal note when a linked item is resolved**
Adds a note to the ticket when engineers fix the item.
**Add an internal note when the fix is released**
Adds a note when the fix ships.
Sends the ticket's agent a notification.
**Tell the customer when the fix is released (“fix released in version X”)**
Sends the customer a reply. It is off by default.
Marks the ticket as waiting for engineering.

blocks.note: A reply template can use placeholders such as `{{engineering.fixVersion}}`, `{{ticket.number}}` and `{{contact.name}}`.

sections.title: Teams and Slack channels
intro: Open **Administration** > **Teams & Slack** to post ticket events to team channels. Each post is a card with the ticket's facts and an **Open in SupportDesk** link.
Agents can also share a ticket to a channel from the internal note box on a ticket.

blocks.caption: The **Teams & Slack** page before any channel is added.
blocks.alt: Teams and Slack page with no channels and the Add channel button highlighted

blocks.p: After you add channels, each row shows the channel's name, its platform and the events it receives. It also shows when it last posted.

list: A red **Failing** badge and an error mean the last post did not arrive.
The switch on the row turns the channel on or off.
**Send test** posts a test card to the channel.
The more menu has **Edit**, **Post log** and **Delete**.

sections.title: Create an incoming webhook in Teams or Slack
sections.intro: SupportDesk posts to a channel through an incoming webhook. A webhook is a private address that accepts posts for one channel.
steps: In Microsoft Teams, open the channel and its **Workflows**.

steps.text: Add the workflow that posts to a channel from a webhook, and copy the address it creates.
steps.note: In Teams, the workflow is called **Post to a channel when a webhook request is received**.

steps: In Slack, create an app with **Incoming Webhooks** turned on.
Add a webhook for your channel, and copy its address. It starts with `https://hooks.slack.com/services/`.
sections.result: You have the address to paste into SupportDesk.

blocks.note: Treat the address like a password. Anyone who has it can post to your channel.

sections.title: Add a Teams or Slack channel
sections.intro: Add a channel and choose which ticket events it receives.
prerequisites: The channel's incoming webhook address. See [Create an incoming webhook in Teams or Slack](#int-collab-webhook).
steps: Select **Administration** > **Teams & Slack**.
Select **Add channel**.
Under **Platform**, choose **Microsoft Teams** or **Slack**.
Enter a **Name**, such as `#support-escalations`.
Paste the **Incoming webhook URL**.

steps.text: Under **Post these events**, tick the events you want.
steps.caption: A new Teams channel for urgent tickets and SLA breaches.
steps.alt: Add channel panel with platform, name, webhook address, events, minimum priority and departments

steps: If you ticked **New urgent ticket**, choose **Urgent means priority at least**.
Optional: tick **Departments** to limit the channel. With none ticked, it covers all departments.
Keep **Active** on, and select **Add channel**.
sections.result: The app shows **Channel added**. Next, select **Send test** on the new row.

sections.title: Events you can post
sections.intro: This table lists the events a Teams or Slack channel can receive.

rows: A ticket is created with at least the channel's minimum priority.
A first-response, next-response or resolution target is missed.
A ticket is escalated by an agent, by automation or by SLA escalation levels.
An agent is @mentioned in an internal note.
A ticket is escalated to, or linked with, an engineering work item.
A linked work item is resolved in the tracker.
The fix for a linked work item is released.

sections.title: Send a test and check the post log
sections.intro: Check that a channel receives posts. Do it after you add a channel, and whenever it shows **Failing**.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Teams & Slack**.
On the channel's row, select **Send test**.

steps.text: Read the message that appears.
steps.note: **Test message posted** means the card arrived. **Test failed** shows the reason.

steps: To see every attempt, open the more menu and select **Post log**.
In the **Posts** panel, read the status code, the time taken and any error for each post.
sections.result: The test card appears in the Teams or Slack channel.

sections.title: Pause, change or delete a Teams or Slack channel
sections.intro: Pause a channel for a while, change its events, or remove it.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Teams & Slack**.
To pause or restart posts, use the switch on the channel's row.
To change the channel, open the more menu and select **Edit**. Make your changes and select **Save**.
To remove the channel, open the more menu and select **Delete**. In the dialog, select **Delete**.
sections.result: The app shows **Channel saved** or **Channel deleted**.

blocks.note: You cannot change the platform of a saved channel. Leave **Incoming webhook URL** empty to keep the stored address.

chapters.title: Audit log and compliance
intro: This chapter is for administrators and the people who handle data protection. It explains the audit log, which records sensitive actions in a way nobody can quietly change.
It also covers the **Compliance** page. There you set how long to keep data, place legal holds, handle customers' data requests and decide on support access.

sections.title: What the audit log records
intro: The audit log records sensitive actions in your workspace. You need the **View audit logs and verify integrity** permission to open it.
Every change and its log entry are saved together, so no change goes unrecorded.

list: Sign-ins and two-step verification.
Changes to roles, permissions and settings.
Exports, deletions, merges and entitlement overrides.
Keys and OAuth clients, AI actions and subscription changes.

blocks.p: Every few seconds, SupportDesk seals new entries into a chain. Each sealed entry carries a fingerprint of the entry before it. If anyone changes or removes an entry, the chain breaks, and **Verify chain** finds it.
New entries show **sealing** until they are sealed. When a retention policy removes old entries, the check starts from a recorded starting point.

sections.title: The Audit log page
sections.intro: Open it with **Administration** > **Audit log**. The newest entries come first.

blocks.caption: The **Audit log** page. The newest entry still shows **sealing**.
blocks.alt: Audit log page with Export CSV, Verify chain, the filter form and the list of entries

callouts: **Export CSV** saves the filtered entries as a spreadsheet file.
**Verify chain** checks that no entry was changed or removed.
The filters. **Apply** filters the list and **Clear** resets it.
One entry. **#** shows its place in the chain, or **sealing** while it is new.

blocks.p: The columns are **When**, **Actor**, **Action**, **Entity**, **Summary**, **IP** and **#**. Select **Load more** at the bottom to see older entries.

sections.title: Find audit entries
sections.intro: Filter the log to answer a question, such as who changed a role last week.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Audit log**.
Fill in one or more filters. See the table below.
Select **Apply**.
To see more entries, select **Load more** at the bottom.
sections.result: The list shows only matching entries. If nothing matches, it says **No audit entries match**.

rows: One kind of action, such as `auth.login`.
The kind of record, such as **User** or **Tenant**.
The full identifier of one record. Copy it from another entry.
The first and last day to include.
The start of a network address, such as `10.0.`.

sections.title: Open an audit entry
sections.intro: Open an entry to see exactly what changed.
steps: In the audit log, select the entry.

steps.text: Read the facts and the **Changes** table.
steps.caption: The **Audit entry** panel for a sign-in, with what it recorded.
steps.alt: Audit entry panel with when, actor, action, entity, summary, client, sequence, hashes and the changes table

steps: Select the close button to return to the list.
sections.result: You see who did what, when, from where, and each field's value before and after.

rows: When it happened, who did it and what they did.
The record it affected, and a short description.
The network address and the browser or app used.
A reference shared by all entries from one action. Use it to find related entries.
The entry's place in the chain and its fingerprints.
Each field with its **Before** and **After** value.
Everything the entry stored, in full.

sections.title: Export the audit log
sections.intro: Export entries for an auditor or for your own records.
prerequisites: Your plan includes **Audit export**.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Audit log**.
Set the filters for the entries you need, and select **Apply**.
Select **Export CSV**.
sections.result: Your browser saves a file named `audit-` followed by the date. It opens in Excel or any spreadsheet app.

blocks.note: One export holds up to 50,000 entries. Cells that a spreadsheet could run as formulas are made safe. The export itself is recorded in the audit log.

sections.title: Verify the audit chain
sections.intro: Check that no audit entry was changed or removed. Do it before an audit, or when you suspect tampering.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Audit log**.
Select **Verify chain**.
Read the result at the top of the page.
sections.result: **Audit chain intact.** means the log is complete. The line below says how many entries were checked and how many still wait for sealing.

blocks.warning: If the result says **Audit chain broken!**, select **Open entry** to see the first bad entry. Tell your security team and your SupportDesk provider at once.

blocks.note: Each check is itself recorded in the audit log.

sections.title: The Compliance page
intro: Open it with **Administration** > **Compliance**. You need the **Retention, legal holds, data export and erasure** permission.
The page has four tabs: **Retention**, **Legal holds**, **Data requests** and **Support access**.

blocks.caption: The **Retention** tab with the demo workspace's three policies.
blocks.alt: Compliance page on the Retention tab with three policies and their actions

callouts: The four tabs of the **Compliance** page.
**New policy** creates a retention policy.
A policy: its name, its rule, its last run and whether it is **Active** or **Paused**.
**Dry run**, **Run now**, the edit button and the delete button.

sections.title: Retention data and actions
intro: A retention policy removes or hides data after a number of days. Each kind of data allows some actions and has a minimum age.
Records covered by an active legal hold are never archived, anonymised or deleted.

rows: Tickets closed more than the set number of days ago.
Raw e-mail, chat and social messages. The ticket conversation stays.
Old sealed audit entries. The chain stays checkable.
Records of AI calls and their results.

list: **Archive** hides closed tickets from queues.
**Anonymize** keeps the numbers for reports, but removes the text. A ticket's subject becomes `[redacted]`. Its description, resolution, survey comment, AI summary and custom fields are cleared.
**Delete** removes the records, their search entries and unused files for good.
A run on the audit log removes only the oldest sealed entries, up to 10,000 a run.

blocks.warning: Deleted records cannot be recovered.

sections.title: Create a retention policy
sections.intro: Create a policy to keep data only as long as you need it.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Compliance**. The **Retention** tab opens.
Select **New policy**.
Enter a **Name**, such as `Archive old closed tickets`.
In **Data**, choose the kind of data. The hint below explains it.
Choose the **Action**, and enter **After (days)**.
To run the policy on its own, keep **Run automatically every day** on.

steps.text: Read the blue box. It says how many records the policy would affect now.
steps.caption: A new policy that archives closed tickets after 730 days.
steps.alt: New retention policy panel with name, data, action, days, the automatic switch and the live count

steps: Select **Create policy**.
sections.result: The app shows **Policy created**. The policy appears in the list.

blocks.note: Active policies run every six hours, in batches.

sections.title: Check a policy with a dry run
sections.intro: A dry run counts what a policy would affect now. It changes nothing.
steps: On the **Retention** tab, find the policy.

steps.text: Select **Dry run**.
steps.caption: The result line under a policy after a dry run.
steps.alt: Retention policy list with a dry-run result line under the closed tickets policy

sections.result: A line under the policy shows how many records it would affect, and how many legal holds keep. It also shows the cut-off date.

sections.title: Run a retention policy now
sections.intro: Run a policy at once instead of waiting for the automatic run.
steps: On the **Retention** tab, select **Dry run** on the policy, and check the numbers.

steps.text: Select **Run now**.
steps.warning: A **Delete** policy removes records for good. Check the dry run first.

steps: In the dialog, select **Run now**.
sections.result: The app shows **Retention run complete** with the number of records affected and kept by legal holds.

blocks.note: One run handles up to 1,000 records. Run it again for more. Every run is recorded in the audit log.

sections.title: Change, pause or delete a retention policy
sections.intro: Change a policy's rule, stop it from running on its own, or remove it.
steps: On the **Retention** tab, select the edit button on the policy's row.
In **Edit retention policy**, make your changes.
To pause the policy, turn off **Run automatically every day**.
Select **Save**.
To remove a policy, select the delete button on its row. In the dialog, select **Delete**.
sections.result: The app shows **Policy saved**. A paused policy shows **Paused** in the **Active** column.

sections.title: Legal holds
intro: A legal hold preserves records during a dispute, an audit or an investigation. A hold covers the tickets that match all the criteria you set.
Held tickets keep their messages, attachments and AI records. Retention skips them, and nobody can delete them. A hold also blocks erasure of the contacts involved.

blocks.caption: The **Legal holds** tab with one active hold.
blocks.alt: Legal holds tab with the Show released holds switch, the Place legal hold button and one active hold

callouts: **Show released holds** adds released holds to the list.
**Place legal hold** creates a new hold.

blocks.p: Each hold shows its name, reason and who placed it. **Covers** lists its criteria. **Tickets** counts the tickets it covers now. **Status** is **Active** or **Released**.

blocks.note: You cannot change a hold. To change one, place a new hold, and then release the old one.

sections.title: Place a legal hold
sections.intro: Place a hold as soon as you learn that records may be needed as evidence.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Compliance** > **Legal holds**.
Select **Place legal hold**.
Enter a **Name** and the **Reason / matter**.
Set at least one criterion: **Customer**, **Contact**, **Ticket numbers** or the **Created from** and **Created until** dates.

steps.text: For **Ticket numbers**, press [[Enter]] after each number.
steps.caption: The **Place legal hold** panel with a name filled in.
steps.alt: Place legal hold panel with name, reason, customer, contact, ticket numbers and created dates

steps: Select **Place hold**.
sections.result: The app shows **Legal hold placed** with the number of tickets now preserved.

sections.title: Release a legal hold
sections.intro: Release a hold when the matter is closed.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Compliance** > **Legal holds**.
On the hold's row, select **Release**.
In the dialog, select **Release hold**.
sections.result: The app shows **Legal hold released**. The records follow the retention policies and erasure requests again.

blocks.tip: Turn on **Show released holds** to see past holds.

sections.title: Data-subject requests
intro: Customers can ask for a copy of their data, or ask you to erase it. Record such requests on the **Data requests** tab. Every step is recorded in the audit log.
A contact can have only one open request of each type.

blocks.caption: The **Data requests** tab before any request is recorded.
blocks.alt: Data requests tab with the Status filter and the New request button

callouts: The **Status** filter.
**New request** records an export or an erasure request.

rows: An erasure request waits for an administrator's decision.
SupportDesk is building the export or erasing the data. The list refreshes on its own.
The export is ready, or the erasure is done.
An administrator rejected the erasure. The reason shows under the status.
Something went wrong. The error shows under the status.

sections.title: Export a contact's data
sections.intro: Give a customer a copy of the data you hold about them.
prerequisites: You have checked the person's identity.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Compliance** > **Data requests**.
Select **New request**, and choose **Export**.
In **Contact**, search for and choose the person.

steps.text: In **Notes**, record how the request arrived and how you checked the person's identity.
steps.caption: A new export request with notes about the identity check.
steps.alt: New data-subject request panel with Export chosen, the contact search and notes

steps: Select **Start export**.
When the status changes to **Completed**, select **Get link**.
Select **Download export**, and send the file to the customer securely.
sections.result: Your browser saves a zip file with the contact's profile, identities, consents, tickets, messages and attachments.

blocks.warning: The link works once and expires after 24 hours. SupportDesk removes the export after the download.

sections.title: Request erasure of a contact's data
sections.intro: Record a customer's request to be forgotten. The erasure waits for approval.
prerequisites: You have checked the person's identity.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Compliance** > **Data requests**.
Select **New request**, and choose **Erasure**.
In **Contact**, choose the person.
In **Notes**, record how the request arrived and how you checked the identity.
Select **Request erasure**.
sections.result: The app shows **Erasure requested**. The request waits with the status **Awaiting approval**.

sections.title: Approve or reject an erasure
sections.intro: Decide on an erasure request after you check it.
prerequisites: Another administrator made the request. If someone else holds the compliance permission, you cannot approve your own request.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Compliance** > **Data requests**.
In **Status**, choose **Awaiting approval**.
To reject, select **Reject**. Enter a **Reason**, and select **Reject**.

steps.text: To approve, select **Approve erasure**.
steps.warning: **Approve erasure** asks for no confirmation. The erasure cannot be undone.

sections.result: The app shows **Erasure approved**. SupportDesk erases the contact in the background.

blocks.p: Erasure renames the contact to **Erased contact** and clears their personal details, identities, consents and portal access. Their messages become `[erased at the customer's request]`, and their uploads are deleted. Ticket statistics stay.

blocks.note: If a legal hold covers the contact, the row says **Blocked by a legal hold**. **Approve erasure** is then greyed out.

sections.title: Support access
intro: SupportDesk staff never sign in as your users. When they need to diagnose a problem, they ask for read-only access for a limited time.
During access, they see usage, configuration counts, failed jobs and recent audit entries. They never see tickets or customer data.

blocks.caption: The **Support access** tab with one pending request from the platform operator.
blocks.alt: Support access tab with a pending request and the Reject and Approve buttons highlighted

blocks.p: Each request shows who asked, when, for how many minutes and why. **Status** shows **Pending** until you decide. While access is active, the row shows when it ends.

sections.title: Approve, reject or revoke support access
sections.intro: Decide on a support access request, or end access early.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Compliance** > **Support access**.
Read the reason and the duration of the request.
To approve, select **Approve**. In the dialog, select **Approve**.

steps.text: To refuse, select **Reject**.
steps.note: **Reject** asks for no confirmation.

steps: To end active access early, select **Revoke**.
sections.result: The app shows **Access approved**, **Request rejected** or **Access revoked**.

blocks.note: Every step is recorded in your audit log and in the platform's audit log. While your workspace is suspended, you cannot approve access.

chapters.title: Configuration transfer
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It explains how to copy configuration from one workspace to another. For example, you can copy it from a test workspace to your live one.
It also covers snapshots. A snapshot records your whole configuration, so you can roll back after a bad change.

sections.title: The Configuration transfer page
sections.intro: Open it with **Administration** > **Configuration transfer**. You need the **Export, import, publish and roll back configuration** permission.

blocks.caption: The **Configuration transfer** page. The number after each section counts its items.
blocks.alt: Configuration transfer page with the Export and Import cards and the Snapshots table

callouts: The **Export** card. Tick sections and save them to a file.
The **Import** card. Choose a file from this or another workspace. Drafts waiting for review appear here too.
**Capture snapshot** records the current configuration.
The **Snapshots** table, with a download button and **Roll back** on each row.

blocks.p: Every import, publish and rollback is recorded in the audit log.

sections.title: What a configuration file contains
sections.intro: An export holds the settings that shape how your desk works. It holds no tickets, customers or other business data.

list: Business calendars, ticket statuses, issue types and pick lists, such as resolution codes and root causes.
Ticket categories, custom fields and form layouts.
SLA policies and shared reply templates.
Knowledge base categories and AI prompt templates.
Channel definitions, blueprints and automation rules.

blocks.p: Settings can point to departments, teams, users, roles, brands, products and skills. The file stores these by name. On import, SupportDesk looks for the same names in the target workspace. It never creates them.

blocks.note: Passwords and other secrets are never exported. Imported channels start inactive, so you must enter their sign-in details again.

sections.title: Export configuration
sections.intro: Save some or all of your configuration to a file.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Configuration transfer**.

steps.text: In the **Export** card, tick the sections you need.
steps.caption: Two sections ticked. The button now says **Export 2 section(s)**.
steps.alt: Export card with Ticket statuses and Ticket categories ticked and the Export 2 sections button

steps: To export everything, leave all boxes clear. **All sections** clears the ticks.
Select **Export everything**, or **Export** with the number of sections.
sections.result: Your browser saves a file named `supportdesk-config-` followed by the workspace and the date.

sections.title: Import a configuration file
sections.intro: Bring an exported file into this workspace. Nothing changes until you publish it.
prerequisites: An export file from this or another SupportDesk workspace. It can be up to 20 MB.
The departments, teams, users and brands that the file names exist in this workspace.
steps: Sign in to the workspace that should receive the configuration.
Select **Administration** > **Configuration transfer**.
In the **Import** card, select **Choose a configuration file (.json)**.
Choose the file, and select **Open**.
sections.result: SupportDesk turns the file into a draft and opens it for review. The draft also appears under **Drafts** with the status **Draft**.

blocks.tip: Capture a snapshot before you publish a large import. Then you can roll back if needed.

sections.title: Review and publish an import
sections.intro: Compare the file with this workspace, choose what to do with each item, and publish.
steps: Under **Drafts**, select **Review** on the draft.
Read the badges at the top. They count the **new**, **changed** and **unchanged** items.
Read any yellow warnings, such as names that this workspace does not have.
For each item, choose what to do in the list on its right. See [Import choices](#cfg-resolutions).
For **Import as copy (rename)**, enter a **New name**.
To compare a changed item, open its line of differing fields. It shows **This workspace** and **File** side by side.
Select **Save choices** to keep your choices for later.
Select **Publish**. In the dialog, select **Publish**.
sections.result: The app shows a message such as **Published as v3**. It also counts the items created, updated and skipped.

blocks.p: Turn off **Hide unchanged** to see every item. The first publish in a workspace also captures a snapshot named **Baseline before the first import**.

blocks.note: If the app says some references were not found, the file names things this workspace lacks. Create them, and import the file again.

sections.title: Import choices
sections.intro: Each item in a draft has a status. The status decides which choices you have.

rows: The item does not exist in this workspace.
The item exists, but some fields differ.
The item is the same in both.

blocks.note: AI prompt templates cannot be imported as a copy.

sections.title: Discard an import draft
sections.intro: Throw a draft away when you do not want to publish it.
steps: Under **Drafts**, select **Review** on the draft.
Select **Discard draft**.
In the dialog, select **Discard**.
sections.result: The draft closes. Nothing in your configuration changes.

sections.title: Snapshots
intro: A snapshot is your complete configuration at one moment. Each one gets a version number, such as **v1**.
Publishing an import and rolling back create snapshots on their own. You can also capture one by hand.

rows: You select **Capture snapshot**, or before your first import.
You roll back. SupportDesk saves the state from before the rollback.

blocks.p: The download button on a row saves the snapshot as a configuration file. You can import that file into another workspace.

sections.title: Capture a snapshot
sections.intro: Capture a snapshot before large changes, so that you can roll back.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Configuration transfer**.
Under **Snapshots**, select **Capture snapshot**.
sections.result: The app shows a message such as **Snapshot v2 captured**. The new snapshot appears at the top of the table.

sections.title: Roll back to a snapshot
sections.intro: Return your configuration to an earlier snapshot after a bad change.
steps: Select **Administration** > **Configuration transfer**.
In the **Snapshots** table, find the version you want.

steps.text: On its row, select **Roll back**.
steps.note: The newest version cannot be rolled back to, because it is the current state.

steps: In the dialog, type the version, such as `v3`, to confirm.
Select **Roll back to** and the version.
sections.result: The app shows a message such as **Rolled back — now v4**. It also counts the items restored, reverted and deactivated.

blocks.warning: A rollback changes your live configuration at once. Items added after the snapshot are deactivated, not deleted. SupportDesk saves the current state first as a **Before rollback** snapshot.

chapters.title: Subscription, billing and free trial
intro: This chapter is for administrators who look after the SupportDesk subscription. It covers your plan, usage and limits, plan changes, invoices, payment and suspension.
It also shows how a new company starts a free trial of SupportDesk.

sections.title: The Subscription page
intro: Open it with **Subscription** in the left rail, or with **Administration** > **Subscription & billing**. You need the **Manage subscription, plan and billing** permission.
The page keeps working while your workspace is suspended, so that you can always pay.

blocks.caption: The **Subscription** page of the demo workspace. A banner warns that payment is overdue.
blocks.alt: Subscription page with the plan, usage meters, usage history chart, invoices and billing contact

callouts: **Compare & change plan** opens the plan comparison. **Refresh** loads the page again.
**Current plan**: the plan, the price per agent, seats, billing cycle, period, next invoice, payment method and included features.
**Usage vs limits**, updated every 15 minutes.
**Usage history** for one measure over 30 days, 90 days or 12 months.
**Invoices**, each with a button that downloads its PDF.
**Billing contact**: where invoices are addressed and sent.

blocks.p: A banner at the top tells you when something needs action. It shows the days left in a trial, an overdue payment, a suspension, or a plan change booked for later.

sections.title: Subscription statuses
sections.intro: The badge on the **Current plan** card shows the state of your subscription.

rows: You are trying SupportDesk. Everything in the chosen plan is available. The banner shows the days left.
The subscription is paid and up to date.
A trial ended without a paid plan, or an invoice is overdue. The workspace keeps working until the grace period ends.
The grace period ended. People can sign in, read and pay, but cannot change anything.
The subscription has ended. Contact your SupportDesk provider.

sections.title: Usage and limits
sections.intro: Each plan sets limits. The **Usage vs limits** card compares your use with them, and refreshes every 15 minutes.

list: The measures are agents, light agents, portal users, storage, channels and attachments.
AI tokens and calls from other systems count for the current month only.
A bar turns amber at 80 % and shows the percentage used.
Over the limit, the card says **Over the plan limit — new items are blocked.** You cannot add more until you upgrade or remove some.
**unlimited** means the plan sets no limit for that measure.

blocks.p: In **Usage history**, choose a measure and a range to see how use changed. SupportDesk records usage once a day.

sections.title: Compare plans and change your plan
sections.intro: Change your plan, your number of seats or your billing cycle. The app shows the cost before anything changes.

steps.text: On the **Subscription** page, select **Compare & change plan**.
steps.caption: The **Compare plans** panel. The current plan is shaded and marked **Current**.
steps.alt: Compare plans panel with seats, billing cycle and a table of prices, limits and features for four plans

steps: In **Seats (agent licences)**, enter the number of agent licences.
In **Billing cycle**, choose **Monthly** or **Annual (2 months free)**.
Under the plan you want, select **Select**. For your current plan, select **Change seats**.

steps.text: Read the preview. It shows what you pay now and per period from then on.
steps.caption: The preview for a move from Enterprise to Professional, which starts at the end of the period.
steps.alt: Plan change preview with the effective date, the new price and the Back and Schedule change buttons

steps: Select **Upgrade now**, **Apply now** or **Schedule change**. To choose again, select **Back**.
sections.result: The app shows **Subscription updated**. A booked change appears in a banner on the **Subscription** page.

blocks.note: You are never billed for fewer seats than you have active agents. Once you pay for a plan, you cannot go back to **Trial**.

sections.title: When a plan change takes effect
sections.intro: This table shows when each kind of change starts and how it is billed.

rows: A new period starts, with a new invoice.
An invoice for the rest of the current period, pro rata.
At the end of the current period
No charge now. You can cancel the booked change.
Fewer seats on the same plan

blocks.note: The app refuses any change that your current usage does not fit. For example, you cannot move to a plan that allows fewer agents than you have. The preview lists each conflict.

sections.title: Cancel a booked plan change
sections.intro: Keep your current plan after you booked a downgrade for the end of the period.
steps: Open the **Subscription** page.
In the banner that says when your plan changes, select **Keep** and your current plan's name.
sections.result: The app shows **Scheduled change cancelled**. The banner disappears.

sections.title: View and download an invoice
sections.intro: Open an invoice to check it, or download it as a PDF for your accounts team.
steps: On the **Subscription** page, go to the **Invoices** card.

steps.text: Select the invoice.
steps.caption: An open subscription invoice with its lines, totals and payment instructions.
steps.alt: Invoice panel with period, dates, bill-to details, invoice lines, totals, how to pay and Download PDF

steps: Check the period, the dates, the bill-to details and the lines.
Select **Download PDF**.
sections.result: Your browser saves the invoice as a PDF file.

blocks.tip: To download without opening the invoice, select the download button at the end of its row.

rows: Open, and the due date has passed.
Your SupportDesk provider recorded the payment.
Cancelled by your SupportDesk provider. Do not pay it.

sections.title: Update the billing contact
sections.intro: Keep the billing contact current, so that invoices reach the right person.
steps: On the **Subscription** page, go to the **Billing contact** card.
Enter the **Name** and **E-mail** of the person who receives invoices.
Enter the **Billing address** and your **Tax id (GSTIN / VAT)** if your invoices need them.
Select **Save contact**.
sections.result: The app shows **Billing contact saved**. New invoices use these details.

sections.title: Paying invoices and suspension
intro: You pay invoices offline by bank transfer. Each invoice shows **How to pay**. Quote the invoice number as the payment reference.
Your SupportDesk provider marks the invoice paid when the money arrives. SupportDesk never stores card details.

blocks.heading: What happens when a payment is late

rows: A trial ended, or an invoice is overdue. A grace period starts, usually 7 days. The workspace keeps working.
The grace period ended. People can still sign in, read and pay. The app refuses other changes with a message that the account is suspended.
When you pay all overdue invoices, the workspace works normally again.

blocks.note: During a suspension, the **Subscription** page and the customer portal still work.

blocks.p: You cannot cancel the subscription yourself. Contact your SupportDesk provider.

sections.title: The free trial
intro: A new company can try SupportDesk without a card. The trial gives a new workspace with 3 seats and every feature of the chosen plan.
The trial lasts at least 14 days. The person who signs up becomes the workspace's administrator.

blocks.p: During the trial, a banner on the **Subscription** page shows the days left. Select **Choose a plan** to move to a paid plan at any time.
If the trial ends without a paid plan, the subscription becomes **Past due**. After the grace period, the workspace is suspended.

sections.title: Start a free trial
sections.intro: Create a new SupportDesk workspace for your company. You do not need an account yet.
prerequisites: A work e-mail address that you can open now.
steps: On the SupportDesk sign-in page, select **Start a free trial**.
Enter your **Company name**. SupportDesk suggests a **Workspace name** from it.

steps.text: Check the **Workspace name**.
steps.note: A green tick means the name is free. If someone already uses it, select the suggested name.

steps: Enter **Your name** and your **Work e-mail**.
Enter a **Password** of at least 10 characters, with upper-case and lower-case letters and a digit.
In **Plan to try**, choose a plan.

steps.text: Select **Create workspace**.
steps.caption: The **Start your free trial** form for a sample company. The green tick shows the workspace name is free.
steps.alt: Start your free trial form with company, workspace name, your name, work e-mail, password and plan

sections.result: The **Check your inbox** page opens. SupportDesk sends a 6-digit code to your e-mail.

sections.title: Verify your e-mail and open your workspace
sections.intro: Finish the sign-up with the code from your e-mail.
steps: Open the e-mail from SupportDesk, and note the 6-digit code.
On the **Check your inbox** page, enter it in **Verification code**.
Select **Verify and create workspace**.
On the **Your workspace is ready** page, select **Sign in to** and your workspace name.
Sign in with your work e-mail and password.
sections.result: Your new workspace opens, with you as its administrator.

blocks.note: The code expires after 30 minutes, and you can try it 5 times. To fix a typing mistake in your details, select **Change details**.

chapters.title: Customer portal
intro: This chapter is for customers who use the support portal. Agents who help customers can read it to see what customers see.
In the portal you raise tickets and follow them up. You also read help articles, ask the community, use step-by-step guides and chat with support.
Your support team decides which parts of the portal you see. If this chapter names a page you cannot find, your support team has switched it off.

sections.title: The portal at a glance
intro: Your support team gives you the portal address. It ends with your portal name, for example `/portal/wings/`.
Each portal has its own name, colours and welcome text. You can read articles and the community without signing in. Sign in to raise tickets and follow them up.

blocks.caption: The portal home page before you sign in.
blocks.alt: Wings Help Center home page with the menu, the search box, Submit a ticket, Sign in and Ask highlighted and numbered

callouts: The menu opens **Home**, **Knowledge Base**, **Community**, **Help** and **My tickets**.
The search box finds help articles and community topics.
**Submit a ticket** opens the ticket form.
**Sign in** opens the sign-in page. After you sign in, your name appears here instead.
**Ask** opens the assistant, which answers questions from the help articles.

blocks.tip: The moon icon next to **Sign in** switches the portal between light and dark colours.

blocks.note: On a phone, the menu is behind the menu icon at the top right.

sections.title: Open your portal
sections.intro: Use this task if you know the portal name but not the full address.
steps: Open the support portal address without a portal name, such as `/portal/`.

steps.text: In **Portal name**, enter the name your support team gave you, such as `wings`.
steps.note: Use letters, numbers and dashes only.

steps: Select **Continue**.
sections.result: Your portal home page opens. Bookmark it for next time.

sections.title: Sign in with your password
sections.intro: Sign in to see your tickets, raise new ones and join the community.
prerequisites: Your support team has given you portal access.
steps: Select **Sign in** at the top right.

steps.text: On the **Password** tab, enter your **E-mail** and **Password**.
steps.caption: The sign-in page with the **Password** tab open.
steps.alt: Sign in to Wings Help Center card with the Password and E-mail code tabs, the e-mail field and the Sign in button

steps: Select **Sign in**.
sections.result: The home page opens and greets you by your first name.

blocks.note: After five wrong passwords, your account locks for 15 minutes. You can still sign in with an e-mail code during that time.

sections.title: Sign in with an e-mail code
sections.intro: You do not need a password. The portal e-mails you a one-time code instead. Use this method if you forgot your password.
steps: Select **Sign in** at the top right.

steps.text: Select the **E-mail code** tab.
steps.caption: The **E-mail code** tab, ready to send a code.
steps.alt: Sign-in card with the E-mail code tab selected, an e-mail field and the Send code button
steps.tip: On the **Password** tab, **Forgot your password? Sign in with an e-mail code** opens the same tab.

steps: Enter your **E-mail**, and then select **Send code**.

steps.text: Open the e-mail, and enter the 6-digit code in **Code**.
steps.note: The code works for 10 minutes. If it does not arrive, select **Send a new code**.

steps: Select **Sign in**.
sections.result: The home page opens and greets you by your first name.

blocks.p: To use another address, select **Use a different e-mail**. Some portals use your organisation's account. Their sign-in page shows a note, and you always sign in with an e-mail code.

sections.title: Create an account
sections.intro: Some portals let you create your own account. If yours does not, ask your support team for access.
steps: Select **Sign in**.
Under **New here?**, select **Create an account**.

steps.text: Fill in the form.
substeps: Enter your **Full name** and **Work e-mail**.
Optionally, enter your **Company** and **Phone**.
Enter a **Password** of at least 8 characters. The eye icon shows what you typed.
steps.caption: The **Create your account** form with sample details.
steps.alt: Create your account form with Full name, Work e-mail, Company, Phone and Password fields and the Create account button

steps: Select **Create account**.
sections.result: You are signed in, and a welcome message appears. If your e-mail domain belongs to a customer of your support team, your account joins that company.

blocks.note: If an account already exists for your e-mail, the form says so. Select **Sign in with an e-mail code** to get in.

sections.title: Your home page after you sign in
sections.intro: After you sign in, the home page adds a summary of your tickets. Your name at the top right opens the account menu.

blocks.caption: The home page for a signed-in customer.
blocks.alt: Home page greeting Ramesh, with the Your tickets panel and the account menu button highlighted and numbered

callouts: **Your tickets** counts your **Open** tickets and the ones **Awaiting your reply** or **Awaiting your confirmation**. Select a count to open the matching list.
Your name opens the account menu: **My tickets**, **Account**, **Contracts & products** and **Sign out**.

blocks.p: Below the summary, the home page shows announcements, help topics, popular and recent articles, step-by-step guides and recent community topics.

sections.title: Ticket scopes
intro: Your support team decides how many tickets you can see. This is your ticket scope. To change it, ask your support team.
Your scope also appears on the **Account** page as **Ticket access**.

rows: Your tickets and the tickets of colleagues at your branch or site.

blocks.p: If you can see more than your own tickets, a switcher appears above the list. It offers **Mine**, **My location** and **My organisation**. Location and organisation users also see contracts, licences, installations and planned maintenance on the **Account** page.

sections.title: Find a ticket
sections.intro: **My tickets** lists your tickets. Tickets that need you are marked, so you can act on them first.
steps: Select **My tickets** in the menu.
If you see the scope switcher, choose **Mine**, **My location** or **My organisation**.
Choose a status filter: **Open**, **Awaiting you**, **Closed** or **All**.

steps.text: To find one ticket, enter its number or part of the subject in **Search by number or subject**.
steps.tip: Select **Load more** at the end of the list to see older tickets.

steps: Select the ticket subject to open it.
sections.result: The ticket page opens.

blocks.caption: **My tickets** showing the whole organisation's open tickets.
blocks.alt: Organisation tickets list with the scope switcher, status filters, search box, column headings and Submit a ticket button highlighted and numbered

callouts: The scope switcher. It appears only if you may see more than your own tickets.
Status filters. **Awaiting you** lists tickets where support replied or asked you to confirm.
Search by ticket number or subject.
The list shows the status, who raised the ticket, the priority, the last update and the creation date.
**Submit a ticket** opens a new ticket form.

blocks.p: Two badges point out tickets that need you. **Awaiting your reply** means support asked you something. A second badge asks you to confirm the resolution. It means support thinks the problem is solved.

blocks.note: The list updates while you have it open. When something changes, **Some of your tickets have been updated** appears. Select **Refresh list** to see the changes.

sections.title: The ticket page
sections.intro: The ticket page shows your request, the conversation with support and the ticket details. It updates by itself while it is open.

blocks.caption: A ticket that is waiting for the customer's reply.
blocks.alt: Ticket 1200 page with the header, Original request, Conversation, Add a reply and Details card highlighted and numbered

callouts: The ticket number, status and priority. **Live** means the page updates by itself.
**Original request** shows what was first written, with any attachments.
**Conversation** shows every public message. Replies from the team carry a **Support** badge. New messages carry a **New** badge.
**Add a reply** sends a message to the support team.
**Details** shows who raised the ticket, the organisation, location, department, product, channel and dates. **Additional information** shows any extra fields.

blocks.note: You never see the team's internal notes. You see only the messages written for you.

sections.title: Submit a ticket
sections.intro: Raise a ticket when you need help from the support team. While you type, the portal suggests articles that may already answer your question.
prerequisites: You are signed in. To submit without an account, see [Submit a ticket without an account](#portal-anonymous).
steps: Select **Submit a ticket**.

steps.text: Enter a **Subject** of at least 5 characters.
steps.note: Articles that match appear under **These articles might help**.

steps: Describe the problem in **Description**. Say what happened, what you expected and any error message.

steps.text: Optionally, select a suggested article to read it in a side panel.
steps.caption: A suggested article open in the side panel.
steps.alt: Side panel showing the article Fix GST rounding differences with This solved my problem, Back to my request and New tab buttons
substeps: If it solves the problem, select **This solved my problem**. No ticket is created.
If not, select **Back to my request**.

steps.text: Under **About your request**, choose the **Department**, **Category**, **Product**, **Installation / site** and **Priority**.
steps.note: Leave **Priority** as **Normal (let support decide)** if you are unsure. Choosing an installation fills in its product.

steps: Fill in any fields under **Additional information**. Your support team decides which fields appear.

steps.text: To attach files, drag them onto **Attachments** or select **choose files**.
steps.note: The box shows the size limit for each file.

steps.text: Select **Submit ticket**.
steps.caption: The ticket form filled in, with suggested articles.
steps.alt: Submit a ticket form with Subject, Description, suggested articles, About your request, Additional information, Attachments and the Submit ticket button

sections.result: A page says **Ticket … submitted**. Select **View your ticket** to open it, or **Submit another**. Replies also reach you by e-mail.

blocks.tip: An article page has a **Submit a ticket** button under **Still need help?**. It notes the article you read in the description.

sections.title: Reply to a ticket
sections.intro: Answer a question from support, or add new information to your ticket.
steps: Open the ticket from **My tickets**.
Write your message in **Add a reply**. Use the toolbar for bold text, lists and links.
To attach files, drag them onto the box below the editor, or select **choose files**.

steps.text: Select **Send reply**, or press [[Ctrl+Enter]].
steps.caption: A reply ready to send.
steps.alt: Add a reply box with sample text, the formatting toolbar, the attachment box and the Send reply button

sections.result: Your message appears in the conversation, and **Reply sent** confirms it.

blocks.note: A reply to a resolved ticket reopens it. A reply to a closed ticket reopens it too, but only until the reopen date. After that, the page says the ticket is closed. Submit a new ticket instead.

sections.title: Confirm a resolution
sections.intro: When support thinks your problem is solved, they may ask you to confirm. The ticket then shows **Is your issue resolved?**, and the list asks you to confirm the resolution.
steps: Open the ticket.

steps.text: Under **Is your issue resolved?**, choose an answer.
substeps: If the problem is solved, select **Yes, it's resolved**.
If it is not, select **No, I still need help**.

steps: If you selected **No, I still need help**, describe what is still wrong in **What is still not working?**.
Select **Send and keep it open**.
sections.result: **Yes, it's resolved** closes the ticket. **Send and keep it open** keeps the ticket open, and the team gets your comment.

sections.title: Reopen a ticket
sections.intro: If a problem comes back after the ticket is resolved or closed, reopen the ticket. You can do this until the date shown on the ticket.

steps.text: Open the resolved or closed ticket.
steps.caption: A closed ticket that you can still reopen and rate.
steps.alt: Closed ticket 1202 with the reopen banner and the How did we do? rating card highlighted and numbered

steps: In the banner, select **Reopen ticket**.

steps.text: In **Why are you reopening it?**, say what is wrong.
steps.caption: The reason for reopening, ready to send.
steps.alt: This ticket is closed banner with the reason box filled in and the Reopen ticket and Cancel buttons

steps: Select **Reopen ticket**.
sections.result: **Ticket reopened** appears, and the team picks the ticket up again.

callouts: The reopen banner shows the last date you can reopen the ticket.
**How did we do?** lets you rate the support you received.

blocks.note: Your support team sets how long you can reopen tickets. They can also switch reopening off. If you see no **Reopen ticket** button, submit a new ticket.

sections.title: Rate the support you received
sections.intro: Tell the team how they did on a resolved or closed ticket. You can rate each ticket once.
steps: Open the resolved or closed ticket.
Under **How did we do?**, select from 1 to 5 stars. The label shows what each star means, from **Very poor** to **Excellent**.

steps.text: Optionally, enter a **Comment**.
steps.caption: A four-star rating with a comment.
steps.alt: How did we do? card with four stars selected, the label Good, a comment and the Submit rating button

steps: Select **Submit rating**.
sections.result: The card changes to **Your rating** and shows your stars and comment.

sections.title: Answer a satisfaction survey from an e-mail
sections.intro: After a ticket is resolved, your support team may e-mail you a short survey. You do not need to sign in to answer it.
steps: In the survey e-mail, select the link.
On the **How did we do?** page, select from 1 to 5 stars.
Optionally, write in **Anything you'd like to tell us?**.
Select **Send feedback**.
sections.result: **Thank you for your feedback** appears with your rating.

blocks.note: The page shows the last date you can answer. After that date, it says the survey has closed.

sections.title: Submit a ticket without an account
sections.intro: Some portals accept tickets from people who are not signed in. You get a ticket number, and replies come by e-mail.
