prerequisites: Your support team allows tickets without an account. Otherwise, the form asks you to sign in.
steps: Select **Submit a ticket** without signing in.
Enter **Your name** and **E-mail**. Optionally, enter your **Phone**.
Optionally, choose a **Department**, **Category** and **Product**. Leave **Not sure** if you do not know.
Enter a **Subject** of at least 5 characters.
Describe the problem in **Description**, in at least 10 characters.
Check the suggested articles under **These articles might help**.

steps.text: Select **Submit ticket**.
steps.caption: The ticket form for visitors who are not signed in.
steps.alt: Submit a ticket form for visitors with Your name, E-mail, Phone, Department, Category, Product, Subject and Description, and suggested articles

sections.result: A page says **Request … received**. The team replies to the e-mail address you entered.

blocks.note: You cannot attach files without an account. Sign in to attach files and follow your tickets online.

sections.title: Search the help center
sections.intro: Search finds help articles and community topics in one go.

steps.text: Type a few words in the search box on the home page or the **Knowledge Base** page.
steps.note: After three characters, matching articles appear below the box. Select one to open it.

steps: Press [[Enter]], or select **Search**.
On the results page, select an article or a topic.
sections.result: The results page lists **Articles** and **Community** topics that match your words.

blocks.caption: Search results for the word password.
blocks.alt: Search results page with matching articles and community topics, and the Didn't find what you need? bar

blocks.p: Under **Didn't find what you need?**, select **Submit a ticket** or **Ask the community**.

sections.title: Read a help article
sections.intro: The **Knowledge Base** holds answers, how-to guides and FAQs from the support team.

steps.text: Select **Knowledge Base** in the menu.
steps.caption: The **Knowledge Base** page.
steps.alt: Knowledge Base page with the search box, the first topic card and the Popular articles panel highlighted and numbered

steps: Select a topic or a section to see its articles. You can also pick one from **Popular articles** or **Recently updated**.
Select an article to open it.
If the article exists in other languages, choose one in the **Language** list.
sections.result: The article opens with related articles beside it.

callouts: Search the articles.
A topic card. Its sections are listed below the description.
**Popular articles** and **Recently updated** list articles to start with.

blocks.caption: A help article.
blocks.alt: Article How to reset your Wings ERP password with the details line, the feedback box and Still need help? highlighted and numbered

callouts: The article type, product, last update, number of views and how many readers found it helpful.
**Was this article helpful?** asks for your feedback.
**Still need help?** opens a ticket form or the community.

blocks.p: Select a tag under the article to find other articles with that tag. If a translation is missing or out of date, a note at the top says so.

blocks.note: Some articles are only for signed-in customers. If an article is not found, sign in and try again.

sections.title: Tell us whether an article helped
sections.intro: Your answer helps the team improve its articles.
steps: At the end of the article, under **Was this article helpful?**, select **Yes** or **No**.

steps.text: Optionally, select stars under **Rate this article (optional)**, and add a comment.
steps.caption: The feedback box after **Yes**, with five stars.
steps.alt: Glad it helped! Anything to add? box with five stars, a comment field and the Send feedback and Skip buttons

steps: Select **Send feedback**, or select **Skip** to send only your answer.
sections.result: **Thanks for your feedback!** appears. After **No**, a link lets you submit a ticket.

blocks.warning: Do not include personal information in your comment.

sections.title: The community
intro: The community is a forum where customers and the support team share questions, ideas and tips.
Anyone can read it. Sign in to post, reply and vote.

blocks.caption: The **Community** page.
blocks.alt: Community page with Start a topic, the search and sort bar, status filters, the first topic and the Join the conversation card highlighted and numbered

callouts: **Start a topic** asks a question or starts a discussion.
Search the topics. **Sort** orders them by **Recent activity**, **Newest**, **Most votes** or **Unanswered first**. **Tag** shows one tag only.
Filter by **All**, **Unanswered**, **Answered**, **Open** or **Closed**.
Each topic shows its votes, replies, type, tags, author and last activity. A green tick on the replies means the question has an accepted answer.
**Sign in** appears when you are not signed in. **Before you post** gives tips, and **Tags** filters by a tag.

sections.title: Start a topic
sections.intro: Ask other customers and the support team a question, or share an idea.
prerequisites: You are signed in.
steps: Select **Community**, and then select **Start a topic**.
Under **What kind of topic is it?**, choose **Question** or **Discussion**.

steps.text: Enter a **Title** of at least 5 characters.
steps.note: Matching articles appear. If one answers you, select **This solved my problem** in the article panel. Your topic is not posted.

steps: Write at least 10 characters in **Details**.

steps.text: Optionally, add **Tags**. Press [[Enter]] after each tag.
steps.note: A topic keeps up to five tags.

steps.text: Select **Post topic**.
steps.caption: A new question with suggested articles.
steps.alt: Start a topic form with Question selected, a title, suggested articles, Details, Tags, Cancel and Post topic

sections.result: **Topic posted** appears, and your topic opens. You hear when someone replies.

sections.title: Reply, vote and accept an answer
sections.intro: Help others with your knowledge, and mark the reply that answered your question.
prerequisites: You are signed in. If not, **Sign in to reply** takes you to the sign-in page and back.
steps: Open a topic from the **Community** page.
To vote for a topic or a reply, select its arrow.
To reply, write in **Your reply**, and then select **Post reply**.
If you asked the question, select **Accept as answer** under the reply that solved it.
sections.result: Your reply appears in the list. An accepted answer moves to the top, and **Accepted answer** links to it.

blocks.caption: A question with an accepted answer from the support team.
blocks.alt: Community topic with the vote button, the Accepted answer summary, the Accept as answer button and the Your reply box highlighted and numbered

callouts: Vote for the topic. Select the arrow again to remove your vote.
**Accepted answer** shows who answered and jumps to the answer.
**Accept as answer** appears on replies to your own question.
**Your reply** posts an answer or a comment.

list: You cannot vote for your own topic or reply.
Replies from the support team carry a **Support team** badge.
A closed topic takes no new replies.
If the team turned a topic into a ticket, the topic shows the ticket number.

sections.title: Ask the assistant
sections.intro: The assistant answers your questions from the help articles. It shows the articles it used as numbered sources.
steps: Select **Ask** at the bottom right of any page.

steps.text: Type your question in **Ask a question…**.
steps.caption: The assistant panel with a question typed.
steps.alt: Ask Wings Help Center side panel with the assistant greeting, a typed question and the send button

steps: Press [[Enter]], or select the send button.
Read the answer. Select a source to open the article.
If the assistant suggests it, select **Create a ticket**. The portal copies your question into the ticket form.
sections.result: The answer appears in the panel, with its sources.

list: Press [[Shift+Enter]] to start a new line without sending.
Select **Clear conversation** to start again.
The conversation is lost when you reload the page.

blocks.note: Answers come from the help articles and may not be perfect. If something is important, check the article or ask the team.

sections.title: Use a troubleshooting guide
sections.intro: A troubleshooting guide asks a few questions and walks you to a fix. If the guide cannot help, it hands your answers to the support team.

steps.text: Select **Help** in the menu. On the home page, you can also select **Troubleshoot a problem**.
steps.caption: The **Help & contact** page.
steps.alt: Help and contact page with Guided troubleshooting guides, Other ways to get help and Contact us with the support team and departments

steps: Under **Guided troubleshooting**, select a guide.

steps.text: Answer each question.
steps.caption: The first question of a guide.
steps.alt: Invoice GST total doesn't match guide at step 1 with Yes and No answers and the Back and Start over buttons

steps: When the guide suggests a fix, try it. Then answer **Did this solve your problem?** with **Yes, it's fixed** or **No**.
If the guide reaches **Let's get our team on it**, select **Create a ticket**.
sections.result: After **Yes, it's fixed**, the guide closes with a thank-you. After **Create a ticket**, the ticket form opens with the guide name and your answers filled in.

blocks.p: Select **Back** to change your last answer. Select **Start over** to begin again.
The **Help & contact** page also lists other ways to get help. **Contact us** shows the support team's e-mail and phone and each department. After you sign in, it also shows your account manager.

sections.title: Chat with support on a website
sections.intro: Your support team can add a chat button to its website. The assistant may answer first, and you can ask for a person at any time.
steps: On the website, select the round chat button at the bottom right.

steps.text: Enter your **Name**, **E-mail** and **Message**.
steps.caption: The chat window open on a website, before the chat starts.
steps.alt: Website page with the Chat with Wings Support window open, showing Name, E-mail and Message fields and the Start chat button
steps.note: Some websites need your e-mail before you can chat.

steps: Select **Start chat**.
Type your messages in **Type your message…**, and select **Send**.
To reach a person, select **Talk to a person**. The window shows **Connecting you to an agent…** until someone answers.
sections.result: The window shows the name of the agent you are chatting with.

list: **Verify my e-mail** sends you a 6-digit code. Enter it to link the chat to your customer record.
**–** minimises the window. The chat goes on, and a number on the button counts new messages.
**✕** ends the chat after you confirm. You can then rate the chat from 1 to 5 stars, or select **Start a new chat**.

blocks.note: When no agent is online, the window says so. Leave a message, and the team replies later.

blocks.tip: Administrators add the chat button to a website as described in [Set up the chat widget](#ch-chat-widget).

sections.title: Your account
sections.intro: The **Account** page holds your profile and preferences. For location and organisation users, it also shows your company's contracts and products.

blocks.caption: The **Account** page with the **Profile** tab open.
blocks.alt: Account page for Ramesh Kumar with the header, the tabs, the profile form and the account summary highlighted and numbered

callouts: Your name, e-mail, company, location and ticket access.
The tabs of the account page.
The **Profile** form.
Your organisation, location, ticket access and last sign-in.

rows: Your name, phone numbers, job title, language and time zone.
How and in which language the team contacts you, and which messages you agree to receive.
Your company's support contracts and what each one covers. Location and organisation users only.
Licensed products, seats, masked licence keys and expiry dates. Location and organisation users only.
Each installation with its product, version, environment, location and users. Location and organisation users only.
Planned and past maintenance, upgrades, training and visits. Location and organisation users only.
The support team's e-mail and phone, your account manager and the departments.

sections.title: Update your profile
sections.intro: Keep your contact details up to date so the team can reach you.
steps: Select your name at the top right, and then select **Account**.
On the **Profile** tab, change **Full name**, **Phone**, **Mobile** or **Job title**.
Choose your **Language**. The team uses it for e-mails and articles when it can.
Choose your **Time zone**, or keep **Use my browser's time zone**.
Select **Save profile**.
sections.result: **Profile saved** appears.

blocks.p: To undo your changes before saving, select **Discard changes**.

blocks.note: You cannot change your sign-in e-mail here. Ask the support team to change it.

sections.title: Choose how we contact you
sections.intro: Choose your preferred channel, and which kinds of messages you agree to receive.
steps: Open **Account**, and select the **Notifications** tab.
Under **Preferred channel**, choose **No preference**, **E-mail**, **WhatsApp** or **SMS**.
Choose a **Language**.

steps.text: Under **What we may send you**, turn each message type on or off for each channel.
steps.caption: The **Notifications** tab.
steps.alt: Notifications tab with Preferred channel options, Language and a table of Ticket updates, News and offers and Surveys switches for e-mail, WhatsApp and SMS

steps: Select **Save preferences**.
sections.result: **Preferences saved** appears.

rows: Replies, status changes and confirmations about your requests.
Short feedback requests after the team helps you.

blocks.note: Replies to a ticket arrive through the channel the ticket came in on. Replies to portal tickets arrive by e-mail.

sections.title: Change your password
sections.intro: Change your portal password. You need your current password to do this.
steps: Open **Account**, and select the **Password** tab.
Enter your **Current password**.
Enter a **New password** of at least 8 characters.

steps.text: Enter it again in **Confirm new password**.
steps.caption: The **Password** tab.
steps.alt: Password tab with a note, Current password, New password and Confirm new password fields and the Change password button

steps: Select **Change password**.
sections.result: **Password changed** appears. Use the new password next time you sign in.

blocks.note: If you forgot your password, you cannot replace it here. Sign in with an e-mail code instead. If you have no password yet, ask the team through **Help & contact**.

sections.title: Check your contracts and products
sections.intro: See what your company's support covers, and for how long.
prerequisites: Your ticket access is **Your location** or **Your whole organisation**.
steps: Select your name at the top right, and then select **Contracts & products**.
On the **Contracts** tab, check each contract's status, period, time left, renewal and on-site support.
Check the **Entitlements** under each contract. They show the products covered and the incidents and hours used.
Select **Products & licences**, **Installations** or **Maintenance** for more details.
sections.result: You see what your company has and what its support covers.

blocks.caption: The **Contracts** tab with two active contracts and an expired one.
blocks.alt: Contracts tab listing a POS hardware warranty, a Premium AMC and an expired annual maintenance contract with periods, renewal and entitlements

blocks.p: **Time left** shows the days until the end date. For a contract that has ended, it shows **Ended** and how many days ago. A contract with prepaid hours also shows how many hours are used. **Covered channels** lists the ways you may contact support under the contract.

chapters.title: Mobile app
intro: This chapter is for agents and customers who use SupportDesk on a phone.
The SupportDesk app has two modes. In agent mode, you work on tickets, alerts and approvals. In customer mode, you follow your own requests and read help articles.
The app keeps working with a weak connection. It shows saved copies of the screens you opened and sends your messages when the connection returns.

sections.title: Get the app
intro: Your administrator tells you how to install the app on your phone.
The app follows your phone's light or dark setting. You can change this on the **Me** tab.

sections.title: Sign in as an agent
sections.intro: Agents sign in with the same details they use on the desk.
prerequisites: You have a SupportDesk agent account and a connection to the internet.
steps: Open the app.
At the top of the sign-in screen, select **Agent**.

steps.text: Enter your **Workspace**, **Work e-mail** and **Password**.
steps.caption: The sign-in screen in agent mode.
steps.alt: SupportDesk mobile sign-in screen with the Agent and Customer choice, the Workspace, Work e-mail and Password fields and the Sign in button, numbered

steps: Select **Sign in**.

steps.text: If the app asks for a verification code, enter it in **Code**, and then select **Verify**.
steps.note: The code comes from your authenticator app or by e-mail. Select **Back** to return to the first screen.

sections.result: The **Home** tab opens. The app keeps you signed in on this phone.

sections.title: Sign in as a customer
sections.intro: Customers use the same e-mail as on the support portal. You can sign in with a password or with a code sent by e-mail.
prerequisites: You have access to your support team's portal.
steps: Open the app, and select **Customer**.

steps.text: In **Help center**, enter your portal name, such as `wings`.
steps.note: The portal name is the part of the portal address after `/portal/`.

steps: Enter your **E-mail**.

steps.text: Choose **Password** or **E-mail me a code**.
steps.caption: The sign-in screen in customer mode.
steps.alt: Mobile sign-in screen in customer mode with Help center and E-mail fields, the Password and E-mail me a code choice and the Sign in button, numbered

steps.text: Finish signing in.
substeps: With **Password**, enter your **Password**, and then select **Sign in**.
With **E-mail me a code**, select **Send me a code**. Enter the code in **Code from the e-mail**, and then select **Verify code**.

sections.result: The **My tickets** tab opens. The app keeps you signed in on this phone.

blocks.tip: If the code does not arrive, select **Send a new code**.

blocks.note: The app has no single sign-on, no account creation and no password change. Use the web portal for those.

sections.title: The Home tab for agents
sections.intro: **Home** gives you a quick view of your work. Pull the screen down to refresh it.

blocks.caption: The **Home** tab in agent mode.
blocks.alt: Agent Home tab with the availability button, the Mine queue tile, an SLA chip in My next deadlines and the Tickets tab highlighted and numbered

callouts: Your availability. Select it to change it.
**My queues** shows how many tickets wait in each queue. Select a tile to open that list.
**My next deadlines** lists your open tickets with the nearest SLA deadlines. The chip shows the time left, or how long ago the deadline passed.
The tab bar opens **Home**, **Tickets**, **Alerts**, **Approvals** and **Me**. A number on a tab counts your tickets or unread alerts.

blocks.p: If approvals wait for your decision, **Approvals waiting for you** appears below the tiles.

sections.title: Change your availability
sections.intro: Routing only assigns new tickets to you while you are **Online**. Set yourself to **Away** or **Busy** when you step out.
steps: On **Home**, select your availability at the top right.
Choose **Online**, **Away**, **Busy** or **Offline**. Your current choice says **(current)**.
sections.result: A message confirms your new availability, such as **You are Away.**

blocks.tip: You can also change it on the **Me** tab, under **Availability**.

sections.title: Find and act on tickets
sections.intro: The **Tickets** tab lists tickets by queue. You can search, assign tickets to yourself and close them from the list.
steps: Select the **Tickets** tab.
Choose a queue: **Mine**, **Unassigned**, **Overdue**, **At risk**, **Escalated**, **Waiting**, **Watching** or **All open**. Swipe the row of queues to see them all.
To find a ticket, enter its number, subject or customer in **Search number, subject, customer**.

steps.text: To act on a ticket, select the three dots at the end of its row.
steps.caption: The actions for an unassigned ticket.
steps.alt: Tickets list in the Unassigned queue with an action sheet offering Assign to me, Close ticket and Cancel

steps: Choose **Assign to me** or **Close ticket**. Choose **Cancel** to do nothing.
To open a ticket, select it in the list.
sections.result: The ticket opens, or the list shows the change you made.

blocks.caption: The **Tickets** tab with the **Mine** queue.
blocks.alt: Tickets tab with the search box, the Mine queue, the priority and SLA chips of the first ticket and its actions button highlighted and numbered

callouts: Search by number, subject or customer.
The queues. The selected one is underlined.
Each ticket shows its priority, **Escalated** when escalated, and its SLA chip.
The three dots open the ticket's actions.

list: Swipe a ticket to the right for **Assign to me**. Swipe it to the left for **Close**.
A blue dot next to the status means the customer replied.
**Close ticket** asks you to confirm. The customer is not asked to confirm, and you can reopen the ticket later.
When tickets change, **New activity — refresh** appears at the top. Select it to reload the list.
Pull the list down, or select the refresh button, to reload it. Scroll down to load more tickets.

blocks.note: You see **Assign to me** and **Close** only if your role allows them.

sections.title: Work on a ticket
sections.intro: The ticket screen shows the SLA timers and the conversation. You can change the status, priority and assignee from the top of the screen.
steps: Open the ticket from **Tickets**, **Home** or **Alerts**.

steps.text: To change the status, select the status chip, and choose the new status.
steps.caption: The **Change status** list.
steps.alt: Change status action sheet listing Open, Assigned, Waiting on Customer, Waiting on Third Party, Escalated to Engineering, Resolved, Closed and Cancel

steps: To change the priority, select the priority chip, and choose the new priority.

steps.text: To change the assignee, select the person chip, and choose an option.
steps.note: The list offers **Assign to me**, other agents with their availability and load, and **Unassign**.

steps: Select **Customer** to see the contact, the customer, contracts and previous tickets. Select **Conversation** to go back.
sections.result: **Ticket updated** appears, and the timeline shows the change.

blocks.caption: A ticket in agent mode.
blocks.alt: Ticket 1195 with the status, priority and assignee chips, the SLA chips, the Conversation and Customer choice and the reply box highlighted and numbered

callouts: The status, priority and assignee chips. A grey chip means you cannot change it.
The SLA chips show the time left for the first response, the next response and the resolution. **Escalated** shows the escalation level.
**Conversation** shows the messages and events. **Customer** shows who the customer is.
The reply box. See [Reply or add a note](#mobile-reply).

blocks.caption: The **Customer** section of a ticket.
blocks.alt: Customer section with the contact's name, job, e-mail and phone, the customer with its tier and account manager, and ticket statistics

blocks.p: When colleagues open the same ticket, a line under the details says who is viewing or replying.

blocks.note: If someone else changed the ticket first, the app shows the latest version. Make your change again.

sections.title: Reply or add a note
sections.intro: Reply to the customer, or write an internal note for other agents. You can add photos, files and templates.
steps: Open the ticket, and stay on **Conversation**.
Choose **Reply** or **Internal note** above the text box.
Type your message.

steps.text: Optionally, add attachments or a template.
substeps: The camera button takes a photo.
The paper clip button attaches files from your phone.
The page button inserts a reply template.

steps.text: Select **Send**. For a note, select **Add note**.
steps.caption: A reply ready to send, with the camera, file and template buttons.
steps.alt: Mobile reply box with Reply and Internal note, a typed message, camera, attach and template buttons and the Send button

sections.result: **Reply sent.** or **Note added.** appears, and your message joins the conversation.

list: You can attach up to 10 files to a message.
The app saves what you type on the phone. If you leave the ticket, your text is still there when you come back.
Without a connection, the button says **Queue**. See [Work offline](#mobile-offline).

blocks.note: If new messages arrived while you were writing, the app holds your reply. Read the new messages, and then choose **Send anyway**, **Edit** or **Discard**.

sections.title: Read and acknowledge alerts
sections.intro: The **Alerts** tab shows your notifications, such as assignments, mentions and SLA warnings. Critical alerts need an acknowledgement.
steps: Select the **Alerts** tab. The number on the tab counts unread alerts.
Select an alert to open its ticket. The app marks the alert read.
For a critical alert, select **Acknowledge**.
To mark every alert read, select **Mark all read**.
sections.result: **Acknowledged** replaces the button, and the unread count goes down.

blocks.caption: The **Notifications** screen with SLA alerts.
blocks.alt: Notifications screen listing SLA breach and escalation alerts, some with an Acknowledge button, and Mark all read at the top

blocks.note: Some alerts open in the desktop desk only. The app then says **This item opens in the desktop workbench.**

sections.title: Approve or reject a request
sections.intro: Approvers decide on transfer and workflow requests from the **Approvals** tab.
prerequisites: Your role lets you decide approvals.
steps: Select the **Approvals** tab.
On **To decide**, read the request. Select the ticket line to open the ticket.
Select **Approve** or **Reject**.
Enter a note. For a rejection, explain why, because the requester sees your note.
Select **Approve** or **Reject** in the dialog.
sections.result: **Approved.** or **Rejected.** appears, and the request shows who decided.

blocks.p: **Raised by me** lists the approvals you asked for, with their status.

sections.title: The Me tab
sections.intro: **Me** shows who you are signed in as and holds your settings.

blocks.caption: The **Me** tab in agent mode.
blocks.alt: Me tab with the agent's name, Availability, Appearance, Notifications, Unsent messages and the Sign out button

rows: Shows whether push notifications work on this phone. See [Push notifications](#mobile-push).
Lists messages that wait for a connection, with **Retry** and **Discard**.
Signs you out of this mode on this phone.

blocks.warning: Signing out deletes unsent messages from this phone. The app warns you first. Send or discard them before you sign out.

sections.title: Follow your requests
sections.intro: In customer mode, **My tickets** lists your requests. If your support team allows it, you also see your location's or organisation's tickets.
steps: Select the **My tickets** tab.
If you see **Mine**, **Location** and **Organisation**, choose whose tickets to show.
Choose **Open**, **Needs me**, **Closed** or **All**.
To find a request, type in **Search your tickets**.
Select a request to open it.
sections.result: The request opens with its conversation.

blocks.caption: **My tickets** in customer mode.
blocks.alt: My tickets tab with the Mine scope, the Open filter, the search box and the new request button highlighted and numbered

callouts: Whose tickets to show. It appears only if you may see more than your own.
The status filter. **Needs me** lists requests that wait for your reply or confirmation.
Search your tickets.
The plus button starts a new request.

blocks.p: The **Waiting for your reply** badge marks requests where support asked you something. Another badge asks you to confirm the fix.

sections.title: Reply, confirm, reopen or rate a request
sections.intro: Open a request to reply to support. You can also confirm a fix, reopen a request and rate the support you received.
steps: Open the request from **My tickets**.
To reply, type in **Write a reply…**, add photos or files if needed, and select **Send**.

steps.text: If you see **Did this solve your problem?**, answer it.
substeps: Select **Yes, close it** if the problem is solved.
Select **No, still a problem**, and say what is still not working. Then select **Reopen**.

steps.text: To reopen a closed request, select **Reopen request**. Enter the reason, and then select **Reopen**.
steps.caption: The **Reopen this request?** dialog.
steps.alt: Reopen this request? dialog with a reason typed and the Cancel and Reopen buttons

steps: To rate the support, select from 1 to 5 stars under **How did we do?**. Add a comment if you like, and then select **Send rating**.
sections.result: A message confirms each action, such as **Reply sent.** or **Thank you for your feedback!**

blocks.caption: A closed request that you can rate and reopen.
blocks.alt: Request 1202 with the How did we do? rating card, the Reopen request button and the reply box highlighted and numbered

callouts: Rate the support. **Send rating** appears after you select the stars.
**Reopen request** and the last date you can reopen.
The reply box. Without a connection, the button says **Queue**.

blocks.warning: **Yes, close it** closes the request at once. It does not ask you to confirm.

sections.title: Start a new request
sections.intro: The **New request** form matches the portal's ticket form. It suggests articles that may already answer your question.
steps: Select the **New request** tab, or the plus button on **My tickets**.

steps.text: Enter a **Subject** of at least 5 characters.
steps.caption: The **New request** form with suggested articles.
steps.alt: New request form with a subject, suggested articles, Description and the About your request fields Department, Category, Product, Installation and Priority
steps.note: If a suggested article answers your question, select it to read it.

steps: Describe the problem in **Description**.
Choose the **Department**, **Category**, **Product**, **Installation** and **Priority**.
Fill in any extra fields. You must fill in the fields that have an asterisk.
To attach files, select **Camera** or **Files**.
Select **Submit request**.
sections.result: A message gives the new request number, such as **Request #1206 created — we will be in touch.**

blocks.p: The app saves the form on your phone as you type. Select **Clear form** to start again.

blocks.note: Without a connection, the button says **Save — submit when online**. The app submits the request when the connection returns.

sections.title: Read help articles
sections.intro: The **Help** tab has the same articles as the portal's knowledge base.
steps: Select the **Help** tab.
Choose a category chip, or keep **All** to see **Popular articles** and **Recently updated**.
To search, type in **Search the help center**.
Select an article to read it.
At the end, answer **Was this article helpful?** with **Yes** or **No**.
sections.result: **Thanks for the feedback!** appears. After **No**, you can select **New request**.

blocks.caption: The **Help** tab with categories and popular articles.
blocks.alt: Help tab with a search box, category chips and a list of popular articles

blocks.note: **Yes** and **No** send your answer at once. Search needs a connection, but articles you opened before stay readable offline.

blocks.p: Customer mode does not include the community, the assistant, troubleshooting guides, profile changes or contracts. Use the web portal for those.

sections.title: Work offline
intro: The app keeps a copy of the screens you opened. When the connection drops, you can still read them.
A banner under the title says you are offline. It also says how many messages wait to be sent.

blocks.caption: A ticket while the phone is offline, with a reply ready to queue.
blocks.alt: Ticket screen with the banner You are offline — showing saved data, read-only, grey chips, and a reply with the Queue button

rows: Show the saved copy, with the time it was saved. They refresh when the connection returns.
Saved on the phone as you type.
Wait in a queue. The button says **Queue**. The app sends them, with their attachments, when the connection returns.
Status, priority, assignee, approvals and ratings
Need a connection. Their buttons are grey while you are offline.
Needs a connection. If you were already signed in, the app opens your saved data.

blocks.p: A queued message is never sent twice, even if the app retries. If the team rejects a queued message, for example because the ticket closed, it shows **Not sent**. Choose **Retry**, **Edit** or **Discard**.
If a colleague replied first, a queued agent reply shows **Not sent — new messages arrived**. Read the new messages, and then choose **Send anyway**, **Edit** or **Discard**.

blocks.warning: Signing out deletes unsent messages from this phone. Check **Unsent messages** on the **Me** tab first.

sections.title: Push notifications
intro: The standard app does not send push notifications yet. The **Me** tab shows **Not available in this build**.
While the app is open, updates still arrive live. Agents see new alerts on the **Alerts** tab at once.
Your organisation can build a version of the app with push notifications. Then the **Me** tab has a **Push notifications on this device** switch.

chapters.title: Platform console
intro: This chapter is for platform operators. They are the people who run the SupportDesk service for all customer companies.
Each customer company is a tenant with its own workspace. In the platform console you look after tenants, plans, invoices and support access. You never see a tenant's tickets or customer data.

sections.title: What the platform console is for
intro: The platform console is separate from every workspace. You sign in with your own operator account, not with a workspace account.
Workspace users cannot open the console. Operators cannot open a workspace or act as one of its users. When a tenant needs help, you ask for support access instead.
The console records every change you make in the platform audit trail.

rows: See tenant counts, revenue and what needs your attention.
Find a tenant and see its subscription and usage. Suspend, reactivate, extend, change or cancel it.
Set the prices, limits and features that tenants can buy.
Check the invoices of all tenants. Record offline payments and void invoices.
Follow your requests to view a tenant's diagnostics, and open them once approved.
Search the record of platform actions and check that nobody changed it.

sections.title: Sign in to the platform console
sections.intro: Use your operator e-mail address and password. The console has its own sign-in page.
prerequisites: You have a platform operator account.

steps.text: On the desk sign-in page, select **Platform console**.
steps.caption: The **Platform console** link at the bottom of the desk sign-in page.
steps.alt: Desk sign-in card with the Platform console link highlighted
steps.tip: You can also open the console address that your team gave you.

steps: In **Operator e-mail**, enter the e-mail address of your operator account.
In **Password**, enter your password.
Select **Sign in**.
If the **Authenticator code** box appears, enter the code from your authenticator app. Then select **Sign in** again.
sections.result: The **Overview** page opens. Your name and the time left in your session show at the top right.

blocks.caption: The platform console sign-in page.
blocks.alt: Platform console sign-in card with numbered e-mail, password and Sign in controls

callouts: **Operator e-mail**: the e-mail address of your operator account.
**Password**: your operator password.
**Sign in**: checks your details and opens the console.

blocks.note: The **here** link under the title opens the workspace sign-in page. Use it if you meant to sign in to a workspace.

blocks: If a box is empty or the e-mail address is incomplete, a red message asks for both. Correct the boxes and select **Sign in** again.

blocks.caption: The message that asks for your e-mail address and password.
blocks.alt: Platform console sign-in card with the red message Enter your e-mail address and password.

sections.title: Your console session
intro: A console session lasts 30 minutes. The top bar shows the time left, for example **session ends in 12 min**.
When the time runs out, the sign-in page opens with a message. Sign in again to go on.
Reloading the page in the browser also ends the session. Move between pages with the console menu instead.

blocks.caption: The message on the sign-in page after your session ends.
blocks.alt: Platform console sign-in card with the message Your platform session ended. Sign in again.

steps: At the top right, select **Sign out**.

blocks: The sign-in page opens. Sign out when you finish, especially on a shared computer.

blocks.tip: The moon button next to your name switches to the dark theme. The sun button switches back.

sections.title: The Overview page
sections.intro: **Overview** is the first page after you sign in. It shows how the service is doing and what needs your attention.

blocks.caption: The **Overview** page with the figure tiles, the newest trials and recent platform activity.
blocks.alt: Platform console Overview page with six numbered areas

callouts: The console menu: **Overview**, **Tenants**, **Plans**, **Invoices**, **Support access** and **Audit**.
Your name, the time left in your session, the theme button and **Sign out**.
**Refresh** loads the latest figures.
The figure tiles. Select a tile to open the matching list.
**Trials**: the newest trial workspaces, with the trial end date and the subscription status.
**Recent platform activity**: the latest platform actions. **Open audit** opens the full trail.

rows: Workspaces still on their free trial.
The monthly value of all active and past-due subscriptions. Annual plans count as one twelfth.
Nothing. The tile only shows the figure.
The total of all unpaid invoices.
Unpaid invoices past their due date.
Support access requests that wait for a tenant's decision.

blocks.note: If the page cannot load, it says **The overview could not be loaded**. Select **Try again**.

sections.title: Find a tenant
sections.intro: Use **Tenants** to find a workspace and open its page.
steps: In the console menu, select **Tenants**.
In **Search**, enter part of the company name or the workspace name.

steps.text: In the **Status** list, choose a status, or choose **All**.
steps.note: The list updates as soon as you choose a status.

steps: Select **Search**.
Select the tenant's row.
sections.result: The tenant's page opens. It shows the workspace, subscription, usage, invoices, support access and recent activity.

blocks.caption: The **Tenants** list with the search box and the status filter.
blocks.alt: Tenants page with numbered Search box, Status list, Search button and a tenant row

callouts: **Search**: part of a company name or a workspace name.
**Status**: show only tenants with one status.
**Search**: runs the search.
A tenant row. Select it to open the tenant's page.

blocks.tip: On **Overview**, select the **On trial**, **Active** or **Suspended** tile. The list opens with that status already chosen.

blocks.note: The list shows 50 tenants at a time. To see more, select **Load more** at the bottom.

blocks: If nothing matches, the list says **No tenants match**. Clear the search box or the status filter.

sections.title: Tenant list columns and statuses
sections.intro: A tenant has a status of its own. Its subscription has a separate status, shown under the plan name.

rows: The company name, with the workspace name below. The words **dedicated DB** after it mean that the tenant's data is stored on its own.
The tenant's status. For a trial, the trial end date shows below.
The plan name, with the subscription status below.
The number of agents in the workspace.
The space that the workspace's files use.
The date the workspace was created.
How long ago someone last used the workspace. A dash means never.
The workspace is on its free trial.
Users can sign in, read and pay invoices. They cannot make any other change.
Access has stopped. The data is kept until the deletion date.
The deletion date has passed. The data is waiting to be deleted, and you cannot reactivate the tenant.
The trial ended or an invoice is overdue. The workspace keeps working until the grace period ends.
The grace period ended without payment, or an operator suspended the tenant.

sections.title: A tenant's page
sections.intro: A tenant's page brings together everything you need to look after that tenant. The **Actions** menu at the top right holds the changes you can make.

blocks.caption: The page of the tenant Wings Software.
blocks.alt: Tenant page with eight numbered areas from the breadcrumb to the activity list

callouts: The breadcrumb. Select **Tenants** to go back to the list.
**Actions**: the changes you can make to this tenant.
**Workspace**: status, workspace name, dates, country and time zone, and where the data is stored.
**Subscription**: plan, seats, billing cycle, status, key dates, amount due and billing contact.
**Usage vs limits**: what the workspace uses against the limits of its plan.
**Invoices**: recent invoices. Open invoices have a **Mark paid** button. The download button saves the PDF.
**Support access**: your requests to view this tenant's diagnostics. **Diagnostics** shows on your own requests while access is active.
**Recent platform and billing activity**: the latest operator, billing and system events for this tenant.

blocks: There is one meter for each plan limit, such as agents, portal users, storage and AI tokens. A striped bar means the plan has no limit.

list: The bar turns amber when the workspace uses 80% of a limit.
Over a limit, the meter says **Over the plan limit — new items are blocked.**
Monthly meters, such as AI tokens, start again each month.

blocks: A red banner shows on a suspended tenant. It gives the date and the reason for the suspension.
An amber banner shows on a cancelled tenant or one pending deletion. It gives the date when the data is deleted.

blocks.caption: A suspended tenant. The banner gives the date and the reason.
blocks.alt: Tenant page of Globex Retail with the red Suspended banner highlighted

sections.title: The Actions menu
sections.intro: Select **Actions** on a tenant's page to see what you can change. Items you cannot use right now are dimmed.

blocks.caption: The **Actions** menu of an active tenant. **Extend trial…** is dimmed because the tenant has no trial.
blocks.alt: Open Actions menu with Reactivate, Suspend, Extend trial, Change plan, Request support access, Move to dedicated database and Cancel subscription

rows: Restores full access after a suspension or a missed payment.
The tenant is suspended, or its subscription is **Past due**. Not when it is pending deletion.
Blocks all changes in the workspace at once. Users can still sign in, read and pay.
The tenant is not already suspended, cancelled or pending deletion.
Adds 1 to 90 days to the free trial.
The subscription has a trial end date.
Moves the tenant to another plan at once.
The tenant is not cancelled or pending deletion.
Asks the tenant for short, read-only access to diagnostics.
The tenant is not cancelled or pending deletion.
Moves the tenant's data to storage of its own.
The tenant uses shared storage and is not cancelled or pending deletion.
Stops access now and sets a date to delete the data.
The tenant is not already cancelled or pending deletion.

blocks.note: Each action takes effect as soon as you confirm it. The platform audit records who did it and why.

sections.title: Suspend a tenant
sections.intro: Suspend a tenant to stop all changes in its workspace at once. For example, do it before a move or when the customer asks for a pause.
prerequisites: The tenant is not already suspended, cancelled or pending deletion.
steps: Open the tenant's page. See [Find a tenant](#platform-find-tenant).
Select **Actions**.
Select **Suspend…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, enter why you are suspending the tenant.
steps.caption: The **Suspend tenant** panel with a reason filled in.
steps.alt: Suspend tenant panel with the Reason box and the Suspend button
steps.note: The tenant's administrators see this reason. Write it for them.

steps: Select **Suspend**.
sections.result: A message confirms **Tenant suspended**. A red banner on the tenant's page shows the date and your reason. Users can still sign in, read and pay, but they cannot make other changes.

blocks.note: Paying invoices does not lift a suspension that an operator set. Use [Reactivate a tenant](#platform-reactivate) to lift it.

sections.title: Reactivate a tenant
sections.intro: Reactivate a tenant to give back full access after a suspension or a missed payment.
prerequisites: The tenant is suspended, or its subscription is **Past due**.
The tenant is not pending deletion.
steps: Open the tenant's page.
Select **Actions**.
Select **Reactivate**.

steps.text: Optionally, in **Note**, enter why you are reactivating the tenant.
steps.caption: The **Reactivate tenant** panel.
steps.alt: Reactivate tenant panel with an optional Note box

steps: Select **Reactivate**.
sections.result: A message confirms **Tenant reactivated**. The workspace can make changes again.

blocks.note: A tenant that never moved to a paid plan returns to its trial. If the trial has already ended, extend it as well. See [Extend a trial](#platform-extend-trial).

sections.title: Extend a trial
sections.intro: Give a trial tenant more time to decide. This also works for a trial that has already ended.
prerequisites: The tenant's subscription has a trial end date.
steps: Open the tenant's page.
Select **Actions**.
Select **Extend trial…**.

steps.text: In **Extend the trial by (days)**, enter a number from 1 to 90.
steps.caption: The **Extend trial** panel. It suggests 14 days.
steps.alt: Extend trial panel with the number of days set to 14

steps: Select **Extend trial**.
sections.result: A message confirms **Trial extended**. The new trial end date shows under **Subscription**.

blocks.note: The extra days count from the current trial end or from today, whichever is later. Extending also lifts a past-due state or a suspension.

sections.title: Change a tenant's plan
sections.intro: Move a tenant to another plan, or change its seats or billing cycle. Use this when you agree a change with the customer.
prerequisites: The tenant is not cancelled or pending deletion.
steps: Open the tenant's page.
Select **Actions**.
Select **Change plan…**.

steps.text: In the **Plan** list, choose the new plan.
steps.caption: The **Change plan** panel with the tenant's current plan, seats and billing cycle.
steps.alt: Change plan panel with the Plan list, Seats box and Billing cycle list
steps.note: The list shows every plan with its price per agent per month, including hidden plans.

steps: In **Seats**, enter the number of agent seats.
In the **Billing cycle** list, choose **Monthly** or **Annual**.
Select **Change plan**.
sections.result: A message confirms **Plan changed**. The **Subscription** card shows the new plan.

blocks.warning: The change applies at once, without an extra invoice for the rest of the period. The console does not check that the tenant's current usage fits the new plan.

blocks: When a tenant administrator changes the plan in the workspace, the usual billing rules apply instead. Chapter 28 describes them.

sections.title: Request support access
sections.intro: Ask a tenant for short, read-only access to its diagnostics. Do this when the tenant asks for help with a problem you must look into.
prerequisites: The tenant is not cancelled or pending deletion.
You have no other pending or active request for this tenant.
steps: Open the tenant's page.
Select **Actions**.
Select **Request support access…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, explain why you need access. Name the ticket or case.
steps.caption: The **Request support access** panel with a reason and a duration.
steps.alt: Request support access panel with Reason box and Duration list
steps.note: The reason needs 10 to 1000 characters. The tenant's administrators read it before they decide.

steps: In the **Duration** list, choose **30 minutes**, **1 hour**, **4 hours** or **24 hours**.
Select **Send request**.
sections.result: A message confirms **Request sent**. The request shows with the status **Pending** on the tenant's page and on **Support access**.
blocks: The tenant's administrators approve or reject the request in their workspace. Chapter 26 describes their side. Once they approve it, the time you chose starts.

sections.title: Cancel a tenant's subscription
sections.intro: Cancel a subscription when a customer leaves. Tenants cannot cancel by themselves, so they ask you.
prerequisites: The tenant is not already cancelled or pending deletion.
steps: Open the tenant's page.
Select **Actions**.
Select **Cancel subscription…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, enter why the subscription ends.
steps.caption: The **Cancel subscription** panel with a reason and the number of days to keep the data.
steps.alt: Cancel subscription panel with Reason box and Keep data for (days) box

steps: In **Keep data for (days)**, enter how long to keep the data, from 0 to 365. The panel suggests 30.

steps.text: Select **Cancel subscription**.
steps.warning: Access stops at once. You cannot undo a cancellation in the console.

sections.result: A message confirms **Subscription cancelled**. An amber banner shows the date when the data is deleted. After that date, the tenant becomes **Pending deletion**.

sections.title: The Invoices page
sections.intro: **Invoices** lists the invoices of all tenants, newest first. SupportDesk issues them when a subscription period starts or a plan is upgraded. Tenants pay offline, for example by bank transfer.

blocks.caption: The **Invoices** page with invoices from several tenants.
blocks.alt: Invoices page with numbered status filter, invoice number, tenant name, status badge and Mark paid button

callouts: **Status**: show only invoices with one status.
The invoice number. Select it to open the invoice.
The tenant. Select it to open the tenant's page.
The invoice status.
**Mark paid**: records an offline payment. It shows only on unpaid invoices.

rows: The invoice waits for payment and is not yet due.
The invoice is unpaid after its due date.
An operator cancelled the invoice. Nobody needs to pay it.

blocks: The kind shows under the invoice number. **Subscription** is the regular invoice for a period. **Proration** charges for an upgrade in the middle of a period. **Manual** is a one-off invoice.

blocks.note: The list shows 50 invoices at a time. To see more, select **Load more**.

sections.title: Open an invoice and download its PDF
sections.intro: Open an invoice to check its lines and payment details, or to save it as a PDF.
steps: In the console menu, select **Invoices**.

steps.text: Select the invoice number.
steps.caption: An open invoice with its lines, totals and payment instructions.
steps.alt: Invoice panel for SD-WINGS-0006 with Download PDF, Void and Mark paid buttons

steps: To save the invoice, select **Download PDF**.
sections.result: The panel shows the period, the issue and due dates, the customer details, the lines and the totals. **How to pay** repeats the payment instructions printed on the invoice.

blocks.tip: On a tenant's page, the download button next to each invoice saves the PDF directly.

sections.title: Record an offline payment
sections.intro: When a tenant's bank transfer or cheque arrives, mark the invoice as paid. SupportDesk never stores card details.
prerequisites: The invoice is **Open** or **Overdue**.
You have checked that the money arrived.
steps: In the console menu, select **Invoices**.

steps.text: In the invoice's row, select **Mark paid**.
steps.note: You can also select **Mark paid…** in the invoice panel, or **Mark paid** on the tenant's page.

steps.text: Optionally, in **Payment reference**, enter the bank transfer number or the cheque number.
steps.caption: The panel that records an offline payment.
steps.alt: Mark SD-WINGS-0006 paid panel with the Payment reference box

steps.text: Select **Mark paid**.
steps.warning: You cannot undo this in the console.

sections.result: A message confirms that the invoice is marked paid. Its status changes to **Paid**.
blocks: If this was the tenant's last overdue invoice, the past-due state ends. A suspension caused by missed payment lifts too.

blocks.note: Payment does not lift a suspension that an operator set. Use [Reactivate a tenant](#platform-reactivate) for that.

sections.title: Void an invoice
sections.intro: Void an invoice that nobody should pay, for example one issued by mistake.
prerequisites: The invoice is **Open** or **Overdue**.
steps: In the console menu, select **Invoices**.
Select the invoice number.
Select **Void…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, enter why you are voiding the invoice.
steps.caption: The panel that voids an invoice. A reason is required.
steps.alt: Void SD-WINGS-0006 panel with the Reason box and the Void invoice button

steps.text: Select **Void invoice**.
steps.warning: You cannot undo this in the console.

sections.result: A message confirms that the invoice is voided. Its status changes to **Void**, and its notes keep your reason.

sections.title: The Plans page
sections.intro: **Plans** shows every plan as a card. Tenants choose from these plans at sign-up and when they change plan.

blocks.caption: The **Plans** page with the Trial, Starter, Professional and Enterprise plans.
blocks.alt: Plans page with numbered areas on the Starter plan card

callouts: **New plan**: creates a plan.
The number of tenants on the plan. A **Hidden** badge shows when new customers cannot choose the plan.
The price per agent per month, and per agent per year.
The plan's limits. **Unlimited** means there is no limit.
The features that the plan includes.
**Delete** and **Edit**. **Delete** is dimmed while tenants use the plan.

blocks.note: Large numbers follow your computer's regional format. For example, with Indian English settings, 1L is one lakh (100,000) and 1Cr is one crore (10,000,000).

sections.title: Create or edit a plan
sections.intro: Create a plan to offer a new package, or edit a plan to change its prices, limits or features.
steps: In the console menu, select **Plans**.
Select **New plan**, or select **Edit** on a plan's card.

steps.text: Fill in the plan details.
steps.caption: The **Edit plan** panel for the Professional plan.
steps.alt: Edit plan panel with code, name, prices, currency, trial days, limits, features and the sign-up switch
substeps: Enter the **Code** and the **Name**.
Enter the **Monthly price / agent**, the **Annual price / agent** and the **Currency**.
Enter the **Trial days** and the **Sort order**.

steps: Under **Limits**, enter the most that each tenant may use. Leave a box empty for no limit.
Under **Features**, tick the features that the plan includes.
Turn **Offered at sign-up and in plan comparison** on or off.
Select **Create plan** for a new plan, or **Save** for an existing one.
sections.result: A message confirms **Plan created** or **Plan saved**. The plan's card shows the new details.

blocks.warning: Changes to an existing plan apply to every tenant on it.

rows: A short lower-case name, such as `growth`. You cannot change it later.
The name that tenants see. Up to 100 characters.
The price for one agent for one month, from 0 to 1,000,000.
The price for one agent for one year, from 0 to 12,000,000.
A three-letter currency code, such as `USD` or `INR`.
The length of the free trial, from 0 to 365.
The plan's place in lists. Lower numbers come first.
**Agents**, **Light agents**, **Portal users**, **Storage (MB)**, **Channels**, **AI tokens / month**, **API calls / month**, **Attachment size (MB)** and **Brands**. Empty means unlimited.
The parts of SupportDesk that tenants on this plan may use, such as **AI assistant** or **Single sign-on**.
**Offered at sign-up and in plan comparison**
On: new customers can choose the plan. Off: the plan is hidden, but its tenants keep it.

blocks.note: These features are not enforced yet: **Automation rules**, **Blueprint workflows**, **Advanced analytics**, **Community forums**, **Telephony** and **ERP integration**. Turning them off does not block them in the app.

sections.title: Delete a plan
sections.intro: Delete a plan that no tenant uses. To retire a plan that tenants still use, hide it instead.
prerequisites: No tenant uses the plan. Its card says **0 tenants**.
The plan is not the trial plan, because sign-up needs it.
steps: In the console menu, select **Plans**.

steps.text: On the plan's card, select **Delete**.
steps.caption: The question that asks you to confirm the deletion.
steps.alt: Delete plan Professional dialog with Cancel and Delete buttons

steps.text: Select **Delete**.
steps.warning: The plan is removed for good. You cannot undo this.

sections.result: A message confirms **Plan deleted**. The card disappears from the page.

blocks.tip: To hide a plan, edit it and turn off **Offered at sign-up and in plan comparison**. Its card then shows a **Hidden** badge.

sections.title: Support access and diagnostics
intro: Operators never sign in as a tenant's users. When a tenant needs help, you ask for support access instead. The tenant's administrators decide, and the access ends on its own.
**Support access** lists the requests of all operators for all tenants, newest first.

blocks.caption: The **Support access** page with one request waiting for the tenant.
blocks.alt: Support access page with numbered Refresh button, tenant name, reason and Pending status

callouts: **Refresh** loads the latest decisions.
The tenant. Select it to open the tenant's page.
The reason given in the request.
The status. While access is active, the time left shows below it. After a decision, the name of the person who decided shows below it.

rows: The tenant's administrators have not decided yet.
You can open the diagnostics until the access ends.
The tenant's administrators ended the access early.
The time you asked for has run out.

list: The time when your access ends.
The usage meters, as on the tenant's page.
Counts of users, departments, statuses, categories, SLA policies, automation rules, channels and open tickets.
**Failed jobs**: background tasks that failed.
**Dead-letter events**: messages that the app gave up delivering after several tries.
**Recent audit**: the tenant's last 25 audit entries.

blocks.note: Diagnostics never show tickets, messages or customer details. Each view is recorded in the tenant's audit trail and in the platform audit.

sections.title: View a tenant's diagnostics
sections.intro: Look at a tenant's diagnostics while your approved access lasts.
prerequisites: The tenant's administrators approved your request, and the access has not ended.
You made the request yourself. Other operators cannot open your access.
steps: In the console menu, select **Support access**.
Find the request with the status **Approved**.
Select **Diagnostics**.
Read the usage, configuration and recent audit details.
Select **Close**.
sections.result: The **Diagnostics** panel opens with the details listed in [Support access and diagnostics](#platform-support-access).

blocks.tip: The tenant's page has the same **Diagnostics** button in its **Support access** list.

sections.title: Platform audit
intro: **Audit** is a tamper-evident record of platform operations. Each entry is sealed in a chain, so a changed or missing entry shows up when you check the chain.
The trail records operator sign-ins and every action an operator takes on tenants, plans, invoices and support access. It also records new sign-ups.

blocks.caption: The **Platform audit** page after **Verify chain**.
blocks.alt: Platform audit page with numbered Verify chain button, result message, search box, action filter and entries

callouts: **Verify chain**: checks that no sealed entry was changed or removed.
The result of the check.
**Search**: words from the summary, or the name of the person or service that acted.
**Action**: show only one kind of action.
The entries, newest first.

rows: The date and time of the action.
Who acted, with the kind of actor and the network address below.
A short name for the kind of action.
The tenant concerned. Select it to open the tenant's page. A dash means no tenant.
The entry's place in the chain. Three dots mean the entry is not sealed yet.

sections.title: Search the platform audit
sections.intro: Find out who did what, for example who suspended a tenant.
steps: In the console menu, select **Audit**.
In **Search**, enter words from the summary or the name of the person who acted.
In the **Action** list, choose a kind of action, or choose **All actions**.
Select **Search**.
sections.result: The list shows the matching entries, newest first. If nothing matches, it says **No audit entries match**.

blocks.note: The list shows 50 entries at a time. To see more, select **Load more**.

sections.title: Verify the audit chain
sections.intro: Check that nobody changed or removed platform audit entries. Do this regularly, and before you hand the trail to an auditor.
steps: In the console menu, select **Audit**.
Select **Verify chain**.
Read the message above the search box.
sections.result: **Chain intact** in green means the trail is complete. The message gives the number of sealed entries checked.

blocks.warning: **Chain broken** in red means an entry was changed or removed. The message gives the number of the first broken entry. Report it to your security lead at once.

blocks.note: This check covers the platform trail only. Each workspace checks its own trail in its audit log.

sections.title: Public sign-up
intro: New customers can start a free trial on their own from the sign-up page. Chapter 28 shows the steps they follow.
As an operator, you control which plans they can choose and how long their trial lasts. You do this on the **Plans** page.

list: The sign-up page offers every plan with **Offered at sign-up and in plan comparison** turned on.
The trial lasts as many days as the plan's **Trial days**, but never less than 14 days.
You cannot delete the trial plan, because sign-up needs it.
Each new workspace starts with 3 seats. The person who signs up becomes its administrator.
The new customer confirms their e-mail address with a 6-digit code. The code works for 30 minutes and allows 5 tries.
Taken and reserved workspace names are refused, for example `admin`, `support` or `demo`.
The app limits how many sign-ups come from one network or one e-mail address in an hour.
Each new trial shows on **Overview** under **Trials**, and in the platform audit.

blocks.warning: For testing, your hosting team can show the e-mail code on the sign-up page. This setting must stay off in the live service.

sections.title: Dedicated storage for large tenants
intro: By default, all tenants share one data store, and each tenant sees only its own data. A large tenant can move to a data store of its own.
The list of tenants always stays in the shared store.

list: The tenant's plan includes the **Dedicated database** feature. Of the standard plans, only Enterprise does.
Your hosting team has prepared a connection name for the tenant. The console never asks for technical connection details.
The app copies data only within the same storage system. To place a tenant elsewhere, your hosting team copies its data by hand first.
You have agreed a time with the tenant. Everyone in the workspace must sign in again after the move.

blocks: The app creates the new store and prepares it. It copies all the tenant's data, then switches the tenant over. Background work, such as sending e-mail and checking SLA timers, follows the tenant.

blocks.note: The old copy of the data stays in the shared store for safety. The console has no tool to remove it or to move the tenant back. Your hosting team does both by hand.

sections.title: Move a tenant to dedicated storage
sections.intro: Follow these steps in order. They keep the tenant's data safe during the copy.
prerequisites: You have read [Dedicated storage for large tenants](#platform-dedicated-about).
The tenant uses shared storage and is not cancelled or pending deletion.
steps: Suspend the tenant, so that nobody changes data during the copy. See [Suspend a tenant](#platform-suspend).
On the tenant's page, select **Actions** > **Move to dedicated database…**.

steps.text: Check the **Connection name**. The console suggests `tenant_` followed by the workspace name.
steps.caption: The panel that moves a tenant, with the suggested connection name.
steps.alt: Panel with the Connection name box set to tenant_wings and the Provision and move button
steps.note: Use 3 to 40 lower-case letters, digits or underscores. No other tenant may use the same name.

steps.text: Select **Provision and move**.
steps.warning: The move starts at once. You cannot undo it in the console.

steps: Wait for the result. It shows the new store's name, how much data was copied, and each step taken.
Select **Close**.
Check with the tenant that its users can sign in and see their data.
Reactivate the tenant. See [Reactivate a tenant](#platform-reactivate).
Ask your hosting team to remove the old copy from the shared store.
sections.result: On the tenant's page, **Workspace** shows the storage as **Dedicated**, with the connection name. The tenant list shows **dedicated DB** under the tenant's name.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **The workspace, e-mail or password is incorrect.**
troubleshooting.cause: One of the three details is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the workspace name, your e-mail and your password. Use the eye button to see what you typed.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **Enter your workspace name.**, **Enter a valid e-mail address.** or **Enter your password.**
troubleshooting.cause: A field is empty, or the e-mail address is not complete.
troubleshooting.fix: Fill in every field, then select **Sign in** again.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says your account is locked and gives a time to try again.
troubleshooting.cause: There were too many failed sign-ins in a row.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait until the time shown, then sign in again. Ask an administrator if you have forgotten your password.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.**
troubleshooting.cause: Too many sign-in attempts came in a short time.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait one minute, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **This workspace is suspended. Contact your administrator.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your company's subscription is suspended.
troubleshooting.fix: Contact your administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page says **Cannot reach SupportDesk. Check your connection and try again.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your device cannot reach SupportDesk.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your network connection, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page refuses your network or asks for single sign-on.
troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace allows sign-in only from certain networks, or requires single sign-on.
troubleshooting.fix: Connect from your office network or company VPN. Otherwise, ask your administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: **Two-step verification** says **That code is not valid or has expired.**
troubleshooting.cause: The code is wrong or too old.
troubleshooting.fix: Get a new code from the e-mail or the app, and enter it at once.

troubleshooting.problem: **Two-step verification** says **Enter the code (digits only).**
troubleshooting.cause: The code contains letters or spaces.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter only the digits of the code.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Password expired** page opens after you sign in.
troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace makes passwords expire after a set time.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to reset your password. Then select **Back to sign in**.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-in page shows **Your session ended.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your session timed out, or an administrator signed you out.
troubleshooting.fix: Sign in again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Change password** says **Use at least 12 characters.** or **The passwords do not match.**
troubleshooting.cause: The new password is too short, or the two new passwords differ.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a new password of 12 characters or more in both fields.

troubleshooting.problem: **Turn on** says **That code did not match. Try the current code.**
troubleshooting.cause: The code from the app was old or mistyped.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the app to show a new code, and enter it at once. Check that your phone's clock is correct.

troubleshooting.problem: A **Could not change availability** message appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The change did not reach SupportDesk.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your connection, then choose your availability again.

troubleshooting.problem: A bar says **Live updates paused — reconnecting…**
troubleshooting.cause: The live connection to SupportDesk dropped.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait. The bar disappears when the connection returns. Reload the page if it stays for long.

troubleshooting.problem: A Command Center card shows an error message with **Retry**.
troubleshooting.cause: The card could not load its data.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Retry**. If it fails again, check your connection.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Pending approvals** tile shows 0, but a colleague says a request is waiting.
troubleshooting.cause: You may not have permission to decide that request, or it belongs to another department.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your supervisor or administrator who can decide it.

troubleshooting.problem: **Approve** and **Reject** do not appear on a request.
troubleshooting.cause: You raised the request yourself, or your role cannot decide approvals.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask another supervisor to decide it.

troubleshooting.problem: An error appears when you select **Approve** or **Reject**.
troubleshooting.cause: Someone else decided the request first, or it has expired.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the message. The list reloads with the current status.

troubleshooting.problem: **Enable desktop alerts** does not appear on the Command Center.
troubleshooting.cause: You have already allowed or blocked desktop alerts in this browser.
troubleshooting.fix: To change your answer, open your browser's site settings for SupportDesk.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Deleted tickets** queue is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: You do not have the permission to delete tickets.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask a supervisor to restore the ticket, or ask your administrator for the permission.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Shared** option in **New view** shows **Needs supervisor rights**.
troubleshooting.cause: Only supervisors and administrators can share views.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a **Personal** view, or ask a supervisor to create the shared view.

troubleshooting.problem: **Create view** shows **Give the view a name.**
troubleshooting.cause: The **Name** field is empty.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a name, then select **Create view** again.

troubleshooting.problem: The bulk actions bar shows a permission message instead of buttons.
troubleshooting.cause: You do not have the bulk update permission.
troubleshooting.fix: Update the tickets one at a time, or ask a supervisor to do it.

troubleshooting.problem: A bulk update shows **Not updated** for some tickets.
troubleshooting.cause: Each listed ticket failed a rule, such as a status that is not allowed next.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the reason next to each ticket. Fix those tickets one at a time. They stay selected for you.

troubleshooting.problem: The list shows **No tickets match your filter**.
troubleshooting.cause: Nothing in this queue or view matches the text in the filter box.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the text, or clear the filter with [[Esc]]. Try another queue such as **All open**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Create ticket** does nothing, and some fields turn red.
troubleshooting.cause: A required field is empty or has the wrong format. For example, **Subject** shows **Enter a subject.**
troubleshooting.fix: Fix each field shown in red, then select **Create ticket** again.

troubleshooting.problem: A new contact shows **Give an e-mail address or a phone number.**
troubleshooting.cause: A new contact needs a way to reach them.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter an e-mail address, a phone number or both.

troubleshooting.problem: An attached file shows **Blocked by the virus scanner**.
troubleshooting.cause: The malware scan found a problem in the file.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the file. Ask the customer for a clean copy.

troubleshooting.problem: **Ticket not found** appears when you open a ticket.
troubleshooting.cause: The ticket was deleted or merged, or it is outside what you are allowed to see.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Close tab**. Check the number. If the ticket was merged, open the ticket it was merged into.

troubleshooting.problem: The quick edit fields or menu items are greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: You lack the permission, or someone else locked the ticket.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the header for **Locked by**. Wait for the lock to end, or ask a supervisor to unlock it.

troubleshooting.problem: The status you want is not in the **Status** list.
troubleshooting.cause: Your administrator limits which status can follow the current one, or the ticket follows a blueprint.
troubleshooting.fix: Move through an allowed status first, or use the **Blueprint** tab.

troubleshooting.problem: A status change shows **Some values were not accepted**.
troubleshooting.cause: A field is required for the new status, such as a vendor reference.
troubleshooting.fix: Fill in the field on the **Details** tab, select **Save**, then change the status again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Resolve** shows **Pick a resolution code.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace requires a resolution code.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a code in **Resolution code**, then select **Resolve**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Escalate** shows **Say why the ticket needs escalating.**
troubleshooting.cause: The **Reason** field is empty.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a reason, then select **Escalate** again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Reopen** shows **Say why the ticket is reopened.**
troubleshooting.cause: The **Reason** field is empty.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a reason, then select **Reopen** again.

troubleshooting.problem: A transfer shows **Approval requested** and the ticket does not move.
troubleshooting.cause: The department needs a supervisor's approval for transfers.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the approval. Check its progress on the **Approvals** page.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Someone else changed this ticket** dialog opens.
troubleshooting.cause: A colleague saved the ticket after you opened it.
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the values. Select **Keep theirs** or **Re-apply my change**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Split** shows **The new ticket needs a subject.**
troubleshooting.cause: The **New subject** field is empty.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a subject for the new ticket, then select **Split**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Send** stays greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: The editor is empty, a file is still uploading, or an e-mail reply has no address in **To**.
troubleshooting.fix: Write the message, wait for the uploads, and add a recipient.

troubleshooting.problem: The composer shows **You can view this ticket but not reply to it.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your role may view the ticket but not reply or add notes.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator for the reply or note permission, or ask a colleague to reply.

troubleshooting.problem: A panel says that new entries were added while you were writing.
troubleshooting.cause: The customer or a colleague posted on the ticket after you started typing.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the entries. Select **I've reviewed them — keep editing**, or **Send anyway**.

troubleshooting.problem: The reply was not sent, and a message says your text is kept.
troubleshooting.cause: The connection dropped, or SupportDesk refused the reply.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your connection and try again. Your text stays in the composer.

troubleshooting.problem: The draft status shows **Draft not saved**.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk could not save the draft, often because of the connection.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep the composer open. The draft saves again when you type, once the connection is back.

troubleshooting.problem: **Templates** shows **No templates available**.
troubleshooting.cause: No template is shared with you, and you have no personal templates.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to add templates for your team or department.

troubleshooting.problem: An attachment shows **Blocked by the virus scanner**.
troubleshooting.cause: The malware scan found a problem in the file.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the file and attach a clean copy.

troubleshooting.problem: **Share to Teams/Slack** shows **No channels**.
troubleshooting.cause: No Teams or Slack channel is set up for the workspace.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to add one under **Administration** > **Teams & Slack**.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Accept** buttons in the Live chat console are greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: You are at your chat limit. The counter next to **Waiting** is red.
troubleshooting.fix: End or transfer one of your chats. If you need more chats at once, ask your manager to raise your chat limit.

troubleshooting.problem: You see **Your routing profile does not allow live chats (chat limit 0).**
troubleshooting.cause: Your chat limit is 0, so you take no chats.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your manager to set a chat limit above 0 in your routing profile.

troubleshooting.problem: You see **Another agent already accepted this chat.**
troubleshooting.cause: A colleague accepted the same chat a moment before you.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another chat in the **Waiting** list.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Templates** menu in a chat is greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: The chat has no ticket yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Accept the chat first. SupportDesk creates the ticket when an agent takes the chat.

troubleshooting.problem: There is no reply box for an e-mail or WhatsApp conversation.
troubleshooting.cause: Only live chats have a reply box in the Inbox.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Reply on ticket #** and reply on the ticket. The reply goes out on the same channel.

troubleshooting.problem: A transfer shows **The chat is already with this agent.** or says the agent is not a member of that department.
