troubleshooting.cause: You chose the agent who already has the chat, or an agent outside the chosen department.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another agent, or choose **Another department** and pick the right department first.

troubleshooting.problem: A message in the Inbox says **Could not load conversations**.
troubleshooting.cause: The connection to SupportDesk dropped for a moment.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Retry**. If it keeps happening, check your network connection.

troubleshooting.problem: You do not hear a sound for new chats.
troubleshooting.cause: The sound is off, or your browser blocks desktop alerts.
troubleshooting.fix: In the Live chat console, turn the sound button on. Select the bell button and allow notifications in your browser.

troubleshooting.problem: A customer page says **Customer not found**.
troubleshooting.cause: The customer was deleted, or your role shows only the customers you manage.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the name in the **Customers** list. Ask your supervisor if you need to see that customer.

troubleshooting.problem: A customer page says **This customer was merged**.
troubleshooting.cause: Someone merged this customer into another one.
troubleshooting.fix: Select the button on the page to open the customer that was kept.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Merge…** or **Review & merge** button is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: You do not have permission to merge customers or contacts.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask a supervisor or an administrator to do the merge.

troubleshooting.problem: Saving a new contact fails and the message suggests the duplicate finder.
troubleshooting.cause: Another contact already uses the same e-mail address or phone number.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the **Duplicates** tab and merge the two contacts, or edit the existing contact instead.

troubleshooting.problem: **Location** and **Department** are greyed out in the contact form.
troubleshooting.cause: No customer is chosen yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose the **Customer** first. Its locations and departments then appear.

troubleshooting.problem: A deleted location is still listed, marked **Inactive**.
troubleshooting.cause: Contacts, installations or tickets use it, so SupportDesk keeps it for history.
troubleshooting.fix: No action is needed. An inactive location is not offered for new records.

troubleshooting.problem: **Send invitation** is missing on a contact's page.
troubleshooting.cause: The contact has no e-mail address, is not active, or you cannot manage portal access.
troubleshooting.fix: Add an e-mail address and make sure the contact is active. Ask an administrator for the permission if needed.

troubleshooting.problem: The **ERP records** tab says **Wings ERP is not connected**.
troubleshooting.cause: Nobody has connected Wings ERP to SupportDesk yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to connect it under **Products & Assets** > **ERP integration**.

troubleshooting.problem: The **ERP records** tab says **ERP records unavailable**.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk could not reach Wings ERP at that moment.
troubleshooting.fix: Try again later. If the message stays, tell your administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot see **New product**, **Edit** or the delete buttons in the catalog.
troubleshooting.cause: By default, only administrators can manage products.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to make the change.

troubleshooting.problem: Deleting a product, version, installation or asset did not remove it.
troubleshooting.cause: Tickets, installations or contracts refer to it. SupportDesk retires it, marks it **End of life** or **Decommissioned**, and keeps it for history.
troubleshooting.fix: No action is needed. It can no longer be chosen for new records.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says a family still has products.
troubleshooting.cause: You tried to delete a family that has products.
troubleshooting.fix: Edit each product and choose another family. Then delete the family.

troubleshooting.problem: The bin button of a release is greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: Installations run this release.
troubleshooting.fix: Move those installations to another release first, or keep the release.

troubleshooting.problem: A ticket shows **Not entitled** although the customer has an active contract.
troubleshooting.cause: The contract's entitlements do not cover the ticket's product, installation or asset, or the allowance is used up.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the contract's entitlements. If the work should go ahead, override the eligibility with a reason.

troubleshooting.problem: **Override entitlement…** is greyed out in the **More actions** menu.
troubleshooting.cause: You do not have permission to override eligibility.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask a supervisor to override it.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Override entitlement** dialog says **A reason is required for the audit trail.**
troubleshooting.cause: The **Reason** box is empty.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter why you are overriding, then select **Override**.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says **Eligibility check failed**.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk could not check the contracts at that moment.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Check** again. If it keeps failing, tell your administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: Saving an article shows **Check the highlighted fields**.
troubleshooting.cause: A required field is empty or a value is not allowed.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the red message under each field. For example, give the article a title, write a body, or add an access rule.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **The expiry date is before the review date** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: **Expires** is earlier than **Review due**.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose an expiry date after the review date, or clear one of them.

troubleshooting.problem: The dialog **Someone else changed this article** appears when you save.
troubleshooting.cause: Another person saved a newer version after you opened the article.
troubleshooting.fix: Copy your changes, then select **Reload latest** and add them again. Or select **Keep editing**.

troubleshooting.problem: A note says **You can read this article but not edit it in its current state**.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role cannot edit articles in this status, such as articles in review.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask a reviewer or publisher, or wait until the article is a draft again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Article not found** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The article was deleted, or you cannot see internal articles.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Back to articles**. Ask an administrator if you need access to internal articles.

troubleshooting.problem: **Image upload failed** appears in the editor.
troubleshooting.cause: The image could not be uploaded, for example because it is too large.
troubleshooting.fix: Make the image smaller and try again.

troubleshooting.problem: A category cannot be deleted.
troubleshooting.cause: It still contains articles or sub-categories.
troubleshooting.fix: Move its articles and sub-categories to another category first.

troubleshooting.problem: **Publish** is missing on a flow.
troubleshooting.cause: Only people who can publish articles can publish flows.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask a publisher to publish the flow.

troubleshooting.problem: **Import failed** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The file type or its content could not be read.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a file exported from SupportDesk, or a ZIP, Markdown or HTML file. Check the **Issues** list after a partial import.

troubleshooting.problem: An AI button shows **AI is turned off for this organisation**.
troubleshooting.cause: An administrator turned off AI.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to turn it on in **AI settings**.

troubleshooting.problem: An AI part says the feature is turned off.
troubleshooting.cause: An administrator turned off this AI feature.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to turn the feature on in **AI settings**.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **This AI feature is not included in your plan** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: Your subscription does not include the feature.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator about upgrading the plan.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **Your role cannot use this AI feature** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role is not allowed to use that AI feature.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to change your role.

troubleshooting.problem: An AI request fails with a message about the monthly budget.
troubleshooting.cause: The workspace has used its AI budget for this month.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to raise the budget, or wait for the next month.

troubleshooting.problem: The **AI** tab or the **AI Assistant** menu item is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: You lack the AI permission, or your plan has no AI.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **Use AI assistance (summaries, suggestions, classification)** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: **Ask analytics** shows **No matching tickets**.
troubleshooting.cause: No tickets match the question in that period.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask about a longer period, such as the last 90 days.

troubleshooting.problem: **Approve & apply**, **Reject** and **Revert** are missing on proposals.
troubleshooting.cause: You can view proposals but not decide them.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: The page says **Personal analytics** and shows only your tickets.
troubleshooting.cause: You do not have team analytics.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **View team, department and organisation analytics** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: A widget or report says **No data**.
troubleshooting.cause: Nothing matches the period and filters.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a longer period or remove some filters.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Scheduled** or **Exports** tab is missing, or says it is not available.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role lacks the schedule or export permission.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for **Schedule report delivery** or **Export reports (CSV/Excel/PDF)**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Export failed** or **Download failed** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The file could not be built or fetched.
troubleshooting.fix: Try again. If it keeps failing, export a shorter period.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **Export still running** appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The report is large.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the **Exports** tab later and select **Download**.

troubleshooting.problem: Saving a schedule shows a red message under a field.
troubleshooting.cause: A value is missing or not allowed, such as a wrong e-mail address or time zone.
troubleshooting.fix: Correct the field. Use a time zone name such as `Asia/Kolkata`.

troubleshooting.problem: Figures look out of date.
troubleshooting.cause: Some ticket figures have not been calculated yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **...** > **Rebuild metrics from tickets**, or ask a supervisor to do it.

troubleshooting.problem: The board says **The built-in tracker is not set up**.
troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace does not use the built-in engineering board yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to set it up under **Administration** > **Engineering**.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Engineering** menu item or the ticket's **Engineering** tab is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role does not include an engineering permission.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **View the engineering board, work items and releases** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot drag cards, and the card menu is missing.
troubleshooting.cause: You can view the board but not change work items.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator for the **Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases** permission.

troubleshooting.problem: The ticket's **Engineering** tab says that no engineering tracker is set up.
troubleshooting.cause: No tracker is connected.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to connect Azure DevOps, GitHub or the built-in board.

troubleshooting.problem: A linked work item shows **Sync failed**.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk could not reach the external tracker.
troubleshooting.fix: Select the refresh button on the item later. If it keeps failing, tell your administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: The bin button of a release is unavailable.
troubleshooting.cause: Work items are still planned for that release.
troubleshooting.fix: Move those work items to another release, or set them to **Not planned**. Then delete the release.

troubleshooting.problem: The message **Could not move** a work item appears.
troubleshooting.cause: Someone else changed the work item at the same time.
troubleshooting.fix: The board reloads. Move the card again.

troubleshooting.problem: The bell panel says **Notifications could not be loaded.**
troubleshooting.cause: The desk could not fetch your notifications.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Retry**. If it fails again, check your connection.

troubleshooting.problem: Some notifications stay unread after **Mark all read**.
troubleshooting.cause: Items that need acknowledgement are not marked by **Mark all read**.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Acknowledge** on each of them.

troubleshooting.problem: The number on the bell is lower than the **Unread** count on the **Notifications** page.
troubleshooting.cause: The bell counts only the latest notifications in its panel.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the **Notifications** page and use the **Unread** filter.

troubleshooting.problem: A **Could not acknowledge** or **Could not mark all as read** message appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The change did not reach SupportDesk.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your connection, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: You get no desktop alerts.
troubleshooting.cause: Desktop alerts are not allowed in this browser, or your computer is in a do-not-disturb mode.
troubleshooting.fix: Allow notifications for SupportDesk in your browser's site settings. Check your computer's notification settings too.

troubleshooting.problem: Your plan allows a number of agents and they are in use.
troubleshooting.cause: Every agent seat of the plan is taken. Pending invitations also use a seat.
troubleshooting.fix: Deactivate an agent or revoke an unused invitation. Or upgrade the plan.

troubleshooting.problem: Your plan allows a number of light agents and they are in use.
troubleshooting.cause: The light-agent limit of the plan is reached.
troubleshooting.fix: Deactivate a light agent, or upgrade the plan.

troubleshooting.problem: "The department has 21 open tickets. Choose a department to move them to."
troubleshooting.cause: You archive a department that still has open tickets.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a department in **Move open tickets to**, then select **Archive**.

troubleshooting.problem: "A brand/portal uses this department as its default."
troubleshooting.cause: A brand sends its portal tickets to this department.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the brand's default department first, then archive.

troubleshooting.problem: "10 open tickets are queued in this team. Move them before deleting the team."
troubleshooting.cause: The team still has tickets in its queue.
troubleshooting.fix: Assign or move the queued tickets, then delete the team.

troubleshooting.problem: "This is a department's default routing team."
troubleshooting.cause: You try to delete a department's routing team.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another **Routing team** on the department first.

troubleshooting.problem: "You cannot deactivate your own account."
troubleshooting.cause: You opened your own agent page.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask another administrator to deactivate your account.

troubleshooting.problem: "This overlaps another leave request."
troubleshooting.cause: The agent already has leave in that period.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the dates, or cancel the other request first.

troubleshooting.problem: "Another delegation for this agent overlaps the period."
troubleshooting.cause: Two delegations of one agent cannot cover the same time.
troubleshooting.fix: End or edit the other delegation, or pick other dates.

troubleshooting.problem: An agent never gets new tickets.
troubleshooting.cause: The agent is offline, off shift, on leave, delegated, at capacity, a light agent, or not a team member.
troubleshooting.fix: Use **Test routing** on the **Teams** tab. The **Result** column gives the reason for each agent.

troubleshooting.problem: "The default policy cannot be deleted."
troubleshooting.cause: Every workspace needs a fallback policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Make another policy the default first. Then delete the old one.

troubleshooting.problem: "Tickets have used this policy, so it is kept for reproducibility."
troubleshooting.cause: Past tickets refer to the policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Clear **Active** and save the policy instead of deleting it.

troubleshooting.problem: "Contracts reference this policy."
troubleshooting.cause: One or more contracts name this policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Change those contracts first, then delete the policy.

troubleshooting.problem: "Departments, SLA policies or contracts use this calendar."
troubleshooting.cause: You try to delete a calendar that is in use.
troubleshooting.fix: Check **Used by** under the calendar. Change those items first.

troubleshooting.problem: "The default calendar cannot be deleted."
troubleshooting.cause: The default calendar is the fallback for new items.
troubleshooting.fix: Make another calendar the default first.

troubleshooting.problem: A ticket gets the wrong policy.
troubleshooting.cause: A policy higher in the evaluation order also matches, or a contract sets the policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Open a policy and use **Simulate against a ticket**. The list shows why each policy was selected or skipped.

troubleshooting.problem: Due times ignore weekends.
troubleshooting.cause: **Business** is not ticked for that target, or the calendar is open 24x7.
troubleshooting.fix: Tick **Business** for the target and choose a calendar with weekly hours.

troubleshooting.problem: The policy form fields are greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role does not include `admin.sla`.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator to change the policy, or to give you the permission.

troubleshooting.problem: **New role** and **Clone** are turned off.
troubleshooting.cause: Your plan does not include custom roles.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade to a plan with custom roles, such as Professional or Enterprise.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says you cannot manage a role because it includes permissions you do not have.
troubleshooting.cause: The escalation guard stops you giving or editing rights you do not hold yourself.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator who holds those permissions to make the change.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says you cannot manage a role because its data scope is broader than yours.
troubleshooting.cause: The role sees more tickets or customers than you do.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator with a broader scope to make the change.

troubleshooting.problem: "This change would leave the organisation without an administrator."
troubleshooting.cause: The change removes the last active user who can manage roles.
troubleshooting.fix: Give another user the Administrator role first.

troubleshooting.problem: "System roles cannot be changed. Clone the role to customise it."
troubleshooting.cause: Built-in roles are read-only.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Clone to customise** and edit the copy.

troubleshooting.problem: "Single sign-on gives this role to new users."
troubleshooting.cause: You try to delete the single sign-on default role.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another default role under **Security & sign-in** > single sign-on first.

troubleshooting.problem: A user still cannot see some tickets after you add a permission.
troubleshooting.cause: The data scope of their roles hides those tickets.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the **Data scope** of the user's roles. The broadest scope across their roles applies.

troubleshooting.problem: "Every category needs at least one active status."
troubleshooting.cause: You turned off the last active status of a category.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep at least one active status in each category, or create another one first.

troubleshooting.problem: "Built-in statuses cannot be deleted."
troubleshooting.cause: The status has the **Built-in** badge.
troubleshooting.fix: Rename it, or turn off **Active** if the category has another active status.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says tickets use the status you want to delete.
troubleshooting.cause: Tickets still have this status.
troubleshooting.fix: Move those tickets to another status, or turn off **Active**.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says tickets use the category or issue type you want to delete.
troubleshooting.cause: Tickets refer to the category or issue type.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off **Active**. The item disappears from forms but stays on old tickets.

troubleshooting.problem: "Delete or move the subcategories first."
troubleshooting.cause: The category still has subcategories.
troubleshooting.fix: Delete the subcategories, or give them another parent category.

troubleshooting.problem: "Another field already uses this key."
troubleshooting.cause: Keys must be unique for each record type.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a different **Key**.

troubleshooting.problem: "A field must be visible in the portal to be editable there."
troubleshooting.cause: **Customers can fill it in when raising a ticket** is on, but **Customers see it in the portal** is off.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on **Customers see it in the portal** too.

troubleshooting.problem: "Another active layout already covers this department, brand and channel."
troubleshooting.cause: Two active layouts would apply to the same form.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the department, brand or channel, or turn off **Active** on one layout.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says a field cannot be placed on a portal form.
troubleshooting.cause: The field is not one customers may fill in.
troubleshooting.fix: Use it on an agent form, or set the custom field as editable in the portal.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says a channel for this address already exists.
troubleshooting.cause: Another channel of the same type already uses that address or number.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the existing channel and change it, or use a different address.

troubleshooting.problem: The app asks for the number in international format.
troubleshooting.cause: The number does not start with + and the country code.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter the number like `+91 80 4000 1234`.

troubleshooting.problem: **Test connection** shows **Failed**.
troubleshooting.cause: A server name, port, security option or credential is wrong, or the provider is not reachable.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the reason under the buttons. Check the values with your provider, save, and test again.

troubleshooting.problem: A mailbox stopped receiving mail after a server change.
troubleshooting.cause: The server's encryption key changed, so saved credentials cannot be read.
troubleshooting.fix: Open each channel, type the credentials again and select **Save changes**.

troubleshooting.problem: The provider stopped delivering messages after **Rotate key**.
troubleshooting.cause: Rotating the key ends the old callback address at once.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Copy URL** and enter the new address at the provider.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot add another channel.
troubleshooting.cause: Your plan allows a set number of channels.
troubleshooting.fix: Deactivate a channel you do not use, or ask for a bigger plan.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the channel was changed by someone else.
troubleshooting.cause: Another administrator saved the channel after you opened it.
troubleshooting.fix: Reload the page, make your change again and save.

troubleshooting.problem: Customers do not get an acknowledgement e-mail.
troubleshooting.cause: The mailbox switch or the workspace setting is off, or the sender reached three acknowledgements in an hour.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on **Send automatic acknowledgements** on the mailbox. Also turn on the acknowledgement setting in ticket configuration.

troubleshooting.problem: **Publish** stays greyed out, or a red box lists problems.
troubleshooting.cause: The rule or blueprint has errors, such as a missing action or an unknown field.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Check**, then fix each item under **Fix these before publishing:**.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot turn on a rule's switch.
troubleshooting.cause: The rule has no published version.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the rule and select **Publish** first.

troubleshooting.problem: A rule did not act on a ticket.
troubleshooting.cause: The conditions did not match, the rule was inactive, or an earlier rule stopped processing.
troubleshooting.fix: Open **Executions**, enter the ticket number and select **Details** on the run.

troubleshooting.problem: A rule shows **Skipped Loop**.
troubleshooting.cause: Rules started each other in a long chain, so SupportDesk stopped it.
troubleshooting.fix: Add a condition so that the rules do not trigger each other.

troubleshooting.problem: The webhook address is refused.
troubleshooting.cause: It is not a full web address, contains a user name or password, or points inside your network.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a full public address that starts with https://.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the signing secret is too short.
troubleshooting.cause: Secrets need at least 16 characters.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a longer secret, or leave the field empty to let SupportDesk create one.

troubleshooting.problem: A webhook switched itself off.
troubleshooting.cause: It failed 20 times in a row.
troubleshooting.fix: Fix the receiving system. Turn the webhook on, then redeliver the failed messages.

troubleshooting.problem: **Delete blueprint** is greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: Open tickets still follow the blueprint.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off the blueprint's switch. Delete it after its tickets are closed.

troubleshooting.problem: **Test saved provider** shows **Chat failed**.
troubleshooting.cause: The model name, address or key is wrong, or the service cannot be reached.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the values with your AI account, select **Save settings** and test again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Embeddings failed** after you switch provider.
troubleshooting.cause: The provider cannot create embeddings, or the embedding model is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose **Local (feature hashing, 384 dims)** as the **Embedding provider**, save, and test again.

troubleshooting.problem: AI features stop working in the middle of the month.
troubleshooting.cause: The monthly budget is used up and the budget action is **Block**.
troubleshooting.fix: Raise the **Monthly budget** or choose **Warn**, then save. The log shows **Budget exceeded** for blocked calls.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says to check the highlighted fields.
troubleshooting.cause: A setting is outside its allowed range, such as a log period under 7 days.
troubleshooting.fix: Correct the fields marked in red and save again.

troubleshooting.problem: The auto-responder never replies by itself.
troubleshooting.cause: No enabled scenario matches, the agent is in **Suggest only** mode, or the ticket is critical.
troubleshooting.fix: Add and enable a scenario, and set the agent to **Act on low-risk**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says every scenario needs a name.
troubleshooting.cause: A scenario card has an empty **Name**.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a name or remove the empty card, then select **Save scenarios**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the portal address is already taken.
troubleshooting.cause: Another workspace or brand uses that address.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another **Portal address**, for example by adding your city or product.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the address is reserved.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk uses that word itself, such as `admin` or `portal`.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another **Portal address**.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot create another brand.
troubleshooting.cause: Your plan allows a set number of brands.
troubleshooting.fix: Delete or reuse a brand you do not need, or ask for a bigger plan.

troubleshooting.problem: **Help center is online** cannot be switched off.
troubleshooting.cause: It is the default brand. Its help center must stay online.
troubleshooting.fix: Make another brand the default first.

troubleshooting.problem: **Make default brand** is greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: The brand's help center is offline.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on **Help center is online**, save, and try again.

troubleshooting.problem: A brand cannot be deleted.
troubleshooting.cause: It is the default brand, or tickets or channels belong to it.
troubleshooting.fix: Move its channels to another brand, or switch its help center off instead.

troubleshooting.problem: The logo upload fails.
troubleshooting.cause: The file is over 2 MB, or it is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image.
troubleshooting.fix: Make the image smaller or save it in a supported format.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the domain is already used.
troubleshooting.cause: Another help center uses that domain.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a different domain, or remove it from the other brand first.

troubleshooting.problem: **Check DNS** shows **Points elsewhere**.
troubleshooting.cause: The DNS record points to another address, or the change has not spread yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your IT team to check the record against the **Points to** value. Wait an hour and check again.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the template has unknown placeholders.
troubleshooting.cause: The subject or body contains a placeholder that this template does not support.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove it, or insert one of the chips shown next to **Insert:**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app asks for a subject or a body.
troubleshooting.cause: The **Subject** or **Body (HTML)** is empty or too long.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a subject of up to 500 characters and a body.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says to set both the start and the end of quiet hours.
troubleshooting.cause: Only one of **From** and **Until** has a time.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter both times, or turn off **Quiet hours**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says quiet hours must end at a different time.
troubleshooting.cause: **From** and **Until** are the same.
troubleshooting.fix: Change one of the times.

troubleshooting.problem: A **Discard unsaved changes?** message appears when you leave the page.
troubleshooting.cause: You changed something and did not save it.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Keep editing** and save. Or select **Discard changes** to leave without saving.

troubleshooting.problem: Agents get no notification e-mails at night.
troubleshooting.cause: Quiet hours are on. E-mail and push wait until they end.
troubleshooting.fix: This is expected. Critical alerts still go out.

troubleshooting.problem: The app does not save the allow-list. It says saving would lock you out.
troubleshooting.cause: Your own address is not in **Addresses and ranges**.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Add my address**, and then select **Save policies**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says an entry is not an IP address or range.
troubleshooting.cause: An entry in **Addresses and ranges** has a typing mistake.
troubleshooting.fix: Put one entry on each line, such as `203.0.113.7` or `10.0.0.0/8`.

troubleshooting.problem: An agent sees that access from their network is not allowed by your organisation.
troubleshooting.cause: The agent works from an address outside the agent IP allow-list.
troubleshooting.fix: Add their office range to the list, or ask them to connect through the company network.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the idle timeout cannot exceed the absolute lifetime.
troubleshooting.cause: **Idle timeout (minutes)** is longer than **Absolute session lifetime (hours)**.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower the idle timeout, or raise the absolute lifetime.

troubleshooting.problem: **Test connection** on the **Single sign-on** tab shows **Failed**.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk cannot reach the issuer address, or the address is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check **Authority (issuer)**. It must start with `https://` and match the address your provider shows.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the scopes must include openid.
troubleshooting.cause: The **Scopes** field on the **Single sign-on** tab lacks `openid`.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter `openid profile email`, or add `openid` to your list.

troubleshooting.problem: A scope has a lock icon, or the app says the scopes grant rights you do not have.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role lacks the rights that the scope gives.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator who holds those rights to create the credential.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says only administrators who see the whole organisation can issue credentials.
troubleshooting.cause: Your role sees only some departments or teams.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator with organisation-wide data scope.

troubleshooting.problem: The app asks you to choose an expiry between now and three years ahead.
troubleshooting.cause: **Expires on** is too soon or too far away.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a date from tomorrow up to three years ahead, or leave it empty.

troubleshooting.problem: An integration stopped working after you replaced a secret.
troubleshooting.cause: The other system still uses the old secret.
troubleshooting.fix: Update the other system with the new client secret, or create a new key.

troubleshooting.problem: The ERP status shows **Error**.
troubleshooting.cause: The ERP did not answer, or it refused SupportDesk's sign-in.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the error next to the badge. Select **Test connection**, then check the address, the sign-in details and the integration log.

troubleshooting.problem: **Sync now** is greyed out on the ERP page.
troubleshooting.cause: **Integration enabled** is off.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on **Integration enabled**, and select **Save settings**.

troubleshooting.problem: A tracker test shows **Connection problem**.
troubleshooting.cause: The address, the project or repository, or the token is wrong. The token may also lack rights.
troubleshooting.fix: Edit the tracker and check each field. Give the token the rights listed under its field.

troubleshooting.problem: Escalated tickets do not update when engineers fix the work item.
troubleshooting.cause: The tracker webhook is not set up, or its secret is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check **Deliveries & call log**. Set up the webhook again, or replace the webhook secret.

troubleshooting.problem: A Teams or Slack channel shows **Failing**.
troubleshooting.cause: Someone removed or changed the webhook in Teams or Slack.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a new incoming webhook. Edit the channel, paste the new address and select **Send test**.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says to choose at least one event.
troubleshooting.cause: No event is ticked under **Post these events**.
troubleshooting.fix: Tick at least one event, and save again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Entity id** shows an error when you select **Apply**.
troubleshooting.cause: The value is not a complete record identifier.
troubleshooting.fix: Copy the identifier from the **Entity** line of another entry, or clear the field.

troubleshooting.problem: **Export CSV** is refused.
troubleshooting.cause: Your plan does not include **Audit export**.
troubleshooting.fix: Change to a plan with **Audit export**. See the plan comparison on the **Subscription** page.

troubleshooting.problem: **Verify chain** says **Audit chain broken!**.
troubleshooting.cause: An audit entry was changed or removed outside SupportDesk.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Open entry** to see the first bad entry. Tell your security team and your SupportDesk provider at once.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says a policy must keep data for at least a number of days.
troubleshooting.cause: **After (days)** is below the minimum for that kind of data.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter at least the minimum shown under **After (days)**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Approve erasure** is greyed out, and the row says **Blocked by a legal hold**.
troubleshooting.cause: An active legal hold covers the contact.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait until the matter is closed. Then release the hold and approve the request.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says another compliance administrator must approve the erasure.
troubleshooting.cause: You made the request yourself. A second person must approve it.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask another administrator with the compliance permission to approve it.

troubleshooting.problem: The export download link does not work.
troubleshooting.cause: The link works once and expires after 24 hours.
troubleshooting.fix: Record a new export request for the contact.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the file is larger than 20 MB.
troubleshooting.cause: The file is too big to import.
troubleshooting.fix: Export fewer sections in the source workspace, and import them in parts.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the file is not valid.
troubleshooting.cause: The file is not a SupportDesk configuration export, or someone edited it.
troubleshooting.fix: Export the file again from the source workspace. Do not edit it by hand.

troubleshooting.problem: After publishing, the app says some references were not found.
troubleshooting.cause: The file names departments, teams, users or brands that this workspace does not have.
troubleshooting.fix: Create the missing items with the same names. Then import the file again.

troubleshooting.problem: Imported channels do not receive messages.
troubleshooting.cause: Imported channels start inactive, without passwords or tokens.
troubleshooting.fix: Open each channel, enter its sign-in details and activate it.

troubleshooting.problem: **Roll back** is greyed out on a snapshot.
troubleshooting.cause: It is the newest snapshot, which matches the current state.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose an older snapshot.

troubleshooting.problem: A plan change is refused because current usage does not fit the plan.
troubleshooting.cause: You use more agents, portal users, storage or channels than the new plan allows.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the conflicts in the preview. Reduce your usage, or choose a larger plan.

troubleshooting.problem: A usage meter says **Over the plan limit — new items are blocked.**
troubleshooting.cause: You reached a hard limit of your plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade the plan, or remove items you no longer need.

troubleshooting.problem: Every change fails with a message that the account is suspended.
troubleshooting.cause: Invoices stayed unpaid after the grace period.
troubleshooting.fix: Pay the overdue invoices by bank transfer. The **Subscription** page lists them. If you already paid, contact your SupportDesk provider.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-up form says the workspace name is not available.
troubleshooting.cause: Another company uses that name, or it is reserved.
troubleshooting.fix: Select the suggested name, or enter another one of at least 3 letters or digits.

troubleshooting.problem: The sign-up code does not work.
troubleshooting.cause: The code expired after 30 minutes, or you used all 5 attempts.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Change details**, and send the form again for a new code.

troubleshooting.problem: The portal says **Support portal not found**.
troubleshooting.cause: The portal name in the address is wrong, or the portal is no longer available.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the address with your support team. Open `/portal/` and enter the portal name they give you.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in says **The e-mail, password or code is not correct.**
troubleshooting.cause: The e-mail, password or code has a typing error, or the code has expired.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your typing. Codes work for 10 minutes. Select **Send a new code** to get another one.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot sign in with your password after several tries.
troubleshooting.cause: After five wrong passwords, the account locks for 15 minutes.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait 15 minutes, or sign in with an e-mail code.

troubleshooting.problem: The ticket form asks you to sign in.
troubleshooting.cause: Your portal does not accept tickets from people who are not signed in.
troubleshooting.fix: Sign in, or create an account if the portal offers it.

troubleshooting.problem: A form asks you to check the highlighted fields.
troubleshooting.cause: A required field is empty or too short. For example, a subject needs at least 5 characters.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the message under each red field, correct it and submit again.

troubleshooting.problem: A file shows **Larger than the … MB limit** and is not attached.
troubleshooting.cause: The file is bigger than your support team allows.
troubleshooting.fix: Make the file smaller, for example by compressing it or taking a smaller screenshot. Then attach it again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Wait for the attachments to finish uploading.** appears when you send a reply.
troubleshooting.cause: A file is still uploading.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait until each file shows **Attached**, and then send again.

troubleshooting.problem: The ticket says **This ticket is closed** and has no reply box.
troubleshooting.cause: The reopen period for the ticket has ended.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Submit a new ticket**, and mention the old ticket number.

troubleshooting.problem: A ticket opens with **Ticket not found**.
troubleshooting.cause: The ticket does not exist, or it is not shared with your account.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the link, or look for the ticket in **My tickets**. Ask the team if you need wider ticket access.

troubleshooting.problem: **Your current password is not correct.** appears when you change your password.
troubleshooting.cause: The current password you entered is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter the password you sign in with now. If you forgot it, sign in with an e-mail code.

troubleshooting.problem: A satisfaction survey link says **This survey has closed**.
troubleshooting.cause: The time to answer the survey has passed.
troubleshooting.fix: Rate the ticket from the ticket page instead, if the **How did we do?** card is still there.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says **You are offline. Signing in needs a connection.**
troubleshooting.cause: The phone has no connection, so the app cannot check your details.
troubleshooting.fix: Connect to Wi-Fi or mobile data, and then sign in again.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in says **The details you entered are not correct.**
troubleshooting.cause: The e-mail, password or code is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your typing. Customers can choose **E-mail me a code** instead of a password.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in says **That help center or workspace does not exist.**
troubleshooting.cause: The **Workspace** or **Help center** name is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the name with your administrator or support team. For customers, it is the part of the portal address after `/portal/`.

troubleshooting.problem: Sign-in says **Your password has expired. Ask an administrator to reset it.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your agent password is too old.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to reset your password, and then sign in again.

troubleshooting.problem: A message shows **Not sent** on a ticket or on the **Me** tab.
troubleshooting.cause: The team rejected the message, for example because the ticket is now closed.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the reason under the message. Choose **Retry**, **Edit** or **Discard**.

troubleshooting.problem: A file is not attached, and the app says it is larger than the limit.
troubleshooting.cause: The file is too big, or the message already has 10 attachments.
troubleshooting.fix: Attach a smaller file, or send the extra files in another message.

troubleshooting.problem: A screen says **This list has not been saved on this device yet.**
troubleshooting.cause: You are offline and never opened this screen while online.
troubleshooting.fix: Reconnect, and open the screen once. After that, it is available offline.

troubleshooting.problem: A change says **Someone else changed this ticket — showing the latest version. Try again.**
troubleshooting.cause: A colleague changed the ticket while you were looking at it.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the latest version, and make your change again if it is still needed.

troubleshooting.problem: The console sign-in page says **Enter your e-mail address and password.**
troubleshooting.cause: A box is empty, or the e-mail address is not complete.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter your full operator e-mail address and your password. Then select **Sign in**.

troubleshooting.problem: The console sign-in page says **Invalid credentials.**
troubleshooting.cause: The e-mail address or the password is wrong, or your operator account is switched off.
troubleshooting.fix: Check both and try again. If it still fails, ask the team that runs SupportDesk.

troubleshooting.problem: The console asks **Enter your authenticator code.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your operator account uses an authenticator app.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter the current code from the app in **Authenticator code**, then select **Sign in**.

troubleshooting.problem: The console says **That code is not correct.**
troubleshooting.cause: The authenticator code was mistyped or has already changed.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the next code in the app and enter it.

troubleshooting.problem: The console says **Your platform session ended. Sign in again.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your 30-minute session ran out, or you reloaded the page.
troubleshooting.fix: Sign in again. Move between pages with the console menu, not the browser's reload button.

troubleshooting.problem: A tenant action fails with **Give a reason.**
troubleshooting.cause: **Suspend…**, **Cancel subscription…** and **Void…** need a reason.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a reason, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Extend trial…** says **This tenant is not on a trial.**
troubleshooting.cause: The subscription has no trial end date.
troubleshooting.fix: Use **Reactivate** or **Change plan…** instead.

troubleshooting.problem: **Reactivate** says **The tenant is pending deletion and cannot be reactivated.**
troubleshooting.cause: The keep-data period after cancellation has ended.
troubleshooting.fix: The tenant cannot come back. The customer must sign up again.

troubleshooting.problem: A support access request fails with **You already have a pending or active support-access request for this tenant.**
troubleshooting.cause: You can have only one open request for each tenant.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the tenant's decision, or for your current access to end.

troubleshooting.problem: A support access request fails with **Explain why access is needed (10–1000 characters).**
troubleshooting.cause: The reason is too short or too long.
troubleshooting.fix: Name the ticket or case and describe the problem in a sentence or two.

troubleshooting.problem: **Diagnostics** says **Support access is not active (pending, rejected, revoked or expired).**
troubleshooting.cause: The tenant has not approved the request, or the access has ended.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the status on **Support access**. If you still need access, send a new request.

troubleshooting.problem: Deleting a plan fails with **Tenants are subscribed to this plan.**
troubleshooting.cause: At least one tenant uses the plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Edit the plan and turn off **Offered at sign-up and in plan comparison** to hide it instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Deleting the trial plan fails with **The trial plan is required for self-service sign-up.**
troubleshooting.cause: Sign-up always uses the trial plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep the trial plan. Edit its limits or trial days instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Saving a plan fails with **A plan with code … already exists.**
troubleshooting.cause: Each plan code must be unique.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another code.

troubleshooting.problem: Saving a plan shows **Use a 3-letter ISO currency code.** under **Currency**.
troubleshooting.cause: The currency is not a three-letter code.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a code such as `USD`, `EUR` or `INR`.

troubleshooting.problem: Moving a tenant fails with **Use 3–40 lower-case letters, digits or underscores.**
troubleshooting.cause: The connection name has capital letters, spaces or other characters, or is too short or too long.
troubleshooting.fix: Correct the **Connection name**, then select **Provision and move** again.

troubleshooting.problem: Moving a tenant fails because the plan does not include dedicated storage.
troubleshooting.cause: The tenant's plan does not include dedicated storage.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the tenant's plan first, for example to Enterprise.

troubleshooting.problem: Moving a tenant fails with **Another tenant already uses this connection name.**
troubleshooting.cause: Each tenant needs its own connection name.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a different connection name.

troubleshooting.problem: Moving a tenant fails with a message about the connection or the storage system.
troubleshooting.cause: Your hosting team has not prepared the connection name, or it points somewhere the app cannot copy to.
troubleshooting.fix: Send the message to your hosting team. Try again after they fix it.

troubleshooting.problem: **Mark paid** or **Void…** fails with a message such as **Invoice SD-WINGS-0006 is Paid.**
troubleshooting.cause: Someone already paid or voided the invoice.
troubleshooting.fix: Refresh the list. The invoice no longer needs any action.

troubleshooting.problem: **Verify chain** shows **Chain broken**.
troubleshooting.cause: A platform audit entry was changed or removed.
troubleshooting.fix: Note the number of the first broken entry. Report it to your security lead at once.

faq.q: Can I reset my own password if I forget it?
faq.a: Not yet. Ask your SupportDesk administrator to reset it. When you are signed in, you can change your password on **My profile**.

faq.q: Why does a colleague see modules that I do not?
faq.a: Each person sees only the modules their role allows. Ask your administrator if you need another module for your work.

faq.q: Does the desk remember my password?
faq.a: No. The sign-in page remembers only your workspace and e-mail on that device. Your browser may offer to save the password. Do not let it on a shared computer.

faq.q: Can I sign in with my company's single sign-on?
faq.a: Not from the desk sign-in page yet. Sign in with your workspace, e-mail and password.

faq.q: Why are my numbers different from my supervisor's?
faq.a: Supervisors see numbers for their whole departments. Agents see their own work and their teams. The tiles that start with **My** count only the signed-in person's tickets.

faq.q: How often does the Command Center update?
faq.a: It updates live, as tickets change and alerts arrive. The SLA risk board also re-sorts every minute. You do not need to reload the page.

faq.q: Can I approve my own request?
faq.a: No. Another person with the right permission must decide it.

faq.q: Why do I see fewer tickets than my colleague in the same queue?
faq.a: Each role has a data scope, such as your own departments. Queues and views only show tickets inside your scope.

faq.q: Can a saved view show each agent their own tickets?
faq.a: Yes. In the **Assignee** condition, choose the option that ends with **(whoever views it)**. Share the view, and each person sees their own tickets.

faq.q: Does deleting a ticket remove it for good?
faq.a: No. Deleted and spam tickets go to the recycle bin. Anyone with the delete permission can restore them.

faq.q: Why did the list not refresh when a ticket changed?
faq.a: The list refreshes itself only while nothing is selected. Otherwise it shows **New activity**. Select it to reload.

faq.q: Why do all the countdowns in the header turn red after one target is missed?
faq.a: The header countdowns use the ticket's overall SLA state. The SLA section of the context pane shows the real state of each target.

faq.q: Does the customer see that I escalated or locked a ticket?
faq.a: No. Escalations, locks, tasks, time entries and follow-ups are only visible to agents.

faq.q: What happens to a resolved ticket that nobody touches?
faq.a: It closes itself after the number of days your administrator sets. The standard is 7 days.

faq.q: Can I undo a merge?
faq.a: No. Check the tickets in the **Merge tickets** dialog before you select **Merge**.

faq.q: Do customers ever see internal notes or handover notes?
faq.a: No. Only agents see them. The customer portal never shows them, and replies never include them.

faq.q: I closed the browser while writing. Is my reply lost?
faq.a: No. The composer saves a draft as you type. Open the ticket again on any device to carry on.

faq.q: Can I create my own reply templates?
faq.a: Not in the desk. Ask your administrator to add the template for you.

faq.q: Why did my colleague become a collaborator?
faq.a: You mentioned them with `@` in an internal note. Mentioning someone adds them as a collaborator and notifies them.

faq.q: Can I turn a WhatsApp conversation into a ticket myself?
faq.a: No. SupportDesk does it for you. The message joins the customer's open ticket, or SupportDesk creates a new one.

faq.q: Why did my WhatsApp reply go out as a template?
faq.a: WhatsApp allows free replies only for 24 hours after the customer's last message. After that, SupportDesk sends a pre-approved template instead.

faq.q: What does the number next to Waiting mean, such as 1/3?
faq.a: It is your chat load. The first number is the chats you have now. The second is the most you may take at once.

faq.q: Where does the chat go when it ends?
faq.a: The full chat is saved as a **Chat transcript** entry on the ticket. You and your colleagues can read it there.

faq.q: Can I undo a merge of two customers or two contacts?
faq.a: No. A merge cannot be undone. Check the comparison carefully before you select the merge button.

faq.q: Why was a new contact linked to a customer by itself?
faq.a: The contact's e-mail domain matches one of the customer's **E-mail domains**. SupportDesk links such contacts automatically.

faq.q: What does a customer's tier change?
faq.a: The tier decides which SLA policy applies to the customer's tickets. A Platinum customer can get faster targets than a Standard one.

faq.q: Can I change Wings ERP invoices from SupportDesk?
faq.a: No. The **ERP records** tab is read-only. Change the records in Wings ERP itself.

faq.q: Does an expired contract stop agents from working on a ticket?
faq.a: No. The eligibility check never blocks work. It shows the result so that your team can decide, for example to override it or to bill the time.

faq.q: How do I renew a contract?
faq.a: SupportDesk has no renew button. Add a new contract for the next period. The account manager gets reminders 30 and 7 days before the old one ends.

faq.q: Why can I not see the full licence key?
faq.a: SupportDesk masks licence keys when they are saved, so nobody can copy them from the desk. Keep the full key in your licensing system.

faq.q: What happens to tickets when I add a contract?
faq.a: SupportDesk checks the customer's open tickets again. Tickets that the new contract covers become **Entitled**.

faq.q: Can I schedule an article to publish later?
faq.a: No. Publish it when it is ready. You can set an **Expires** date so it is unpublished automatically.

faq.q: Do readers see my changes to a live article at once?
faq.a: No. Your saves create a new version. Readers keep seeing the published version until you publish again.

faq.q: Does SupportDesk translate articles automatically?
faq.a: No. A person writes each translation. Tick **Machine translated (flag for human review)** if a tool helped.

faq.q: Can agents run a troubleshooting flow for a customer on a ticket?
faq.a: No. Customers run flows in the portal. An **Escalate** step lets them open a ticket with their answers attached.

faq.q: Does the AI send anything to customers by itself?
faq.a: Only if your administrator allows automatic replies for approved situations. Otherwise every reply waits for a person. Automatic replies are blocked for critical tickets and frustrated customers.

faq.q: Can I undo an AI change?
faq.a: You can revert category, product, department, priority and tag changes on the **Proposals** tab. Messages that were sent cannot be undone.

faq.q: Where do the AI's answers come from?
faq.a: From your published articles and resolved tickets. A reply draft lists its sources under the text.

faq.q: Why did a proposal expire?
faq.a: Nobody approved or rejected it within 14 days.

faq.q: Why do my numbers differ from a colleague's?
faq.a: Each person sees only the tickets in their data scope. A team lead may see one team, and a manager the whole organisation.

faq.q: Can I build my own report?
faq.a: No. Use the ten standard reports with filters, or build a dashboard with your own widgets.

faq.q: Whose data does a scheduled report contain?
faq.a: It uses the data scope of the person who owns the schedule. Recipients see what the owner would see.

faq.q: What does (bh) mean next to a time?
faq.a: Business hours. Nights, weekends and holidays outside business hours are not counted.

faq.q: Can one work item cover several tickets?
faq.a: Yes. Link each ticket to the same work item. All linked tickets get the updates when the item is resolved or released.

faq.q: Is the customer told when a fix ships?
faq.a: Only if your administrator turned on automatic notices. Then the customer gets a “fix released” reply when the release is published. The work item shows **Customer notified**.

faq.q: Can I link a ticket to a Jira issue?
faq.a: No. SupportDesk works with the built-in board, Azure DevOps and GitHub.

faq.q: Can I choose which notifications I get?
faq.a: Not yet. Your administrator sets which events reach you in the app, by e-mail, by push or in a digest.

faq.q: Why does the bell show fewer notifications than the Notifications page?
faq.a: The bell shows only your latest notifications. The **Notifications** page shows the latest 200, with filters.

faq.q: Do I get desktop alerts for every notification?
faq.a: No. Desktop alerts and pop-up messages are only for warnings and critical items.

faq.q: Does approved leave move an agent's tickets?
faq.a: No. Approved leave only stops new tickets from reaching the agent. To hand over open tickets, reassign them. Or set up a delegation with **Also move open tickets when the window starts**.

faq.q: Why does an agent without a shift still get tickets at night?
faq.a: Agents without a shift count as always on shift. Shifts also matter only for teams with **Skip agents who are off shift** turned on.

faq.q: Can a light agent be a team member?
faq.a: Yes. Light agents can be members and see the team's tickets. Routing never gives them tickets, and they cannot own tickets.

faq.q: Does Test routing assign the sample ticket?
faq.a: No. **Test routing** only shows who would get the ticket and why. Nothing is created or assigned.

faq.q: Does the first response clock pause when the ticket waits on the customer?
faq.a: No. The first response clock never pauses. Pause statuses stop only the next response and resolution clocks.

faq.q: What happens to open tickets when I change a policy?
faq.a: Saving creates a new version of the policy. Open tickets are recalculated, and time already elapsed is kept.

faq.q: Why does a ticket appear twice on Live breaches?
faq.a: The list shows milestones, not tickets. A ticket shows once for each milestone that is at risk or breached.

faq.q: What happens when a user holds two roles?
faq.a: They get every permission of both roles. Their data scope is the broadest scope of the two.

faq.q: Do role changes need the user to sign in again?
faq.a: No. Changes apply to the user's open sessions at once.

faq.q: Can a light agent reply to customers if their role allows it?
faq.a: No. Light agents can never reply, own, transfer, bulk-edit or delete tickets, whatever their permissions say.

faq.q: Why do I not see some cards on the Administration home?
faq.a: A card shows only when your role holds one of its permissions. Ask an administrator if you need another area.

faq.q: Can I rename the built-in statuses?
faq.a: Yes. You can rename them and change their colour and customer label. You cannot delete them or change their category.

faq.q: Why can a ticket not move to a status I expect?
faq.a: The current status may restrict the allowed next statuses. Tickets that follow a blueprint use the blueprint's moves instead.

faq.q: What happens to stored values when I delete a custom field?
faq.a: They are kept but hidden. The field is removed from every form layout.

faq.q: Do I need a form layout?
faq.a: No. Without a layout, forms show every field that applies in the default order. Layouts let you group, order and require fields.

faq.q: Can I change the type or provider of a channel?
faq.a: No. Add a new channel with the right type and provider. Then turn off **Active** on the old one.

faq.q: Why did **Delete channel** only deactivate my channel?
faq.a: The channel has conversations. SupportDesk keeps it so that the ticket history stays complete.

faq.q: Does the channel simulator send real messages?
faq.a: No. It records outbound messages without sending them. Inbound simulations do create real tickets in your workspace.

faq.q: Does a simulation change my tickets?
faq.a: No. It only shows what would happen. The run is recorded as **Simulated** on the **Executions** tab.

faq.q: Can a rule change the status of a blueprint ticket?
faq.a: No. The **Set status** action is not allowed on blueprint tickets. Use a blueprint transition instead.

faq.q: What happens to running tickets when I publish a new blueprint version?
faq.a: New tickets use the new version. Tickets already on the blueprint keep the version they started with.

faq.q: Does the built-in AI send our data anywhere?
faq.a: No. The **Local (built-in)** provider runs inside SupportDesk. Nothing leaves your servers.

faq.q: Can an AI agent issue a refund or change a contract?
faq.a: No. Requests with real consequences always go to a person for a decision.

faq.q: Where do agents approve AI proposals?
faq.a: On the **Proposals** tab of the AI Assistant. They need the **Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions** permission.

faq.q: Can customers use our own domain for the help center now?
faq.a: Not yet. You can save the domain and check its DNS record, but customers must use the standard portal address for now.

faq.q: Do brands share the knowledge base?
faq.a: Yes, unless you limit a category to some brands. A category's **Brands** setting decides which help centers show it.

faq.q: What happens to tickets of a brand whose help center is offline?
faq.a: Nothing. Agents keep working on them. Customers of that brand can no longer use the help center.

faq.q: Can I send a test e-mail from a template?
faq.a: No. Use the **Preview**, which fills in sample values and adds the brand's footer.

faq.q: Can each brand have its own template?
faq.a: No. Each template is shared by all brands. Use `{{brand.name}}` for the brand name. SupportDesk adds each brand's e-mail footer to customer e-mails.

faq.q: Why do agents get a digest instead of separate e-mails?
faq.a: For events where both **E-mail** and **Digest** are ticked, SupportDesk bundles the event into the digest.

faq.q: Can I see a key or a client secret again later?
faq.a: No. The app shows it only once. If you lose it, create a new credential, update the integration and revoke the old one.

faq.q: Does the agent IP allow-list affect customers?
faq.a: No. It applies to agents only. Customers, connected systems and the platform operator can still reach SupportDesk.

faq.q: Why does one person have several sessions?
faq.a: Each browser, phone or new sign-in is its own session. A person can have up to the **Concurrent sessions per user** limit at once.

faq.q: Does SupportDesk change data in Wings ERP?
faq.a: The sync reads customers, installations, licences and contracts from the ERP. ERP screens can create tickets in SupportDesk through their own key.

faq.q: Will a sync overwrite what my team typed in SupportDesk?
faq.a: No. Fields your team owns, such as tier, account manager, SLA and coverage, are never overwritten.

faq.q: Do I need Azure DevOps or GitHub to escalate tickets?
faq.a: No. The built-in engineering board works on every plan and keeps work items inside SupportDesk.

faq.q: Can SupportDesk staff read our tickets?
faq.a: No. With approved support access, they see only usage, configuration counts, failed jobs and recent audit entries. They never see tickets or customer data.

faq.q: Can I undo an erasure or a deletion?
faq.a: No. Erased and deleted data cannot be recovered. Use **Dry run** and check requests before you approve them.

faq.q: Does a legal hold stop agents from working on tickets?
faq.a: No. Agents work as usual. The hold only stops retention, deletion and erasure of the covered records.

faq.q: Does a configuration export include tickets or customers?
faq.a: No. It holds only settings, such as statuses, fields, SLA policies and rules.

faq.q: Are passwords and secrets copied to the other workspace?
faq.a: No. Secrets are never exported. Enter them again in the target workspace.

faq.q: How do we pay SupportDesk invoices?
faq.a: By bank transfer. Each invoice shows how to pay. Quote the invoice number as the payment reference.

faq.q: What happens when our trial ends?
faq.a: The subscription becomes past due, and a grace period starts. Choose a paid plan before it ends to avoid suspension.

faq.q: Can we cancel our subscription ourselves?
faq.a: No. Contact your SupportDesk provider to cancel.

faq.q: Do I need an account to use the portal?
faq.a: No. You can read articles, search and read the community without signing in. Some portals also accept tickets without an account. You need an account to follow tickets online, attach files and post in the community.

faq.q: Why can I see tickets that I did not raise?
faq.a: Your support team gave you location or organisation access. You then see your colleagues' tickets too. The **Raised by** column shows who raised each ticket.

faq.q: I forgot my portal password. What do I do?
faq.a: Sign in with an e-mail code. The portal cannot replace a forgotten password, so keep using codes or ask the support team for help.

faq.q: How long can I reopen a closed ticket?
faq.a: Your support team decides. The ticket shows the last date you can reopen it. After that, submit a new ticket.

faq.q: Does the assistant create tickets by itself?
faq.a: No. It only answers from the help articles. If it cannot help, select **Create a ticket**, check the form and submit it yourself.

faq.q: Can I use agent mode and customer mode on the same phone?
faq.a: Yes. Choose the mode on the sign-in screen. The app keeps a separate sign-in for each mode.

faq.q: Will a reply I queued offline be sent twice?
faq.a: No. Each queued message has its own marker, so a retry never creates a duplicate.

faq.q: Why don't I get push notifications?
faq.a: The standard app does not include push notifications. Keep the app open to get live updates, or ask your organisation about a build with push notifications.

faq.q: What happens to my unsent messages if I sign out?
faq.a: They are deleted from the phone. The app warns you first, so send or discard them before you sign out.

faq.q: Can I open a tenant's tickets or sign in as one of its users?
faq.a: No. Operators never see tickets or customer data, and they cannot act as a tenant's users. Ask for support access to see read-only diagnostics instead.

faq.q: Why does reloading the console page sign me out?
faq.a: For safety, the console keeps your session only while the page stays open. Reloading ends it. Move between pages with the console menu.

faq.q: Does marking an invoice paid lift a suspension?
faq.a: It lifts a suspension caused by missed payment once no overdue invoice is left. It does not lift a suspension that an operator set. Use **Reactivate** for that.

faq.q: What happens to a tenant's data after I cancel its subscription?
faq.a: Access stops at once. The data is kept for the number of days you chose, from 0 to 365. After that date, the tenant becomes **Pending deletion**.

faq.q: How do I stop new customers from choosing a plan?
faq.a: Edit the plan and turn off **Offered at sign-up and in plan comparison**. Tenants already on the plan keep it.

glossary.definition: A support team member who answers tickets and chats in the desk.
A team lead who watches the queue, SLA risk and the team's workload, and moves work between agents.
A person who sets up the workspace: users, roles, channels, policies, security and billing.
A person at the company that runs the SupportDesk service. Operators manage workspaces, plans and invoices in the platform console.
One customer question or problem, with all its messages, notes and changes. Each ticket has a number.
Service level agreement. The response and resolution times the team promises, measured by timers on each ticket.
A way customers reach you, such as e-mail, the portal, live chat, a messaging app or phone.
Your organisation's own SupportDesk, with its own users, customers and settings. You enter its short name when you sign in.
A company name, logo and customer portal. One workspace can serve several brands.
The website where customers raise and follow tickets, read help articles and chat with support.
The SupportDesk app that agents, supervisors and administrators use in a web browser.
A sign-in check that asks for a short code after your password. The code comes by e-mail or from an authenticator app. On your profile it is called two-factor authentication.
A phone app, such as Microsoft Authenticator, that shows a new 6-digit sign-in code every few seconds.
A search box that opens with Ctrl+K. It lets you find tickets and run commands from the keyboard.
Your working status: Online, Away, Busy or Offline. Routing uses it to decide who gets new work.
The column on the left of the desk that lists the modules you can open.
The time between signing in and signing out. A session also ends after a set time, or when an administrator ends it.
Text that SupportDesk adds to the end of each e-mail reply you send. You set it on your profile.
The desk's live overview page with key numbers, SLA risk, team workload, replies, approvals and escalations.
An SLA target whose time has passed before the ticket met it.
An SLA target that is close to its due time and not yet met.
A ready-made ticket list, such as your own tickets, unassigned tickets or escalated tickets.
The most open tickets an agent should hold at one time. Administrators set it.
Raising a ticket to a higher level of attention, such as a senior agent, a supervisor or engineering.
A request that a supervisor must approve before an action, such as a department transfer, can go ahead.
A ticket list defined by conditions, such as all critical tickets assigned to you. It can be personal or shared.
The saved view that opens when you go to Tickets without choosing a list. It has a star in the Views panel.
A change applied to many selected tickets at once, such as assigning or closing them.
The Deleted tickets list. It holds deleted and spam tickets until someone restores them.
The part of the help desk a role may see, such as its own departments. Lists never show tickets outside it.
One of six fixed groups every status belongs to: Open, Assigned, In progress, Waiting, Resolved or Closed.
A finer reason inside a status, such as information requested inside Waiting on Customer.
A time limit from the SLA policy, such as first response, next response or resolution.
A number that goes up each time a ticket is escalated, by a person or by the service clock.
Moving the conversation of duplicate tickets into one ticket and closing the duplicates.
Moving some messages of a ticket into a new ticket for the same customer.
Creating a new ticket with the same customer, fields and description, but without the conversation.
A person who gets a notification about every update on a ticket.
An agent who helps with a ticket. Mentioning someone in an internal note makes them a collaborator.
A person given access to a ticket until a set end date.
A reminder to check back on a ticket at a set time.
A 10-minute hold that stops others from editing, assigning or resolving a ticket while you work on it.
The avatars in the ticket header that show who else has the ticket open and who is typing.
The right-hand pane of the ticket workspace with the customer, contact, service targets, contracts and earlier tickets.
Whether a customer's contract covers a request. The ticket header shows it as a badge.
The writing area at the bottom of a ticket, used for replies, internal notes and handover notes.
A note on a ticket that only agents can see. It has an amber background.
An internal note for the next agent who works on the ticket.
Ready-made reply text with placeholders that SupportDesk fills in, such as the contact's name.
A code in a template, such as {{contact.name}}, that SupportDesk replaces with real details.
An unsent reply or note that SupportDesk saves as you type.
Typing @ and a colleague's name in a note. It notifies them and makes them a collaborator.
When someone posts on a ticket while you are writing a reply. SupportDesk shows the new entries before you send.
A thread of messages with one person on one channel, such as an e-mail thread, a WhatsApp chat or a phone call. Conversations appear in the Inbox.
The screen where agents accept, answer, transfer and end website chats.
The most live chats an agent may handle at the same time. A manager sets it. The default is 3.
The 24 hours after a customer's last WhatsApp message. Inside it you can reply freely. After it, replies go out as pre-approved templates.
The full text of a live chat, saved on the ticket when the chat ends.
A person who starts a chat on your website. A visitor may not be a known contact yet.
An organisation that you support. Customers can have a parent company and subsidiaries.
A person who works for a customer and contacts your support team.
The page that shows everything about one customer: tickets, contacts, locations, products, contracts, activities and Wings ERP records.
A customer's service level: Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze or Standard. It decides which SLA policy applies.
The person in your team who looks after a customer. They get reminders before the customer's contracts end.
A customer that belongs to a parent customer, such as a branch company or a franchise.
An e-mail address, phone number or messaging id that links incoming messages to a contact.
A contact's choice to receive or refuse messages, per channel and purpose.
A named set of customers, such as Key Accounts, used to filter lists and in knowledge base access rules.
A planned visit, session, training, maintenance, upgrade, call or meeting with a customer.
Which tickets a contact can see in the customer portal: none, their own, their location's or their whole organisation's.
Software or hardware that you support. It has modules, versions and releases.
A part of a product, such as Finance or Payroll. Agents choose it on a ticket.
A build of a product version, such as a patch or a hotfix.
The date after which you no longer support a product version.
One place where a customer runs one of your products, with its version, environment and setup.
A serialised item at a customer site, such as a POS terminal, with its warranty.
All the installations of your products, counted by version.
What a customer bought: a warranty, an AMC or another kind of support for a period.
Annual maintenance contract: a yearly support contract.
Whether a ticket is covered by an active contract: Entitled, Not entitled, Expired, Entitlement unknown or Overridden.
A recorded decision to work on a ticket that a contract does not cover. It needs a reason.
A help page in the knowledge base. It can be public, for signed-in customers, internal or restricted.
Said of an article whose published version readers can see.
A condition on customer, customer group, tier or product that decides who can read a restricted article.
A search that found no article. It shows a topic you may need to write about.
A decision tree of questions that leads customers to a solution, an article or an agent.
A question, idea or tip that a customer posts in the portal's community forums.
A translation made before the original article was last published. It needs updating.
An action that an AI agent suggests for a ticket, such as a new priority or a reply. A person approves or rejects it.
An automatic AI helper that checks tickets and makes proposals, such as the triage assistant.
Said of an AI draft that is based on your own articles or resolved tickets.
A search that finds items with the same meaning as your words, even when the wording differs.
A day with far more tickets than usual for a product, version, customer or category.
The customer's mood as the AI reads it: positive, neutral, negative or frustrated.
How sure the AI is about a suggestion, shown as a bar or a percentage.
A page of widgets that show support figures, charts and tables.
One figure, chart or table on a dashboard.
Selecting a figure, bar or row to see the tickets behind it.
The share of tickets solved with the first reply, without further back and forth.
Working hours set by your administrator. Times marked (bh) count only these hours.
A standard report that is e-mailed as an attachment on a regular day and time.
A bug, feature or task for engineers, with a key such as ENG-12. Tickets link to work items to follow a fix.
The release that will ship, or has shipped, the fix for a work item.
The steps that reproduce a problem. Engineers use them to see the defect for themselves.
Sending a ticket's product defect to engineers by creating a work item from the ticket.
A message from SupportDesk about something that needs you, such as an assignment, a customer reply or an SLA breach.
Confirm that you have seen a critical notification. It also stops further copies of that alert.
A notification that your browser shows on your computer's desktop, outside the desk page. You must allow it once.
A single e-mail that collects several notifications, sent hourly or daily.
Hours when SupportDesk holds back e-mail and push notifications. Critical alerts still go out.
The rule a team uses to pick the agent for a new ticket: Manual, Round robin, Load balanced, Skill based or Territory.
An out-of-office arrangement. While it is active, the away agent's new assignments and approval requests go to a delegate.
The team that receives a team's new tickets when none of its own members can take them.
